Title: Speech at the Listing Ceremony of the Bank of Communications
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 23 Jun 2005 Bank of Communications Celebratory Cocktail Reception Speech on the Listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange Chi-gang Yim is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Chairman Jiang, President Zhang, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, First of all, on behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, I would like to express my warm congratulations to Bank of Communications on its successful listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The Bank of Communications is the first joint-stock bank in China to be successfully listed in Hong Kong, marking an important step forward for the state in the reform of the banking system The outstanding achievements of the Bank of Communications are obvious to all, and it is in a leading position in the reform process of mainland banks. Bank of Communications is the first nationwide joint-stock commercial bank re-established in 1987 after the country's reform and opening up. After the State Council approved the overall reform plan of the Bank of Communications in June last year, the reform process of the Bank of Communications was very fast, first completing the financial reorganization, and then introducing HSBC as a strategic partner, and the level of corporate governance, risk management and operational efficiency is constantly improving, laying a good foundation for meeting the challenges of the future. The fact that Bank of Communications is able to list in Hong Kong today not only means that banks meet the standards for Hong Kong listing in all aspects, but also marks an important step in the reform of the mainland's banking sector and provides a demonstration role for other mainland banks that are undergoing reforms. Following the Bank of Communications, the four state-owned commercial banks and other mainland banks are also undergoing reform and restructuring, introducing strategic investors and seeking overseas listings to develop their business. As we all know, most of the current work of financial integration in the mainland relies on the banking system as an intermediary channel. Among the new financing channels in the mainland last year, the proportion of financing in the form of loans was still the highest, with more than 90%. In the long run, of course, there is a need for the mainland to develop more other channels of financial intermediation and to diversify financial integration, which is very important for the stable operation of the financial system and the sustained development of the economy. However, at present, the development of the mainland's capital market has just started, and it is also facing some difficulties in development, so the banking system will remain the most important financial intermediary channel for the mainland's financial integration for a long time to come, and play a core role in the mainland's economic development. In addition, with China's accession to the WTO and its agreement to fully open up its banking sector to the outside world by the end of 2006, mainland banks will face fierce competition from foreign-funded financial institutions with abundant capital, abundant talents, strong financial innovation capabilities, and rich international experience. Therefore, strengthening the governance of the mainland banking industry and enhancing its efficiency and competitiveness will be a major direction in the process of financial reform and opening up in the mainland, and the listing of mainland banks through overseas listing is one of the important driving forces, because this can not only enhance the capital strength of banks, but also further promote the diversification of shares, and improve corporate governance through the supervision mechanism of the capital market. Improving the level of operation and management will also help the mainland banking industry to integrate with the international market in the long run. As an advanced financial centre in China, Hong Kong has a diversified, multi-currency, sound, international level and state-of-the-art payment and settlement arrangement financial platform, and is the best venue for mainland enterprises to raise international funds. However, I believe that with the appropriate arrangements in place, Hong Kong's financial platform can also provide financial services that are lacking in the Mainland for capital financing in the Mainland, and make greater contributions to the sustainable economic development of the Mainland. Finally, on behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, I would like to express my heartfelt wishes for the listing of Bank of Communications on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange and hope that the banking business of Bank of Communications will flourish day by day and develop its great achievements. Thank you! Last revision date: 23 June 2005

Title: Remarks at the Signing Ceremony for the Launch of Retail Renminbi Non-deliverable Forward Contracts
text: 19/09/22, 15:59 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Remarks at the Signing Ceremony for the Launch of Retail Renminbi Non-deliverable Forwar... Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 26 Sep 2005 Remarks at the Signing Ceremony for the Launch of Retail Renminbi Non-deliverable Forward Contracts Y K Choi, Chairman of Treasury Markets Forum of Hong Kong Ladies and gentlemen, 1. On behalf of the Treasury Markets Forum of Hong Kong (TMF), I would like to welcome you all to this signing ceremony for the launch of retail renminbi non-deliverable forward contracts. 2. Following recent reforms to the renminbi exchange rate regime, there is an increasing demand from small and medium-sized enterprises and other retail customers for financial products to hedge their renminbi exposures. In view of such market development, the TMF responded quickly and formed a Working Group in August to consider and develop a product to meet the market demand. The Working Group has now completed its study and recommended the launch of a product - retail Renminbi non-deliverable forward contracts, in Hong Kong. 3.1 will leave it to Ms Anita Fung, the Chairman of the TMF's Market and Product Development Sub-Committee, to explain the main features of the product to you. I would like to take this opportunity to thank Anita and other members of the Working Group for their contribution in developing the product within such a short time frame. This is a clear demonstration that the TMF, with the help and cooperation of market practitioners, is able to react to market developments quickly and efficiently, and this is very important for the development of Hong Kong's treasury markets. 4. The conviction that "the whole is greater than the sum of its parts" is indeed what drove the establishment of the TMF last year. By bringing together bankers, brokers, corporate treasurers and other market professionals, the TMF's objective is to raise the level of professionalism of market practitioners and the overall competitiveness of Hong Kong's treasury markets. 5. The TMF has made a number of achievements since its establishment last year. The launch of this retail renminbi NDF product is a clear example of how the TMF leverages on the coordinated efforts of its members to drive market and product developments. 6. This spirit of cooperation actually extends beyond market and product developments. Last year, the TMF joined hands with the ACI-The Financial Markets of Hong Kong (ACIHK) to launch a membership drive. As a result, ACIHK's membership rose sharply from 500 to more than 2,000. Furthermore, an educational programme was launched concurrently in / 1/2 19/09/22, 15:59 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Remarks at the Signing Ceremony for the Launch of Retail Renminbi Non-deliverable Forwar... conjunction with two local universities, with the aim of raising the professionalism of treasury market practitioners in Hong Kong. 7. Apart from these achievements, the TMF has also contributed to the promotion of Hong Kong's treasury markets, through participating in conferences and exhibitions overseas and on the Mainland, and in the formulation of industry codes and standards. These efforts have been made a lot more effective by having the industry participants working together through the TMF platform. 8. To consolidate the success achieved so far by the TMF, and to provide a solid institutional structure to take forward further initiatives for market development, the TMF is working to establish a Treasury Markets Association (TMA) through a merger with the ACIHK. Preparatory work is progressing well and we expect the TMA to be formally established by the end of this year. The TMA will continue to work closely with the industry to foster financial innovation, enhance the skills of market professionals and strengthen Hong Kong's position as a regional hub for treasury markets business. 9.1 believe that the achievements made by the TMF so far, including the launch of the retail renminbi NDF product today, are only a start. The establishment of the TMA later this year should provide an even better platform from which to continue and intensify these collaborative efforts. 10. Last but not least, I would like to thank once again all the Working Group members for their efforts in developing and launching this retail RMB NDF product in such a short time. This is a very good demonstration of the efficiency of bankers in this vibrant and dynamic market. 11. Thank you. Last revision date : 26 September 2005 / 2/2

Title: A Financial Development Strategy for Hong Kong
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 2006/03/23 Hong Kong's financial development strategy Chi-gang Yim is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (At the Pan-Pearl River Delta Visiting Group Financial Services Forum, published in Volume 47 of the Quarterly Report of the Monetary Authority). Hello leaders, ladies and gentlemen. First of all, friends from the Pan-Pearl River region are very welcome to Hong Kong to participate in this financial services forum. The Pan-Pearl River region has very close relations from trade, resident exchanges, to finance and investment. All regions in the pan-PRC region have their own economic characteristics and advantages, and cooperation with each other can play the role of mutual assistance and development. As part of the Pan-Pearl River region, Hong Kong's greatest contribution may be finance. It is a great honor for me to have the opportunity to speak here today to share my views on financial issues and to introduce a strategy for Hong Kong's financial development. I hope and believe that this strategy will enable Hong Kong to make greater contributions to the country's reform and opening up, and will also play a great role in deepening and expanding the cooperative relationship in the pan-PRD region. I also hope that everyone can agree with this financial development strategy and, if there is a chance, make appropriate and policy cooperation and support in the mainland. In fact, I would like to talk about an important responsibility of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, that is, how to maintain Hong Kong's status as an international financial center in accordance with Article 109 of the Basic Law. Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre Of course, Hong Kong is now a leading international financial centre in Asia: in terms of financial infrastructure, Hong Kong has the most advanced multi-currency payment, settlement and custody system in Asia at the international level, providing a safe and secure environment for all kinds of financial transactions. In terms of market activity, the Hong Kong stock market is one of the top ten markets in the world, and in 2005, it surpassed Japan to become the largest market in Asia in terms of capital raising and can be said to be the IPO center in the region; With a total asset value of HK3,618 billion at the end of 2004, Hong Kong's fund management business is one of the largest asset management centres in the region. At present, only a small number of fund-raising activities carried out in Hong Kong are directly related to local economic activities, and most of them are transferred overseas funds through Hong Kong to production activities outside Hong Kong. For example, the vast majority of mainland enterprises issuing H-shares in Hong Kong to raise funds are purchased by overseas investors, and in fact overseas funds are transferred to mainland investments through Hong Kong. As of the end of 2005, a total of 209 mainland limited companies (H shares) and mainland related companies (red chip stocks) were listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, accounting for one-third of the total market capitalization. In 2005 alone, H shares and red chips raised nearly HK180 billion, representing 60% of the total market offering. In addition, H-shares and red-chip stocks accounted for 40% of the total market transactions. Times As an intermediary between the mainland and overseas capital financing, Hong Kong has become the core task of Hong Kong's international financial center. I believe that all leaders will agree that it is necessary to think of danger in times of peace. Whether or not we can maintain our status as an international financial center in accordance with the provisions of the Basic Law is an issue that we should actively study. In fact, under the accelerated reform of the financial system in the mainland, Hong Kong's status as a financial intermediary between the mainland and overseas is likely to be marginalized. Therefore, what we want to study is how Hong Kong's international financial center should keep pace with the times under the trend of national reform and opening up, developed information technology and market globalization. Different people have different opinions on this issue, such as hoping that Hong Kong can become Manhattan in China or Switzerland in Asia, or suggesting that Hong Kong imitate the characteristics of overseas financial centers and move various products or operating models to Hong Kong. But I have pointed out before that of course we must learn from other financial centers, but Hong Kong is Hong Kong, which is different from other places in economic, geographical, political, and cultural terms, especially in the face of the rapidly developing mainland under the reform and opening up, and the role that Hong Kong can play in the financial field is more complex and more challenging than Manhattan, London, or Switzerland. At present, there are still many aspects of control in the financial system in the mainland. Under such conditions, given Hong Kong's special status, does Hong Kong's competitiveness depend only on whether we can replicate Manhattan-style derivatives and hedge funds, or Swiss-style wealth management arrangements? I don't think the financial development strategy in the form of labels and slogans makes much sense. Deng Xiaoping once said: We must seek truth from facts, tell the truth, and do honest things. In the final analysis, the function of financial centers is to provide a platform for financial integration activities to take place, that is, to efficiently transfer savings to investment and to productive economic links. Therefore, I believe that as the "Hong Kong of China" under one country, two systems, it is more important to strengthen our role in the mainland's financial integration process in the future in order to maintain Hong Kong's status as an international financial center. To do this effectively, we need to know more about the situation in the mainland so that we can expand new business opportunities and achieve mutual benefit and win-win results in serving mainland investors and fund-raisers. Financial conditions in the Mainland Based on our observations in Hong Kong, the current financial situation on the mainland is worth noting in three ways: First, over the past decade, the mainland's savings rate has continued to grow, reaching more than 45 per cent of GDP in 2004. In such a high local savings rate environment, there are now some questions about whether companies need to raise funds outside and whether foreign direct investment is a good thing in any case. I personally believe that relative to attracting foreign investment, the priority to the mainland's financial reform now is to open up diversified channels for the mainland's savers and fund-raisers , so that they can touch them in the market environment, directly or indirectly, through financial intermediaries to meet the needs of both sides for investment and fundraising. Second, the continuous inflow of foreign exchange in recent years has put upward pressure on the renminbi and increased the difficulty of currency and exchange rate management. In 2005, the mainland's foreign exchange reserves increased by US208.9 billion to US818.9 billion, and the relevant departments also needed to write off the excessive base currency of the renminbi, increasing the difficulty and cost of currency management. Therefore, there is now a need to adjust the foreign exchange policy of "restricting the entry and exit of the prize" or "lenient in and strict exit" to allow and even encourage funds to "go out" and "hide them in the people." In the long run, of course, the capital account should be fully opened to make RMB freely convertible. Third, the reform of the mainland's financial market is still ongoing. At present, the efficiency of financial integration is low and it is excessively concentrated in banking channels, and more than 80% of corporate financing is bank loans. The variety of investment instruments on the market is not abundant. However, in the past few years, the stock market has been sluggish, and many good mainland enterprises have chosen to list overseas, so that mainland investors cannot buy shares of these enterprises. This is unfair to them, there is a need to take care of their interests, open up investment opportunities in the capital market for them, let their savings get a higher return, thereby increasing consumption and promoting sustained economic growth. Hong Kong's future financial development strategy To maintain Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre, I believe that Hong Kong's development strategy needs to evolve with the times and align with the three relevant and changing financial conditions on the mainland that I just mentioned. On the one hand, Hong Kong should strengthen and continue to issue measures to provide convenient, low-risk and effective channels for financial integration between the mainland and the mainland, bring savings funds to the mainland to meet some of the needs of mainland fundraisers, and also provide investment tools to meet the needs of mainland savers for overseas investment. On the other hand, Hong Kong needs to actively expand the financing of the mainland itself, that is to say, to provide an equally convenient, low-risk and effective platform for the combination of mainland investors and fund-raisers. In the environment of developed information technology, financial integration services, especially through the capital market, can be exempted from geographical restrictions. At the very least, services at the wholesale level are not necessarily required to be provided locally. Someone told me that if I want to arrange the mainland's own financial financing in Hong Kong, is it not that Hong Kong wants to "fish across the border"? Some people have also reminded me that with regard to the policy of one country, two systems, Hong Kong should not overstep its bounds. I disagree with these views. At present, it is in our national interest to improve the efficiency of financial integration in the Mainland, so that rapid economic growth and development can be sustained. "Finance is very important and is the core of the modern economy," which is also what Deng Xiaoping said. Under one country, two systems, our country has two financial systems, and it is natural and appropriate to use the strengths of one financial system to make up for the shortcomings of the other financial system, and to use the effective financial integration platform in one of the financial systems to assist the financial integration in the other system. Of course, there are still many aspects of the mainland's financial system, such as those under the capital account, so it still does not fully utilize the strengths of Hong Kong's financial system. Hong Kong has also failed to contribute fully to the mainland's financial facilities. However, I personally believe that the current monetary and financial conditions in the mainland are a golden opportunity for further financial opening-up. Risk management is certainly needed, but we can establish appropriate, monitorable, adjustable and highly controllable channels to make good use of Hong Kong's financial facilities to assist the Mainland, while also supporting Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre. I think Hong Kong's future financial sand strategy should have 5 directions: (1) Hong Kong financial institutions "walk in" to the Mainland to provide services; (b) Hong Kong as the gateway for Mainland funds to "go global"; (c) Hong Kong financial instruments, especially those issued by Mainland enterprises in Hong Kong, "going into" the Mainland; (d) the strengthening of the capacity of the Hong Kong financial system to process transactions in renminbi as a unit of currency; And (v) Strengthen the links between the financial infrastructure of the two places. This strategy is a win-win situation and is good for both the mainland and Hong Kong. Now I will explain these five directions more specifically. (1) Hong Kong financial institutions "walk in" to the Mainland For the huge market of the mainland, Hong Kong financial institutions should actively "go in" to provide mainland customers with geographically restricted financial services such as retail banking, and expand the scope of services in Hong Kong's financial industry. In this regard, the Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA) has played a significant role in gradually easing the restrictions on Hong Kong financial institutions entering the mainland market. Under the CEPA framework, Hong Kong banks are already able to enjoy a number of benefits compared to other foreign banks, such as lower capital requirements for setting up branches. As a result of this lower requirement, Hong Kong's medium-sized banks were able to set up new bases in Shenzhen and other places to strengthen Hong Kong's financial ties with the Pan-Pearl River. Other benefits also include the ability to apply for RMB business with more relaxed opening period rules and profit assessments, as well as more relaxed working capital requirements. In the next step, Hong Kong's financial institutions should make better use of CEPA and other ways to go to the mainland, strengthen their service scope and categories in the mainland, and actively explore the mainland market. For the mainland, Hong Kong's financial institutions are more familiar with the situation on the mainland and have international experience, and entering the mainland market will have the effect of technology transfer, and at the same time provide more choices of financial tools and services for enterprises and ordinary people in the mainland. (2) Hong Kong serves as the gateway for Mainland funds to "go global" Hong Kong can become the gateway for the mainland's savings funds to go global. Hong Kong has an efficient and multi-currency fundraising platform that allows the mainland's savings and funds to be pooled with the mainland's investment needs, enabling mainland investors to directly or indirectly purchase high-quality state-owned enterprise shares listed in Hong Kong. At the beginning of this year, the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) has set actively expanding the channels for capital outflow and steadily promoting the convertibility of capital accounts as one of its work goals for 2006. Qualified Domestic Institutional Investors (QDIIs) are expected to step out. Hong Kong's financial institutions are very familiar with the operation of the Mainland and international financial markets, and have cultural, linguistic advantages over other foreign institutions when serving mainland investors. Mainland investors are also more familiar with the Hong Kong market than other markets, and consider first focusing on investing in stocks and bonds issued by mainland enterprises in Hong Kong, which not only achieves the purpose of orderly exit of mainland funds, supports the development of mainland enterprises listed in Hong Kong, but also opens up an effective channel for the mainland's own capital financing in Hong Kong. (3) Hong Kong financial instruments "go in" to the Mainland In order to facilitate mainland residents to invest in enterprises raising funds in Hong Kong, consideration should be given to introducing Hong Kong's financial tools, especially securities issued by mainland institutions, into the mainland for sale when permitted by the relevant regulations of the mainland. There are many specific practices, such as the use of depository securities or dual listing, which allows investors in both places to buy and sell Hong Kong-listed shares. But one thing worth noting is that no matter what way it is taken, there may be a problem, that is, the same stock has different prices. To solve this problem, an arbitrage mechanism needs to be introduced to balance the prices of the stocks in question in both places. If Hong Kong's financial instruments can be "walked in" and the reasonable needs of mainland investors can be met, not only can Hong Kong's IPO center position be sustained, but also for mainland fundraisers, such as enterprises in the Pan-Pearl River region, they can continue to use Hong Kong's international financing platform to raise more funds. This can not only enrich the product range of mainland investment, but also improve the efficiency of financial integration in the mainland. (d) Hong Kong's financial system strengthens its ability to handle transactions in RMB as a monetary unit The renminbi is the currency used by mainland investors and fundraisers, and in order for Hong Kong to better meet the mainland's needs for financial integration, it is necessary for Hong Kong to strengthen its financial system's ability to handle the use of renminbi as a trading currency. The development of Hong Kong's RMB business in recent years is the first step in this direction. Since its inception in early 2004, the business has been developing steadily and in an orderly manner. At the end of 2005, there were a total of RMB22.6 billion in deposits, 428,000 RMB accounts opened, and 38 Hong Kong banks (i.e. almost all banks operating retail business in Hong Kong) had set up relevant businesses. Hong Kong's RMB business will help to promote the economic integration of the two places, especially the Pan-Pearl River region, and facilitate the travel and consumption of residents of the two places. As for the next step in the RMB business, we are actively negotiating with the People's Bank of China to allow the issuance of RMB bonds in Hong Kong and the payment of trade in RMB . Further expansion of RMB business can not only enhance Hong Kong's status as an international financial center, but can also be seen as a test of the renminbi's move towards full convertibility. (v) Strengthening the links between the two places The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has been cooperating with relevant authorities in Shenzhen, Guangzhou and Beijing for many years in the financial infrastructure of payment, settlement and custody systems. Several different currencies and different regions of the payment system are now connected, and research is also being made to continue to expand the link between the bond and equity central settlement systems in the future. Coupled with the expansion of Hong Kong's renminbi financial infrastructure and its networking with its mainland counterparts, these developments have helped to ensure that the increasing flow of funds and financial activities between the two places takes place in a safe, reliable and efficient manner. Financial cooperation If Hong Kong's financial cooperation with the Mainland can develop in the five directions of this strategy with the times, it will certainly greatly enhance the efficiency of financial integration in the Mainland, while at the same time maintaining the status of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region as an international financial centre in accordance with Article 109 of the Basic Law. Under the capitalist free-market economy, the financial system and market of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region are very free. There are no policy problems in going in these five directions, and you can do it at any time. Technically, there is not much of a problem, such as adding RMB to our multi-currency instant payment system, the preliminary work has been fully done, if the green light is on, we can complete it in just five weeks, reaching the simultaneous settlement of RMB, Hong Kong dollars, US dollars and euros in Hong Kong, and reaching the highest level of managing payment risks. In addition, the mechanism for issuing RMB bonds can be activated at any time as long as the mainland authorities give the green light and agree that the issuer will repatriate the RMB funds raised to the mainland. The strategy has five directions and the expectations have five. We look forward to the green light: we look forward to the Mainland reaching consensus on relevant policies: We look forward to the introduction of more and more concrete measures to improve the efficiency of financial integration in the Mainland in the process of implementing the Eleventh Five-Year Plan ; Looking forward to Hong Kong making greater and more comprehensive contributions to the country's financial facilities: Looking forward to being able to handle the provisions of Article 109 of the Basic Law with peace of mind and maintain Hong Kong's status as an international financial center. The green light can also bring a lot of business opportunities to the Pan-Pearl River region. Many of the Mainland enterprises listed in Hong Kong are from the Pan-Pearl River region. Banks and financial institutions in Hong Kong have seen the good economic development situation in the Pan-PRD region and have continued to open branches in the Pan-PRD region in recent years. At present, Hong Kong banks have 69 branches in the Mainland, of which more than half are located in the Pan-PRD region. Much of the financial infrastructure links between Hong Kong and the Mainland began in the Pan-Pearl River region. For example, the existing cross-border Hong Kong dollar and US dollar cheque settlement mechanism between Hong Kong and the Mainland is first connected to Shenzhen and Guangdong before being further extended to other regions. On 6 March, Hong Kong banks launched their latest RMB business, RMB cheques, which was also the first to be piloted in Guangdong Province. These collaborative projects show the strategic role of the Pan-Pearl River region. summary In my speech today, I put forward a five-way financial development strategy for enhancing the efficiency of financial integration in the mainland and maintaining Hong Kong's status as an international financial center, and I also look forward to the early realization of the five expectations. Hong Kong's past and present position is based on its window role in attracting foreign investment to the Mainland. As for the future, in the rapidly changing international financial environment, Hong Kong needs to seize the opportunities brought about by the mainland's reform and opening up, take the lead and keep pace with the times before other overseas financial centers, and fully participate in the mainland's capital financing in order to strengthen its status as an IPO and asset management center. At the same time, Hong Kong should also cooperate with the reform strategy of the Mainland to provide a testing ground for the reform of the Mainland and provide suitable and diversified services for fundraisers and investors in the Mainland, especially in the Pan-PRD region. The mainland economy is now the fourth largest economic entity in the world. The continued growth and development of the Mainland's economy provides the best opportunity for Hong Kong to maintain and enhance its status as an international financial centre. Thank you. Title: Keynote Speech at the Seminar on Financial Infrastructure held in Beijing
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 06 Jun 2006 Keynote Speech: Give full play to Hong Kong's financial infrastructure advantages - Accelerate the reform of the financial system in line with the National Eleventh Five-Year Plan Chi-gang Yim is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Financial Infrastructure Seminar in Beijing) Dear President Zhou Xiaochuan, ladies and gentlemen, good morning. 1 The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is proud to co-host this financial infrastructure seminar with People's Bank of China in Beijing and Shanghai. Speaking here today, I have a dual identity and a dual purpose. On the one hand, as the head of banking supervision in an international financial center, I would like to study with you the problem that most banks overlook, that is, how to properly manage the liquidation risks arising from their activities in the money market and the foreign exchange market. On the other hand, as a designer of financial infrastructure in an international financial centre, I would also like to sell to you as a salesman how mainland banks can use Hong Kong's financial infrastructure to effectively manage foreign exchange clearing risks. Reform of the financial system 2 To discuss this special topic, there must also be a starting point. At this time and in this place, the best starting point is, of course, the country's Eleventh Five-Year Plan. There are 48 chapters in the 11th Five-Year Plan, of which the 33rd chapter directly addresses finance, the "core of the modern economy," entitled "Accelerating the Reform of the Financial System." The third section of this chapter shows that it is necessary to improve the financial regulation and control mechanism, and I see that there are two scopes in it, one is about the currency market, and the other is about foreign exchange. Say yes respectively: 95 Steadily develop the money market, rationalize the transmission mechanism of monetary policy, and promote the reform of interest rate marketization; And 95 Improve the managed floating exchange rate system and gradually realize the convertibility of RMB capital account. 3 After I have seen the scope of these two accelerated financial system reforms, and together with the other reform proposals in Chapter 33, such as "Deepening Financial Enterprise Reform" in Section I and "Accelerating Development of Direct Financing" in Section II, I have a view on the prospects of the Mainland's currency and foreign exchange markets, that is, the trading activity of the market will grow rapidly in the future. Effective Transmission of Monetary Policy and Marketization of Interest Rates requires an active and deep money market, and only in this context can banks efficiently borrow money across the industry. In addition, in the process of improving the management of floating exchange rates and capital account account convertibility, it will also significantly increase the volume of foreign exchange transactions, in the case of free conversion and exchange rate floating, capital accounts include cross-border financial investment, foreign exchange arbitrage, market making, and even speculation generated by foreign exchange trading, the amount can be more than dozens of times the current account. 4 In Hong Kong, for example, the gross domestic product (GDP) for a full year is about HK1,400 billion, but the foreign exchange trading of the US dollar against the Hong Kong dollar on a single day is more than US26 billion (about US26 billion). HK200 billion). About 7 days of foreign exchange trading is equivalent to the GDP of a full year. In addition to the foreign exchange trading of USD/HKD, the average daily trading volume of the Hong Kong dollar currency market is also HK250 billion, and the combined trading volume of the two markets is already HK450 billion, which is 14% of the total Hong Kong dollar assets of banks. Hong Kong's Hong Kong Dollar Instant Payment System has a liquidation amount of approximately HK400 billion to HK600 billion per day. Whenever there is a new listing, the amount of liquidation tends to be higher, such as the recent day when the Bank of China was listed in Hong Kong, when the Hong Kong dollar instant payment system cleared up to a record HK1,230 billion, which is almost the size of Hong Kong's GDP in a year. The growth of the mainland's currency and foreign exchange trading activities in the future is, of course, dependent on the speed of financial reform and opening up. Chapter 33 of the 11th Five-Year Plan says to "accelerate the reform of the financial system." Judging from Hong Kong's experience in this free market, I think it is inevitable that the mainland's trading volume in the currency and foreign exchange markets will grow rapidly in the future. Commercial banks should, of course, be fully prepared psychologically and commercially. But allow me to say in my capacity as a person in charge of banking supervision in Hong Kong, it is more important to do a good job in risk management. The nature of liquidation risk 5 The risks faced by banks operating in the currency and foreign exchange markets are manifold. In this seminar I am not going to talk about interest rate risk, exchange rate risk or counterparty credit risk, I just want to focus on liquidation risk. Many people think that liquidation risk is a low risk, so it is also an unimportant risk, and they are a bit careless about it. If the clearing system is sound and the liquidation process is very efficient, I agree that the liquidation risk should be very low, there is no risk after a transaction is liquidated, and the liquidation time is a process of moments, and it will pass quickly. However, if the market transaction volume is getting larger and larger, the liquidation risk will increase relatively. One in ten thousand risks, one million yuan transaction is only a hundred yuan less, but if the transaction volume rises rapidly to one hundred million, one in ten thousand is one hundred thousand. As the saying goes, "Don't be afraid of ten thousand, just in case." If the liquidation risk is only one in 10,000, but if the transaction volume is large, as long as it occurs once, the loss number may be very large. 6 In fact, saying that the probability of risk is only one in ten thousand is likely to underestimate the actual situation. But what is certain is that the likelihood of liquidation risks is increasing. On the one hand, due to the globalization of the market, the scope of risks has expanded from the level of local prediction and management to the level of global more difficult prediction and management. On the other hand, information technology is developed, and funds can quickly circulate by telex, and I don't know where to go in the blink of an eye. Even if it knows where it goes, it may not be regulated and guaranteed by the laws and regulations of the source of funds. 7 Liquidation risk is not only a matter for individual banks, the nature of risk is systematic. If a bank has difficulties in liquidation, it will cause disasters to its peers and affect the entire banking system, and systemic problems will arise. In many places, the money market and foreign exchange market transactions assume that the money from the previous transaction will come, and once the money that should come does not come, its subsequent transactions may not be liquidated, and the money or goods should be in place but not in place, which has a great negative impact on individual banks, the entire banking system, and the entire economic system. Unfortunately, the importance of the clearing system, although indispensable for financial and monetary stability and sustained economic growth, is often overlooked. The payment and clearing system, like the water, electricity, and coal of a house, it seems natural that nothing goes wrong, but whenever there is a problem, it usually causes a lot of trouble. 8There are two types of liquidation risks: (1) The time difference between the transaction and the liquidation; And (ii) "Goods" are different from "silver". (0 Transaction and clearing time difference.) 9The time difference between the transaction and the liquidation should be as short as possible within the range possible, and the most ideal is that the transaction is cleared in real time after the transaction is completed. However, there is still a Tl, T2 or longer trading and clearing time difference in the market. In the case of advanced information technology, the time difference between trading and clearing can be greatly shortened, and T0, or instant clearing technology, is not difficult to achieve. But market habits are sometimes difficult to change, perhaps because the interests of intermediaries are involved. In TX, X gives intermediaries a little space, which is supposed to facilitate them to arrange the work on liquidation, but this space also provides them with some opportunities to make money for themselves in the market. These activities tend to amplify the volatility of the market itself, creating systemic problems for the market. If you can overdo it, re-plan the clearing arrangements for transactions, payments, etc., and the ideal arrangement is instant liquidation, each independent payment. Hong Kong needed to use Exchange funds in the 1980s to solve a series of banking problems that arose at that time, one of the reasons was that there was no Instant Payment System (RTGS) at that time, and under the influence of the chain, a bank with payment problems could stop the entire interbank payment system. Monetary confidence was also suddenly affected. If there were instant payment systems at the time, there might have been different forms of risk, the cost might be less, and the way to deal with payment problems at banks might be more efficient and less expensive. (H) "Goods" are different from "silver" 10 The difference between "goods" and "silver" is another type of liquidation risk, most obviously reflected in the foreign exchange market, where two different currencies are cleared in an out-of-sync manner. The collapse of Hurst Bank in 1974 fully reflected the risks posed by payment arrangements in different time zones. The Hirst Bank was a medium-sized bank in West Germany at the time but very active in the foreign exchange market. Its counterparty paid the mark to the Hearst Bank during the West German business hours, but then in the American market it could not receive the US dollar due to the collapse of the Hearst Bank, which caused its counterparty to lose the entire principal, which affected other participants in the market, causing systemic problems and large losses. After the collapse of the Hearst Bank, it became famous in the central banking circles, and everyone knew that Hearst had become a proper term to describe the liquidation risk of foreign exchange transactions - clearing different currencies involved in foreign exchange transactions in different time zones, if there is no coordination link in the middle, the liquidation risk is extremely high, and even the entire principal is lost. 11 The world's central banks agree that a safe and effective clearing system is essential to the stability of every financial system and its economic development. The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have conducted a lot of research on clearing risks, especially those related to foreign exchange transactions, and proposed that the only way to completely eliminate clearing risks is to carry out simultaneous settlement of foreign exchange transactions. This is also the reason why Hong Kong wants to provide a major foreign currency clearing platform in the Asian time zone, linking the clearing of major foreign currencies with the Hong Kong dollar, and even other Asian currencies, so as to achieve synchronous settlement of foreign exchange transactions. Of course, this is also a strategic focus for us to maintain Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre in accordance with the provisions of the Basic Law. Management of liquidation risks 12 The best model for managing liquidation risk is instant payments (RTGS), with simultaneous settlement (PvP) for foreign exchange transactions and two deposits for securities (DvP). If these financial infrastructures are readily available, banks should try to use these models for clearing, and the central bank also has the responsibility to encourage banks to use them, mainly because the liquidation risk is systematic, and once a problem occurs, it has a great negative impact on the industry. Managing clearing risks is one of the important elements of financial security and financial stability. Take advantage of Hong Kong's clearing platform 13 As just mentioned, as the mainland accelerates the reform of the financial system, we must pay attention to managing liquidation risks. In this regard, mainland financial institutions can make good use of Hong Kong's clearing platform. Let me step into the role of a salesman to introduce you to the current situation of the Hong Kong clearing platform, and then make some specific suggestions to allow mainland banks and foreign exchange market makers to reduce the risk of clearing. 14 Hong Kong now has a multi-dimensional, multi-currency payment, clearing and custody system with international advanced level, providing a safe, secure, efficient and comprehensive financial infrastructure platform for the clearing of various types of financial transactions. The established large-value instant payment (RTGS) system includes the Hong Kong dollar, US dollar and euro instant payment system, and has also established a clearing system for RMB business in Hong Kong, which can provide synchronous settlement of foreign exchange transactions in these currencies; It can also provide two liquidations of goods and silver. Financial products derived from financial financing and economic activities in Hong Kong, whether in currency, whether it is individual retail or the wholesale activities of enterprises and banks, are smooth and unimpeded, just like the construction of cross-border elevated roads and bridges on the financial network, which are closely linked but the roads are smooth. 15 At the same time, the HKMA has been committed to building a sound cross-border financial bridge with the Mainland to provide faster and more convenient cross-border capital disbursements for the Mainland. Over the past few years, the HKMA has been discussing with the relevant departments in Beijing, Guangzhou and Shenzhen the development and gradual implementation of cross-border payment and clearing cooperation projects between the two places: including cross-border Hong Kong dollar and US dollar instant payment with Guangdong Province and Shenzhen Municipality, as well as cross-border Hong Kong dollar, US dollar and RMB cheque settlement. This clearing platform in Hong Kong can not only meet the needs of Hong Kong banks for capital transfer and payment , but also provide the same efficient payment services for capital financing between the Mainland and Hong Kong 16 As the Mainland accelerates its financial reforms, there will be more money "coming in" and "going out", many of which have passed through Hong Kong's efficient springboard for currency conversion and investment. In the context of accelerating the reform of the mainland's foreign exchange market and liberalizing the overseas investment of mainland institutions and individuals, the opportunity to use Hong Kong's clearing platform is, in my opinion, growing. 17 In fact, with the exception of the Mainland and Hong Kong, Hong Kong's clearing platform has gradually become a cross-border fund transfer station in the region. Malaysia's central bank decided last year to connect the RM clearing system in Kuala Lumpur with the US dollar clearing system in Hong Kong in November this year. Banks in Malaysia open USD accounts in Hong Kong to clear USD funds involved in foreign exchange transactions. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority plans to negotiate with other central banks in the region a synchronous settlement of cross-border foreign exchange transactions of the same nature against other currencies in the region. These networking is actually very necessary. Hong Kong's dollar clearing system plays that role. Specific recommendations (i) Simultaneous zone liquidation 18 In January 2006, the Mainland's foreign exchange trading channel was added to the inquiry (OTC) foreign exchange transaction and allowed the relevant inquiry foreign exchange transaction to be cleared overseas by the agreement of the two parties to the transaction. However, at present, most of the foreign currency funds for foreign exchange transactions in the mainland are still mainly cleared in the United States and Europe. With the increasing popularity of OTC foreign exchange trading, the amount of foreign exchange transactions that need to be cleared every day will increase significantly, resulting in banks, market makers and foreign exchange dealers having higher and higher risk of foreign exchange trading clearing due to the impact of time difference. "Don't be afraid of ten thousand, just in case", if a bank's counterparty fails at New York opening time after the mainland closes, it is a copy of the collapse of Hearst Bank, and the risk to the bank's financial system in the mainland can be extremely high. 19 From the perspective of bank risk management, or the responsibility of central banks to maintain financial stability, it is necessary to guard against the recurrence of Hearst banking events at all times, and to minimize or even eliminate Herstatt risk. I believe President Zhou will agree with me. At present, the fastest and most effective way to reduce this risk is to let the mainland's foreign exchange transactions use Hong Kong's platform to clear foreign currencies, so that the clearing risk can be immediately reduced, the efficiency of financial integration, and the ability to operate funds can be improved; It is also in line with the mainland's policy objectives of monitoring financial risks and maintaining financial stability. In April this year, the HKMA upgraded the relevant functions of Hong Kong's multi-currency clearing system, especially for foreign exchange transactions related to RMB in the mainland, and provided services for the settlement of foreign currencies in Hong Kong in the same region , so as to minimize the Hearst risks that may be caused by foreign exchange transactions in the mainland through overseas clearing channels such as the United States and Europe. 20 Now four banks and market makers use Hong Kong's platform to clear their foreign exchange trades on the mainland. I hope that other banks and market makers will do the same and manage the risk of foreign currency clearing. The specific arrangement is actually convenient and simple. Please take a moment to visit the off-site booth of Hong Kong Correspondent Bank, I am sure they will do their best to arrange and provide you with the best foreign currency clearing services. (ii) Towards the highest international standard: Simultaneous Settlement (PvP) of Forex Transactions 21 In the long run, if you want to move towards the highest standard of managing foreign exchange clearing risk, you need to provide a settlement model of simultaneous settlement (PvP) of foreign exchange transactions to completely eliminate liquidation risks. There are different ways to achieve simultaneous settlement in the mainland, and my personal view is that we should choose a fast and cost-effective method to achieve simultaneous settlement of RMB and major foreign currencies in the shortest possible time to match the rapid development of the mainland currency and foreign exchange markets. In this regard, we have also shared our experience with the People's Bank of China, including proposing that the Mainland's RMB payment system be networked with the payment system of Hong Kong's foreign currency (including Hong Kong Dollar), so that foreign exchange transactions in the Mainland can be settled simultaneously with different currencies in the Asian time zone , just as we are gradually implementing the networking model with Malaysia. summary 22 Today, when China's financial and foreign exchange market reform has been in full swing, it is urgent to develop financial infrastructure, and I hope that Hong Kong can help and make a little contribution in this link. Therefore, I would like to take this opportunity, with the consent of President Zhou, to encourage local financial institutions to adopt the Hong Kong system for foreign currency clearing and cross-border payments, on the one hand, in line with the direction of accelerating the reform of the financial system in the Eleventh Five-Year Plan , and also to implement the goals of the plan to support Hong Kong's development of the financial services industry and maintain Hong Kong's status as an international financial center.
