Title: Opening Remarks at the Conference "Efficiency and Stability of the Financial System in Mainland China"
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech October 16, 2008 Opening remarks Pang Xingtang is a Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Seminar on "Chinese mainland the Efficiency and Stability of the Financial System", October 16-17, 2008) Good morning, dear guests On behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Hong Kong Centre for Financial Research, I would like to welcome you to the Sixth Chinese mainland Economy Symposium. Last year, we and the Wang Yanan Institute of Economics of Xiamen University successfully co-hosted the fifth symposium, and we are very pleased to have the opportunity to cooperate again this year. I would like to express my heartfelt thanks to all the speakers, panelists and moderators for their contributions to this conference. The theme of the seminar was Chinese mainland the efficiency and stability of the financial system. This issue is very important for the long-term development of the Mainland's economy from two perspectives. First, after nearly a decade of development, the mainland's financial system has gradually gained scale in terms of markets, products and participants, and when considering the important policy of capital account opening, it is inevitable to look at the impact of integration with the international market on the efficiency and stability of the mainland's financial system. Second, when studying this important topic, we can certainly draw different and important enlightenments from the Asian financial crisis that occurred a decade ago and the "financial tsunami" that is now engulfing the United States and Europe and posing a great threat to global financial stability. In my view, the Asian financial crisis has shown that an underdeveloped and inefficient financial system poses a risk of financial instability under conditions of gradual opening up of the capital account. Inefficient allocation of funds encourages domestic savings to flow to more efficient and developed financial markets, while on the other hand, funds return to these relatively underdeveloped economies in the form of short-term portfolio investments or "hot money", creating a double "mismatch of currency and term" for financial institutions and enterprises "? As soon as there is a wind blowing, these short-term capitals will reverse. Large fluctuations in short-term capital, for smaller and open economies, are like an elephant stepping into a small pond, which can be hugely damaging to the local financial system. But does efficiency alone necessarily strengthen the stability of the financial system? The current financial crisis, triggered by the US subprime mortgage , shows that a highly developed and efficient financial system can be more destructive to the global financial system if the framework of prudential regulation lags behind the speed of financial innovation . The experience of the United States shows that in the environment of continuous loose monetary policy and weak prudential supervision, financial institutions have a strong interest in driving them to develop high-risk financial innovations and derivatives. Some derivatives are intended to diversify the risk of the underlying assets through the process of spin-offs and packaging. But what is unexpected is that this model also takes credit risk away from lenders, leaving them with no incentive to maintain prudent approval standards. The process of credit risk securitization also rapidly diversifies the potential risks associated with them to other financial systems. When the underlying assets on which these derivatives depend, such as real estate, bubble and finally collapse, the value of these derivatives ceases to exist, causing a serious blow to the stability of the global financial system. I think the above two financial crises offer a useful lesson. That is, a healthy financial system must strike a good balance between efficiency and stability. While vigorously developing financial markets with depth, breadth and efficiency, it is also necessary to raise the level of supervision and risk disclosure, so as to avoid the framework of prudential supervision lagging behind the speed of financial innovation. As a major international financial centre in Asia, Hong Kong has extensive experience in improving the efficiency of its financial system and maintaining financial stability. The HKMA is constantly reviewing and improving our policy framework and regulatory level, and is more than happy to share our experience with relevant mainland institutions, as well as experts and scholars. I believe that by absorbing the lessons of the Asian financial crisis and the current international financial tsunami, the development of China's financial industry will have very good prospects. The HKMA will continue to work closely with relevant institutions in the Mainland in the spirit of "complementarity, mutual assistance and interaction" to jointly enhance the efficiency and stability of China's financial system. Eleven papers will be presented at this conference. These papers cover different categories: the characteristics of volatility in domestic capital markets, the impact of institutional investors on the efficiency and stability of financial markets; The efficiency of the banking system and the operating mechanisms and characteristics of private finance; Financial markets are affected by exogenous shocks and the pattern of capital account opening; The formulation and transmission mechanism of monetary policy, and so on. The ideas put forward in the papers will certainly be of great benefit and inspiration to understanding the efficiency and stability of the domestic financial system and the role that Hong Kong can play in China's financial reform and opening up. Finally, I sincerely wish this seminar a success, thank you! Last revision date: 16 October 2008

Title: Remarks at the Meeting with Representatives from the Banking Industry in Shenzhen, China
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 2009/04/20 Delivered a speech at the meeting with representatives of the banking industry in Shenzhen, China Pang Xingtang is a Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. Honorable Vice President Zhang Jianjun, bank representatives, distinguished guests, good morning. 2. This morning, I have the honor to have the opportunity to join hands with Vice President Zhang Jianjun of the People's Bank of Shenzhen and Mr. Xiao Guangchang, General Manager of Shenzhen Financial Electronic Settlement Center, to meet with senior representatives of banks to introduce an important cooperation project to strengthen cooperation between Shenzhen and Hong Kong, promote financial development and stability, and promote Shenzhen's financial innovation. I would like to express my heartfelt thanks to all the delegates and guests for their attendance. 3. In June last year, Mr. Xu Zongheng, Mayor of Shenzhen, Mr. Luo Bochuan, President of the People's Bank of Shenzhen, and Mr. Ren Zhigang, President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, met in Shenzhen to discuss opportunities for strengthening financial cooperation and deepening development between Shenzhen and Hong Kong. Both Shenzhen and Hong Kong have affirmed and expressed their positive support for the plan to set up a joint venture mortgage guarantee company in Shenzhen, and determined that this cooperation project can take a positive step towards strengthening financial cooperation and financial innovation between Shenzhen and Hong Kong. 4. The joint venture between the Settlement Centre of the People's Bank of Shenzhen and the Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation Limited under the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) are a joint venture to establish a joint venture guarantee company in Shenzhen. The registered capital of the company is approximately RMB 100 million. The proportion of capital contribution of mortgage securities companies accounts for 90%, and the settlement center is 10%. The total investment of the company is about 300 million yuan. 5. The Mortgage Securities Company is a wholly-owned company owned by the HKSAR Government through the Exchange Fund and mainly develops two aspects of the business. The first is to provide liquidity for banks by purchasing mortgage loans from banks. The second is to provide mortgage insurance to help banks effectively manage the risks associated with mortgage loans. With the rich operational experience of mortgage securities companies in the secondary mortgage market and mortgage guarantee market; Coupled with the Clearing Center's in-depth understanding of the Shenzhen market, I am confident that the joint venture company can actively provide and develop various suitable and innovative mortgage guarantee products and related services for banks in Shenzhen to help banks improve the risk management effectiveness of their mortgage business. 6. At the same time, the joint venture also hopes to assist Shenzhen in optimizing the structure of the mortgage market (e.g. to serve as a demonstration for the standardization of the mortgage market). Contribute to the stable development of the mortgage market and to strengthening the risk management of the banking system. From the above perspective, the relevant cooperation projects also respond to an important enlightenment brought about by the US sub-press crisis and the current global financial crisis: that is, a healthy housing financial system must strike the right balance between efficiency, innovation and stability. While vigorously developing the housing financial market, it is necessary to improve the effective risk management level accordingly to avoid the framework of risk management lagging behind the speed of housing finance innovation, thus endangering the long-term and stable development of the banking system. 7. As a major shareholder of a joint venture, a mortgage securities company has several advantages. The Chairman of the Company is the Financial Secretary of Hong Kong The Vice-Chairman is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. In addition to being wholly owned by the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region through the Exchange Fund, the Exchange Fund is also At the same time for the company to provide up to300HK100 million of standby revolving credit line to support the huge amount of money. Coupled with the always prudent karma In the operational policy, mortgage companies are awarded the highest credit rating by credit rating agencies. Currently, mortgage securities companies are The first and only Hong Kong company to receive Moody'sAaaLong-term rating; The relevant rating given by Standard & Poor's is AA b0 8. In recent years, mortgage securities companies have been actively expanding their overseas business and extending Hong Kong's successful model to other regions. At present, the joint venture company established in Shenzhen is the second joint venture company established outside Hong Kong by a mortgage securities company. In 2008, Mortgage Securities has set up a joint venture with Cagamas Berhad in Malaysia to provide mortgage guarantees to banks in Malaysia. 9. We expect the joint venture to be officially operational in the third quarter of this year. First of all, to provide the market with second-hand building redemption loan guarantee products, the purpose is to adapt to the current market conditions as soon as possible, establish the market brand and establish a good cooperative relationship with the bank. I hope that the joint venture's redemption loan guarantee business can be put on track as soon as possible, after which we will move on to the second phase of development: further negotiations with banks to provide guarantees for the existing mortgage portfolio. As for further development, it depends on the direction of the development of national policies and the needs of banks in the market. The joint venture will adopt a flexible and diversified business development path to complement it. 10. Finally, let me briefly introduce the leaders of the shareholders of both sides of the joint venture, namely Mr. Xiao Guangchang, General Manager of the Settlement Center, and Mr. Liu Yixiang, President of the Mortgage Securities Company. At present, all banks and the clearing center have established close business relations, and I believe that all of you here will have a considerable understanding of the background of the clearing center. For some of the friends here, the background and business operations of mortgage securities companies may be relatively unfamiliar; Therefore, I would like to invite Mr. Liu Yixiang to further introduce the background information and business development of mortgage securities companies in the future, so that everyone can have a deeper understanding of mortgage securities companies. 11. After this meeting with the representatives of the banks, the business development personnel of the joint venture company will visit the banks one after another to discuss the arrangements for business cooperation between the two sides, and I hope that you will support them at that time. Thank you! Last revision date: 20 April 2009
