Title: Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority
text: 19/09/22, 15:53 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 19 Nov 2010 Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority With the launch of the second phase of Quantitative Easing (QE2) by the US, the global financial environment is now in a rather abnormal state. While the efficacy of QE2 in achieving the desired objectives of stimulating the US economy and improving the job market is too early to tell, the negative side effects of such policy on the Emerging Market Economies are likely to continue and intensify. As a result, the risk of asset bubbles in the EMEs is rising. In this connection, Hong Kong is not immune. 2. Following the package of measures introduced by the SAR Government and the HKMA in mid-August, the property market seemed to have slowed down somewhat in September and early October. From mid-October, the property market has picked up again, as reflected in the rising transaction volume and prices. Under the present environment in which interest rates are exceptionally low and there is a huge amount of excessive liquidity flooding the banking system, many investors may easily overlook the fact that the income level of Hong Kong people is increasingly trailing the property prices, and tend to harbour rather unreasonable expectations that interest rates would stay at such low level for a very long time and that housing prices can only go up and not down. Under the circumstances, we are very concerned that the housing market and consequently the mortgage market will become even more exuberant, thereby exposing the banking system to higher risks. 3. In order to protect banking stability, the HKMA has just issued a set of new guidelines to banks requiring them to further strengthen their risk management standards by adopting the following measures: (a) for residential properties valued at HK12 mn or above, the maximum Loan to Valuation Ratio (LTV) for mortgage loans will be lowered from 60% to 50%; (b) for residential properties valued between HK8 mn and HK12 mn, the maximum LTV will be lowered from 70% to 60%, with the maximum loan amount not exceeding HK6 mn; (c) for residential properties valued at HK8 mn or below, the maximum LTV will be maintained at 70%, with the maximum loan amount not exceeding HK4.8 mn; and (d) for all non-owner-occupied residential properties, all properties held by companies and all industrial/commercial properties, the maximum LTV will be lowered to 50%, regardless of the value of the properties. / 1/2 19/09/22, 15:53 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority 4. The above measures will take effect immediately, although mortgage loan applications with the provisional Sale and Purchase Agreements signed today or earlier will not be affected. My colleagues will explain the details of these new measures in a separate press briefing later today. 5. In the interest of enhancing risk management, the Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation has also decided to modify its Mortgage Insurance Programme. The details of the modifications will be announced by the HKMC later today. 6. Following consultation with the Personal Data Privacy Commission, it has been agreed that the public consultation on the proposal to develop a Positive Mortgage Data Sharing Scheme will be undertaken early next year with a view to making the Scheme ready for implementation before the end of the first quarter next year. Needless to say, the launch of the Scheme will be of considerable help to banks in making more reliable assessment on the credit worthiness of mortgage applicants. 7.1 would like to reiterate the point that Hong Kong is now facing an exceptionally unusual macro-financial environment, a situation that cannot continue indefinitely. While I am not in a position to foretell precisely when the adjustment will occur, I am sure that such adjustment will definitely come one day. As the gate-keeper of Hong Kong's banking system, the HKMA must introduce appropriate prudential measures in a timely manner to ensure that our banks adopt the necessary risk management standards and practices and to make our banking system more resilient to shocks, so as to dampen the damage that would be inflicted by the bursting of the asset bubble when there are adjustments to the macro environment. 8. Lastly, I wish to remind everyone that it is not enough to rely solely on the measures introduced by the Government. The entire community must heighten their awareness of the risks that lie ahead and work together to make the necessary preparation to tackle this difficult situation. It is therefore essential that people of Hong Kong do not overstretch themselves by borrowing beyond their means, bearing in mind that interest rates will one day return to more normal, but significantly higher levels. We must learn from the experience of the bursting of the last asset bubble and work together in order to avoid a recurrence of the very difficult situation. Last revision date : 19 November 2010 / 2/2

Title: Hong Kong as an Offshore Renminbi Business Centre and its Business Collaboration with Sichuan
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 25 Mar 2011 Opportunities for cooperation between Hong Kong and Sichuan as an offshore RMB business hub Pang Xingtang is a Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Yuchuan-Hong Kong Financial Cooperation Forum) Honorable Governor Jiang Jufeng, distinguished guests, good morning: I am very pleased to participate in the "Sichuan-Hong Kong Financial Cooperation Forum" today. We would like to take this opportunity to introduce the development of offshore RMB business in Hong Kong and put forward some ideas and suggestions on the cooperation between Sichuan and Hong Kong. Since its launch in 2004, Hong Kong's offshore RMB business has undergone continuous expansion and deepening over the years with the strong support of the relevant central and mainland departments. The process of development can be divided into two main stages. When Hong Kong's offshore RMB business was first launched in 2004, the scope of business was limited to banks providing basic services such as deposits, exchanges, remittances and bank cards to individual customers. As for the RMB clearing and circulation mechanism between the Mainland and Hong Kong, it is basically a "one-way return" design: after Hong Kong banks accept the exchange and deposits of local residents, they deposit all of them in the mainland through the clearing banks. By 2007, mainland financial institutions could issue RMB bonds in Hong Kong and then remit the RMB funds raised back to the Mainland for use. This is also the beginning of RMB financing activities in Hong Kong. In mid-2009, the pilot project of RMB settlement for cross-border trade was introduced, which is an important step in promoting and implementing the RMB going out policy. Hong Kong's offshore RMB market has also undergone breakthrough developments. Hong Kong banks can provide relevant services for enterprises that use RMB for settlement of trade with the Mainland, and have established a two-way flow mechanism between the Mainland and the Mainland. Since then, the scope of RMB trade settlement has expanded significantly in June last year, and current account transactions between the mainland including 20 provinces and cities in Sichuan and around the world can be settled in RMB. As a result, Hong Kong's RMB trade settlement volume has also increased significantly, from an average of about 4 billion yuan per month in the first half of last year to an average of 57 billion yuan per month in the second half of the year. In January and February this year, it increased to an average of about 95 billion yuan per month. At present, more than 70% of RMB trade settlement between the mainland and overseas is carried out through Hong Kong. The funds accumulated from RMB trade settlement have also become the main source of corporate deposits within Hong Kong's banking system. By the end of January 2011, Hong Kong's RMB deposits had reached RMB370 billion, and it is estimated that by the end of February, deposits will exceed 4,000 In 2010, Hong Kong's RMB bonds were issued more than RMB35 billion, and the issuers of bonds were expanded from the original mainland policy banks and commercial banks to local and multinational enterprises in Hong Kong and international financial institutions such as the Asian Development Bank, and the maturity of the bonds was also extended 10-year bonds. Banks and financial institutions in Hong Kong have also launched a variety of RMB wealth management products, including insurance products and investment funds. This provides a hedging tool for Hong Kong's RMB funds and helps to increase the willingness of enterprises to use RMB. In general, driven by the mutual promotion of RMB trade settlement, financing and asset management, Hong Kong's offshore RMB market has gradually taken shape. At the same time, after years of development, the relevant financial infrastructure and payment systems have been established, with the advantage of "pioneering". Recently, the central government has explicitly supported the development of Hong Kong into an offshore RMB business center in the 12th Five-Year Plan, and we will continue to promote relevant work to gradually increase the circulation and interaction between Hong Kong's offshore RMB market and the mainland's onshore market in accordance with the principle of step-by-step and risk controllability, and support trade, direct investment and other real economic activities. I have the following three suggestions on how Hong Kong and Sichuan can have more cooperation in RMB cross-border business First, promote enterprises in Sichuan to use Hong Kong's offshore RMB settlement platform to expand the use of RMB in cross-border trade to reduce exchange rate risks and exchange costs in cross-border trade. According to the Sichuan Provincial Department of Commerce, Sichuan's exports reached 18.8 billion in 2010, with Hong Kong's share accounting for almost 15 percent. In addition, Sichuan imported US13.9 billion, and Hong Kong's share also accounted for more than 6%. It can be seen that the trade relationship between Sichuan and Hong Kong is very close, and the RMB trade business between the two places has great potential for development. Second, promote cross-border direct investment in Sichuan to be paid and settled in RMB through Hong Kong's platform. According to statistics, Sichuan's non-financial outward direct investment in 2010 reached US300 million, and it is believed that most of it was invested in Hong Kong or through Hong Kong to invest in various parts of the world. At the beginning of this year, the mainland promulgated the pilot management measures, allowing domestic institutions to use RMB funds for overseas direct investment. Sichuan enterprises can make full use of Hong Kong's multi-currency and multi-functional financial platform to carry out foreign investment activities. At the same time, in the other direction, it is also possible to promote foreign direct investment projects in Sichuan in RMB. Hong Kong is the largest source of foreign investment in Sichuan, with an investment volume of more than US3.7 billion in 2010, accounting for more than 60% of the total foreign investment in Sichuan. Last year, a number of cases were approved, and foreign enterprises, after examination and approval by the relevant departments on the mainland, repatriated the RMB funds raised in Hong Kong to the mainland. This can provide greater flexibility for foreign enterprises investing in Sichuan. Third, promote enterprises in Sichuan, especially those that go global, to use Hong Kong's RMB market for financing. With the continuous development of RMB trade settlement, the scale of RMB funds in Hong Kong has also increased accordingly, especially in terms of cost, providing very favorable conditions for financing activities. Finally, we look forward to closer cooperation between Hong Kong and Sichuan in the future, fully grasping the business opportunities provided by the renminbi going global, and also contributing to the reform and modernization of the country's financial system, the gradual opening up of the capital account, and the international and gradual transformation of the renminbi toward free convertibility. Thank you! Last revision date: 25 March 2011

Title: Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority
text: 19/09/22, 15:52 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 28 Apr 2011 Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. The Federal Open Markets Committee (FOMC) indicated that it will complete purchases of Treasury Securities under QE2 by the end of June as planned, and did not suggest further quantitative easing thereafter. 2. The Fed's decision indicates that the US monetary conditions may move gradually towards normalization from June onward. 3. It is now difficult to predict the timetable and scale of the Fed's exit strategy. The market generally expects the Fed to start raising interest rates in the first half of next year. But in light of the persistently high levels of global energy and commodity prices, US inflation may face further upward pressure, and the Fed may have to raise interest rates faster than expected. 4.1 would like to remind the public that HKD interest rates may rise even before the Fed's rate hikes. Apart from following USD interest rates, HKD interest rates are also affected by changes in the demand and supply of HKD in the local banking system. As HKD loans have grown faster than HKD deposits since last year, the loan-to-deposit ratio of banks in Hong Kong has risen from 71 % at the beginning of last year to 81 % in February this year. Quite a number of banks have already raised HKD lending and deposit rates. Since the HKD loan demand is likely to remain strong, local banks' HKD interest rates may face further upward pressure. 5. Under the Linked Exchange Rate System, when USD interest rates start to rise, interest rate arbitrage activities will kick in, triggering substantial outflows from the HKD and pushing up HKD interest rates. Therefore, I anticipate that the HK640 billion inflows into Hong Kong during late 2008 to 2009 would gradually flow out upon commencement of the US tightening cycle. Nevertheless, we should all be well prepared for this as Hong Kong must go through this process in order to restore its monetary conditions to more normal state under the currency board arrangements. 6. In light of the uncertainties over the interest rate environment of Hong Kong and the possibility of interest rate adjustments ahead, members of the public should manage interest rate risk carefully and avoid over-stretching themselves. Last revision date : 28 April 2011 / 1/2 19/09/22, 15:52 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority / 2/2

HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY ftiftratftffl!fcj Speeches 10 Jun 2011 Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the media on 10 June 2011 Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. Since the introduction of a series of measures by the SAR Government and the HKMA in November last year, the property market has been volatile. Although the property market cooled down a bit in March and April this year, there are now signs of renewed exuberance following high transaction prices recorded in recent government land sale auctions. Not just the current property prices have exceeded their peak levels in 1997, interest rate risk is also much higher than that in 1997. The mortgage rates then were usually over 10% while the present mortgage rates are only around 1 %. The present unusually low interest rate environment will not last forever. 2. In view of the increasing risk on mortgage lending, the HKMA has just issued new guidelines to banks, requiring them to implement the following measures to further strengthen risk management in their mortgage business for the purpose of protecting banking stability: (I) The 50% maximum loan-to-value (LTV) ratio for residential mortgages will apply to residential properties with a value of HK10 million or above. (II) The maximum LTV ratio for residential properties with value between HK7 million and HK10 million will be lowered to 60%, with the maximum loan amount capped at HK5 million. (III) The maximum LTV ratio for residential properties with a value below HK7 million will be 70%, with the maximum loan amount capped at HK4.2 million. (IV) If the principal income of the mortgage loan applicant is not derived from Hong Kong, the applicable maximum LTV ratio will be lowered by at least 10 percentage points regardless of property types or values. (V) The maximum LTV ratio for properties under the net worth-based mortgage will be lowered from 50% to 40%. 3. The above measures take effect immediately. However, loan applications in respect of property transactions with provisional sale and purchase agreements signed on or before today will not be affected. Details of these measures will be explained by our Deputy Chief Executive Mr Arthur Yuen later. 4. The Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation Limited (HKMC) will also revise its Mortgage Insurance Programme, the details of which will be announced by the HKMC later. 5. The HKMA has all along required banks to be prudent and vigilant in managing credit risk. As the boom cycle in the property market continues to evolve, the risks associated / 1/2 19/09/22, 15:52 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the... with banks' mortgage lending business increase correspondingly. There is therefore a continuing need for banks to enhance their risk management for their mortgage lending business. This is the fourth time the HKMA introduced countercyclical supervisory measures since October 2009. We will continue to monitor market situation closely and introduce appropriate measures as and when necessary to safeguard banking stability. Last revision date : 10 June 2011 / 2/2

Title: Remarks at the Unveiling Ceremony of the New Series Hong Kong Banknotes
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 07-22-2011 Speech at the announcement ceremony of Hong Kong's new banknotes Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. Distinguished guests, friends of the media. Welcome to the announcement ceremony of the new banknote designs of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the three banknote issuing banks. 2. The new series of 1,000 and 500 bills were launched in December last year and February this year, respectively. Many members of the public have a very positive evaluation of the design of the new banknote series. In addition, we used the new engraving technology to add braille and feel line designs to the banknotes, and we were very happy to receive the "Barrier-free Hero Award" presented by the Hong Kong Blind Internet Society. 3. Banknotes are our most commonly used payment medium and are a very important part of the Hong Kong dollar monetary system. The higher the public's acceptance and confidence in Hong Kong's currency, the more it will be able to promote the circulation and use of the currency, thus achieving the HKMA's goal of maintaining the stability of the monetary system. Even as e-money and credit cards have become more common in recent years, the issuance of Hong Kong dollar banknotes has continued to increase. The total circulation in 2001 was HK108 billion, equivalent to 8% of the gross domestic product at that time. By 2010, circulation had doubled to HK227 billion, representing 13% of GDP. This reflects the fact that the public's demand and confidence in the use of Hong Kong dollar banknotes as payments has remained at a high level. 4. To further strengthen public confidence in Hong Kong's currency, we have added advanced and easily recognizable anti-counterfeiting features to our new banknote collection. You may ask, does this mean that the old banknote series in circulation is easy to be counterfeited? You don't have to worry about that. In Hong Kong, the number of counterfeit banknotes has been at an extremely low level in the world. In the past two years, the total number of counterfeit banknotes seized by the Police each year has been just over 1,000, equivalent to only 1 in every million banknotes in circulation, reflecting the success of Hong Kong's consistent anti-counterfeiting work. 5. The new 100, 50 and 20 bills will be launched in November this year, which can be used by the public to seal profits in the Lunar New Year next year. The three banknote issuing banks will later introduce the design of each of the three new banknotes. 6. Although our banknotes have advanced anti-counterfeiting design, it is also important that citizens and merchants are familiar with these new anti-counterfeiting features and can easily distinguish between real and fake banknotes. Over the past year, we have organised a series of promotional activities, including a travelling exhibition and a series of seminars, for banking and retail practitioners, the elderly, students, the visually impaired and the general public. I am delighted to be able to participate in some of these promotional activities with our student ambassadors, distributing leaflets to merchants and personally promoting the new banknote collection and their new design features to the city's citizens. 7. This year we will continue to hold a traveling exhibition to introduce the design and security features of the entire new banknote collection. One of the features of this promotion is the display of landmark buildings that have appeared on Hong Kong banknotes from different eras, allowing you to look back at the evolution of Hong Kong over the past few decades. We will also organise a photo contest to invite members of the public to participate in capturing the faces of these landmarks today with their lenses and creativity. We will hold our first stop at IFC Mall next Wednesday, followed by an exhibition in five districts of Hong Kong, Kowloon, and the New Territories for the convenience of the public from all districts. 8. Finally, I would like to introduce my six elaborate commemorative cards, each of which showcases a very familiar Hong Kong landmark: City Hall, the Old Pavilion on the Hilltop, the Tsim Sha Tsui Clock Tower and three old buildings of the banknote issuing bank. If you are willing to use some thought and effort, you can 'transform' the commemorative card into a good and distinctive three-dimensional model (showing six models). These six commemorative cards will be distributed in the touring exhibition venues, as long as you participate in the computer games at the booth, and answer a few questions that are not too difficult, you can get one of the commemorative cards, if you can store a complete set of six, it is very commemorative value. Don't miss this opportunity! 9. Thank you! Last revision date: 22 July 2011

Title: Statement to the media
text: 19/09/22, 15:52 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the... Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 08 Aug 2011 Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the media on 8 August 2011 Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Translation) The downgrading of US by S&P's did not come as a big surprise. In a way, it reflects the market concern on the determination and ability of the US Government to pursue fiscal consolidation in the medium to longer term. However, we do not believe the downgrading last Friday would have significant impact on the yields of the US Treasuries. We have observed that on previous occasions when market turbulence and risk aversion occurred, the demand for US Treasuries as safe haven assets actually increased. This was also true during the last two weeks when the US and global stock markets declined rather sharply. Similarly, the downgrading of US's credit rating by one notch should not affect US dollar's position as a major pricing and settlement currency in international trade and financial markets. In the past, whenever market turbulence happened, even though when it originated from the US, risk aversion activities would help mitigate downward pressure on US dollar exchange rate. Therefore, the downgrading of US's credit rating should not bring about major pressure on US dollar exchange rate in the short run. As a matter of fact, there were no significant changes in the yields of the US Treasuries and US dollar exchange rate after the markets opened in Tokyo early this morning. Given the present unfavourable economic and financial conditions in Europe and in the US, we expect that there would continue to be significant market volatilities going forward. It will be crucial that the authorities in Europe and in the US will take further steps to allay the concerns of the market by implementing bold fiscal plans and other appropriate measures. At the same time, Hong Kong should continue to strengthen the resilience of its financial system to cope with such volatilities. I wish to reaffirm that we remain fully committed to the Linked Exchange Rate System, which has served Hong Kong very well as the anchor for monetary and financial stability since 1983. We have no intention to change the Link. / 1/2 19/09/22, 15:52 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the... Title: Statement to the media
text: 19/09/22, 15:51 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the... Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 22 Sep 2011 Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the media on 22 September 2011 Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Translation) The Federal Open Market Committee of the US Federal Reserve has just finished a two-day meeting. We note the Federal Reserve has decided to sell US400 billion of short-term Treasury debts in exchange for longer-term Treasury debts by end-June 2012, with an aim of lowering longer-term interest rates. To support conditions in mortgage market, the Federal Reserve has also decided to reinvest principal payments from its holdings of agency debt and mortgage-backed securities in agency mortgage-backed securities. The Federal Reserve also sees significant downside risks to the economic outlook. 2. By further lowering the US dollar long-term interest rates through these measures, the Federal Reserve aims to reduce the cost of credit so as to stimulate economic growth and employment. However, due to the very subdued US housing market and the high indebtedness of US households, the effectiveness of these new measures in stimulating the US real economy remains to be seen. In terms of the implications on local interest rates, as Hong Kong Interbank Offer Rates (HIBORs) are already extremely low at levels near zero, the new measures of the Federal Reserve will not have any substantive impact on HIBORs. However, there has been an upward trend for the deposit rates and lending rates in Hong Kong since the first quarter because of changes in the supply of and demand for funds within Hong Kong's banking sector. I believe this trend will continue, and will not be affected by the new measures introduced by the US Federal Reserve. 3. At present, Hong Kong is facing a very unusual macro environment. The persistently low interest rates in the advanced economies have led to massive capital flows into emerging market economies in the past two years, fuelling over-heating pressures and heightening the risks of inflation and asset price bubble. As economic growth in the US has decelerated sharply, the Federal Reserve is anticipating the maintenance of an accommodative monetary policy for a longer period of time. Therefore, we must not loosen our guard against the risk of Hong Kong's property market heating up again. We stand ready to introduce further measures as needed to maintain banking stability in Hong Kong. But at the same time, Hong Kong also needs to prepare for possible worsening of the European sovereign debt problems and the consequential shocks on the global financial system and the real economy. 4. In such an uncertain external environment, we have to stay vigilant. The HKMA has introduced a series of countercyclical supervisory measures requiring banks to continue to strengthen risk management. We have also repeatedly reminded the public to be careful / 1/2 19/09/22, 15:51 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Statement by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the... and avoid over-stretching themselves financially. The purpose of all these is to strengthen the resilience of Hong Kongs banking and financial systems, so that they can cope with possible turbulences and shocks in the future. Title: Over-the-Counter Derivatives Market Reforms in Hong Kong
text: 19/09/22, 15:51 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Over-the-Counter Derivatives Market Reforms in Hong Kong Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 25 Oct 2011 Over-the-Counter Derivatives Market Reforms in Hong Kong Edmond Lau, Executive Director (Monetary Management), Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Keynote Address at the 2011 ISDA Annual Conference: Shaping the Future of Derivatives, Hong Kong) Good morning ladies and gentlemen. It is my great pleasure to be here today to discuss and share with you, the future we envision for OTC derivatives market in Hong Kong. Before we look into the future, we must reflect on the past to understand why we are at the cross-roads that we are at today, and why reform is necessary. Whilst this should rightfully invoke thoughts about the 2008 collapse of Lehman Brothers it is crucial we remember that this event only triggered the financial tsunami and that the core of the problem required deeper analysis. Background of the crisis The scale of the crisis was amplified by two key characteristics of the OTC derivatives market: interconnectivitv and opaqueness. Firstly, on interconnectivity - whilst it is normal for firms to become connected to each other through their normal trades and dealings - the g/oba/nature of OTC derivatives intensified this interconnectivity to unseen levels. The increased ease of communication supported by technology advancements led entities to become more connected with each other either directly through their own engagement with a larger variety of market players, or indirectly through their counterparties engagement with others. However, this increase in interconnectivity was not always obvious- which brings me to the second characteristic of OTC derivatives markets, opaqueness. Like we may not be aware that our mutual friends on such social networks as Facebook connect us to someone half- way across the globe, financial institutions similarly did not know the degree to which they were connected to other financial or non-financial entities. The bilateral nature of OTC derivative trades meant that only the counterparties to a transaction were privy to the details of the trade; their other affiliates and trade partners were completely unaware of the extent and nature of their dealings with others, including the risks they were taking and the degree to which they were leveraging. Taken together, interconnectivity and opaqueness were a perfect recipe for disaster. Interconnectivity meant high contagion risks and the ability for a single failure to spread to the entire financial system. Opaqueness meant that many firms were simply unaware of / 1/6 19/09/22, 15:51 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Over-the-Counter Derivatives Market Reforms in Hong Kong these contagion risks and therefore failure to implement appropriate risk management practices. This was compounded by the fact that even regulators lacked the information required to properly assess the build-up of exposures in the market and devise preventive measures. It was in this sort of opaque and interconnected context that Lehman Brothers failed. Internationally Coordinated Regulatory Reform It was against such background that regulators worldwide came to work together on the reform of this market. Given the highly globalized nature of the OTC derivatives market, any reform solution must be internationally co-ordinated. Such a movement emerged in 2009 when the G20 leaders agreed in Pittsburgh in September 2009 that: "All standardised OTC derivative contracts should be traded on exchanges or electronic trading platforms, where appropriate, and cleared through central counterparties by end- 2012 at the latest. OTC derivative contracts should be reported to trade repositories. Non-centrally cleared contracts should be subject to higher capital requirements." These proposals aim to : firstly, enhance transparency by requiring all OTC derivatives transactions be reported to trade repositories; and secondly, lower the degree of interconnectivity between market players to reduce contagion risks, by interjecting central counterparties between buyers and sellers. In circumstances where interconnectivity cannot be lowered through such means, these connections will at least be better protected by requiring higher capital standards. The Hong Kong Proposal Since jurisdictions around the world are now working together to develop the regulatory framework required to support the G20 commitment, Hong Kong has also been taking steps to introduce a regulatory regime in line with these global standards. Last week, the HKMA and the SFC issued a joint consultation paper which sets out preliminary proposals on how to regulate this market with a view to promoting the transparency and resilience of this market in Hong Kong. Before I introduce the proposed regulatory regime, I would like to outline some of the key principles that have guided us during the development of our regime. This will provide you with a better understanding of our main intentions and considerations, and highlight the foundation on which our regime is built. First and foremost, we are committed to designing a regime that successfully ensures financial stability and resilience without compromising the ability of market players to engage in derivatives activities. We believe OTC derivatives (including those that cannot be standardised) do have their place in the financial market and therefore they should only be regulated but not banned altogether. / 2/6 19/09/22, 15:51 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Over-the-Counter Derivatives Market Reforms in Hong Kong Secondly, given the relatively smaller size of Hong Kong's OTC derivatives market, we are mindful that we cannot be the leader in the reform process but at the same time, we cannot lag too far behind our global counterparts. This recognizes the cross-border nature of these transactions. If Hong Kong does not follow the rule of the game globally, international financial institutions would withdraw liquidity from Hong Kong to the detriment of our market. The importance of aligning with international standards is akin to how one can achieve success in dragon boat racing (a popular sport which celebrates the Tuen Ng festival). Rowers can only reach their destination if they paddle in sync and towards the same direction - if even one rower deviates from this, the boat will flip or go in circles. In our context, international regulators, like rowers in a race, share a common destination: global financial stability and resilience of the derivatives market. If some rowers decide to paddle the other way, say by imposing less stringent requirements, thereby creating regulatory gaps that market participants can take advantage of - the entire boat will fail to reach its destination. Together, these two principles lay the basic foundation for our new regulatory regime: dictating that it needs to be one that is aligned with international standards but takes into consideration local market factors and characteristics to ensure the achievement of financial stability. Features of the regulatory framework in Hong Kong Let me now turn to the proposed regulatory regime. We propose that Authorized Institutions (Als), Licensed Corporations (LCs) and other non-FI participants in this market should be brought under the same regulatory framework under the Securities and Futures Ordinance to ensure a level playing field among all participants. The primary legislation will establish the new mandatory obligations on central clearing, reporting, and where appropriate, trading on exchanges or electronic trading platforms as well as confer the necessary rule making powers on the regulators. The detailed requirements such as which types of persons and what types of transactions will be subject to the mandatory obligations will be specified in the rules by the regulators. Such an approach would give us the flexibility to monitor the developments elsewhere and needs of our own market before we decide to specify new product classes in the rules for the purpose of the clearing, reporting and trading requirements. The regime will be jointly administered by the HKMA and the SFC in that the HKMA, being the principal regulator for banks in Hong Kong, will be responsible for overseeing and regulating the OTC derivatives activities of Als while the SFC will be responsible for overseeing and regulating the OTC derivatives activities of non-Als. To support the central clearing and reporting requirements, as announced in December 2010, the Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited will develop a new local CCP for OTC derivatives, and HKMA's Central Moneymarkets Unit will also establish a new TR where trades of systemic relevance to Hong Kong must be reported. These two important pieces of infrastructure are expected to be launched in the third quarter of 2012. When the clearing and reporting requirements are first introduced, tentatively in January 2013, they will only apply to certain products and market players. Product-wise, only certain / 3/6 19/09/22, 15:51 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Over-the-Counter Derivatives Market Reforms in Hong Kong types of interest rate swaps and non-deliverable forwards will initially be identified as clearing eligible transactions or reportable transactions that must be centrally cleared through a designated CCP and reported to the HKMA-TR respectively. They are the two most common types of derivatives transactions in Hong Kong after foreign exchange derivatives. FX derivatives like foreign exchange swaps and forwards are not included in the initial stage of implementation because they are usually shorter-dated and settled through the Continuous Linked Settlement system (CLS system), which pose lesser risk to the financial system. The scope of coverage will, however, be gradually extended to other OTC derivatives asset classes as appropriate. Under our proposed regime, all Als, LCs and those identified as Hong Kong persons will come under our purview, although the manner in which the requirements applicable to them will differ. In addition, financial intermediaries, other than Als, who provide dealing, advising or clearing agent service in the OTC derivatives market will have to register for a licence with the SFC. They will become LCs in the process and thus subject to the regulation by the SFC as well as the mandatory reporting, clearing and trading requirements. We are also considering to subject large market players, whose positions may present systemic risk concerns, to some oversight requirements, even though they may not be carrying on any intermediary function. This is to enable us to monitor and contain the build-up of systemic risks in the market. I would now like to take the opportunity here to explain two special features in the proposed mandatory clearing and reporting requirements that are particularly relevant to Als: the applicability of the mandatory obligations to the locally incorporated Als on a consolidated basis; and the reporting of Hong Kong connected transactions by foreign incorporated Als. For locally incorporated Als, the HKMA has always been supervising these institutions on a consolidated basis. This reflects the role of the HKMA as the home regulator of these entities. It is thus important that we are in a position to monitor the risks of the institutions on a group basis regardless of the location where such risks might be assumed. Therefore if the HKMA has decided to specify certain subsidiaries of a local Al for inclusion into the relevant requirement, the Al has to ensure that the relevant transactions be reported to the HKMA-TR or cleared through a designated CCP. However, the clearing and reporting obligation will only rest with the Al rather than its subsidiaries. Foreign Als are not required to comply with the mandatory obligations on a consolidated basis because consolidated supervision is the responsibility of their home supervisor rather than the HKMA as the host supervisor for their Hong Kong offices. It follows that the mandatory reporting and clearing obligation would usually apply to the OTC derivatives activities of these institutions that are conducted through the Hong Kong branch. However, in cases where the transactions have a Hong Kong nexus (e.g. when the underlying assets of the derivatives contract are denominated in Hong Kong dollar), we would also expect the foreign Al to report such transactions to our Trade Repository even though such transactions may not involve the Hong Kong branch in any way. We believe this can be justified because the regulatory access to such Hong Kong connected transactions would be critical to the assessment of risks to our monetary and financial system. To facilitate compliance, market players will be able to comply with the clearing and reporting requirements through both direct and indirect channels. For clearing, entities can either become a direct member of a designated CCP or clear the transaction indirectly / 4/6 19/09/22, 15:51 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Over-the-Counter Derivatives Market Reforms in Hong Kong through such a clearing member. As for reporting to the HKMA-TR, the TR will accept both direct reports to it or reports from agents, e.g. trade-matching platforms or a foreign TR, acting on behalf of the reporting entity. Overseas persons will be exempted from both requirements under most situations. For reporting, they will be completely exempted. As for clearing, they will only be affected if they engage in a clearing eligible transaction with an Al, LC or Hong Kong person. However, trades conducted between two overseas counterparties that have been cleared in accordance with the laws of an acceptable overseas jurisdiction or exempted from clearing by those laws will be unaffected by Hong Kong's obligations. We have also proposed to provide the end-users in the OTC derivatives market with some relief in respect of the reporting requirement. Our current intention is that an end-user (i.e. other than an Al or LC) will not need to report a transaction if it is already a transaction reportable by an Al or LC. Since an end-user in the OTC derivatives market will usually deal with an Al or LC, this should provide relief to an end-user from the reporting obligation in most cases. Apart from the requirements discussed above, there are still a number of important requirements that will need to be introduced at a later stage, but they can only be finalised upon further guidance from the relevant international bodies. For example, we are currently considering how to impose higher capital requirements on non-centrally cleared trades based on the guidelines and standards provided by the Basel Committee. We are also taking part in international discussion under the auspices of the Financial Stability Board on whether and how we should introduce margin requirements for non-centrally cleared trades. Issues of international concern Before I close, I would also like to mention two topical issues of concern on the radar screen of the international discussion on this subject. One area which has been the subject of contention is that of mutual recognition of CCPs. At this stage of regulatory reform, some jurisdictions have rather stringent requirement in terms of designating CCP for compliance purposes, to the extent that CCPs located outside the jurisdiction will not be accepted. As it is likely that global and regional CCPs will co-exist with each other in the evolving landscape of the OTC derivatives market, it is critical that market participants can choose a CCP which meets certain internationally recognised standards, for them to comply with the regulatory requirement effectively. In this regard, we support any effort to develop an international framework for recognition of CCPs for OTC derivatives products. Such a framework would allow mutual recognition of CCPs provided that they meet the international standards in terms of risk management, governance, operations and other necessary criteria, which in turn would avoid financial disintermediation in the OTC derivatives market. Another prevalent issue of concern relates to the international cooperation on regulatory access to data stored in TRs, in order to fulfil their regulatory mandates. The problem can be amplified when indemnification requirements are imposed on overseas regulators in exchange for data access in some jurisdictions. Given the cross-border nature of OTC derivatives activities, this would impede regulators' ability to access data relating to the overseas transactions of the financial institutions under their supervision, thus defeating the / 5/6 19/09/22, 15:51 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Over-the-Counter Derivatives Market Reforms in Hong Kong purpose of mandatory reporting. Regulators worldwide are currently seeking agreement on the data sharing framework that governs the rules, format and level of data from TRs and CCPs through discussion at international forums such as the OTC Derivatives Regulators' Forum (ODRF). Through highlighting these examples, I hope to emphasize that the regulatory standards for regulation of OTC derivatives are still evolving. This underscores the importance of designing our regulatory regime with flexibility so that it is not cast in stone but is progressing in times with the needs of the market. Conclusion Ladies and gentlemen, I began this speech by looking into the past, but we must not linger there after learning its lessons. After all, we are here today to shape the future of the derivatives market, one which I am confident will be characterized by greater transparency, resilience and most importantly, stability in the future. But this will be a formidable task which requires strenuous and concerted efforts of all of us involved in this market. Thank you very much. Last revision date : 25 October 2011 / 6/6

Title: Development of Renminbi Offshore Market and Market Infrastructure in Hong Kong
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 06-21-2012 Hong Kong RMB offshore market development and market infrastructure construction Pang Xingtang is a Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Seminar on RMB Treasury Bond Issuance and Hong Kong Bond Market Development) Director Sun, Director Chen, and distinguished guests: Thank you for attending today's Treasury Debt Seminar. Hong Kong's offshore RMB platform has developed rapidly in recent years, not only because Hong Kong has always been the most important window for trade and investment between the mainland and the rest of the world, but also because Hong Kong has advanced international financial centre facilities. The development of all offshore RMB businesses goes through three important processes: the first is the formulation of policy frameworks, the second is the construction of financial infrastructure, and the third is the development of financial products. Among them, financial infrastructure must be based on an appropriate policy framework and be forward-looking, provide sufficient support and support for the design and launch of financial products, and keep pace with the development of financial products. The focus of my talk today is to introduce the important role of financial infrastructure in the process of deepening and diversifying offshore RMB business. The first phase of offshore RMB business in Hong Kong (2004-2007). Hong Kong's offshore RMB business has been launched since 2004, and the first stage is the Zou-type of Hong Kong RMB business, the main purpose of which is to facilitate the exchange and consumption of residents of the two places. Banks in Hong Kong began providing basic services such as deposits, exchanges, remittances, cheques and bank cards to individual customers. In view of these developments, Hong Kong launched a RMB clearing platform in 2006 to transfer the RMB funds needed in Hong Kong from Shanghai to Hong Kong , so that RMB funds in Shanghai can be effectively transferred to Hong Kong's offshore market, and began to establish an overseas RMB capital pool to create the necessary conditions for RMB financing, including RMB bonds. Phase II of Hong Kong's offshore RMB business (2007-present). In 2007, RMB products entered a new stage of diversification with the expansion of the policy framework and the corresponding coordination of financial infrastructure. Since 2007, mainland financial institutions have been able to issue RMB bonds in Hong Kong, which has become the starting point for RMB financing activities in Hong Kong. In the same year, Hong Kong's RMB clearing platform was further developed into a RMB instant payment system to facilitate the transfer of funds immediately. Hong Kong's Central Clearing and Settlement System (CMU) for Debt Instruments (CMU) also joins the RMB currency and is networked with Hong Kong's RMB Instant Payment and Settlement System, enabling both parties to RMB bonds to conduct a DvP transaction. Settlement, greatly reducing the risk of settlement. The establishment of the RMB instant payment system also provides the necessary conditions for inter-bank RMB transfers, providing the necessary operating conditions for financial institutions to launch a variety of financial investment products, including RMB retail bonds. With the strong support of the relevant central and mainland departments, the RMB cross-border trade settlement pilot launched in July 2009 established a two-way flow mechanism between the onshore and offshore RMB markets, which has made a breakthrough in Hong Kong's offshore RMB business. Between 2009 and 2010, Hong Kong's RMB instant payment system fully adopted an open platform to facilitate overseas banks' direct or indirect participation in Hong Kong's RMB payment platforms and activities, fully cooperating with the development of RMB cross-border trade settlement. As the only RMB payment and settlement system outside of China, and with the advantage of networking with the country's modern payment system (CNAPS), Hong Kong's RMB instant payment system has attracted 196 directly participating institutions, of which 170 are foreign banks. Hong Kong's RMB real-time payment and settlement system now trades between RMB150 billion and RMB200 billion per day; This makes the renminbi the second most important trading currency in Hong Kong after the Hong Kong dollar. Hong Kong's RMB Instant Payment and Settlement System has established a synchronous settlement (PvP) network for foreign exchange transactions with the Hong Kong Dollar, US Dollar and EUR Instant Payment and Settlement System respectively, which greatly reduces the risk of transaction settlement and activates the offshore RMB foreign exchange market. In addition, Hong Kong's RMB Instant Payment and Settlement System has established a DvP network with CMU System and Central Clearing and Settlement System (CCASS) respectively In order to create a suitable environment for the diversification of Renminbi-denominated products, Hong Kong's first RMB stock was successfully launched in 2011. Phase III: Establishment of a globally important offshore RMB center Renminbi cross-border and offshore business has made considerable progress so far, and the three aspects of RMB trade settlement, financing and asset management have promoted each other, making Hong Kong an international hub for offshore RMB business. As the world's premier offshore RMB centre, Hong Kong needs to continuously optimize its RMB financial infrastructure to provide an efficient and reliable platform for RMB business in other financial centres . This year, in line with the expanding payment and settlement needs of financial institutions in London and other financial centres in the European time zone, the Hong Kong RMB Instant Payment and Settlement System will be extended from 25 June from 8:30 a.m. to 18:00 p.m. Hong Kong time Extended from 6:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m., providing a 15-hour operating window to further expand cross-market banks in Hong Kong and other financial centres Interbank payment settlement and financing activities. CMU systems are currently being networked with systems of international and regional custodians, allowing overseas investors to participate in the local bond market. RMB bonds (including treasury bonds, corporate bonds and bank certificates of deposit) currently held at CMU amount to RMB 280 billion, of which three are RMB bonds held by international investors through the system of international custodians. On this basis, in March this year, the HKMA, together with Bank Negara Malaysia and the Bank for European Settlements, launched a pilot platform for cross-border bond investment and settlement, which further encourages overseas investors to purchase and hold RMB bonds issued in Hong Kong through the settlement method of goods and banks and carry out cross-border bond settlement; It also promotes international bond issuers to issue more RMB bonds in Hong Kong. In addition, in order to make more effective use of Hong Kong's RMB pool, the HKMA will also launch a cross-border collateral management platform and services at the end of June to allow overseas financial institutions to obtain particularly RMB-based liquidity through repurchase financing transactions with local banks, which will contribute to the development of global RMB business. Development of the RMB bond market With the support of a sound bond settlement system, the development of RMB bonds in Hong Kong is very vigorous. As of the end of March this year, foreign currency bonds deposited in the CMU system accounted for 30% of the total bonds issued by private institutions in Hong Kong, with the development of RMB bonds being the most notable. In the non-treasury bond market, RMB bonds (including bank deposit certificates) issued in 2011 amounted to RMB152 billion. In the first five months of this year, the issuance of RMB bonds and deposit certificates has reached RMB100.6 billion. In terms of the treasury bond market, the Ministry of Finance has issued a total of 34 billion yuan of government bonds in Hong Kong in the past three years, and the market response has been enthusiastic. The Ministry of Finance and the HKMA signed a Memorandum of Understanding in 2010 to use the CMU bond bidding platform to bid for RMB Treasury bonds in order to optimize the issuance of RMB Treasury bonds, improve market transparency and improve the price formation mechanism. In this issuance of treasury bonds, the two sides will further strengthen cooperation and set up a central bank placement coordination window on the CMU bond bidding platform to have treasury bonds Interested central banks around the world will arrange for the placement of Treasury bonds on the bond tender date, and the interest rate will be priced at the winning interest rate of the same year RMB Treasury bonds. The CMU Central Bank Placement Coordination Window is another innovative new issuance channel for the Ministry of Finance to strengthen the role of the winning interest rate and cater to the needs of overseas central banks. This will further enhance the market position of RMB government bonds and set an important milestone for promoting the internationalization of RMB. Summary Like the construction of other physical infrastructure facilities such as highways and ports, the construction of financial infrastructure must also have a certain degree of foresight, so as to meet the needs of long-term development and enable the market to grasp the opportunities for development in a timely manner. In the future, the HKMA will continue to optimize its financial infrastructure in response to the needs of market development, and continue to work closely with relevant institutions and bond market participants in the Mainland and Hong Kong to actively expand Hong Kong's bond market, including Hong Kong's offshore RMB bond market, and further consolidate Hong Kong's advantages as an international financial centre and offshore RMB centre. Thank you." Last revision date: 21 June 2012

Title: Internationalisation of Renminbi and the Development of Hong Kongs Offshore Renminbi Business Centre
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 06-28-2012 RMB internationalization and development of Hong Kong's offshore RMB business center Yuu Wai Man is a Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (At China (Guangzhou) International Financial Exchange Expo) Dear Vice Mayor Ouyang Weimin, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, good morning: 1First of all, thank you very much to the Guangzhou Branch of the People's Bank of China for inviting me to attend this forum. The internationalization of the renminbi has received a lot of attention in the mainland, Hong Kong and around the world. Today I am pleased to take this opportunity to share some of my views with you on the internationalisation of RMB and the development of offshore RMB business in Hong Kong. 2 In the country's "Twelfth Five-Year Plan", the central government clearly put forward the policy of expanding the cross-border use of the renminbi and supported Hong Kong's development into an offshore renminbi business center. Looking back over the past two years, both the cross-border use of RMB and the offshore RMB business in Hong Kong have developed very well. The Department of Peoples is internationalized 3 The launch of the pilot project of cross-border RMB trade settlement in July 2009 is an important step for the state to promote the internationalization of RMB. With the continuous expansion of the pilot, all mainland enterprises with import and export qualifications can now choose to use RMB to settle with trading partners around the world. According to statistics, the proportion of the mainland's foreign trade settled in RMB increased from nothing before June 2009 to about 2% in 2010; In the first quarter of 2012, this proportion has exceeded 8%. According to international experience, about one-third of Japan's foreign trade is settled in Japanese yen; The euro accounts for 50%-60% of European trade settlements; The proportion of the US dollar in the settlement of foreign trade in the United States is 80%-90%. It has only been more than two years since the RMB trade settlement was carried out, and it is expected that there will be a lot of room for growth in the future. 4 In addition to trade settlement, the scope of cross-border use of RMB has also gradually expanded to direct investment and financial market investment. At present, foreign direct investment and overseas direct investment by mainland enterprises can be settled in RMB, which will help enterprises reduce exchange rate risks and reduce exchange costs. The relevant policy was introduced just last year, and at present, 12% of foreign direct investment in the mainland has been settled in renminbi, and 5% of the amount of investment made by mainland enterprises "going out" is also settled in RMB. 5 In terms of financial market investment, foreign institutions, including the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, may invest in the intra-bank bond market within the permitted amount. The policy for Renminbi Qualified Foreign Institutional Investors (RQFIIs) to invest in the mainland securities market has also been introduced and expanded, with the relevant quota recently increasing by 50 billion yuan to the previous year's 20 billion yuan 70 billion yuan people's department. 6 That is to say, the internationalization of the renminbi is advancing steadily in all directions, and the renminbi has begun to play an active role as a pricing unit, trading media, and stored value tool in the international market. Development of Hong Kong's offshore RMB business centre 7 The increased cross-border use of RMB has also laid an important foundation for the development of Hong Kong's offshore RMB market. Over the past two years and more, with the strong support of the central government, Hong Kong, with the advantages of "one country, two systems" and as an international financial center, has now developed into the world's largest and most efficient offshore RMB business center. The following data specifically reflect the development of offshore RMB business in Hong Kong: 95 The amount of RMB trade settlement transactions processed by Hong Kong increased from less than RMB2 billion in 2009 to nearly RMB2,000 billion in 2011. It can be seen that Hong Kong is the hub of global offshore RMB trade settlement. 95 At the end of April 2012, Hong Kong's RMB customer deposits and certificates of deposit balances totaled approximately RMB674 billion, 10 times that of the end of 2009 and the world's largest offshore RMB capital pool. 95 In the past two years, the issuance of "dim sum bonds" in Hong Kong has increased from RMB16 billion at the end of 2009 to RMB108 billion at the end of last year, an increase of nearly 6 Fold. Bond issuers are also diversifying, including corporate and financial institutions around the world, national ministries of finance, and financial institutions and non-financial enterprises on the mainland. Investors come from Europe, the United States, Asia and other regions, including private institutions and overseas central banks. 95 Hong Kong's offshore RMB interbank market and foreign exchange market have taken shape and are gradually maturing. According to market estimates, the average daily offshore spot and forward RMB trading volume in Hong Kong's offshore RMB foreign exchange market is US5 billion, equivalent to RMB32 billion. Hong Kong's offshore RMB foreign exchange trading volume ranks first in the world, with spot foreign exchange trading volume accounting for 56% of the world's total. In addition, according to the Society for Global Banking and Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT), Hong Kong banks account for nearly 80% of the world's RMB receipt and payment volume. Just two weeks ago, the HKMA introduced a RMB liquidity arrangement in Hong Kong for Hong Kong banks to use through currency swap arrangements with the People's Bank of China. This will help further deepen Hong Kong's RMB capital market and strengthen Hong Kong's position as the global hub of offshore RMB business. 8 The Hong Kong offshore RMB business center is growing steadily and diversified, of which I have observed two characteristics that I would like to share with you. 9 First, the development of Hong Kong's offshore RMB business center is an important link in line with the process of RMB internationalization and the gradual opening up of the national capital account. It is worth mentioning that the key to such an ideal development of Hong Kong's offshore RMB business lies in the close economic and financial ties between Hong Kong and the Mainland, as well as the important intermediary role that Hong Kong has always played in cross-border activities on the mainland. For example, 30% of the mainland's foreign trade is arranged or re-exported through Hong Kong, 60% of foreign direct investment is from or through Hong Kong, and 60% of mainland enterprises going out are put into Hong Kong or overseas projects through Hong Kong. As these economic activities make more use of RMB, the demand for RMB financial services will naturally increase accordingly, so Hong Kong's offshore RMB business will continue to flourish. 10 In the economy, finance and other aspects, Hong Kong and Guangdong have always been important partners. Launch of the pilot project on RMB settlement of cross-border trade When it was launched in 2009, several major cities in Hong Kong and Macao and Guangdong Province were the earliest pilot areas. At present, more than 20% of the RMB trade settlements handled by Hong Kong are trade settlement transactions between Guangdong and Hong Kong. In terms of financing, the funds raised by Hopewell Highway Infrastructure, the first enterprise to issue RMB bonds in Hong Kong, were used for infrastructure projects in Guangdong Province. It is believed that in the future, on the basis of the long-established close economic and trade exchanges, Guangdong and Hong Kong will continue to strengthen cooperation and jointly contribute to the internationalization of the RMB and the gradual opening up of the national capital account. 11Second, Hong Kong's development as an offshore RMB business center is no longer limited to serving Hong Kong itself, but supports the development of offshore RMB business in the world to meet market demand. In other words, Hong Kong's role as a global offshore RMB business hub is deepening, playing an important role in promoting the internationalization of RMB in the following aspects: 95 More and more overseas banks are taking advantage of the RMB agency services provided by Hong Kong banks to provide RMB products and services to local customers through the Hong Kong platform. The number of RMB correspondent accounts opened by overseas banks in Hong Kong has increased significantly from less than 200 at the end of 2010 to more than 1,100 at present, with nearly RMB130 billion deposited in the banking system in Hong Kong. The Hong Kong banks also lent about 135 billion yuan in RMB funds to overseas banks. 95 At present, a total of 194 financial institutions have become participating banks in the offshore RMB clearing platform in Hong Kong, of which 170 are branches of overseas banks and overseas branches of mainland banks, forming a settlement network covering more than 30 countries on six continents. Starting this week, the Hong Kong RMB payment system will be extended to 11:30 p.m., providing a longer window for financial institutions in European time zones and some American time zones, and supporting convenient payment and settlement of offshore RMB through the Hong Kong platform. 95 At the same time, since last year, the HKMA has visited Australia, Russia, the United Kingdom, Spain, South America and Yueben to carry out promotional activities, introducing the internationalization of the RMB and the one-stop services provided by the Hong Kong RMB financial platform to overseas enterprises and financial institutions, and deepening their understanding of the internationalization of the RMB. We are also committed to strengthening cooperation links with other international financial centers to more actively promote the internationalization of the renminbi. In January, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the UK Treasury announced the establishment of a Hong Kong-London Cooperation Group comprising representatives of private institutions. The group held its first meeting in Hong Kong at the end of May, where bank members of the two places agreed to work to provide support and related products and services to enterprises that use RMB for trade settlement, including the expansion of cross-time interbank financing activities between Hong Kong and London, the provision of direct foreign exchange quotations between RMB against the British pound and the euro, and the efforts to deepen the personal, The understanding of RMB business by enterprises and financial institutions. Conclusion 12 Vice Premier Li Keqiang mentioned in his speech in Hong Kong last August: "Further giving full play to Hong Kong's unique advantages that have been formed for a long time and giving play to Hong Kong's irreplaceable role in the mainland's reform, opening up and modernization construction is the need of Hong Kong and the needs of the country." Hong Kong's development as an offshore RMB business centre is playing an active role in the process of RMB internationalization and the gradual opening up of the national capital account. Looking ahead, I believe that under the premise of gradual and controllable risks, Hong Kong will seize the opportunity, meet the needs of the country , continue to give full play to the advantages of the global RMB business platform and international financial center, and create a more perfect supporting environment for the country's foreign trade and overall economic development, as well as financial reform and modernization. 13 Thank you!
