Title: E-money and E-payment Development in Hong Kong
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 06-28-2012 Development of e-money and e-payments in Hong Kong Pang Xingtang is a Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (At the inaugural launch ceremony of the "Octopus 95 Lingnantong" Co-branded Card) Distinguished guests, friends of the media: First of all, I congratulate Octopus Card Co., Ltd. and Lingnantong Co., Ltd. on the successful implementation and issuance of the "Octopus Lingnantong Co-Brand Card". The issuance of the Co-Brand Card has taken an important step towards the integration of public transport between Guangdong and Hong Kong and the promotion of e-currency interconnection, and also marked an important milestone in the economic integration of the two places. Looking back at the development of e-money in Hong Kong, when the Octopus system was launched in September 1997, it was only used on buses, railways and other means of transport, and its use was gradually expanded to shops, restaurants, etc. After nearly 15 years of hard work, Octopus Card has become one of the most widely served smart card electronic payment systems in the world. In addition to being available on public transport systems, Octopus also has more than 10,000 retail outlets that accept Octopus payments. Hong Kong has a population of about 7 million, but there are more than 20 million Octopus cards and products in circulation, and the average daily transaction amount through Octopus has exceeded HK120 million. It is encouraging that Octopus has been able to achieve this impressive result in 15 years. Today's other protagonist, Lingnantong, is one of the largest cross-regional interconnected bus card systems in China. Since the first card issuance at the end of 2010, Lingnantong's network has expanded rapidly, covering public transportation and micropayment, and can be applied to 16 cities in Guangzhou, Foshan, Jiangmen, Zhaoqing and other provinces. At present, Lingnan Tong has 1,200 cooperative operators with an average of more than 8.46 million card swipes per day. I believe that the respective impressive achievements of Octopus and Lingnan Tong not only reflect each other, but also the cooperation between the two will further bring great synergy effects, linking the needs of residents of the two places to take public transportation and make merchant shopping consumption in a two-in-one card, providing a wider range of convenient and faster payment services. According to the statistics of the National Tourism Administration and the Hong Kong Tourism Board, Guangdong Province received 20,400,000 Hong Kong visitors in 2011; During the same period, 20,500,000 passengers from Guangdong Province to Hong Kong were also visited. With the opening of the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail (Hong Kong Section) in 2015, Guangdong and Hong Kong residents can travel between the two places more quickly, and the flow of people between the two places is expected to continue to rise, "Octopus Lingnan Tong Joint Brand Card." "The launch will make it easier for them to take advantage of public traffic and make shopping purchases." The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, as regulator, has been encouraging Octopus to provide cross-border payment services. For example, under the impetus of the HKMA and the People's Bank of Shenzhen, Octopus has been used in retail outlets in Shenzhen since August 2006. At present, Octopus has more than 80 Octopus readers in more than 30 retail stores in Shenzhen for easy use by Octopus users, while cross-border Octopus retail consumer transactions reached 800,000 in 2011. Looking ahead, the interconnection of cross-border electronic money will accelerate the integration and development of the living circle in the Pearl River Delta region. In addition, with more provinces and cities in the mainland joining the expansion of the field of micropayment, electronic currency interconnection has become the trend of the times, and one card is a major breakthrough in facilitating Chinese and Hong Kong residents and promoting the flow of logistics funds. With the increasingly close economic and trade activities and social ties between the Mainland and Hong Kong, the demand for efficient and convenient payment media for residents of the two places is increasing. In fact, long before the National Development and Reform Commission issued the Outline Plan for the Reform and Development of the Pearl River Delta Region in December 2008, the HKMA had studied and developed financial infrastructure connectivity between the two places with relevant units in the Mainland to support the increasingly frequent economic and trade exchanges between the two places. The HKMA has been working closely with People's Bank of China Guangzhou Branch (Guangzhou People's Bank) and Shenzhen Central Branch (Shenzhen People's Bank). Since 1998, a number of Guangdong-Hong Kong-Shenzhen-Hong Kong cross-border networking cooperation projects have been launched, including cross-border payment systems and cheque settlement networking, which have effectively promoted financial and business activities in the two places. In 2011, the volume of transactions conducted through the above cross-border networks exceeded 350,000, with a total transaction volume of about HK515 billion. Among them, cross-border payment transactions through payment systems in HKD, USD and EUR accounted for about 25,000 transactions, totalling HK475 billion; Cross-border payment transactions through the HKD, USD and RMB cheque settlement system accounted for approximately 325,000 transactions, totalling HK40 billion. Looking around the world, the rapid development of the network economy is pushing us into a "paperless" e-commerce generation. "Paperless" electronic transactions naturally require "paperless" electronic money and related payment systems. At present, many financial or non-financial institutions around the world have developed different forms of electronic money for consumers to use online or in daily life, and are gradually introducing electronic money into commercial applications. Due to the efficiency and convenience of electronic money, the recognition of the general public is constantly increasing. There is no doubt that e-money and electronic payments have become the core of the development of e-commerce. Their popularity and application will directly affect the development of e-commerce and open up a broader space for the network economy. As an international financial centre, Hong Kong should closely follow the development of the global market and seize the opportunities brought by technological innovation, so as to create a favorable environment for e-money and electronic payment to enter a new field. Until now, local and overseas e-currencies have been dominated by traditional stored value cards. In view of the popularity of smartphones in recent years and the maturity of "Near Field Communication (NFC)" technology in mobile payment applications, some countries have launched related infrastructure packages, And conduct small-scale pilot testing. In addition to being used in electronic money and electronic payment, "Near Field Communication" technology enables smartphones to provide stored value card functions, and is more suitable for a variety of e-commerce activities. For example, when a municipality passes through an advertisement version of a smart poster, they can read product information from the promotional poster with their smartphones, make ordering instructions and enter the delivery location, and make payment with the smartphone; Customers can also apply to the bank to place the contactless credit card in their smartphone, and in the future, when they make retail payments, they only need to put the smartphone on the card reader and enter the password to enter the relevant transaction through the built-in contactless credit card; Airlines can also issue electronic boarding passes to customers to use the automatic boarding system via their smartphones. The application of "Near Field Communication" technology brings more development space and opportunities for the whole e-money and even e-commerce. In view of this development trend, the HKMA will commission a feasibility study on the promotion of a "near field communication"-based mobile phone payment platform in Hong Kong. The consultancy firm will draw on the development strategies, operating models and operational performance of overseas pioneers, draw on their experiences, analyse the elements of successful cases, understand the opinions of local stakeholders including payment service providers, telecommunications network operators and regulators, and analyse market trends and the wishes and tendencies of the public, so as to formulate a long-term development strategy suitable for the Hong Kong model. The HKMA's objective is to provide a fair, open, robust and compatible platform for financial and non-financial institutions to provide diversified micropayment services to the public and enhance public confidence in innovative retail payment instruments. The study will begin in the second half of this year and is expected to be completed by the end of this year or early next year. In addition, to ensure that e-money and retail payment systems can operate in a safe and secure environment so that the interests of users are protected, the HKMA is conducting relevant policy and regulatory research. Apart from taking into account foreign experience, the HKMA will also draft and formulate relevant legislation applicable to Hong Kong in light of the impact of technological developments on e-money and retail payment systems. The HKMA will consult the trade for comments on the relevant draft legislation in due course. The enactment of relevant legislation will provide a more favorable environment and conditions for the development and popularization of electronic money in Hong Kong. "A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step", and today we are here to witness the birth of the "Octopus 95 Lingnan Tong Joint Branding Card", marking a further step forward in the economic integration of Guangdong and Hong Kong. In the future, the HKMA will vigorously promote the development of local and cross-border e-money and payments as in the past, so as to provide a favorable market and regulatory environment for the development of e-commerce in Hong Kong. Finally, I wish the "Octopus 95 Lingnan Tong Co-Brand Card" business a prosperous and prosperous business to meet the needs of residents of Guangdong and Hong Kong. Thank you! Title: Vision of Cooperation between Hong Kong and Qianhai on the Offshore RMB Business and Asset Management Business
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 07-19-2012 Vision of cooperation between Hong Kong and Qianhai in offshore RMB business and asset management business Pang Xingtang is a Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Hong Kong Treasury Markets Association (Opening Remarks at the Treasury Market Symposium on New Business Opportunities for Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Qianhai Cooperation) President Zhang Jianjun, Deputy Director Zhou Ziyou, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, 1. Welcome to today's Treasury Markets Symposium organised by the Hong Kong Treasury Markets Association. It is a great honor for the leaders of Shenzhen and Qianhai to take time out of their busy schedules to attend this symposium and meet with friends from Hong Kong's financial circles to discuss the business opportunities and vision of Shenzhen-Hong Kong co-working and Qianhai's development. The foundation for Qianhai's development and Shenzhen-Hong Kong cooperation 2. At the end of June this year, the State Council officially approved the relevant policies on supporting the development and opening up of the Shenzhen-Qianhai Shenzhen-Hong Kong Modern Service Industry Cooperation Zone, and the purpose of these policies is to promote Shenzhen's industrial transformation and upgrading and move toward the direction of high-value-added services through the opening up of Hong Kong and cooperation with Hong Kong. We believe that Hong Kong and Qianhai have a strong foundation for cooperation, can complement each other's advantages, achieve mutual benefit and win-win results, and create a huge synergy effect of one plus one big and more than two. 3. As a pioneer in promoting the development of the financial services industry and industrial transformation and upgrading, Hong Kong can provide useful experience and market and talent cooperation. Hong Kong's industry has also undergone a transformation from manufacturing to services Journey. In 1970, the share of manufacturing in Hong Kong's GDP was 31%. In the 1980s, seizing the opportunity of the country's reform and opening up, Hong Kong manufacturers gradually moved their manufacturing industry to South China, led by the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone. Hong Kong's development model has also been transformed into a service industry dominated by finance, commerce and trade to match the rapid growth of real economic activities in South China. Today, the service sector accounts for 93% of Hong Kong's GDP and has become the backbone of Hong Kong's economy. 4. Among the many service industries, the financial industry and professional commercial services are high value-added industries. In 2010, these industries accounted for 18.4% of Hong Kong's employed population, but they accounted for 26.4% of total output value. I believe that Hong Kong's development experience is of reference value to the development of the financial industry and modern service industry in Qianhai. Offshore RMB business and asset management are the focus of cooperation between Shenzhen and Hong Kong in Qianhai 5. The offshore RMB business and asset management business vigorously developed by Hong Kong's financial industry in recent years have also provided a strong foundation to support Qianhai's policy goal of being the first to try out in financial reform and innovation, and promoting the construction of a demonstration window for the opening up of the national financial industry to the outside world. 6. Hong Kong is a pioneer in offshore RMB business and has the largest offshore RMB capital pool, with the balance of RMB deposits plus RMB certificates of deposit reaching RMB673.7 billion at the end of May this year. At the same time, Hong Kong is also the world's largest offshore RMB bond market. Since 2007, the total issuance has reached 254.4 billion RMB. In the first six months of this year alone, RMB bond issuance reached RMB72.7 billion, a 65% increase over the same period last year. In the long run, with the gradual increase in the international use of the renminbi, Hong Kong has the ability to develop into a global offshore renminbi hub, providing RMB financing for foreign enterprises that need RMB funds to enter domestic direct investment, as well as mainland enterprises looking for new funds overseas, through bank loans, bond markets and other channels. I believe that Qianhai's first-mover policy in overseas RMB business will provide new impetus for the development of Hong Kong's offshore RMB business, and at the same time bring opportunities for Qianhai to develop overseas business. 7. Asset management is another important area of cooperation between Qianhai and Hong Kong. Hong Kong is one of the largest asset and wealth management centres in the Asia-Pacific region, with hedge funds and equity investment funds particularly prominently in the development. In terms of equity investment funds, Hong Kong's share of the Asian market reached 21.6%, second only to the mainland at 22.6%. In other words, the Mainland and Hong Kong together account for nearly 50% of Asia's equity investment fund market. On this strong foundation, the development potential of cooperation between Qianhai and Hong Kong is very large. 8. Asset management involves different links, in addition to front-end services - i.e. investment managers, traders, researchers, middle and back-office services also involve many links, such as fund management, compliance officer, risk management and fund custody. At present, outside the United States, many investment funds are incorporated in countries such as Luxembourg, and although many investment funds are invested in Asia, some of the middle and back office services are still retained in the countries of registration outside the region. 9. However, this trend has begun to shift with an increasing number of funds investing in Asia interested in incorporation within Asia. This will increase the demand for back-office services in the asset management industry. Moreover, if China and Hong Kong can cooperate in the future to launch China's "fund passport" system, so that funds approved by one party can be sold on the other side at the same time, the front, middle and back office business of the asset management industry in the mainland and Hong Kong will certainly grow rapidly. Judging from the current comparative advantages of Shenzhen and Hong Kong, Hong Kong and Qianhai can divide labor and cooperate, for example, the front-end work of sales and investment management is concentrated in Hong Kong, while the middle and back-office work can be considered in Qianhai. Eight financial-related policy measures in Qianhai 10. Next, let me talk about how Hong Kong can cooperate with the eight policy measures on financial cooperation between Shenzhen and Hong Kong in the State Council's approval document . 3. Overseas RMB capital return channels and cross-border RMB loans 11. The first and second items of policy measures focus on exploring and broadening the channels for the return of overseas RMB funds, supporting the development of Hong Kong's offshore RMB business, and supporting two-way RMB loans between Hong Kong and Qianhai. 12. At present, there are three main channels for the cross-border use and return of overseas RMB. The first is trade settlement; The second is direct investment; The third is investment in financial assets. Among them, the return channels of trade settlement and direct investment, after the expansion of trade pilots and the introduction of direct investment management measures, have a solid basis to expand the scale. The financial asset investment channel is still in its infancy. The current measures (including allowing overseas financial institutions and foreign central banks to enter the Mainland's interbank bond market within a certain amount and investing in the Mainland's securities and bond markets through RQFII) are a good start, but there is still a lot of room for development. To promote the use of the renminbi abroad, we should explore new channels in due course, broaden existing channels (for example, by adjusting the amount, allowing more foreign institutions to enter the mainland interbank bond market, etc.), and increase the efficiency of existing channels. Qianhai's exploration of channels for the return of RMB will be conducive to the development of Hong Kong's offshore RMB market. I am confident that Hong Kong's policy authorities and market participants will fully cooperate. 13. Hong Kong banks also have a good foundation in promoting cross-border RMB lending. Currently, Hong Kong has the largest offshore RMB pool. Driven by RMB FDI, a number of international and Mainland enterprises have raised funds to support their business in the Mainland through Hong Kong's offshore RMB platform. In addition, Hong Kong banks also have extensive experience in syndicated loans, which also helps to develop cross-border RMB lending business. We very much welcome Qianhai to actively study the granting of RMB loans by Hong Kong banking institutions to enterprises or projects established in Qianhai. We hope that in the future, when Hong Kong banks issue loans to institutions and projects in Qianhai, the funds concerned will not be limited to the use of the Qianhai area, but will allow further borrowing units to transfer funds to other parts of the country in due course. Third, Qianhai enterprise institutions come to Hong Kong to issue personal bonds 14. The third policy measure is to support Qianhai's enterprises and financial institutions to issue RMB bonds in Hong Kong to support Qianhai's development and construction. Since the development of offshore RMB business in Hong Kong, the issuance of RMB bonds has risen steadily. For qualified high-quality mainland enterprises, Hong Kong has the advantages of a large network of international investors, mature financial infrastructure and a large number of professional intermediaries, which is a good place to raise funds. Making more use of Hong Kong's platform for debt financing will effectively promote cross-border financial integration with the Mainland, and increase the outlet for Hong Kong's RMB funds and the scale of the bond market. We also believe that there is a strong demand from overseas investors for these bonds supporting Qianhai's development. The Ministry of Finance has committed to the continuous issuance of treasury bonds of different years in Hong Kong, and Qianhai enterprises that intend to issue long-term bonds in Hong Kong can refer to the yield curve of treasury bonds in the offshore market to price their bonds. 4. Equity investment fund of funds and equity investment funds 15. The fourth and fifth items of policy measures support the establishment of Qianhai Equity Investment Fund and support the innovative development of foreign equity investment funds in Qianhai. As mentioned earlier, the Mainland and Hong Kong together account for nearly 50% of Asia's equity investment fund market. At the same time, Shenzhen is also an important concentration of domestic equity investment funds. If we can effectively take advantage of the concentration of emerging industries in Shenzhen and provide exit channels with platforms such as Hong Kong's main board and ChiNext board, as well as the Shenzhen ChiNext Board and the newly established Stock Exchange Center, the Guangdong-Hong Kong region can gather more stock investment funds in the region and become a regional stock investment fund center. In terms of the division of labor arrangement, the two places can implement the different management links involved in the equity investment fund in Hong Kong and Qianhai according to their comparative advantages to enhance the overall efficiency. 6. Reduce the conditions for Hong Kong financial institutions to enter the Qianhai under the CEPA framework 16. The sixth policy measure is to support the reduction of access conditions for Hong Kong financial enterprises to set up institutions and carry out financial business in Qianhai under the CEPA framework. At present, banks, securities and insurance companies in Hong Kong can open on the mainland under the prescribed conditions. With the gradual opening up of the Mainland's capital account, it is the trend of the times to allow Hong Kong's financial institutions to manage assets and invest overseas for mainland customers, and in addition to promoting capital interconnection between the two places, the increase in investment opportunities will also provide impetus for financial innovation. We believe that in addition to lowering the entry threshold, relaxing the business that Hong Kong financial institutions can engage in in the mainland is also an important direction for financial opening-up. 7. Promote financial element trading platforms 17. The seventh policy measure is to support Qianhai to pilot the establishment of innovative financial institutions that are conducive to enhancing market functions and to explore and promote new elements of the trading platform. The financial industry serves the real economy and is an irrefutable law. HKEX has already signed an acquisition agreement with the London Metal Exchange to capitalise on the growing volume of metals trading in the Mainland. We believe that the establishment of a financial element trading platform will be conducive to the development of equity investment funds. Guangdong and Hong Kong may consider setting up relevant financial asset trading platforms to provide exit opportunities for equity investors who have not been able to advance to the first and second boards. In addition, suggestions from some industries can also be considered, such as Qianhai and Guangdong-Hong Kong regions to further grasp China's advantages as a big agricultural country, set up an agricultural products trading center, and promote the merger and development of Hong Kong and Shenzhen into a factor trading center serving the whole country. A'Support financial institutions to set up their headquarters in Qianhai 18. The eighth policy measure is to support domestic and foreign financial institutions to set up international or national management headquarters in Qianhai. Hong Kong has always been an ideal location for multinational companies to set up their Asia Pacific headquarters. According to statistics, more than 3,700 overseas enterprises have set up an Asia-Pacific business center in Hong Kong; More than 70 of the world's top 100 banks are based in Hong Kong. Drawing on experience, the rule of law, free markets, free flow of information, a level playing field and high transparency are all reasons why Hong Kong can attract these enterprises. We would love to share these experiences with Qianhai. Qianhai and Hong Kong are geographically very close, and if the two places can cooperate with each other to attract mainland and international enterprises to set up national and even regional headquarters, I believe that there will be considerable synergies and achieve mutual benefit and double conclusion 19. Finally, we hope that the competent authorities responsible for planning Qianhai's development in the Mainland will publish the relevant policy details and implementation arrangements as soon as possible to help the financial industry of the two places fully understand the opportunities presented by Qianhai. The active participation of the industry is an important part of further strengthening the cooperation between Shenzhen and Hong Kong in these fields. In addition, cost competitiveness, the software and hardware required by financial markets, effective communication channels and the exchange of professionals are also the key to the successful implementation of the pilot policy. In these respects, I deeply hope that the government departments, industries and relevant institutions of the two places can maintain good communication and cooperation, so that the economic development of Shenzhen, Qianhai and Hong Kong can reach a new level. Thank you! Last revision date: 19 July 2012

Title: Speech at Hang Seng NFC Ceremony
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech Nov. 01, 2012 Speech at the launch ceremony of Hang Seng Bank's NFC Mobile Payment Service Pang Xingtang is a Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Dear guests and media friends, I am delighted to be here at the launch ceremony of Hang Seng Bank's NFC Mobile Payment Service today. The introduction of NFC mobile payment services will bring breakthrough development to Hong Kong's retail payments, further promote Hong Kong's mobile commerce (m-commerce) and consolidate Hong Kong's position as an international financial center and payment hub. Hong Kong has many advantages and favorable objective conditions in the implementation of NFC mobile payment. Hong Kong citizens are already familiar with and accustomed to using contactless payment methods such as Octopus and Visa payWave. In terms of hardware support, the penetration rate of mobile phone service users in Hong Kong is as high as 217%. Smartphone users account for as many as 35% of all mobile phone users in Hong Kong, and there are more than 10 smartphones with built-in NFC functions in Hong Kong, providing sufficient hardware support for the widespread use of NFC mobile payments. Together with Hang Seng Bank, we are aware that several banks and payment service providers have begun to study NFC-based e-payment services , and we believe that the public can witness the launch of more NFC mobile payment services in the coming year. Around the world, some countries such as the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Singapore, Japan and South Korea have successively studied or launched NFC mobile payment services, and conducted small-scale trials or tests. Some of the difficulties and challenges encountered by these countries in the process of business development, such as the slow establishment of recognition, the failure of payment services and telecommunications companies to achieve the most effective business cooperation or operating model, resulting in the fragmentation of market products and telecommunications networks, etc., provide useful reference for Hong Kong. The HKMA plays a role in promoting market infrastructure in the development of NFC mobile payments, and we are currently conducting a feasibility study with the objective of formulating a long-term development strategy suitable for Hong Kong based on the development experience and challenges faced by various regions, so as to promote the compatibility of market services and market freedom to promote NFC mobile payment services strike the right balance between services. The HKMA is now conducting further research on the establishment of a common platform for connectivity. The design of the platform will be based on four pillars. NFC mobile payment tools provided by multiple different service providers for customers can be devices per mobile phone; Second, customers using NFC mobile payment services are free to switch to telecommunications networks without affecting the downloaded payment services; Third, NFC mobile payment services need to have a high degree of security and reliability, and comply with relevant international standards; Fourth, the design of the platform needs to be sufficiently resilient and scalable to support future development. The common platform under study can be divided into two levels, one is to develop a set of basic security standards, technical requirements and operational guidelines for all market participants to ensure the security of services and compliance with relevant international standards. This set of uniform guidelines will be launched as soon as the feasibility study is completed at the end of 2012, enabling the market to integrate relevant standards into the design of its products and the operation process of its services while developing NFC mobile payment services, so as to achieve interoperability. The second level is to build a common platform of hardware, providing a shareable interface to connect different payment service providers, telecommunications network operators and other application providers, so that they can more easily promote NFC mobile payment services to the general public, and also benefit users from "one machine can carry more" services It is also possible to bring the convenience of different "service "turntable". Today, in addition to congratulating Hang Seng Bank on taking a valuable step towards the birth of the NFC mobile payment service in Hong Kong, we are also very pleased to see that Hang Seng Bank will adopt the principles of its NFC mobile payment business development in accordance with the interconnection standards and is ready to make relevant preparations and cooperation for the future of the common platform. We expect more banks and telecom operators to collaborate on new NFC mobile payment products in the market. The establishment of a common platform and the formulation of standards will provide an effective connection for these cross-industry cooperation, further enhance the public's recognition and usage habits of this new payment technology, and achieve mutual benefit and win-win results. Finally, the HKMA is committed to working with all sectors to establish a fair, open, robust and compatible development framework to create a better environment for the development of more diversified NFC mobile payment services and to continuously optimize the retail payment infrastructure in Hong Kong. Thank you. Last revision date: 01 November 2012

Title: Remarks on 25 April 2013
text: 19/09/22, 13:05 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Remarks by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority on 25 ... Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 25 Apr 2013 Remarks by Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority on 25 April 2013 Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Translation) Total renminbi deposits and certificates of deposit grew to RMB810 billion at the end of March, a rise of RMB30 billion compared with the previous month. Renminbi trade settlement transactions handled by banks in Hong Kong in the first three months of 2013 reached a record high of RMB830 billion, an increase of 45% over the same period last year. In view of the continuous and steady growth of the renminbi business in Hong Kong, we have decided to introduce new measures to deepen and enhance our renminbi clearing and business platform. First is the launch of the offshore renminbi Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate, or CNH HIBOR Fixing. Following detailed study and a one-year trial, the HKMA and the industry have considered the conditions now ripe for the launch of a formal offshore renminbi interest rate pricing mechanism in Hong Kong. It has been agreed that the Treasury Markets Association will launch the CNH HIBOR Fixing in June this year, covering tenors from overnight to 12 months. It will be the world's first offshore renminbi interbank interest rate fixing. The launch of the CNH HIBOR will promote the development of offshore renminbi loan market and interest rate-related financial products. It can also assist market participants in managing their interest rate risk. It will indeed become an important milestone in further enhancing the status of Hong Kong as an offshore RMB centre. Second, in view of the continuous deepening of the offshore renminbi market in Hong Kong, the HKMA has decided to loosen two of its special regulatory requirements on renminbi business. One is that the renminbi net open position limit will be removed. The other is that the 25% minimum liquidity ratio for renminbi will also be lifted. A circular will be issued later to set out the details. With the removal of the above restrictions, the regulatory requirements for authorized institutions in respect of their management of foreign exchange and liquidity risks associated with renminbi business will be in line with those applicable to other currencies. This will allow more room and flexibility for banks in Hong Kong to further develop their offshore renminbi business. / 1/2 19/09/22, 13:05 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Remarks by Norman T.L. Title: Forum on Mobile Payment  A New Trend for Consumption and Business
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 23 May 2013 Opening Speech at the "Mobile Payments - New Trends in Consumer Business" forum Pang Xingtang is a Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Dear guests, friends in the industry, Thanks to the invitation of the letter, I have the opportunity to share my views on the development of mobile payments and introduce the main work of the HKMA in promoting mobile payment services. The development of science and technology has a profound impact on our living habits. The development of electronic payment from contactless payment, evolution to online transactions, and then evolution to mobile payment, not only the progress of payment technology, but more importantly, the payment technology is more closely integrated with life, bringing great convenience to the public, and creating new business opportunities for more merchants and service providers. Convenience brought by NFC service NFC mobile payment technology has several unique elements that propel retail payment services into a revolutionary new era. First, the multiple functions of NFC telephones combined with the ability of Internet downloads allow users to download various types of payment services (such as credit cards, prepaid cards) to mobile phones, and can also use mobile phones to access the Internet for online transactions, so as to give full play to the payment capabilities of mobile phones. Second, the two-way communication function of NFC telephone breaks through the limitations of one-way contactless payment technology, allowing users to process payments between individuals and merchants in addition to processing payments between individuals and merchants, but also through the "mobile wallet" to process transfers between individuals and individuals, so that payments are more integrated into life. Third, the lifestyle habits of the public to carry mobile phones with them, coupled with the function of receiving messages on NFC mobile phones, enable merchants and service providers to transfer payment-related marketing information and offers to consumers. Through smart phones, consumers can go online to find merchants, receive promotional information, download offers, go to the store to buy, and finally use mobile phone payment, and even point exchange, the entire consumption process, can be completed with a mobile phone. NFC technology can turn your mobile phone into a wallet, put credit cards, tickets, coupons, membership cards, etc. into your mobile phone, and then use it for identity confirmation, payment hitchhiking, shopping, and even open the door. A mobile phone is not only used for communication, but also can be used to pay for travel, shopping, payment and other needs, bringing a convenient and fast life. Business opportunities brought by NFC services These multifaceted features also create new business opportunities for merchants and service providers. Some industries, such as software application developers, advertising agencies, retailers, membership operators, ticketing service providers, etc., can all benefit. From international experience, smartphones have become one of the fastest growing advertising channels. Advertising companies can use the positioning system of mobile phones to issue advertisements and coupons of some nearby merchants according to the user's location for targeted publicity. Consumption card operators also encourage members to use the "Mobile Wallet" for payment purposes. Every time you make a purchase, members only need to shoot their mobile phones on the card reader, and they can update their points at the same time to facilitate consumption. I am sure that the participating business organizations will share with you more specific and detailed the new business opportunities brought about by mobile payments. The precursor to the development of mobile payments in Hong Kong In Hong Kong, the development of NFC mobile payment services is in its infancy. We believe the outlook is quite optimistic. Hong Kong citizens, who have always been at the forefront of the trend, often adapt to new technologies quickly, providing extremely favorable conditions for the development of this new technology. We can refer to the following data: b7 In Hong Kong, non-cash retail consumption expenditure, accounting for the proportion of total private consumption expenditure, increased significantly from 45% in 2002 to more than 70% in 2012. 95 In non-cash transactions, more than g5% of the dial is done contactlessly. 95 The circulation of contactless stored value cards has exceeded 12 million units, with an average of nearly 3 per citizen. 95 Hong Kong's mobile phone service subscriber penetration rate has exceeded 220%, making it one of the highest regions in the world. We would love to see that payment service operators are now actively preparing to launch mobile payment services. At the end of 2012, a major bank in Hong Kong took the lead in launching NFC mobile payment services. We understand that at least two other banks intend to launch similar services by the end of this year. At the application level, large merchants such as convenience stores, chain stores and supermarkets have also begun to update their devices to prepare for NFC mobile payments. The HKMA's policy priorities and directions However, these favorable conditions do not guarantee that Hong Kong can produce an efficient and reliable mobile payment platform. In fact, the operation of mobile payment involves a large number of stakeholders, including payment service providers, telecom providers, merchants, consumers, etc., who have different requirements and interests. To make the development process smoother, the HKMA mainly promotes the development of mobile payment services in the following three aspects. The first is to promote the industry to reach a consensus on the direction of future development. After months of consultancy research and consultation, we have reached four consensus with the industry on the development goals of mobile payments in Hong Kong: 1. Multiple "cards" per machine: The service platform should allow payment services from different banks and payment service operators to download to the same mobile phone with built-in NFC function Second, the turntable is easy: even if the mobile network is converted, the application for payment services can continue to be used Third, the exchange is convenient: even if the NFC mobile phone is replaced, the application for payment services can continue to be used Fourth, strict security: in line with international security standards The second task of the HKMA is to jointly develop a set of standard guidelines with the industry that are in line with the above development objectives. The success of NFC mobile payment services depends on whether the services are widely accepted by consumers. Strict security, reliable and convenient service are the most basic requirements of consumers. To achieve these goals, a set of standards and guidelines shared by the industry is indispensable to the development of an interconnected platform, and also helps to achieve that every aspect of NFC technology can be closely linked to bring the best service to consumers. The consultants commissioned by the HKMA have drafted operational standards relating to mobile payments in accordance with international standards and have assisted the industry in forming a working group within the Hong Kong Association of Banks to discuss the details of the standards. The Sub-group held its first meeting in April this year with the aim of publishing guidelines and standards in the second half of this year to set out best practices for relevant technical standards, security measures for mobile payment services and operational matters. At the same time, the HKMA also encourages payment service providers to establish a common platform to provide efficient connectivity services to members and save development costs. As retail payment products and services, including mobile payments, continue to innovate and become increasingly popular, the HKMA's third priority is to optimize the legal framework and regulatory regime for retail payment services. Extend the scope of regulation from the current multi-purpose stored value cards to non-device-based stored value products and important non-stored value retail payment systems. The HKMA and the Financial Services Bureau have just announced their proposed amendments to the Clearing and Settlement Systems Ordinance to achieve the above objectives. The main elements of the proposal include: 95 Establish a licensing system for stored value payment products, requiring all institutions planning to issue stored value payment products in Hong Kong to obtain a license from the HKMA first ; 95 Legislation to protect the amount of stored value injected by users into the stored value payment system; 95 Establish a retail payment designation system to empower the HKMA to designate important non-stored value retail payment systems and accept their supervision; and 95 Empower the HKMA with relevant regulatory and enforcement powers. The proposal to optimize the regulation of retail payment services has been consulted for three months, and I encourage institutions interested in operating mobile payment services to study the specific content of the proposal and provide comments. conclusion For NFC mobile payment services to develop successfully in Hong Kong, they need to have the right development goals, meet international level operating standards, and have an effective legal framework and regulatory system in order to build consumer confidence and provide operators with the ideal environment to develop sustainable mobile payment services. The HKMA looks forward to working closely with the industry to establish a comprehensive, interconnected, secure and efficient mobile payment network for Hong Kong. Thank you.
