Title: Launching Ceremony for the Electronic Bill Presentment and Payment Service
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech Dec. 11, 2013 Launch Ceremony of e-Billing and Billing Services Pang Xingtang is a Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Dear guests and industry friends, Welcome to the launch ceremony of the e-Billing and Bill Payment Service held today. Every household has to process a large number of bills every month, and the resources that society as a whole spends on processing the bills, including paper, printing and mailing, are huge overall . Members of the public can now pay for purchases and services through online banking services. The e-Bill and Bill Payment Service introduced today features the simultaneous electronicization of bill collection and management functions, and the integration with online banking services, bringing billing processing to a new era of multi-functional and comprehensive "paperless". In the following, I will introduce the benefits of this new service to the public, business and society; the HKMA and the banking community to promote the progress made in this service; and future development priorities. (-) Benefits of e-billing and bill payment services for the public What are the new features and functions of e-billing and bill payment services for the public, especially compared to the existing online banking services ? The biggest advantage of e-billing and billing services is that it makes managing bills easier and more convenient. Through this new service, members of the public can simply log on to their online banking accounts to collect, view and manage e-bills issued by merchants in one stop, and make payments directly through the same platform, the process is fully electronic. 95 Users no longer need to collect bills from different channels such as mail, email or SMS, as new bills are transmitted to their online banking account in the form of electronic files, making it easier for users to manage different electronic bills and no longer need to worry about missing bills because they forgot to check their mailbox. 95 Users no longer need to make room for stacks of bills, because online banking will help you keep your bills and payments on file, which is clean and environmentally friendly. Through the new e-billing and bill payment services, banks will also provide value-added services to customers, such as: 95 Remind you to pay by email or mobile phone before your bill is due, greatly reducing the number of late payments 95 Allow bank customers to set up automatic payment arrangements for different bills, and change the payment date and silver code at any time in online banking, making bill payment more flexible 95 By completing the simple registration process, members of the public can collect bills from third parties (e.g. elderly people in the family, parents) and pay all expenses on their behalf 95 Banks can extend their services to mobile banking services. In the future, we can simply click on our mobile phone and log in to our mobile bank account to check our bills and payments. (ii) Economic and social benefits as a whole In addition, this new service will bring benefits to the economy and society as a whole. Promote business development 95 The one-stop payment and receipt platform will save the cost of printing and mailing bills for participating merchants and improve the operational efficiency of bill reconciliation and payment . At the business level, the new services can improve the efficiency of bill delivery and payment between businesses (B-2-B), thereby improving the convergence between e-commerce and retail payment services and reducing operating costs. 95 Banks can also provide various value-added services according to the business needs of merchants, such as checking payment records, regularly sorting out collection reports, and e.g. reminders of late payment issued by @ customers. These new businesses will further enhance merchants' operational efficiency and competitive advantage. Protect the environment 95 In addition, the use of paperless billing will make an important contribution to the protection of the environment. Assuming that each household receives ten bills per month , they can reduce the number of sheets of paper produced each year by simply converting half of the bills into electronic bills. 95 This means that we have preserved 60,000 trees and can also reduce the carbon dioxide emitted into the air by 4,500 metric tons, the volume of which is equivalent to a thousand standard swimming pools. (3) The progress made by the service and the focus of future development Hong Kong's major financial services such as interbank payments, foreign exchange and securities trading need to rely on a comprehensive set of financial infrastructure support, and then the industry designs and promotes diversified services to meet the needs of different customers. Like these financial services, the birth of electronic billing and payment services needs to go through the following three steps: (1) the development of financial infrastructure; (2) the participation and development tasks of the industry; and (3) Target users to promote and promote. The first stage: _ In the past year during the development phase of e-billing and bill payment services, the HKMA commissioned Hong Kong Interbank Clearing and Clearing Limited to develop this cross-bank central processing platform for e-bill receipt and payment, conduct system and network testing, formulate service agreements and codes of use, complete independent assessment reports, and ensure that the design and operation of the system meets strict security requirements. The entire development phase of the central processing platform has been successfully completed. The second stage: the support of the industry is also quite enthusiastic, with a total of 23 banks having confirmed their participation in the service, and their coverage of online banking accounts is as high as 99%. Among them, 18 banks will launch services to customers from today. Phase III: After the launch of the new service, the Bank will fully promote e-bill and bill payment services to merchants to assist them in preparing and implementing the various steps and system improvement work in which they participate. At present, some merchants have joined the platform and other merchants will join the platform at a later date. In addition, a series of publicity and promotional activities will also be launched to ensure that the general public understands the details and convenience of the service. The entire third phase of the campaign will be officially launched from today. Our focus in the coming year will be on the promotion of merchants and the general public. In terms of merchant promotion, I am pleased to announce that the Government's major billing departments, such as the Water Supplies Department and the Rating and Valuation Department, have been actively engaged in preparatory work to launch the relevant services by the end of next year. In addition, other merchants, including local utilities, insurance companies, property management companies, educational institutions and charities, have also begun to study the relevant services, and some have begun to prepare service details or integrate internal billing systems. I expect that the size, types and number of participating merchants will continue to increase with the launch of the service, further expanding the coverage of e-billing and bill payment services. In terms of public promotion, the public can register for e-billing and bill payment services through the online accounts of participating banks from today. To enable the public to better understand the benefits of the service, the HKMA and the Association of Banks have prepared an electronic leaflet outlining the registration process, service content and usage methods of the service, which will be published on the webpages of the HKMA, the Association of Banks and the participating banks. We will also carry out a series of promotional and publicity activities in the coming days to benefit the general public with the latest developments. (4) Conclusion The birth of e-billing and bill payment services will more closely integrate payment technology and online banking services with daily life, bringing greater convenience and financial flexibility to the public, and bringing greater cost-effectiveness and operational efficiency to merchants. In the process of preparing banks to launch e-bill and bill payment services, many merchants have actively participated in the process of discussing cooperation details with banks . After the launch of the service, I look forward to the bank's accelerated implementation and use it to appeal to merchants and the public to actively participate in and use this service for the benefit of the community as a whole." The HKMA will continue to work with the banking community to enhance the service level of banking services, continuously enhance the development of retail payment infrastructure and the efficiency of its systems, and strive to promote and improve the development of retail payment services. Thanks a lot. Last revision date: 11 December 2013

Title: QC Spirit: Past, Present and Future
text: 19/09/22, 13:04 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - QC Spirit: Past, Present and Future Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 13 Dec 2013 QC Spirit: Past, Present and Future Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Speech at the Queen's College Annual Speech Day) Principal Li Sui-wah, Mr. Lai, Mr. Kan, Mr. Yu, Teachers, Parents, Distinguished Guests and my fellow QC Boys, 1. First time I set foot in this hall was 1966, almost half a century ago. Last time was 1972, when I left after Lower Six to pursue my undergraduate study at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. 2. Like you sitting in front of me, I can recall that I attended a couple of Speech Day gatherings at which some prominent Old Boys or reputable members of the community came to deliver talks, just like what I am doing now. But no matter how hard I try, I simply cannot remember what were said in these speeches, not because my memories are fading but because the speeches were normally too boring for a youth of my age. These speeches seemed to be repeating the same messages, which are high sounding but abstract moral principles, such as need to work hard and excel, never give up, and be honest and kind to other people and contribute to the society etc. 3. So if you don't remember anything that I say this afternoon, don't worry and I'll understand. But I'll try to avoid talking too much about high sounding moral principles. 4.1 propose to talk about "What has changed" vs "What has not changed". 5. What has changed since my time at the Queen's College? There must be quite a long list. Let me cite a few examples of what it was like 40 to 50 years ago and you can judge for yourselves what has changed. 6. In 1966 when I started my first year at Queen's, it wasn't an easy time to attend school. Why? There was an extended period of time in 1966-67 in which bombs (nicknamed locally made Pineapples) were everywhere and streets became highly dangerous for obvious reasons. When a bomb was found, the street would be blocked off by the Police so that the explosive disposal experts could deal with the bomb. So many students had to take a long detour in order to walk to school (bus and tram services of course were stopped at the time). In a way we were risking our lives by coming to school everyday. But nobody seemed to be too bothered and very few students and, for that matter, teachers missed classes as a result. 7. In addition to bombs and riots on the streets, there was a time in the 1960s when Hong Kong suffered water shortage. This was the era before we built the pipes to pump almost / 1/4 19/09/22, 13:04 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - QC Spirit: Past, Present and Future unlimited supply of fresh water from the East River. Many students had to run back home to help store up water when the Government turned on the tap for only four hours in every four days. If you didn't store up enough water during this 4-hour period, you were doomed in the next four days. 8. In my first three years at Queen's, I had to come into the school through the side and back entrances only. The only time I could come in through the Main Entrance was when I was late for school in the morning. At the Main Entrance a group of Prefects were eagerly waiting for the late arrivals and marked down their names for the usual punishment. I did not like this arrangement at all as it was discriminating against the juniors, but interestingly enough I had begun to like it from Form Four onwards when I was allowed to use the Main Entrance all the time. 9. In my time at Queen's, my parents gave me one dollar and thirty cents every morning. The 30 cents was to buy snacks at the morning break, 20 cents for a Vitasoy and 10 cents for a bun. A plate of rice for lunch was one dollar. To save money to buy anything else, including sharing the cost of a leather football amongst classmates, we had to skip snacks and lunch once in a while. 10.1 don't know if you still have annual school excursions and where you would go nowadays. In my time, my first school excursion, at my Form One year, was somewhat disappointing as the destination, you won't believe it, was next door at the Victoria Park! So you can imagine how "excited" I felt a few years later, the excursion took us to the Victoria Peak! I gather from my friends that nowadays some secondary schools in Hong Kong organised trips for students to far away places, such as Shanghai, Beijing, Japan and even Europe and the USA. I hope that Queen's does a better job today than excursions to Victoria Park and the Peak. 11. Quite apart from school excursions, I am sure things are very different now compared to my days at Queen's. At least you don't have to risk your lives coming to school or get water supply only four hours in every four days. These difficult if not unfortunate times have long gone and we all hope that they will never come back again. While Hong Kong has become much more prosperous in the last three decades, things are becoming much more expensive and I doubt if you can survive with one dollar and thirty cents a day as we did. 12. Despite the considerable changes that have occurred since I left Queen's, there is one thing that has not changed. That is the enormous pride I take in telling people which high school I came from. Of course, I also went to the Chinese University of Hong Kong and attended graduate programmes in Oxford and Harvard and am occupying a senior position in the Government. However, I simply cannot hide my sense of pride when it comes to my Alma Mater. One may ask: is it not the common feeling most people harbour about their high schools at which they spent their youthful years? I would say this: our feeling towards Queen's is not the same because Queen's is very, very special and different. 13. Queen's is special not only because of its long history, which dated back to 1862, which was only 20 years after Hong Kong was ceded to Britain after the Opium War. Queen's is special not only because it was the first public school in Hong Kong, but because alumni of Queen's had become important part of the history of Hong Kong and China throughout the last 150 years. I need not remind you that amongst the first students of Queen's College, / 2/4 19/09/22, 13:04 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - QC Spirit: Past, Present and Future which was known as the Central School then, was Dr Sun Yat-sen, the founding father of Modern China. 14. When I say "Modern China", China was not "modern" at all. In 1911, just over 100 years ago, Dr Sun overthrew the weak, decadent and corrupt Imperial Qing Dynasty, but China was then ripped apart by seemingly endless civil wars between the warlords, which were followed by invasion by the Japanese. Hong Kong, and Queen's College, had had its dark days during the three years and eight months of occupation by the Japanese during the World War II. Even as recent as 1979, when Deng Xiaoping launched the reform and opening programme, China was very poor with its population earning on average less than US1 a day. Now China has emerged as the second largest economy in the world, overtaking Japan a few years ago. At the same time, Hong Kong has transformed itself from a refugee centre in the 1950s into a vibrant international financial centre as we know today. Looking back, alumni of Queen's College feature prominently in each and every crucial stage of Hong Kong's history. There is no need for me to mention the key personalities in Hong Kong who were QC Old Boys as they can be easily found on the internet. Even today, Queen's continues to shine with outstanding colours, as we did in the past. 15. In my class, the Year of 1966-73,1 have 23 classmates who have become medical doctors. So when I fall ill my problem is not whether I can find a doctor to help me but who among my classmates to turn to. I believe the same is still true today. Apart from supplying the universities in Hong Kong with the best of students for the medical schools and other faculties, Queens is the source of talents for the community as a whole. There are numerous QC Boys who have become government officials at the top level, Executive Council Members and Legislative Councillors, who together help shape and move Hong Kong into a place as we know it today. In the academic field, two out of the eight universities in Hong Kong are currently headed by QC Boys. There are many, many QC Boys who have excelled in other fields, such as commerce, finance, art, professional and community services. 16. You may ask: these are truly interesting success stories, but what have they got to do with someone like me who have no way of knowing what fortunes or misfortunes would lie ahead? I have no secret recipe for success. In general, I would say follow your heart and you wont be far wrong. That said, there is no guarantee that all of you will become as successful as the prominent alumni before you. However, you should never forget that there is one thing in common between you and them. All QC Boys share the same identity, sense of pride and responsibility for being the cream of the cream in our society for the past 160 years. This proud tradition has become the heritage that is passed down from one generation to the next. It is this tradition or heritage that binds QC Boys together regardless of age and differentiates us from all other schools in Hong Kong. It is this sense of pride that propels QC Boys to excel in all fronts. However, it is also this sense of pride that helps lift QC Boys fighting spirit when we are feeling down and low. 17. QC Boys have all learnt the truth, enshrined in our School Motto, that success can only come from hard work as QC Boys, mostly coming from humble family background, know full well there is no shortcut or easy way out. To be successful we will be judged on the basis of whether we have lived full and meaningful lives, not just in material sense but also in spiritual sense. You don't have to be the richest or most powerful man in town to have a truly meaningful and colourful life. You are not measured according to what you have but / 3/4 19/09/22, 13:04 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - QC Spirit: Past, Present and Future what you are. In this context, the judges who will make the judgements would be our families, our friends, colleagues and society as a whole. 18. Fellow QC Boys, it's a great privilege to me to be given the opportunity here to speak. As with any great tradition, the old generation must pass on its accomplishments and legacy, no matter how great they may be, to the younger generation. It is not possible for the old people to hold anything back because no one can defy the natural law governing life and death. And you, as the youngest generation of Queen's, must do your utmost to hold tight and treasure the baton that has been handed down to you. It will be you who can preserve the proud QC tradition and pass it on to the next generation when you have reached my age. Some of you may feel worried about whether and how you can accomplish this? Don't worry, the QC spirit already runs in your blood by the time you graduate and I can assure you that such spirit will stay with you for your entire life. 19. Thank you for having me and for your kind attention. Last revision date : 13 December 2013 / 4/4

Title: Press Statement by Eddie Yue, Acting Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority
text: Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Press Statement by Eddie Yue, Acting Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ... 19/09/22, 13:03 Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 19 Dec 2013 Press Statement by Eddie Yue, Acting Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority on 19 December 2013 Eddie Yue, Acting Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority The US Federal Open Markets Committee decided yesterday to reduce the amount of debt securities purchase each month from USD85 billion to USD75 billion starting from January 2014. The FOMC decision reflects that the US economic recovery is on a sustainable path and it marks the beginning of the normalization of the US monetary conditions. But, there remains uncertainties on the pace of further reduction. The Fed will take into account the incoming data on labour market and inflation in the US in determining the pace of further reduction, when to cease asset purchases and when to raise the Federal Funds Target Rate. The normalisation of the US monetary conditions will inevitably heighten market volatility. Financial markets will react to changes in incoming US economic data and adjust their expectations of the tapering timetable. In addition, the Fed's quantitative easing policy over the past few years has led to large capital inflows to emerging markets. As the US economy gradually recovers, fund flows may reverse, exerting downward pressure on asset prices in emerging markets. Hong Kong, as an international financial centre, is used to handling fund flows in both directions. The currency board arrangements will effectively anchor stability of the Hong Kong dollar. To maintain banking stability, the HKMA has already reminded banks to step up the management of liquidity and interest-rate risks to cater for possible fund outflows. Likewise, companies and individuals should carefully manage the interest-rate risk and avoid taking on excessive leverage. Last revision date : 19 December 2013 / 1/1

Title: Forum on Electronic Payments - How to Enhance Economic Growth and Efficiency?
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 14 Mar 2014 The Letter Forum "Electronic Payments - How to Improve Economic Growth and Efficiency" Pang Xingtang is a Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Dear guests, friends in the industry, It is a pleasure to participate again in the Electronic Payments Forum of The Letter. 2. Today's topic is to explore the contribution of electronic payments to economic growth and efficiency. I think the relationship between "electronic payment", "economic growth" and "quality of life" is inseparable, because electronic payment is for transactions, and transactions are for life . Electronic payments help drive the economy 3. Recent international experience shows that the widespread application of electronic payment can play a huge role in promoting the economic development of developing and developed countries. 4. In terms of developing countries, the World Bank's "Global Financial Development Report" released earlier this year pointed out that the introduction of innovative services such as mobile spending and financial management has made financial services more convenient and popular in developing countries, which has facilitated financial integration, promoted national savings, corporate lending, and helped promote the economic development of many developing countries. And the Kenyan experience in Africa is the best example. The Case of the Developing World: The Kenyan Story 5. The Kenyan government's success story of driving economic development through e-payment services has become a classic case for payment industry and economic development experts. 6. When M-Pesa, Kenya's main mobile payment system, was launched in 2007 for families participating in the "Microfinance" loan project, allowing them to repay their loans through mobile payment services. The system is popular because it provides convenient and fast banking services for remote villagers. Currently, as many as 17 million Kenyans use mobile phones for daily payments, accounting for two-thirds of the adult population. 7. When financial management becomes convenient, the people have more time to focus on production. Studies have shown that the advent of mobile payment systems has increased the household income of Kenyan farmers by 5-30%. The widespread use of mobile payment has also spawned many innovative technology companies that use the m-Pesa platform to provide value-added services around them. The experience of developed countries 8. Electronic payment services are equally important to developed countries in driving economic development. 9. A report published by ratings agency Moody's after conducting research in 56 countries points out that in 2008-12, as more consumers paid electronically with payment cards, the global economy received about a trillion dollars of additional growth, equivalent to making 190 million 10,000 jobs. 10. For developed countries, the contribution of electronic payment services to promoting economic development mainly comes from three aspects: (1) improving the efficiency of economic activities, (2) saving operating costs, and (3) promoting industrial transformation and innovation. Increase efficiency 11. In terms of improving efficiency, electronic payment makes the entire process of procurement and payment no longer limited by time and geography. I am now going to the theater to see a movie, and I am used to buying tickets on my mobile phone first. I can't remember the last time I went to the theater ticket office to buy tickets . 12. Electronic payment services are often linked to the services of relevant financial institutions, providing customers with more opportunities to use other electronic financial services. In fact, in recent years, in addition to the already mature online banking services, financial institutions have also continuously launched a variety of innovative services to allow customers to pay, manage money and invest online or mobile phones, making life easier and more convenient. 13. Enterprises, especially small and medium-sized enterprises that focus on e-commerce services, can reduce the credit risks that may occur in transaction payment by using a sound and efficient electronic payment system, ensure that funds arrive on schedule, and reduce the pressure of capital turnover. And, if combined with the company's management information system (MIS), it can comprehensively improve the efficiency of processing bills, invoices, payments, and control inventory and cash flow. Cost savings 14. In addition to factors that improve efficiency, there are also considerations for cost control. With the electronic, automated, and "paperless" payment process, society can reduce the use of paper, and the public can save a lot of time, manpower and material resources to process processes such as payment and accounting logarithms, and resources can be used for other more productive economic activities. 15. The RNP study points out 2 that if retail payments use payment cards instead of cash, the cost of the payment process will be reduced by 6 per cent. The Bank of Brazil's research also pointed out that if the payment process is completely "paperless", the cost savings can be as high as one percent of the total economy. 3 Innovation in the industry 16. As for industrial innovation, as the Internet expands from an information platform to a business and trading platform, many enterprises, including small and medium-sized enterprises, have learned to use the advantages of the Internet to expand business opportunities in the mode of "online stores". 17. In response to the general trend, e-commerce service providers have cooperated with different e-payment service providers. PayPal collaboration with eBay is a well-known example of this. 18. Soon after PayPal came out, eBay auctioneers experienced that PayPal collection and payment was quite convenient. As a result, the number of PayPal users rose sharply from 100,000 to more than 3 million in 2000, and eBay acquired in 2002 PayPal, the cooperation platform will be fully integrated. To date, PayPal has 143 million users worldwide. In the fourth quarter of last year, for example, 9 million transactions were processed every day. 19. Online shopping in the mainland, that is, the online shopping boom, is also developing at a high speed, and there is a great potential to catch up later. In fact, Alibaba's online transaction volume surpassed eBay and Amazon in 2012. Taking the "Online Shopping Festival" on November 11 last year, for example, the total transaction volume of all online shopping websites on that day was reported to exceed 40 billion yuan, more than half of the country's total retail consumption in a single day. Alibaba's Alipay reportedly completed a record high of about 190 million transactions on the day of the "Online Shopping Festival". Among them, mobile payments exceeded 45 million cases, which is five times that of the same period in 2012. 20. As the Mainland and the Asia-Pacific region emerge as huge e-commerce markets, e-commerce will become even more important to Hong Kong's economic development. Financial institutions and enterprises need to upgrade their industries and further e-commerce to capture the business opportunities brought about by global e-commerce and mobile payments. 21. However, due to the huge potential of electronic payment services, the large number of users, the large transaction volume and amount, and the continuous innovation of technology, their widespread use also brings some risks, including the stability of the payment system, the protection of user funds and the prevention of being used for money laundering. These risks need to be handled with care and cannot be taken lightly. The HKMA's work to develop electronic payment infrastructure A three-pronged strategy 22. To ensure that electronic and mobile payment services can develop on a robust and fair competition platform, the HKMA adopted a comprehensive and three-pronged development strategy almost two years ago. 23. The first two points are service and infrastructure strategies, namely (i) further e-digitization of payment services and (ii) promotion of mobile payment technology. The third point is the strategy of risk management and public protection, that is, to ensure the safety and stability of electronic stored value payment instruments and retail payment systems by improving the legal framework and strengthening regulatory arrangements, so as to build public confidence in payment products and services and promote the long-term development of the industry. 24. Over the past year, thanks to the active cooperation and support of the banking community, Hong Kong's e-payment services have made encouraging progress in all three areas . NFC mobile payment service 25. First, in terms of promoting NFC mobile payment services, the HKMA commissioned a consultancy firm at the end of 2012 to conduct research to establish a market-led development model for NFC mobile payment. 26. We have also set four long-term development goals of "one machine with multiple cards, easy turnaround, convenient machine change and strict security", so that while NFC mobile payment technology is developing steadily in Hong Kong, the public can more easily and safely enjoy this new payment service . 27. To achieve these objectives, the HKMA and the Working Group of the Association of Banks actively consulted last year and assisted the Association in launching the NFC Mobile Payments Code of Practice in November last year to establish common security standards, technologies and operational process standards and guidelines. 28. We believe that through this Code of Practice, the local market can build interconnected and secure and effective NFC mobile payment infrastructure and services, enabling the market to develop more effectively and sustainably. "E-Bill and Bill Payment Service" 29. In addition, the e-Billing and Billing Service Platform, jointly developed by the HKMA in collaboration with the industry, was also launched in December last year . The processing of bills has begun to enter a new era of comprehensive paperlessness. 30. The platform combines e-bill issuance and payment functions, allowing members of the public to simply log on to their online banking accounts to collect, view and manage different e-bills and make payments online. "e-Billing and Bill Payment Service" is applicable to electronic payments in HKD, RENBI and USD. Customers can connect with merchants in the Mainland and other regions through the same platform to collect and pay cross-border e-bills. 31. 23 banks have confirmed their participation in the new service, covering more than 99% of online banking accounts. The services in the first phase were provided by 18 banks, while some of the leading merchants have joined the platform. Different types of merchants are also preparing to participate in phases. Two of the major government departments, namely the Water Supplies Department and the Rating and Valuation Department, are also planning to launch the services around the end of this year. The HKMA and the industry will organise a series of publicity activities to raise public awareness of e-billing and bill payment services and encourage them to use the relevant services. "E-Cheque" 32. The HKMA is also actively working with the banking community to establish an e-cheque operating platform and plans to launch the "e-Cheque" service in the second half of 2015. At that time, whether we want to "issue" cheques or "deposit" cheques, we can complete them through online banking and mobile services. 33. The benefits of e-Cheque are not only convenience. The interests of e-Cheque invoices and collectors will be protected by the Bills of Exchange Ordinance like traditional cheques. Since e-Cheques will be signed with e-Certificates, the process of issuing cheques will become safer and faster. 34. In addition, "e-Cheque" can be used to pay in Hong Kong dollars, US dollars or renminbi, helping to facilitate cross-border transactions. Overseas residents and merchants who wish to pay for local payments by e-Cheque can use the Services by simply opening an account with a bank in Hong Kong. Cross-border receipt will also become more convenient and secure, as ticket collectors no longer need to worry about delays in receiving payments due to postal errors. 35. For enterprises, "e-Cheque" can automate the process of issuance, signature and receipt of cheques, eliminating the cumbersome steps of the current situation, improving operational efficiency and saving the cost of processing cheques. Banks can also save on the cost of printing and mailing cheque books and handling cheque settlement. 36. As a result, e-cheques not only provide society with safer and more efficient means of payment, but also reduce the cost of economic activity. I believe this new tool will help Hong Kong enterprises, especially SMEs, to expand their e-commerce business, enhance their competitiveness and create more business opportunities for merchants. Legal framework 37. Finally, as I just said, in view of the continuous innovation and popularity of retail payment products and services, the risks involved, including systemic risks and user protection, cannot be ignored. 38. At present, multi-purpose stored value products, in addition to multi-purpose stored value cards, also include other online stored value payment products. They are not based on hardware devices, but provide stored value services through mobile phone network accounts, computer network accounts, etc. We believe there is a need to expand the scope of the current regulatory regime from multi-purpose stored value cards to products that are not hardware-based and important non-stored value retail payment systems. 39. In view of this, the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau and the HKMA proposed to the public last year to establish a licensing and regulatory mechanism for stored value payment products and retail disbursement systems. The main policy objectives are threefold: - To ensure the safe and stable operation of stored value payment products and retail payment systems in Hong Kong; 2. Ensure that the stored value amount stored in the stored value payment products is sufficiently guaranteed and will not be misappropriated; And 3. To promote the innovative development of retail payment products and services in Hong Kong through the formulation of clear legislation and a favourable business environment . 40. We suggest that the new regulatory regime empower the HKMA to fulfil the licence, designation, supervision and enforcement of stored value payment products and retail payment systems , improve the protection of stored value amounts, and enhance the safety and soundness of retail payment products and systems. 41. We completed the public consultation last August. The results of the consultation show that the public generally supports the regulation of stored value payment products and retail payment systems, and believes that the new regulatory regime can promote innovation and development of Hong Kong's payment industry. 42. The HKMA is very grateful to all sectors of the community for their valuable input to this proposal mechanism to improve the arrangement of the proposals. As the Secretary for Finance mentioned in his recently published Budget, we will strive to introduce the relevant ordinance to the Legislative Council in the next legislative year 43. Colleagues from the HKMA are also carrying out internal preparatory work to draft guidelines for the industry on various licensing and regulatory work so that the industry can comply with the new regulatory mechanism. We will consult the industry on the drafting guidelines later. 44. Finally, I would like to emphasize that secure and efficient electronic payment technology can help improve transaction efficiency, open up business opportunities, save precious resources of society, and promote sustainable economic growth as a whole. 45. The HKMA will continue to shoulder its mission of developing and regulating payment systems and work closely with the banking community to promote the launch of more new electronic payment services in the market , so as to enhance the competitiveness of enterprises and enable the public to enjoy more convenient and secure payment services. Thank you. 1 Moody's Analytics (Feb 2013): 'The Impact of Electronic Payments on Economic Growth*. 2 Speech by Dr. Lex Hoogduin 'Payment innovation in a European landscape* (Dutch National Bank, DNB), at the DNB-ECB conference: 'Retail payments: integration and innovation*, May, 2009. 3 From a study conducted by the Central Bank of Brazil. Title: Safe and effective financial infrastructure to serve the public
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 12 June 2014 Safe and efficient financial infrastructure serves the public Lee Kin Ying is the Assistant Chief Executive Officer of the Financial Infrastructure Department of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Speech at the launching ceremony of the "MPF Transfer Electronic Payment" system) Ms. Luo Shengmei, distinguished guests, friends in the industry: 1. Welcome to today's ceremony to witness the launch of the MPF transfer electronic payment system jointly developed by the MPF and the HKMA. The new system will further enhance the efficiency of the industry in handling MPF transfers, allowing MPF Scheme members to more effectively manage their MPF investments. Like everyone else, I am one of the beneficiaries. The smooth development and implementation of the system is not only through the full cooperation between the MPF and the HKMA, but also the strong support of the industry, including MPF trustees and banks. Here, on behalf of the HKMA, I would like to thank the relevant personnel and units involved in the construction of the system. Safe and efficient financial infrastructure is closely related to people's lives 2. The goal of the electronic development of payment is to improve efficiency and bring convenience to the public. The HKMA plays the role of supporter and builder in the process. In response to the needs of the industry and the market, we actively promote, develop and implement various solutions. We believe this is also the society's expectation of the HKMA in addition to its regulatory functions. The collaboration between the HKMA and the MPF is another successful example of this concept 3. The policy objective of MPF Employee Choice Arrangement is to bring greater autonomy to employees and enable them to more actively manage their MPF investments. To this end, the MPF has developed and launched an "Electronic Automated Service System" (ePass) to assist in handling MPF transfers. This central electronic platform improves the efficiency of transfer applications between trustees. 4. The HKMA has actively cooperated from the level of financial infrastructure to develop the electronic payment system for MPF transfer jointly launched today, which further shortens the entire process of MPF transfer to about 2-3 weeks and can be completely completed, and the "investment gap" period can also be shortened. How does MPF Transfer Electronic Payment benefit the public and trustees? 5. Specifically, the new system is to use the existing Hong Kong dollar instant payment system to process payment instructions uploaded electronically by MPF trustees to the HKMA, replacing the cheque clearing process that trustees have been using; Since it is an electronic transfer, the transfer records can be easily checked by the trustee at any time to ensure that they are correct. 6. For trustees, the new system electronizes the transfer of funds between trustees, eliminating the need for trustees to carry out a large number of manual operations such as issuance, verification, mailing, cashing and recording verification of checks, and greatly shortening the process of fund transfer from the previous one-to-two period to two working days. 7. The increase in efficiency will also help trustees to reduce human error in their operations, allocate resources more efficiently and improve their competitiveness. For the general public, the shortening of the processing process reduces the risks that may be borne during the "investment gap" period and improves the efficiency of the management of MPF assets by the market. The new system was first launched on May 19 this year and has been running very smoothly ever since. Looking to the future 8. Looking ahead, the further digitization of financial infrastructure and financial products is the trend of the times. The HKMA will continue to promote the development of new e-payment services and work closely with the MPF in the context of payments to facilitate the transfer of funds for pension management that is of concern to the general public . Thank you. Last revision date: 12 June 2014

Title: Coin Collection Programme Launching Ceremony
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 19 Sep 2014 Coin Collection Program Launch Ceremony Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Dear guests, teachers, classmates and neighbors, today we opened two "cash registers" converted from 10-ton trucks to meet you at Ngau Tau Kok Shang Estate, I believe that Hong Kong will be the first in the world to exchange coins for the public in the form of mobile cash registers, and collect loose silver in a new channel outside the network of bank branches, or commonly known as "Shensha". 2. When you hear Shensha, you may smile heartily, and it is impossible to test whether Shensha is a harmonic sound of "cents" and "immortals" in English . Don't take these "broken pieces of silver" lightly, as they have witnessed the development of Hong Kong since the opening of the port. Hong Kong minted its first set of coins in 1863 and is now 150 years old, and coins are part of the history and life of Hong Kong people. In the nineteenth century, a penny could buy a white porridge and bread, and a millimeter was already two days of labor. Of course, I have seen and used a piece of money, but I remember when I was in elementary and middle school, the daily pocket money was a one-dollar triangle, because one millimeter could buy a bread, two millimeters could buy a vita, and the plate of rice was only a mosquito. 3. We launched this "Shensha" project to recycle and revitalize the "Shensha" in the hope of making the circulation of coins more efficient, which will not only be convenient for the public, but also reduce the cost of minting coins, and comply with environmental protection principles. The two cash registers will take turns in the next two years , with dedicated staff to assist the public and wheelchair lift platforms in the New Territories in the next two years. Coins brought by the public can be converted into cash or used as octopus cards to increase the value after being counted and processed by the counting machine, while there is no charge for the HKMA's service of singing money for the public. 4. I would like to take today's opportunity to thank LCSD for their support and assistance so that cash registers can be parked at mobile library service points in all districts of Hong Kong, which is convenient for the public and does not hinder traffic, and can use preset power supply devices to reduce the use of backup generators in cash registers, which meets environmental requirements. 5. I would also like to thank the Housing Department for its support in allowing cash registers to collect coins from the public in various estates for the convenience of nearby residents and merchants. In addition, I would like to thank Octopus for providing a free "tailor-made" value-added system for HKMA cash registers, with no minimum value-added amount, so that the public can add "a little" to the Octopus card. Of course, the public who do not want to take back their "fractions" can donate them and put them into the Community Chest donation box set up in the cashier's car, of course, the public can also donate all the coins converted into funds, even "plus" donations, in short, the more the merrier. 6. Earlier, we organised a design competition to invite all secondary schools in Hong Kong to participate, and received a total of 840 entries from 56 schools. We use the champion work as a model, design the appearance of the cash register, this is 100% local creation. When the cashier is walking on the road, I believe everyone can recognize it at a glance. 7. Distinguished guests, today is just a cash register launch and trial ceremony. The two cash registers will return to Ngau Tau Kok Shek Estate from 6 to 12 October as the first stop for the official coin collection service. The cashier vans will then take turns to be stationed in other areas, and the service time and location of the cash registers will be published on the HKMA website in detail, which can be freely consulted by the public. At that time, I hope that all neighbors will give more support to this action that is both beneficial to the people and environmentally friendly. Thank you. Last revision date: 19 September 2014

Title: Speech at the 60th Graduation Ceremony of Chung Chi College, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech Nov. 20, 2014 Ideals, dreams, utopias Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Delivered at the 60th Graduation Ceremony of Chongji College, Chinese University of Hong Kong). Chairman Li Guoxing, Dean Chen Weiguang, President Chen Zaobiao, all the school trustees, all the professors and staff of Chongji College, all parents, all students, all guests: I am particularly pleased to have been invited back to my alma mater, Chongji College, to attend the 60th Graduation Ceremony today. I want to share one with you today Here's my view of ideals, dreams and dreams. 2. Let's start with ideals. Many people agree that people cannot lack ideals, and people without ideals are like people who have lost their way, and have a chaotic life and achieve nothing. I have seen a movie by Stephen Chow, and I remember him saying, "If people have no ideals, the same salted fish is no difference!" But everyone's ideals at different stages of life will be different, and they will adjust to changes in the environment. In my own case, I grew up in the fifties and sixties of difficulty and scarcity. It was difficult to find a job in Hong Kong at that time, and even if there was a job, most of the people's wages could only barely make ends meet. Most parents hope that their children will grow tall and grow up quickly, and they can come out to work and help their families. Of course, there are also parents who understand that to really get rid of poverty, it is necessary for their children to study and become mature. Therefore, no matter how hard they work, they must cut back on food and clothing and provide for their children to go to school and study. When I was in elementary school, although I was very young, I also understood the hard work of my parents, so my dream at that time was to get a good score in the entrance examination and enter a good secondary school. In addition to this, another ideal of my elementary school was to be selected to participate in a children's program on a radio station and get a prize that I had always longed for, that is, Coca-Cola's specially customized wooden shake. Unfortunately, after half a century, my wooden shaky ideal has been disappointed to this day. When I arrived in middle school, my ideal was raised again, that is, I hoped that I could get good results in the Secondary 5 and 7th Secondary School examinations and have the opportunity to go to university. As a result, I was admitted to Chongji in 1972, and when I was about to graduate, just like all recent graduates, I kept thinking about where to go from here. My first wish at that time was to go overseas for further study, but based on economic reasons, I had to save enough money before I could go to a master's or doctoral degree. My dream is to get a first-class honor, work as a tutor at a university for two years, earn two years of money and then go to further studies. However, contrary to expectations, the first-level honorary examination could not be passed, the teaching assistant was not me, and the university hired another smart. I had to face reality and desperately look for a job. Although I had not decided in my mind that I wanted to join the government or a private company, my dream was to find a promising job. 3. I remember that I was a fisherman casting a net to go to work. I personally typed 40 cover letters on my manual typewriter and sent them to major companies in Hong Kong that had advertisements for recruitment. But the frustrating thing is that no company wants to think about it, and I didn't even get a chance to interview. Of course, I also applied for government positions, applied for ICAC, AO, E0 and ALO in one go, and all of them were interviewed and accepted. I naturally chose to be the administrative officer. Later, when the HKMA was established in 1993, I left my post as Chief Administrative Officer Department, Archives Authority. I left the HKMA in 2005 for a middle-aged retreat, worked in the private sector for a year and a half, returned to the Government in 2007 as Chief Executive Officer, and took over as HKMA President in October 2009 until now. I have told a whole lot about the history of my work, not to write an autobiography, but to illustrate the subject of today's discussion, that is, "reason." The difference between "thinking", "dreaming" and "dreaming". 4. Everyone's ideals may be different, and some are more ambitious, such as hoping to set goals for ten years or twenty years. Some are more recent or specific, such as those who wish to study overseas after graduating from university, study for a master's or doctoral degree, or obtain a professional qualification, such as a doctor or lawyer. Some are more general, such as wanting to be a successful person, or contributing to society. But no matter what type of personal ideal, there is a very important common point, that is, there is a willingness to achieve the desired goal and a plan and determination to implement the action. For example, if a student wants to study overseas after graduation, he must redouble his efforts to study, strive for good grades, and prepare for financial arrangements for further education. If you want to become a doctor, you have to beat thousands of secondary school candidates before you can be admitted to medical school, even if you want to obtain a specialist qualification after graduating from medical school, you must have a chance to successfully strive for the ideal goal according to your ability and performance. On a TV show a few years ago about management experience, an EMBA classmate asked me how I could become a senior official. My answer is that if you want to become a high-ranking official or a big official, you must first do a good job as a petty official. In the bureaucratic structure of the government, the official rank is a pyramid layer by layer, and the higher the official rank, the fewer positions, and the more fierce the competition. I started doing AO 38 years ago, of course, I hope to have a successful career, but every day in my heart, I ask myself to do my best to do everything in front of me, and I will not waste time to calculate and calculate for 10 years In 20 years, I will rise to several heights. Therefore, being an official is only the way, and doing things is the goal. The English word "present" has two meanings - "now" and "gift", as long as you grasp the "now" and do everything in front of you, you are the best "gift" for yourself. 5. I think another important common denominator for people who can achieve their ideals, in addition to having the willingness and determination, is that they can be down-to-earth and follow the steps to strive for and implement the ideal goals. In other words, just have grand aspirations, but are so ambitious, only to indulge in the grand vision, not willing to do a good job in front of them, often feel that they are overused, and even tend to be eager to win and rush to achieve short-term profits, according to my own observations over the years, these are the main reasons why many smart and capable people have not succeeded in achieving their ideals. 6. Many people misunderstand that as long as there is a lofty intention, there is an ideal. But everyone should pay attention to the fact that if you are not willing to make an effort, if you are not willing to try and struggle, your ideal is likely to become a fantasy. Ideals and fantasies are only a word difference, and the difference between success and failure in our real life may only be a difference between one thought and a line. Dear students, whether you have an ideal or a fantasy or even a delusion in your heart, only you know and can decide which one it is. Let me give you another superficial example, if a male classmate feels that a female classmate is the ideal object in his mind, in your terms, a "goddess", but in his heart he feels that a girl with such good conditions must have many suitors, and her chances are not high, so she has not acted and only buried her admiration in her heart. But then, will the boy have a chance to pursue this girl? The answer is definitely not. Woody Allen once said "70% of success is by being there!" This means that if you don't show up, don't try, don't fight, where will you have a chance to succeed? I think this sentence is very philosophical. Just as HKUST President Professor Chen Fanchang said at the graduation ceremony of Chongji College last year, he originally wanted to transfer schools and apply for Huangren College after the Fifth Examination of Salesian Secondary School, but he could not get the application form, so he wanted to give up, but later reminded by a classmate and mother, "Why not try", and as a result, after the opening of the school, he plucked up the courage to go to Huangren to ask for an interview, and his sincerity actually impressed Vice Principal Huangren, and he was admitted, which also changed his life. Don't taste Try, do not pay, how can there be a chance to succeed! 7. Finally, I want to talk about what is a dream? I think the biggest difference between a dream and an ideal is that even with a few efforts, it may not be possible to achieve the goal of the dream. But dreams are different from dreams, because dreams are generally a lofty and lofty vision, which may not be attainable, but will be fought for as much as they can or in a lifetime. Even if you can't succeed yourself, you want to create better conditions for others or the next generation to achieve this vision. For example, the founder of Chongji College, who came to Hong Kong from the mainland, established Chongji College in 1951, a time of scarcity, just as our school song begins with "South Heaven and Sea, People from All Directions, Tongxing This Academy". The school song also says "Shenzhou academic, long-standing, and number of classics do not forget the ancestors", because the predecessor of Chongji College is 13 very historical universities in China, and the goal of the college is to "help the elite, the heavens descend on great responsibility, and the best and the best to go together". However, the achievements of Chongji College today can only be achieved through the continuous efforts of the first, second and even third generations of teachers and students. From President Lee Ying Lam to the 11th Dean, Professor Chan Wai Kwong, Chung Kee has worked hard for the dream of the founder of Chung Chi College, bit by bit, step by step, to establish a vocational school that Hong Kong people are proud of. This dream has been achieved after 50 to 60 years of efforts by Chongji people, because the students who graduated from Chongji are the elite of society. 8. Students, your dream can be a pursuit that has been buried for many years but does not dare to declare it, it can be as simple as "using your own hands to make the world a better place", or it can be a vision that takes several generations or more than a century to complete. At the same time, you must also be mentally prepared that in the process of experiencing life, it will not be a smooth road. But I can be sure that no matter what line of work or profession you devote yourself to after graduation, as long as you remember Chongji's school motto of "Stop at the Best" and pursue what you think with the attitude of lifelong learning, grasping the present, and tirelessly, you will certainly be able to show your strengths, succeed in your career, and contribute to society and the country. 9. Dear students, I have already written this speech four months ago. A lot has happened in Hong Kong recently, and it is worth reflecting on each of us. In preparation for today's ceremony, I carefully re-read this speech to see if it should be revised, but I feel that the contents, ideas, and reasoning are still the words I want to say to all the teachers, disciples, and sisters on this occasion. Today's Hong Kong is the result of the hard work of several generations, but the future world belongs to your generation, and only when young people have ideals, dreams, and pursuits can society make progress. As a "master brother", I hope that everyone can understand that there are many pursuits - just like the establishment of Chongji in the past - one grass, one tree, one stone and one pillar, all of which are made up of generations of people who work hard to manage and accumulate the results step by step. Everyone must understand that some things require a broad mind and vision to see the distance, to accept that some things cannot be reached overnight, and to know that sometimes we must know what to do. 10. I know that these are some truths that are easier said than done, but I sincerely hope that in the future, on the long road of life and in the pursuit of goals and ideals, you may wish to use what Master Brother said today as a reference. 11. Thank you! Last revision date: 20 November 2014
