Title: RMB Internationalisation Hong Kong: The Bridge Linking China with the Rest of the World
text: 19/09/22, 13:03 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - RMB Internationalisation Hong Kong: The Bridge Linking China with the Rest of the World Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 16 Sep 2015 RMB Internationalisation Hong Kong: The Bridge Linking China with the Rest of the World Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. A very warm welcome to all of you for attending this year's Treasury Markets Summit jointly organised by the Treasury Markets Association and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. 2. For those of you who attended the Treasury Markets Summit last year, you may recall that I talked about "what does it take to become a Global Offshore RMB Hub". In my speech, I presented the proposition that the answer to that question rested with the acronym "PIPs", which stands for Policy, Infrastructure and People/Products. This year, I will again talk about PIPs. Before you ask for your money back, I can promise you that I will try not to repeat word for word on what I said last year. If you are still unhappy afterwards, talk to Jack Cheung, the Chief Executive Officer of the Treasury Markets Association, to see if you can negotiate a mutually acceptable settlement for a rebate. 3. Joking apart, Policy, Infrastructure and People/Products are the three pillars that can support a vibrant offshore RMB centre and will remain so for a very long time to come. So you will have to forgive me for not venturing beyond these paradigms whenever I have the chance to talk to a distinguished group of bankers and market practitioners like you. I will divide my presentation today into three parts. First, I will recap briefly how we managed to achieve what we have today in terms of policy headroom in developing the offshore RMB business in Hong Kong. Second, I will also briefly talk about the present status in the development of the necessary financial market infrastructure in Hong Kong, without which it would not have been possible for us to be where we are today. Third, I will come to the main theme of my presentation today, which is, despite all our achievements, there is still a lot to be done on the 3rd Pillar, "People", if we wish Hong Kong to remain the global hub for offshore RMB businesses. PIPs - Policy Headroom 4. RMB was unique in that there existed a long period of time in which the use or circulation of RMB outside of Mainland China was disallowed. As we know, this policy started to change, only very marginally, in 2004 when the residents of Hong Kong were allowed to open RMB accounts with banks in Hong Kong, with a conversion limit of 20,000 Yuan per day and a daily cross border remittance limit of 80,000 Yuan. It was a very restrictive scheme but an important first step. 5. Then in 2009 a major breakthrough came, with the launch of a pilot scheme to allow cross border trade settlement using the RMB. The scheme was rather limited to begin with, but / 1/6 19/09/22, 13:03 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - RMB Internationalisation Hong Kong: The Bridge Linking China with the Rest of the World many subsequent steps were taken by the authorities in Beijing to widen the eligibility and scope of the use of RMB offshore. So by 2011, the use of RMB in the settlement of trade in both goods and services between Mainland China and the rest of the world was fully liberalised. 6. In 2011, which was a major watershed in the expansion of policy headroom for the development of offshore RMB business, the use of RMB for Overseas Direct Investment and for Foreign Direct Investment was allowed. It was in the same year that the Peoples Bank of China started to allow foreign banks to invest in the interbank bond market on the Mainland; it was also the same year the RMB Qualified Foreign Institutional Investors (RQFII) Scheme was launched. 7. In April 2014, there was another breakthrough when the Mainland and Hong Kong authorities announced the launch of the Hong Kong-Shanghai Stock Connect. Indeed, when the 2014 TMA Summit was held in September last year, we were waiting anxiously for the exact date for the launch of the Connect. As we now know, the Connect was launched in mid-November and has operated smoothly since then. Of course, the policy headroom did not stop there and we have witnessed the launch of the Mutual Recognition of Funds Scheme in July this year and we hope the Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect will be launched in the not too distant future. 8. To sum up, Hong Kong, with the support of the Central People's Government and the relevant Mainland authorities over the last few years, has gone a very long way in establishing ample policy headroom for the offshore RMB business to develop and thrive here. Using the bridge analogy, from a small and narrow bridge that existed in 2004 to 2009, we now have the policy headroom for expanding the bridge, which links the onshore RMB market with the offshore market, into a very wide corridor that can cater for a big volume of traffic. As I said earlier, the policy headroom cannot and should not stop here. We must keep on expanding the bridge in future years as we advance to more mature stages of the offshore market development. However, I should say that, at this stage, Hong Kong has quite ample policy headroom for the industry and other stakeholders to work on in developing the offshore RMB businesses. PIPs - Infrastructure 9.1 do not propose to say too much on the importance of market infrastructure, since most of you here understand clearly that it will not have been possible for us to develop into the global hub for offshore RMB businesses without a world class financial market infrastructure such as the clearing and payment systems. The only point I wish to touch upon here relates to some recent market comments suggesting that the RMB liquidity facilities provided by the HKMA are inadequate when the CNH market is under stress. There is no doubt true that, while Hong Kong has the largest RMB liquidity pool in the offshore market, the depth and breadth of the interbank RMB market cannot match those of the major currencies such as USD, Euro and Yen. It is also true that the liquidity in the CNH market cannot be compared with that in the onshore market where the Mainland banks can access a much bigger pool of RMB liquidity and, in case of need, the liquidity facilities provided by the People's Bank of China. In Hong Kong, our Participating Banks do not have such direct access to the liquidity windows on the Mainland. However, this problem is not unique in the CNH market here in Hong Kong because it exists in every offshore RMB centre all over the world. In a way, the liquidity problem can basically be addressed if the banks / 2/6 19/09/22, 13:03 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - RMB Internationalisation Hong Kong: The Bridge Linking China with the Rest of the World can manage to deal on a T1 basis. But as all bank treasurers know, very often liquidity shortage occurs unexpectedly during the trading day and liquidity support is needed on a T0 basis. This is a tricky problem that cannot be resolved easily in any offshore RMB market. The solution that the HKMA has offered, for the time being, is the following package : the offer of Intraday Repo to facilitate smooth payments flowing through our RTGS system, the offer of Overnight Repo on a T0 basis and the appointment of 7 Primary Liquidity Providers, each of whom has a bilateral repo facility with the HKMA. These three measures were announced by me in the TMA Summit last year and were designed to provide liquidity backstops to banks as the volume and value of the CNH transactions that flow through our banking system steadily increase over time, especially after the launch of the Stock Connect. Our package does have one shortcoming though: the amounts that can be offered by the HKMA are somewhat constrained, unlike the HKD liquidity window. This is because RMB, unlike HKD, is not our domestic currency and the HKMA could only use its own RMB funds parked in Hong Kong to provide liquidity as and when it is needed. The HKMA's RMB liquidity facilities are not meant to be a regular funding source for banks, and are not designed to prevent market interest rates from adjusting in response to market supply and demand of RMB funds. These liquidity facilities are intended to provide short term liquidity in episodes of market tightness and volatility to help banks manage their liquidity. And I should point out that even on 24 and 25 August which were the two most volatile days in CNH money market last month, the HKMA's capacity for offering T0 Overnight Repo was far from being exhausted. So the suggestion that this facility is inadequate to meet demand has not been borne out by facts so far. Nevertheless, there is no room for complacency and the HKMA would keep an open mind in considering suggestions from the market participants on how we can do better in this regard. PIPs - People/Products 10.1 now wish to come to "People", the last of the three component of PIPs. For those of you who attended the previous TMA Summit meetings at which I spoke, you will notice that I have strong conviction on "People". I always talk about the importance of "soft power" and why and how it matters in the fierce competition amongst our peers to become an international financial centre. As I truly believe that "soft power" matters, I do hope that you will understand and forgive me for keeping on coming back to this topic. 11. When it comes to "People", there are three key ingredients that can lead to success or, if you don't get them right, failure. These ingredients can be represented by the acronym "3 Cs", which stands for Competence, Control and Culture. 12. It goes without saying that Hong Kong's practitioners must be technically competent in doing what they do. However, modern banking and finance are getting increasingly complex. Customer needs and the regulatory requirements are constantly evolving. All these developments render it a big challenge to our practitioners in keeping themselves up to date on their technical skills and competence. So what have we done in the area of "Competence"? In collaboration with the industry bodies including the HKAB, TMA, HKIB and HKSI, the HKMA has taken a number of steps in the last few years to promote the professional competence of our practitioners. The most notable example is what we have done to help set up the Private Wealth Management Association in 2013 and the launch of an Enhanced Competency Framework (ECF) and a learning programme for private wealth management practitioners in 2014. Clearly we cant stop here and more is needed to be done to upgrade the professional competence of our practitioners. I am pleased to / 3/6 19/09/22, 13:03 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - RMB Internationalisation Hong Kong: The Bridge Linking China with the Rest of the World announce today that the HKMA will, in collaboration with the industry and HKIB, launch another Enhanced Competency Framework in 2016 on anti-financial crime and compliance to train up more talent and enhance the standards of competence in this area. We aim to start the consultation with the industry in the first quarter of 2016 on the Framework with a view to rolling out the programme within next year. Thereafter, we will further consult the industry on our plan to launch similar capacity building initiatives covering the following four streams of professional work in the banking sector: (a) Treasury management, (b) Retail wealth management, (c) Compliance and Internal Controls, and (d) Credit Risk Management. 13. Having touched upon "Competence", the first "C", I would like to talk about the other two "Cs", Control and Culture. We all appreciate that human behaviours are shaped by "Control" and "Culture". A bank staff is expected to comply with the rules set by the bank, many of which are imposed externally by law or by the regulators. These rules stipulate what a banker can or cannot do. For these rules to be meaningful, a bank must have in place an effective system to police and enforce the rules. A bank staff would understand that he could be punished if he is found by the bank or by the regulator to be in breach of the prescribed rules. Similarly, a bank would face rather unpleasant consequences if it is found to be in breach, either intentionally or unintentionally, of certain prudential or conduct requirements set by the supervisor. The key phrase here is "found to be in breach" of the rules, which means that someone has to be caught for having broken the rules. If you think carefully, this means that if a person can conceal his breaches successfully or if the chance of being caught is very low, then that person might well be tempted to try his luck and misbehave. However, no system is perfect and it is not surprising that from time to time breaches occurred, some with rather serious consequences for the customers and for the bank staff concerned. The problem becomes much more serious if the bank itself was minded to evade or break the prudential or conduct rules in the pursuit of profits. This is why the regulators all over the world have put in place an elaborate framework to ensure compliance of the rules. On this point, I am afraid that, since the eruption of the Global Financial Crisis, the prudential standards, which range from capital adequacy, liquidity, leverage and risk management, have been tightened considerably and so has the regulatory framework for policing and enforcing the compliance with the new global standards and rules. The same applies to the conduct rules as serious breaches and misconduct in a number of areas, such as the rigging of the benchmarks in interest rates, fx and commodities, have been uncovered in recent years. I should quickly mention that the lapses in AML practices in some banks have also led to rather serious consequences for the banks concerned, both in reputational and financial terms. Moreover, there have been many high profile cases across many financial centres that some banks did not take due care of customers' interests when they became overly eager in selling financial products, such as Payment Protection Insurance, Accumulators, ILAS to name just a few examples. As a result of these recent developments, it is not surprising that there is increasing pressure across most financial centres for greater protection of the financial consumers, which necessitates the introduction of stricter rules and standards on conduct for banks and other financial firms. 14. Having touched upon "Competence" and "Control", I would like to talk about the third "C", "Culture", where I wish you to remember as the key takeaway for my presentation today. While "Control" shapes the behaviour of a firm and its staff, it has a major drawback. / 4/6 19/09/22, 13:03 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - RMB Internationalisation Hong Kong: The Bridge Linking China with the Rest of the World "Control" only works when the system can promptly and effectively monitor and detect breaches. This is very difficult indeed, especially when the control system within a bank is less than robust, either by default or by design. A supervisor like the HKMA will certainly provide a powerful external check, but there is a limit to how far we can depend on it. The HKMA simply does not and cannot have enough staff to conduct on-site examinations to check on each and every transaction between a bank and its customers. So the answer must lie in the banking industry adopting the appropriate culture and values that are consistent with the goal of ensuring sustainable long term growth of the business. This would require the change of mind-set amongst some bankers or bank shareholders in such a way that they don't regard profit maximisation as the paramount goal of the banks. Banks should cherish financial prudence over excessive risk taking. Banks should value fair and equitable treatment of customers more than profit maximisation. This would require the banks and their shareholders treasuring long term growth over short term financial performance. How can we achieve this? I must say this is easier said than done, but I am hopeful that we can make meaningful progress in this direction if we and the industry can join hands by trying to do it together. Clearly the culture of a bank cannot be changed from the bottom. It must be done from the top down. The senior management and boards of banks must take primary responsibility in driving this process. The boards must take ownership of instituting and maintaining the right culture and value in governance, risk management and controls of the banks. Most importantly, the boards must put in place the appropriate incentive system, covering both compensation arrangements and human resources system within the organisation that would help nurture the culture and values that the boards desire. Only when the right culture, supported by the appropriate incentive system, filters down to every level of the bank can we be confident that the desired outcomes and behaviours would result, even when the regulator is not looking over the bank's shoulders. This would mean that a bank staff would refrain from misbehaving not because he is afraid of being caught, but because he does not think it is the right thing to do, even though the risk of being caught by the bank or the supervisor is not high. So compliance becomes not a question of whether one "can" or "cannot" but "should" or "should not". 15. Having said all these, you may ask what the HKMA is going to do to encourage the development of the right culture in banks. Since we believe that this process has to be driven from the top down and the boards must play the leading role, the HKMA will step up its collaboration with the banks and their boards on this project. In this context, I have commissioned a small study group with outside experts on corporate governance of banks to come up with recommendations on how Hong Kong could better equip and empower the Independent Non Executive Directors of banks to facilitate the development of good governance and culture in banks. As the work of the study group is still ongoing, there is not much I can tell you now. But I expect the study group would be in a position to present its findings and recommendations by the end of this year. I will then consult the banking industry and the other stakeholders on these recommendations and on the way forward. 16. Ladies and gentlemen, let me say this in conclusion. I am very confident that we have a very bright future ahead of us. Hong Kong is already the global hub for offshore RMB business and we can remain competitive for a long time to come provided we are committed to do the following three things: (a) continue to make the best use of the policy headroom that is made available to Hong Kong by the Mainland authorities in the internationalisation of RMB. I should add that some of the policy headroom would give Hong Kong the first mover advantage, but overtime, such / 5/6 19/09/22, 13:03 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - RMB Internationalisation Hong Kong: The Bridge Linking China with the Rest of the World advantage would diminish or disappear as other centres are given similar policy treatment or access. The bilateral swap agreements with PBoC and RQFII quotas are just two obvious examples that come to mind. However, with our first mover advantage and our other unique advantages as part of China under the One Country, Two Systems arrangements, we are very well equipped to stay ahead of the game; (b) continue to enhance the market infrastructure to ensure that it remains efficient and robust to support the rapidly growing volume and complexity of the offshore RMB financial transactions that are conducted through our banks in Hong Kong. This of course involve the necessary liquidity support and backstops that would facilitate orderly market functioning and developments; and (c) last but not least, continue to work hard to expand and upgrade the human and institutional capability so that we can out-compete our peers in terms of "soft power". 17. All these three things are ongoing endeavours and there is absolutely no room for complacency for any of us. This is just like what the ancient Chinese teaching suggests : "it is like rowing a boat upstream, you either forge ahead or fall behind". 18. Thank you very much. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority While the FOMC decided not to raise policy interest rate last night, it is worth noting that 13 out of 17 members of FOMC expected a lift-off within this year. So it is important that we should not think that the ultra low interest rate environment will last indefinitely. In terms of Hong Kong's property market, the disconnect between the purchasing power of our citizens and the high valuation has become very serious for quite some time. With the recent slowdown of the Mainland and Hong Kong economies, it is important that buyers of property take into full account of the fact that the ultra low mortgage interest rates will not last forever. They should carefully assess their income levels and repayment ability when they take out mortgage loans, so as to avoid running into financial difficulties when interest rates normalise and the property cycle turns. Title: CE's remarks at the Launch ceremony of Mobile Branch of SCBHK
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech Nov. 26, 2015 The Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Mr Chan Tak Lin, delivered a speech at the launching ceremony of Standard Chartered Bank's Mobile Branch Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority President Hong Pizheng, President Chen Xiumei, distinguished guests, and neighbors: I am so pleased to attend the opening ceremony of Standard Chartered Bank's "Mobile Branch" today. 2. As we all know, Hong Kong's banking industry is developing rapidly, and in addition to supervising the soundness of banks, the HKMA attaches great importance to the implementation of the concepts of "customer-oriented" and "universal finance", and there are currently 22 retail banks in Hong Kong with more branches 1,100 rooms and about 5,500 ATMs serving banking customers. 3. However, according to the HKMA's research, the basic services provided by banks in remote areas are not sufficient, and there is room for further improvement. 4. We understand that banks have staffing, foot traffic, costs and other business considerations in terms of business expansion and branch coverage, but the HKMA believes that large retail banks, especially the three banknote issuing banks, should do their best to provide basic banking services to the public. 5. So I'm very happy to see Standard Chartered Bank's "Mobile Branch" officially launched today. The launch of the "Mobile Branch" is a manifestation of Standard Chartered Bank's desire to provide basic banking services to the public. As the name suggests, "Mobile Branch" is a branch that can travel to different places, which also provides a new operating method for banks in Hong Kong's hard-to-find environment, which can enhance services for some areas where the bank branch network is currently insufficient, which is undoubtedly a win-win for banks and communities! In After the "Mobile Branch" is put into operation, residents of Tian Qing Estate can get basic banking services within a 5-minute walk, which is much more convenient than before. 6. In addition to "mobile branches", technological developments have been rapid in recent years, and several banks have now launched or piloted virtual teller services in the form of video calls. I personally went to see these virtual tellers at work, and I felt that this new technology model would provide new mobility for some remote and under-covered areas of traditional bank branches. Because virtual ATMs do not need to occupy such large bunks as traditional branches, they can not only reduce rental costs, but also provide the elderly and other grassroots citizens in need with more comprehensive basic banking services than ordinary ATMs. I look forward to seeing more banks adopt new technologies and more flexible operating models in the coming years to expand their service scope and coverage, especially the three banknote issuers in Hong Kong, which enjoy the unique status of banknote issuers while also taking into account the needs of the public for basic banking services. Thank you. Last revision date: 26 November 2015

Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 17 Dec 2015 Statement by Norman T.L. Chan Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the media on 17 December 2015 Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority As expected, the FOMC decided last night to raise the Fed funds target rate by 25 basis points. In accordance with the Linked Exchange Rate system, the HKMA also raised the Base Rate of the Discount Window by 25 basis points to 0.75%. 2. The FOMC decision on the rate lift-off signifies the beginning of US interest rate normalization after more than 6 years of exceptionally low interest rate coupled with the Quantitative Easing monetary policy. While the Fed has only raised interest rate by 25 basis points and indicated that the pace of future rate hikes would be gradual, significant adjustments in the global economies and in the asset markets are to be expected during this process of US interest rate normalization. For the Emerging Market Economies, they will likely continue to experience outflow of funds as well as pressure on their exchange rates, economic growth and asset markets. 3. As far as Hong Kong is concerned, a rise in US interest rates will eventually lead to a rise in Hong Kong dollar interest rates under the Linked Exchange Rate system. The normalization of Hong Kong interest rates will begin with the outflow of funds from HK dollar triggered by the higher interest rates of the US dollar. Given that the pace of US interest rate hikes would likely be gradual and we have a very big cushion of close to HK1.6 trillion in our monetary base, we presently expect the rise in the Hong Kong dollar interbank interest rates to be incremental. However, the actual speed of outflows from HK dollar will depend on the pace of US interest rate hikes and the interest rate differential between the US dollar and HK dollar. If, for whatever reasons, the US interest rate rises faster than expected, then the outflows from HK dollar and corresponding rise in interest rate will also be quicker. 4. I should add that, under our Currency Board regime, the outflow of HK dollar will occur when the market begins to sell US dollar to the HKMA through the Weak Side Convertibility Undertaking of 7.8500. The trigger of the Weak Side Undertaking is a natural and necessary step in the process of the normalization of the HK dollar interest rates. 5. Lastly, US interest rate normalization is a significant event that affects global financial markets. I would advise members of the public to make the necessary preparations, in terms of managing the credit, liquidity and other relevant risks, in order to cope with possible shocks and adjustments that may result from the normalization of US and HK interest rates. / 1/2 19/09/22, 13:03 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Statement by Norman T.L. Title: HSBC Client Event: Taking Treasury to the Next Level
text: 19/09/22, 13:02 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - HSBC Client Event: Taking Treasury to the Next Level Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 17 Mar 2016 HSBC Client Event: "Taking Treasury to the Next Level" Vincent Lee, Executive Director (External), Hong Kong Monetary Authority Kee Joo, ladies and gentlemen, I am delighted to join you this evening and to speak on treasury management. This might sound a little dry to the uninitiated, but it takes on a new dimension when seen through the title of tonights HSBC client event - "Taking Treasury to the Next Level". It has been said that because of interest rate fluctuations, currency risks, and regulatory changes, the role of treasurer is now more important than ever. It is a fact that corporate treasurers face a complex environment in optimising their financial resources and managing risks. So, tonight, Id like to share with you two important trends which are changing the way corporate treasurers do business. First, the increasing use of renminbi internationally, and secondly the growing trend for corporates to centralise their treasury operations through the establishment of corporate treasury centres, or CTCs, as we like to call them. Progress of RMB internationalisation The growing internationalisation of renminbi has been nothing short of phenomenal since it began in 2009. Today, all direct investment into and out of China, as well as merchandise trade with the country, can be freely settled in RMB. We have also witnessed steady progress in the opening up of Chinas capital account, in particular with the expanding channels for RMB portfolio investment and cross-border cash flows. And here, I would like to give you some examples of what has happened in such a short time -  The Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect was launched towards the end of 2014, allowing international investors to invest in shares listed in Shanghai through the Hong Kong stock exchange, and vice versa.  The implementation of the Mutual Recognition of Funds scheme in July 2015, which allows eligible Mainland and Hong Kong funds to be distributed in each others market through a streamlined vetting process.  The continuous opening up of the onshore interbank bond market and foreign exchange market to overseas participants.  And, over the past 12 months or so, the Chinese authorities have announced new measures which are aimed at further facilitating cross-border cash management and financing activities in renminbi and foreign currencies. / 1/5 19/09/22, 13:02 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - HSBC Client Event: Taking Treasury to the Next Level Who would have imagined these developments just a few short years ago? And there's more to come. In spite of the more challenging market conditions in recent times, the Chinese government has reiterated its commitment to opening wider to the world and accelerating the opening up of its capital market. Underpinning this direction are several important developments:  First, is the inclusion of the renminbi in the IMF's SDR basket. This move will signify greater recognition of the RMB as a freely usable currency that is 'widely used' and 'widely traded', and boost confidence in the use of the RMB for economic and financial transactions in different parts of the world.  Secondly, Chinese financial markets have become more liberalised. For instance, earlier this year, the Chinese authorities further relaxed the Qualified Foreign Institutional Investor arrangement, and removed investment quotas for eligible overseas financial institutions to invest in the Chinese interbank bond market.  And, last but not least, the launch of the "Belt and Road" initiative, which is expected to attract numerous capital investment projects, create new opportunities for the use of the RMB and reinforce Chinas increasingly important role in the region's trade and investment activities. In parallel, the establishment of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank will play an important role in financing infrastructure projects in Asia, thus leading to a more sustainable development of the region. So, we might ask: why does the internationalisation of the RMB matter to corporate treasurers? Let me quote from the Economist's Asia Business Outlook Survey..."In 2011, Western firms said that Asia contributed 19% of their global revenues. In 2012, that figure rose to 22%. By 2017, Western firms expect Asia to contribute 32%. However, this will still be below Asia's estimated 35% share of the global economy in 2017." End of quote. Increasingly, therefore, multinational corporations will find it not only an advantage, but a necessity, to trade more with their Asian counterparts, and to conduct the related financing, investment and hedging activities in the RMB. We should also not overlook the important and growing trend of Chinese companies "going out". With the continuation of RMB internationalisation and the Belt-and-Road initiative, Mainland corporates are "going-out" and expanding their trade and investment from the domestic market to the international marketplace. These trends are driving a much wider international use of the RMB as a currency for trade settlement, financing and payments. The increasing cash and capital flows in the offshore market will, in turn, lead to greater internationalisation of the RMB. Given these trends, it is time for corporate treasurers to think carefully - if they have not done so already - about how they should improve their treasury operations to take advantage of this RMB internationalisation. For our part, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has played a central role in developing Hong Kong as the global hub for offshore RMB business. And, at this point, I would like to introduce a few more facts and figures to clearly illustrate what is happening. Today, Hong Kong is easily the largest renminbi business centre outside the Mainland with a pool of some one trillion renminbi. We are also the largest RMB financing and asset management / 2/5 19/09/22, 13:02 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - HSBC Client Event: Taking Treasury to the Next Level centre outside the Mainland. Our strategy in developing this business in Hong Kong is focused on strengthening our market infrastructure. On liquidity, the HKMA has in place an RMB400 billion currency swap agreement with the Peoples Bank of China which can be activated when market conditions warrant. In addition, we've made available an RMB liquidity facility to banks which is currently offering intraday repos of up to RMB10 billion, as well as overnight funds on a T0 basis and one-day and one-week funds settled on a T1 basis. We've also appointed seven banks as Primary Liquidity Providers and provided each with a bilateral repo facility of up to RMB2 billion. These facilities help banks and their clients, like yourselves, to better manage RMB liquidity. We've also worked with the industry to develop a CNH HIBOR Fixing, which supports the growth of the renminbi market by providing a financial benchmark for loan facilities and assisting in the development of RMB interest rate and credit products. The fixing has increased the ability with which market participants can hedge the interest rate risk of their renminbi businesses. Hong Kong has also developed a highly efficient renminbi clearing and settlement system. Indeed, the average daily turnover of the RMB Real Time Gross Settlement system recently amounted to some one trillion RMB. And, we will continue to enhance the system's capabilities to keep pace with business growth. Our system will complement the Mainlands recently launched Cross-border Interbank Payment System, or CIPS, thus making renminbi business transactions even more convenient. Ladies and gentlemen, you might recall at the beginning of my speech, I mentioned the growing trend of establishing CTCs. So, why is this happening? Corporate treasurers face many other challenges these days. Typically, corporates expanding their trade and investment overseas involve multi-location operations, multi- currency and cross-border supply chain management. This situation applies equally to Western corporates expanding into Asia, and Chinese companies "going out". For corporates, the challenges create additional exposure to a broad array of risks, such as foreign currency risk, interest rate risk, counterparty risk, legal and compliance risk....and the risks go on. Compounding the challenge for treasury management is the regulatory landscape after the global financial crisis. The capability of banks in providing funding and making a market for hedging tools has become more constrained due to deleveraging and the implementation of global regulatory reforms, in particular the Basel III requirements on capital and liquidity. Increased market volatility has also made the raising of funds in the capital market more challenging. Indeed, to stay ahead of the game, corporate treasurers need to ensure treasury functions can be tailored to better support international growth and capture the immense opportunities in Asia. At the same time there is a need to sharpen the management of capital, liquidity, funding and treasury related risks in a highly complex and fast-moving market environment. In this context, a CTC, which is effectively an in-house bank, provides an ideal solution through centralising the management of liquidity, funding and risks arising from the operations of multi-national corporations in multiple jurisdictions. / 3/5 19/09/22, 13:02 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - HSBC Client Event: Taking Treasury to the Next Level Hong Kong as a CTC hub I believe all of you here tonight recognise the advantages Hong Kong has as a CTC hub. And, I'm sure youre well aware of our efforts in working closely with banks and MNCs to make Hong Kong a preferred location for setting up CTCs. Indeed, it is our goal to capture, in particular, the high value-added segments of the CTC value chain, including cash and iiquidity management, corporate finance activities and financial risk management. By attracting more CTCs and corporate activities here, not only will we bolster our financial sector, but advance the headquarters economy of Hong Kong. Therefore, it probably goes without saying, but Ill say it anyway, the interests of MNCs and Hong Kong are very much aligned. Having said that, we are fully aware of the strong competition among financial centres to become a CTC hub. So, there is a need to understand our competitive position, amplify our strengths and double our efforts in areas where we can do more. And, the Government is certainly playing its part in promoting the cause. In his 2015-16 budget speech, the Financial Secretary announced major changes to the tax regime that will make Hong Kong very attractive for MNCs to set up CTCs.  The interest deduction rules under the Inland Revenue Ordinance will be amended so that interest expenses arising from genuine cross border intra-group financing activities, under specified conditions, will be deductible. This will resolve the "tax asymmetry" issue currently perceived by some MNCs as an impediment to their establishing or expanding CTC operations in Hong Kong.  And, qualifying profits derived from corporate treasury activities and transactions conducted by qualifying CTCs will benefit from a half-rate concession. In other words, the applicable tax rate will be cut from the current 16.5% to 8.25%. Broadly speaking, the scope of this concession encompasses corporate finance, liquidity management and risk management activities typically conducted by CTCs for their non-Hong Kong associated corporations. Since the announcement, and following consultations with the industry, the Government introduced a bill into the Legislative Council last December to give effect to the changes. And, it's our target to have the bill passed by the middle of this year. Closing One of the HKMA's mandates is to develop and promote Hong Kong as an international financial centre. We believe with these latest refinements to the tax regime for CTC activities, together with our strengths and attractiveness as a global financial centre and in doing business with China, we will make Hong Kong the preferred location for multinational corporates to set up their CTCs. Ladies and gentlemen, I hope I haven't overstayed my welcome, but as you can gather these are issues that are vitally important for Hong Kong and our continued development. Thank you. And I wish you all an enjoyable evening. / 19/09/22, 13:02 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - HSBC Client Event: Taking Treasury to the Next Level Last revision date : 18 March 2016 / 5/5

Title: Fintech Supervision and Innovation
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 21 Mar 2016 Fintech regulation and innovation Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Delivered a speech at the Ming Pao Summit Forum on "Challenges of Hong Kong's 13th Five-Year Plan for New Opportunities"). Distinguished guests, friends, 1. I am delighted to be attending the Ming Pao Summit Forum on "The Challenges of Hong Kong's 13th Five-Year Plan for New Opportunities" today. Today I would like to talk about the development and application of financial technology (Fintech) in Hong Kong. The latest breakthrough in technology: artificial intelligence 2. Before I talk about fintech, I want to talk about the most recent Go game. South Korean chess champion Lee Se-woo lost 4-1 in a match in Seoul. 3. According to media reports, the opponent was so strong that he was "nervous, shaking his head, and sighing" from the very beginning. Opponents also have no mental fluctuations and are able to concentrate highly. 4. Everyone knows that this is the AlphaGo computer program developed by Google DeepMind. You might say, IBM The "Deep Blue" computer has already defeated the world champion of chess, what is special about this time? 5. This lies in the fact that there are many changes in the moves and winning strategies of Go, which are much more than chess. Google DeepMind experts even believe that the change of Go moves is more than the number of atoms in the universe, almost infinite. 6. Therefore, if the computer wants to defeat humans in the Go game, it is no longer enough to understand the operation; Its artificial intelligence (artificial Intelligence, or Al), is strong enough for programs to develop "human intuition." 7. The way AlphaGo computer programs cultivate "intuition" is to improve their "experience" through millions of simulated chess games, from which they "learn" the reasons for their success and failure. 8. No wonder Li Shimiao said that some of the layouts of AlphaGo were something he had never seen in many years of chess, which made him shoot the case amazingly. Experts also see the result of the game as a milestone in the contest between "man" and "machine". The Evolution and Disruption of Fintech" 9. Of course, what I'm going to talk about today is fintech, not Go. But what is evident in this example is, like AlphaGo, an Al technology, has developed to an almost unimaginable point; The potential of "fintech" that relies on the development of different cutting-edge technologies, including AI, cannot be ignored. 10. While fintech is an emerging term in recent years, the adoption of new technologies by banks and other financial institutions to improve efficiency and improve services has always existed, not been new. 11. Over the past few decades, fintech has been evolving, from automated teller machines (ATMs) a few decades ago, to the advent of the Internet, which has promoted online banking and financial services, to the current advancement of mobile networks and the introduction of mobile banking. 12. Technology has enabled customers of financial services to enjoy greater and greater freedom, because the delivery of financial services has evolved from "in-branch" to "off-branch", from "scheduled service" to "year-round", from "street" to "home", and from "home" to "anytime, anywhere" through mobile phones. 13. So, what exactly is Fintech (Fintech) that everyone is talking about now? 14. With the advent of a variety of innovative information and communication technologies and the increasing service requirements of financial service users, a variety of fintech services have emerged, such as digital payments and remittances, person-to-person (also known as P2P) lending and fundraising platforms, financial product investment and issuance platforms, and big data (big data), data analysis, etc. Since fintech relies on sound and stable network systems, cybersecurity and data security technologies are also an important part of fintech. 15. The emergence of financial technology will certainly help improve the service and efficiency of traditional financial institutions, but at the same time, it can make the public no longer need to rely entirely on traditional banks, and can also meet many payment and financial needs. No wonder some people today even describe the nature of fintech as "disruptive." 16. Taking the P2P lending platform that is more concerned by many people as an example, its main function is to directly match the fund suppliers and capital demanders, and replace the intermediary role of the bank. 17. Another emerging fintech industry is crowdfunding, where fundraisers usually introduce their projects or businesses over the Internet and promise to give the project or company shares, profits or products in return to raise capital. to crowdfund the platform In Kickstarter's case, Zano, a superminiature drone project, attracted more than 10,000 investors and raised more than 3.5 million. How the HKMA views fintech and innovation 18. Fintech involves avant-garde technologies, and the people involved in it come from different sectors such as finance, technology, law, and even psychology , biology, etc., and the level is both multi-faceted and broad. 19. The biggest challenge for the HKMA is how to provide adequate protection for fintech consumers in a rapidly changing environment while retaining the right flexibility to stifle the space for new technology development. There are at least three keys to achieving this goal . 20. The first is to be willing to understand and absorb scientific and technological innovation. Do we, as regulators, fully grasp the characteristics, potential and risks of different fintech services, as well as their advantages and disadvantages to the financial system? 21. In the case of blockchain or artificial intelligence (Al), if it is widely used and involves multiple retail or institutional customer level financial intermediary activities, what are the benefits and risks to the financial system? 22. Second, whether it can maintain good communication with all parties in the industry. In promoting the healthy development of financial technology, close and two-way communication is very important. 23. -A recent example is the licensing regime for stored value payment instruments that we have just introduced through the new legislation. As Hong Kong's stored value payment instruments are becoming more and more innovative and the industry's desire to bring these tools into the HKMA's regulatory scope is clear, the HKMA has introduced new legislation to regulate and license these innovative payment services with peace of mind. 24. Third, it is possible to strike a balance between development and user security in the formulation and implementation of regulatory policies. 25. Looking back, the introduction of new technologies will inevitably lead to some problems, but if the regulatory authorities do everything with "zero wind" The mentality of "risk", "immediate management", and "management to the end", and the reaction of "too hasty" or "too large" are likely to hinder the development and use of Jinrong Science and Technology. I would like to ask that ATMs still have occasional problems, but can it be said that in the past few decades, regulators should have actually banned banks from using ATMs? Internet banking also fails from time to time, do we prohibit the use of online banking? 26. Of course, "completely ignore" is another extreme and undesirable approach, as it arises in the name of using fintech Cases of "bursting pots" and "walking numbers" have emerged in an endless stream. 27. For example, Zano, the crowdfunding project I just mentioned, ended with an application for liquidation, and investors could not get their money back. Another oil and gas company called Ascenergy, which raised money from nearly 100 investors, was found to have most of the money transferred to companies unrelated to energy and has been sued by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. 28. In the mainland, the most eye-catching case in recent times is the P2P platform "e-Rent Treasure" at the end of last year, raising up to 50 billion yuan and 900,000 investors, most of which have been exposed as false financing projects and have now been sealed, but the whereabouts of the funds are unknown. 29. These cases show that as a regulator, we have to "worry about the world before we worry" and think about the possible disadvantages in everything . 30. There are precedents in both the Mainland and overseas in formulating regulatory and development-promoting policies related to fintech, but the forms used are not the same, so we will study and refer to the experience of all aspects. As mentioned earlier, we will also communicate more with the industry to ensure that appropriate and balanced development and regulatory policies are proposed. "FinTech Promotion Office" 31. In the face of the various opportunities and challenges brought by Fintech to the financial industry and the public in Hong Kong, the HKMA has just set up the Fintech Facilitation Office (FFO) to fulfil our functions of maintaining financial stability and developing Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre. 32. The purpose of this office is to assist the fintech community in understanding the regulatory environment in Hong Kong and to promote the stable development of fintech in Hong Kong . We hope to support financial innovation while also safeguarding the public interest. 33. The work of the "Office" (FFO) is mainly carried out in three directions. 34. First, the Office will work with the industry to promote research on fintech so that the HKMA can better understand the characteristics, application potential and risks of individual fintechs, and help us examine how the financial community can apply these technologies more effectively and whether they should be subject to some form of regulation in the application process. Two of the key topics will be prioritized, namely the application of cybersecurity and blockchain technology. 35. I would like to add a little bit about cybersecurity. The Internet is the cornerstone of the fintech and digital world, as it is necessary to build cyber-systems based on security and vulnerability, and financial institutions need to be able to respond to and deal with the associated risks. 36. In view of this, the HKMA has embarked on the development of a cyber security plan for banks in Hong Kong Programme)? The program consists of three main parts: In the first part, we will develop a framework and model for assessing banks' ability to respond to cyber risks; In the second part, we will develop a training and certification program to provide a professional recognition mechanism for cyber security practitioners; In the third part, we will also work with the banking community to establish a new intelligence-sharing platform. 37. In the second direction of the FFO's work, the office will serve as an industry liaison and outreach platform to facilitate the exchange and interaction of fintech developers and founders, users and investors by organizing events such as symposia and conferences. 38. In the third direction, the Office will serve as a bridge and point of contact between the finTech industry and regulators, so that industry players can have a better understanding of the regulatory environment in Hong Kong and promote the launch of suitable and feasible new products and services in the market. 39. We have provided the email address of the dedicated liaison office on the HKMA's website. This is just the beginning. We will enhance communication, exchange and interaction with the industry through various channels. Summary: Regulatory principles - risk-based and tech-neutral 40. Finally, I would like to talk about the HKMA's regulatory principles for the application of financial technology. The regulatory principles adopted by the HKMA are "risk-based supervision" and "technology-neutral". That is to say, when we formulate and implement regulatory frameworks and norms, we will only base ourselves on the nature of financial activities or transactions and the risks arising therefrom, and will not make unreasonable exemptions or requirements because of the use of different technologies, so that market participants can operate in an environment conducive to innovation and fair competition. 41. Using technology to improve financial services is not new, and it has been a way for banks and other financial institutions to survive and win for decades. The only difference is that the development of financial technology has reached a new world and a new era in recent years. 42. In the new world of Fintech, the HKMA fully supports the banking and finance industry in developing and using the new section more and better to provide consumers with fast and diversified but safe financial services. The HKMA is willing to make appropriate arrangements for regulatory arrangements. 43. But at the same time, the HKMA will not abandon our protection of investors or users because of the rapid development of financial technology, as this is the responsibility of the HKMA. 44. The HKMA will be open to listening to the views of all parties and reviewing our work and regulatory framework so that the public can enjoy the benefits and conveniences of fintech without taking unnecessary or excessive risks. 45. Our newly established FinTech Promotion Office is currently in full swing and we will report back to the public on the progress of the work later. At the same time, we welcome all of you and all sectors to interact and discuss with the HKMA on the development and application of financial technology in Hong Kong . Thank you! Title: Hong Kong's Pivotal Role in Belt and Road Initiative
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 03 June 2016 Hong Kong plays an important role in the construction of the Belt and Road Initiative Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Speech at the Senior Bankers Seminar in Hong Kong) Honorable Chairman Shang Fulin, Governor Hu Heping, leaders and friends of the Shaanxi Provincial Government, and distinguished guests Hello everyone! Welcome to the seminar jointly organized by the Shaanxi Provincial Government, the China Banking Regulatory Commission and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA). First of all, I would like to express my heartfelt thanks to the Shaanxi Provincial Government and the China Banking Regulatory Commission for their warm and thoughtful reception. 2. I am very pleased to discuss with you today at Xi'an, the starting point of the ancient Silk Road, how Hong Kong can use its unique advantages to play an active role in the construction of the Belt and Road Initiative. Hong Kong's advantages 3. What are Hong Kong's advantages in implementing the national Belt and Road Initiative? Allow me to quote here the important speech made by Chairman of the National People's Congress, Zhang Dejiang, at the first Belt and Road Forum held in Hong Kong on May 18. The chairman of the committee said that Hong Kong is here The Belt and Road Initiative has many unique advantages, including: Hong Kong's location advantage as a transportation hub in the Asia-Pacific region and countries along the Belt and Road, Hong Kong's first-mover advantage in openness and cooperation as the world's freest economy, and Hong Kong's service industry specialization advantage as an international financial, shipping and trade center; and Hong Kong's cultural advantages as a place where Eastern and Western cultures meet. 4. At the same time, Chairman Cheung Tak Kong mentioned that the central government will support Hong Kong to play an active role in four aspects. First, active docking "Belt and Road", to create an integrated service platform; The second is to aim at financial integration, promote the internationalization of the renminbi and the construction of the "One Belt, One Road" investment and financing platform; The third is to focus on people-to-people exchanges and promote people-to-people ties along the "Belt and Road"; The fourth is to deepen cooperation with the mainland and jointly open up the "Belt and Road" market. Today, I would like to focus on the role that Hong Kong's financial sector and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority can play in promoting the Belt and Road Initiative. How Hong Kong's financial sector can support the Belt and Road Initiative? 5. As we all know, the infrastructure construction of many countries along the "Belt and Road" is relatively backward, which is also an important factor in the local economic development. Belt and Road countries have a lot of demand for infrastructure, but lack technology and capital; But at the same time, there is a lot of money in the market looking for a way out of investment. Over the past many years, there has not been much investment that can be introduced in many areas along the route, reflecting that in the case of huge infrastructure construction and financing needs, a large amount of idle savings and funds have not been effectively absorbed and used. This is a big gap that seriously hinders the economic development and improvement of people's livelihood in the areas along the route. However, this gap cannot be narrowed and improved, and the country's "Belt and Road" is an important strategy to break through this gap. As an international financial centre in Asia, Hong Kong can play an important role, as the Chairman said. 6. First, Hong Kong can become a major investment and financing hub for the Belt and Road Initiative, providing a large number of assets needed for infrastructure construction. Hong Kong is a world-leading equity market, bank lending and Asia's major private equity investment centre, as well as a thriving bond market, where public and private institutions are free to raise capital through a variety of channels such as public offerings, bond issuances and bank and syndicated loans. 7. Second, Hong Kong is the world's largest and most efficient offshore RMB business center, and in the process of implementing the "Belt and Road" strategy, the mainland's trade, investment, financing and economic ties with countries along the route will certainly be greatly enhanced, in addition to the use of US dollars In addition, the renminbi must and must be an option. Hong Kong will certainly be able to provide diversified offshore RMB business support for Mainland enterprises to embark on the Belt and Road Initiative . 8. Of course, I cannot fail to stress that in addition to the role of Hong Kong's financial industry, Hong Kong has a large number of professionals of international level Sufficient to support and manage the construction and operation of the infrastructure of the Belt and Road. Mainland enterprises go out to invest, merge and merge Construction projects often involve complex cross-border matters, including legal, contract drafting, accounting, tax administration, procurement, and research Research on development, logistics and transportation and personnel management. Hong Kong is an international asset management centre and a leading global business hub Provide a variety of professional service support. Background and purpose of the establishment of the Infrastructure Finance Facilitation Office ("IFFO"). 9. Now I would like to talk about the role that the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will play in implementing the Belt and Road Initiative. We are currently in the process of setting up an Infrastructure Finance Facilitation Office (IFFO) within the HKMA. IFFO was established to establish a new platform to bring together relevant stakeholders, including investors, banks and companies developing infrastructure projects, in the hope of promoting and promoting investment and related financing of infrastructure projects along the Belt and Road. The IFFO program officially launched next month, and we have now received a number of major stakeholders to join as IFFO partners. There are basically two types of partners: public and private. Multilateral development and policy banks such as the International Finance Corporation (IFC) under the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the China Development Bank, and the Export-Import Bank of China have agreed to become IFFO partners include the World Bank. In addition, some public international investors and development funds, such as the Canada Pension Investment Corporation (CPPIB) and the Silk Road Fund, have also agreed to join. Private sector partners include some major commercial banks, investment banks, private equity funds, professional service mechanisms, large asset management companies, etc. Private sector partners also include domestic and foreign companies with the capacity and experience to develop infrastructure projects. Due to the large number of partner institutions, I will not list them here. 10. IFFO will organise seminars, workshops and other events that bring together public and private partners with the aim of sharing information, knowledge and experience. We hope that through these exchange platforms, we can have a clearer understanding of the investment potential of the Belt and Road countries and the obstacles to foreign investment, so that the HKMA, together with some multilateral development agencies, can study and propose corresponding solutions, and discuss with the corresponding countries, hoping to promote reforms and make it easier for foreign capital to enter and participate in local infrastructure construction and achieve a win-win situation. conclusion 11. Dear leaders and distinguished guests, I hope and believe that Hong Kong can once again play a role in the country's economic development, especially to contribute to the implementation of the Belt and Road Strategic Plan. The HKMA established IFFO to meet this purpose. All of you here today are elites from the financial and related industries, and here we will discuss the important issue of "one belt and one road" infrastructure investment and financing. I look forward to a frank and constructive discussion and exchange with you today and wish this seminar every success. Thank you! Last revision date: 03 June 2016

Title: CE's remarks at the Launch ceremony of HSBC's Mobile Branch
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 23 June 2016 The Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Mr Chan Tak Lin, delivered a speech at the launching ceremony of HSBC Mobile Branch Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority President Wang Dongsheng, President Shi Yingyin, distinguished guests, and neighbors: I am so pleased to be at the launch of HSBC Mobile Banking today. 2. I have said on various occasions earlier that the HKMA has always been committed to promoting universal finance. The so-called popularization of finance means that all citizens at the grass-roots level should be able to obtain basic banking services. In my opinion, as an international metropolis and financial center, Hong Kong's demand for banking services by citizens, merchants and enterprises is as indispensable as food, clothing, housing and transportation. While providing diversified and high-end services and products, banks cannot neglect to take care of the general public's demand for basic banking services. So I am delighted to see HSBC officially launch its mobile banking service today, which can take care of residents in six PRH estates and beyond. I know that HSBC has plans to launch a few more mobile banking vehicles in more PRH estates, which will provide basic banking services that are more convenient than they are currently in communities with insufficient bank branch coverage. 3. At present, there are more than 1,100 branches of 22 retail banks in Hong Kong and about 5,600 self-service banking facilities, but coverage in some areas is still slightly insufficient. Therefore, I have always believed that the operating model of mobile banking can provide flexible arrangements for some more remote areas to meet the needs of the public for basic banking services such as account opening, deposits and withdrawals. 4. Times are progressing, society is changing, and the principles of universal finance can be applied to small businesses in general. Many of these small businesses are small businesses or family businesses, and they are in great need of opening accounts and receiving basic banking services in banks, whether they are in business or in business, otherwise they will not be able to operate. HSBC is rooted in Hong Kong and is the largest retail bank and banknote issuing bank in Hong Kong, and this launch of mobile banking reflects the principle of "customer-oriented", and I sincerely hope and believe that HSBC can play an active role in cooperating with the HKMA to promote "universal finance" in Hong Kong, benefiting the grassroots and the general public, and sharing the fruits of Hong Kong's economic and financial development. Thank you. Last revision date: 23 June 2016

Title: Remarks at the Signing Ceremony of BOCHK-ASTRI FinTech Collaboration Centre
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 14 Jul 2016 Speech at the signing ceremony of the Fintech Joint Innovation Centre of BOCHK-ASTRI Lee Tak Chi is Senior Assistant President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Director Zeng, General Manager Yue, Chairman Wang, distinguished guests, friends, It is a great honor to attend the signing ceremony of the "BOCHK 1ASTRI Fintech Joint Innovation Centre" today. As Secretary General Zeng just said, "financial technology" is a policy that the government attaches great importance to. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has also been supporting and encouraging banks to make good use of technology to enhance operational efficiency, improve service quality, and improve relevant financial infrastructure facilities and regulatory frameworks so that the public can benefit from the benefits of fintech. In the Budget read out in February this year, the Secretary mentioned that the HKMA and other regulators will set up a dedicated "fintech" platform to maintain communication with the industry. The HKMA then set up the Fintech Facilitation Office (r) (FFO) in March to coordinate related work. I'm happy to tell you that although the FFO has only been established for a few months, a lot of work has already been carried out. Specifically, it can be divided into the following three aspects: 95 First, to promote the research and application of financial technology. First, the HKMA President announced at the Cyber Security Summit in May that the Cyber Defence Scheme for the banking industry has been launched. The plan aims to further enhance the banking industry's ability to respond to cyberattacks and lay the foundation for the development of financial technology from the aspects of risk assessment, talent training and risk information sharing. The Cyber Defense Initiative is the FFO's "first shot" in promoting fintech research and application. Subsequently, the FFO has carried out research work on another important topic with the industry with the support of ASTRI, that is, the application of blockchain technology in different banking businesses, and we expect some phased progress in the coming months. 95 The second is to provide a platform to unite the strength of the industry and facilitate the development of financial technology. We hope that through seminars, workshops and other activities, fintech inventors, users and investors will come together to discuss the feasibility of new technologies to solve problems. We held our first FinTech Industry Gathering on "Cybersecurity" in June. About 200 people attended the day to discuss market developments, and the response was quite positive. We are also preparing to start another type of Programme Workshop in the coming months. Participating financial institutions can explain their business challenges to fintech companies and have them tailor solutions for them. Fintech companies can also showcase their results and explore co-op spaces with users or investors. We welcome organisations interested in participating in these workshops or programme workshops to contact me or my colleagues at FFO. 95 Thirdly, to communicate with the industry, in particular to help the industry better understand the HKMA's regulatory measures, and we can better understand their needs. The FFO has established contacts with a number of industry players through e-mail and meetings to explain the HKMA's regulatory work and introduce various activities to promote the development of the industry. In the future, we will also listen to the views of industry insiders on the work of the HKMA in different ways. The essence of "fintech" is to apply cutting-edge technology to different financial services. The test of kung fu is to integrate specialized knowledge at multiple levels. Therefore, close exchanges and cooperation between the financial and technology sectors are of paramount importance. BOCHK's partnership with ASTRI is proof that they value this. The HKMA will continue to play an active role in enhancing industry cooperation and exchanges, giving full play to the potential of Hong Kong's fintech and promoting the steady development of the industry. Thank you. Last revision date: 14 July 2016
