Title: Speech at the Launching Ceremony for the joint e-Cheque clearing between Hong Kong and Guangdong Province
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 22 Jul 2016 Speech at the press conference of Guangdong-Hong Kong e-Cheque Joint Settlement Business Lee Tak Chi is Senior Assistant President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. Honorable Governor Chen Yunxian, President Wang Jingwu, Deputy Inspector Zhang Ye, and distinguished guests. 2. Welcome to the Guangdong-Hong Kong e-Cheque Joint Settlement Business Launch Co-organized by People's Bank of China Guangzhou Branch and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority . 3. Guangdong Province and Hong Kong have always been neighbors with lips and teeth. With the active economic and commercial activities between the two places and the increasing demand for cross-border payment services from residents and enterprises in Guangdong and Hong Kong, it is particularly important to improve the interconnection of payment systems between the two places. The HKMA has been working closely with the People's Bank of Guangzhou and the People's Bank of Shenzhen to develop and launch a number of cross-border financial infrastructure facilities, including the networking of Hong Kong dollar and US dollar instant payment and settlement systems, and cross-border direct debit payment services in Hong Kong dollars and RMB. Now, we have further expanded our existing cross-border joint settlement service for HKD, USD and RMB cheques to cross-border electronic cheque settlement, making cheque business electronic in both places, which not only effectively improves payment efficiency, but also reduces operating costs. 4. After Hong Kong banks launched their e-Cheque service in December last year, there was a lot of public support and usage was on the rise. Over the past six months, more than 138,000 e-Cheques with a total value of HK4.2 billion were processed by Hong Kong Interbank Clearing Company Limited. At present, Guangdong Province and Hong Kong have joined forces to promote e-Cheque services to cross-border payments, facilitating e-Cheque settlement, cross-border payment and personal remittance activities by citizens and enterprises of the two places. 5. The use of e-cheques for cross-border payments has the following benefits compared to traditional cheques: - Sending cheques through electronic channels can shorten the delivery time, avoid postal delays and reduce mailing costs Use. 2. The online banking platform and the electronic cheque cross-border check-keeping platform operate 24 hours a day, and payers and payees can invoice and deposit invoices and deposits at any time through the online platform or mobile application. 3. Since the payee can receive and deposit the electronic cheque more quickly, the funds can be used earlier. 4. E-Cheques adopt stricter security measures to avoid the risk of cheques being altered or fraudulently signed. 6. According to the Guangdong-Hong Kong Cooperation Framework Agreement, one of the priorities in 2016 will be to explore the cross-border use and clearing of e-Cheques between Guangdong and Hong Kong. Thanks to your efforts, it took us only half a year to implement the cross-border e-Cheque service, and we expect that the number of banks accepting cross-border e-Cheques will gradually increase. 7. Today, I am very pleased to be able to participate in and witness the milestones of cross-border use of e-Cheques. I hope to take this opportunity to thank the Guangdong Provincial Government, the People's Bank of China Payment and Settlement Department, the People's Bank of Guangzhou, the People's Bank of Shenzhen, the two places of settlement companies and other units for their support, and hope that the banks of the two places can promote to customers and let them enjoy the convenience brought by electronic cheques. Thank you! Last revision date: 22 July 2016

Title: Remarks at the Launching Ceremony of BOCHK iService
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 05 Sep 2016 The Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Mr Chan Tak-lin, delivered a speech at the launching ceremony of the Bank of China (Hong Kong) "Dedicated Customer Service" Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority President Yue Yi, distinguished guests, neighbors, and media friends: I am so pleased to attend the inauguration ceremony of BOCHK at Shui Chun O Estate today. 2. In the past, the HKMA has been actively promoting the support and implementation of "universal finance" in Hong Kong's banking industry, hoping to further extend the coverage of the banking network to more remote areas, and has begun to see results. At present, there are more than 1,100 traditional bank branches of 22 retail banks in Hong Kong, as well as 5,700 ATMs and other self-service banking facilities. In addition, a number of retail banks have also used new technologies to launch facilities in some remote areas and PRH estates, including mobile branches and video ATMs, to meet the needs of the grassroots public for basic banking services and implement "universal finance". 3. I am delighted to see today the launch of BOCHK's "Dedicated Customer Service" at the newly completed Shui Chun O Estate, which can provide 24/7 banking services to the public at video ATMs with 24/7 banking services. Together with other facilities in the Self-Service Banking Service Centre, the Customer Service Centre can provide flexible banking services to residents of Shui Chun O Estate located away from the centre of Sha Tin to better meet the needs of the public for various basic banking services. 4. In addition, BOCHK is also currently actively expanding its SME business by "upgrading" all of their retail banking outlets to expand the service targets of branches from individuals to SMEs. In the past, SME customers of BOC were only allowed to open accounts and use banking services at some branches; BOCHK has now expanded its SME service coverage to all branches, enhancing its services to SMEs. Before coming to Shui Quan O Estate today, I also took the opportunity to visit BOCHK's branch at Good Luck Centre in Sha Tin to learn about the bank's actual operation after the enhancement of SME services, as well as to talk to SME customers and understand his recent operations. 5. Dear guests and neighbors, the principle of popularizing finance applies not only to the general public, but also to small businesses in general. In the future, I hope that Hong Kong's large banks, especially banknote issuing banks, will be able to take into account their social responsibilities and always provide appropriate and convenient banking services to the general public in the spirit of "customer-oriented". Thank you. Last revision date: 05 September 2016

Title: Making Hong Kong the top destination for corporate treasury in Asia
text: 19/09/22, 13:02 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Making Hong Kong the top destination for corporate treasury in Asia Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 21 Sep 2016 Making Hong Kong the top destination for corporate treasury in Asia Vincent Lee, Executive Director (External), Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Keynote Address at Asia Treasury Leaders' Forum) Peter (Matza), distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen: 1. Good morning. I would like to thank the Association of Corporate Treasurers for organising the Asia Treasury Leaders Forum in Hong Kong. Its the third time we have joined this hallmark regional forum which gathers together some of the best corporate treasury minds to dissect key trends and opportunities underpinning the industry. The fact that this forum has drawn more than 300 participants from the region is testament to the growing importance of Asia to multinational corporations. And, what better location for such a gathering! 2. Hong Kong has long-been the gateway for corporates expanding into and out of China. And this role has expanded exponentially in recent years. For example, in 2014, China's outward direct investment was in excess of US123 billion, of which nearly 58% came through Hong Kong; while in 2015, foreign direct investment into China amounted to US126 billion, with some 68% coming through Hong Kong as well. So, today, I would like to share with you three specific areas which reinforce Hong Kong's 'gateway' advantage. They cover the renminbi market in Hong Kong; facilitating infrastructure financing; and, finally, making Hong Kong the top destination for corporate treasury activities in Asia. Development of Hong Kong as a Premier Offshore Renminbi Hub 3. First, in relation to the renminbi, the reform of the yuan's exchange rate since August 2015 has resulted in more two-way movement of the exchange rate against other currencies. As a result, some market players have started to query whether the progress of China's capital account liberalisation will continue in the midst of such volatilities. However, from what we have observed, the answer is a definite, "Yes". In the past 12 months, the Central Government has continued to open up the country's capital accounts, and a number of new policies have also been introduced. These include: a) Last months approval of the Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect by the China Securities Regulatory Commission and the Securities and Futures Commission; and the immediate abolition of the existing aggregate quota under the Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect. These decisions will facilitate a greater flow of two-way equity investments between China and rest of the world through Hong Kong. b) In February, access by overseas institutional investors to the onshore interbank -2/ 1/7 19/09/22, 13:02 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Making Hong Kong the top destination for corporate treasury in Asia bond market was liberalised. And, since May this year, Mainland corporates have been able to obtain cross-border financing with a simplified registration process without the need for pre-approval from the regulators. 4. In addition, from the beginning of next month, renminbi will be included as one of the IMF's Special Drawing Rights currencies, signifying a greater international recognition of the renminbi as a 'widely used' and 'widely traded' currency. Indeed, more countries are considering including the renminbi as part of their foreign reserves. All these developments show that despite challenges in the foreign exchange market, there is continued momentum driving the capital account liberalisation process. 5. As such, Hong Kong is well-positioned to benefit from this trend. We are the world's largest offshore hub for renminbi business, with a liquidity pool of close to RMB 750 billion. More than 200 banks from all over the world are using our renminbi clearing platform to conduct a wide range of business activities. And, our platform responds to the global trends and continues to offer new products. For instance: a) Over the past few years, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange has launched a series of exchange-traded renminbi products to meet the market needs for standardised risk management solutions of the currency. b) And, in the first six months of this year, more than RMB 3.3 billion worth of fund units were sold to investors in Mainland China from Hong Kong through the Mainland- Hong Kong Mutual Recognition of Funds scheme. 6. Thus, the large suite of renminbi products allows Hong Kong to maintain its attractiveness for new fund flows, and its leading position as the world's largest offshore renminbi centre. 7. Indeed, a significant role of the HKMA is to promote offshore renminbi business development through securing the necessary policy headroom, facilitating liquidity management and building a robust infrastructure for conducting the business. To help make this possible, we have put in place a RMB400 billion currency swap agreement with the People's Bank of China, which can be activated when market conditions warrant. We have also made available renminbi liquidity facilities to banks in Hong Kong in the form of an intraday repo facility of RMB10 billion, and a bilateral repo line of RMB2 billion with each of the seven Primary Liquidity Providers. And to give you just one more impressive statistic, our renminbi real time gross settlement system, has been handling over RMB800 billion worth of transactions every day since July. Facilitation of Infrastructure Financing 8. Let me now turn to another key area of our work, also heavily linked to the China theme - infrastructure financing in relation to what is now commonly known as the Belt and Road Initiative. As you are no doubt aware, the initiative was announced by the Central Government in May last year to stimulate economic co-operation among countries along the Silk Road Economic Belt and 21st Century Maritime Silk Road. 9. One of the major goals is to promote connectivity in the region through the development of infrastructure. Asian Development Bank estimates put the overall infrastructure investment needs of Asia at US800 billion a year from now to the year 2020. Under the B&R Initiative, many Chinese corporates will be looking to invest in infrastructure projects in these countries. Hence, we believe the financing and fund management -2/ 2/7 19/09/22, 13:02 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Making Hong Kong the top destination for corporate treasury in Asia needs of the region will open up immense business opportunities for the financial sector. 10. To capitalise on this, the HKMA established the Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office, or IFFO, in July to expedite infrastructure investments and their financing by providing a platform for information exchange and experience sharing; building capacity and knowledge on infrastructure investments and financing; promoting market and product development; and facilitating infrastructure investment and financing flows. 11. So far, 41 organisations from Mainland China, Hong Kong and overseas have joined IFFO as Partners. They include multilateral financial agencies and development banks, public sector investors, private sector investors and asset managers, commercial and investment banks, infrastructure project developers and operators, and professional service firms. IFFO will continue to expand by inviting key stakeholders with deep experience in infrastructure investment and their financing to be our partners, particularly in greenfield projects and emerging markets. Development of Hong Kong into a CTC Hub 12. The third area I briefly referred to earlier, which reinforces Hong Kong's gateway advantage, relates to corporate treasury development. Today, corporates face both headwinds and tailwinds in their operating environment. I believe there are three key trends treasurers should pay attention to in order to mitigate the risks and optimise the benefits. And these are: a) The growing outward investment from China; b) The divergent monetary policies across economies; and c) The regulatory changes in the financial industry sector. Key Trends that drive changes in corporate treasury activities 13. First, the volume of outward investment from China stands at a high level under the 'Going out strategy as Mainland corporates express greater interest in foreign assets. In the latest 2016 Fortune Global 500 list, more than one out of five corporates is from China, showing many Chinese companies have already grown to the point where they are large enough to acquire these assets. According to PwC, in the 1st half of 2016, the transaction amount of China's overseas M&A activities reached US134 billion, almost a three-fold growth over the same period last year. 14. With the increasing international business exposure, these Mainland corporates are facing new challenges in international treasury management. This includes obtaining enough funding for cross-border acquisitions, centralising liquidity and risk management, and upgrading technology and systems for transactions on international markets. The demand for more sophisticated treasury management is, therefore, stronger than ever. More corporates recognise the value of having a corporate treasury centre, or CTC, to plan, co-ordinate, manage and control their international treasury activities. 15. Secondly, the diverging monetary policies of the major economies have made it more challenging for treasurers to manage liquidity. In the US, in the past 12 months, interest rate movement has lacked clear direction with fluctuating economic growth. Meanwhile, major economies like the Eurozone and Japan have gradually cut their interest rate targets to negative levels, resulting in some deposits becoming unattractive to financial 3/7 -2/ 19/09/22, 13:02 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Making Hong Kong the top destination for corporate treasury in Asia institutions. Treasurers need to be more nimble in managing their currency exposures to avoid interest costs arising from the negative rates, whiling exploiting opportunities to reduce financing costs for the corporates. To achieve these, corporates need to centralise their exposure and enhance their treasury operation efficiency to give treasurers an holistic view over their cash positions on a real time basis. 16. Thirdly, reforms on banking regulations continue to reshape the landscape of corporate treasury management. The introduction of BASEL III aims to improve the strength and resiliency of the global banking system. In effect, banks are required to meet new requirements in areas including capital management, liquidity management, market and counterparty credit risk management. Banks also have to face more stringent compliance and customer due diligence requirements. 17. These regulatory changes will have implications for the cost structure of banks as they offer treasury and risk management products to their customers. As a result, corporates may need to consolidate their banking relationships and work with those banks which can comprehensively satisfy their treasury requirements globally and take on the necessary compliance processes efficiently. What does this mean to the CTC platform of Hong Kong? 18. So, what does this mean for Hong Kongs corporate treasury centre platform? With all these external trends and changes, corporates have greater incentives to centralise their treasury operations for optimal management. And this is where our unique position comes into play. We are keen to attract multinational corporates from overseas and the Mainland to set up their global or regional treasury centres here. Attracting more of these activities to Hong Kong will stimulate more business opportunities for our financial services and deepen our capital markets. 19. That's why the HKMA has been working with marketing partners, such as banks, accounting firms, industry associations and government agencies, to showcase our CTC platform and the latest CTC tax regime which is designed to assist corporates. Over the past two years, we have met with over 280 parties, including more than 200 corporates, to promote Hong Kong as a regional hub for CTCs. From this interaction, we received much valuable feedback that helped us identify the challenges faced by corporate treasurers. We were then able to assess how the Hong Kong platform could help corporates meet these challenges. Key ingredients fora successful CTC operation 20. As a result, corporates agreed that Hong Kong had all the key elements for a successful CTC operation. And now, with your indulgence, I would like to quote from several corporate treasurers who have already established their CTCs in Hong Kong: The first is from an APAC treasurer of an international media company, and I quote, "our company prefers to work closely with our global banking partners in Hong Kong because these banks understand our business and have regional teams to co-ordinate the requirements across all countries." In another endorsement, an international treasurer of a Chinese energy company, says "Through the debt issuance process, we discovered that the Hong Kong market is very transparent, with very little restrictions compared to our home market." -2/ 4/7 19/09/22, 13:02 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Making Hong Kong the top destination for corporate treasury in Asia And, finally, a treasurer of a US electronics parts supplier told us: "We have renminbi exposure in China and we perform the hedging in Hong Kong. This is because Hong Kong does not have any FX control. And the CNH market in Hong Kong is highly liquid." 21. As you can see, this small sample of testimonials highlights some of Hong Kong's key strengths for a successful CTC operation: 22. First, our extensive network of corporate and investment banks. Around 70 of the worlds 100 largest banks have a presence in Hong Kong. So, whether you are a corporate trying to centralise all your regional treasury activities with a single bank to maximise efficiency, or a corporate seeking to diversify your portfolio of banking partners for the lowest cost provider, Hong Kong's banking market is able to provide the right solution to meet your corporate objectives. In addition, our capital markets are highly competitive and efficient. CTCs operating here are able to capitalise on the deep liquidity of our markets to lower their costs when obtaining financial or risk management products. 23. Secondly, our simple and transparent regulatory environment. Many corporate treasurers recognise that the absence of any capital or foreign exchange controls in Hong Kong facilitate their cross-border cash movements and for obtaining financing in foreign currencies. Hence, corporates can achieve their treasury objectives with minimal regulatory cost. 24. Thirdly, we are a regional hub for commercial activities and a home for many buyers and suppliers. Many of the corporates we spoke to had set up their supply chain hubs or regional headquarters in Hong Kong, and it was a natural progression to also establish their corporate functions, including CTCs, to closely support their business operations here. 25. Fourthly, Hong Kong, as I explained earlier, is a gateway to and from China. Many companies have leveraged on our position as the largest offshore renminbi centre and chosen to centralise their global renminbi positions in Hong Kong to tap our large liquidity pool. They also utilise the cross-border cash pooling structures between Mainland China and Hong Kong to move funds to and from the country. 26. And, last, but not least, our talent pool. With an abundance of trilingual finance and accounting professionals, there is little difficulty for corporates to hire the right staff. As you are well aware, throughout the process of establishing CTCs, corporates require external advice in areas like tax and treasury structures, systems integration and operating procedures. Hong Kongs professional services industry, including accounting and consulting firms, and the various technology solution providers, are invaluable in assisting corporates through this process. Hong Kong's CTC tax regime 27. But the assistance doesn't stop there. We already have a well-recognised low and competitive tax regime for commercial activities. But in order to attract more corporate treasury services and further develop our strengths as a CTC hub, the Government explored various options, including amending the Inland Revenue Ordinance to further improve the tax environment. And, I'm delighted to tell you the relevant legislation was passed and came into operation in June this year. 28. Under the Ordinance, the interest deduction rules have been amended so that interest expenses arising from genuine cross-border intra-group financing activities, under specified conditions, are now deductible. This will lower the overall tax cost and resolve -2/ 19/09/22, 13:02 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Making Hong Kong the top destination for corporate treasury in Asia the "tax asymmetry" issue currently perceived by some MNCs as an impediment to their establishing or expanding CTC operations in Hong Kong. 29. In addition, the qualifying profits derived from corporate treasury activities and transactions conducted by qualifying CTCs now benefit from a half-rate concession. In other words, the applicable tax rate has been cut from the current 16.5% to 8.25%. Broadly speaking, the scope of this concession encompasses corporate finance, liquidity management and risk management activities typically conducted by CTCs for their non-Hong Kong associated corporations. 30. In terms of the effective date, the half rate concession applies to relevant sums accrued on or after 1 April 2016 and the new interest deduction rule applies to interest payable on or after the same date, 1 April 2016. 31.1 would also like to highlight the fact that the tax regime is simple and transparent. There is no separate approval process for corporates to go through and for interest deductibility, any corporate can enjoy the deduction as long as the transactions meet the specific conditions. For the half-rate deduction, eligible corporates can elect into the regime during their annual tax filing. 32. As a result of the improved tax environment, some corporates have already made a move to review their treasury structures and consider conducting more corporate treasury activities in Hong Kong, such as cash pooling, financing and FX management. And we hope to convince even more of them to set up their CTCs here. 33. However, revising the tax regime does not mark the end of our work. It is an ongoing process as we strive to make the Hong Kong platform even more attractive. Indeed, some of you have expressed the view that we should do more to expand our double taxation relief network. Well, I can say that in 2009, there were only five countries in the network. Today, that figure has grown to 35 countries with another 13 under negotiation. And, the Government will continue in this direction, but I would like to add that while the number of DTAs is important, the quality of the DTAs also matters. Given that our agreements were negotiated more recently, we have more certainty in matching the latest developments in international tax standards, for example, the "Base Erosion and Profit Shifting Project, by the OECD. Closing 34. Ladies and gentlemen, I realise I have been on my feet for some little while - some might even say for too long! But, I always like to take the opportunity to promote Hong Kong's advantages whenever I can. There are certainly many changes on the horizon, creating a more complex operating environment for corporate treasurers. So, Im pleased to note the Forum will discuss other timely topics such as further liberalisation of the renminbi, Fin tech and treasury technology trends, and the implications of Brexit. I hope the upcoming sessions will inspire new ideas for treasury management, and I wish you all a very successful conference. Thank you. Title: Statement to the media
text: Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Statement by Norman T. L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to th... 19/09/22, 13:02 Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 15 Dec 2016 Statement by Norman T. L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the media on 15 December 2016 (Abridged version) Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Abridged version) As expected, the FOMC increased the Fed funds target rate by 25 basis points last night. While the Fed anticipated a gradual path of interest rate increases in the next three years, there remains considerable uncertainties over the pace of US monetary policy normalisation because of the following three factors: (i) the tightening labour market; (ii) rising energy and commodity prices; (iii) the fiscal policy of the incoming US administration. These three factors may have significant effects on inflation and inflation expectation going forward. Under the Linked Exchange Rate System, the Hong Kong Dollar interest rate will over time track the movements in the US dollar interest rate. Recently, the 1 -month HIBOR has increased from a low of 0.24% in early September to 0.66% yesterday. The rising trend is expected to continue to be affected by the scale of outflows from the Hong Kong Dollar, international developments, and other related factors, and it will be difficult to forecast precisely the pace of Hong Kong Dollar interest rate normalisation. Title: Statement to the media
text: 19/09/22, 13:01 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Statement by Norman T. L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to th... Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 15 Dec 2016 Statement by Norman T. L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the media on 15 December 2016 (Full version) Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Full version) 1. The FOMC decided last night to raise the Fed funds target rate by 25 basis points. This morning, the HKMA also raised the Base Rate of the Discount Window by 25 basis points to 1.00%. 2. While the Fed's move to raise rate yesterday was widely anticipated, the market focus has shifted to the pace of US monetary policy normalisation going forward. Although the Fed anticipated a gradual path of increases in the federal funds rate in the next three years, I believe we should pay attention to the following three factors influencing the US inflation and interest rate movements: i. The US labor market continued to strengthen, with unemployment rate in November declining to 4.6%, the lowest level in more than nine years. In the period ahead, the upward pressure on wages in the US might become more pronounced, which may translate into upward pressure on consumer prices; ii. Recently energy and commodity prices have stabilized and appeared to trend higher. This would exert rising pressure on consumer prices and inflation in the US. iii. The incoming US administration announced plans to cut tax and increase infrastructure spending. In the short run, the expectation of such policy changes may stimulate consumption and boost economic growth. 3. It is noticed that the 10-year US Treasury yields rose from a low of 1.36% in July to 1.83% before the US election, and have risen after the US election to a high of 2.57% recently. This reflects a shift in US inflation expectations in the market. 4. The pace of US monetary policy normalization is set to have some impacts on capital flows, exchange rates and asset prices in the global market. Under the Linked Exchange Rate System, Hong Kong has experienced a strong capital inflow since 2008, which amounts to over US130 billion. The Monetary Base has expanded substantially to HK1.6 trillion, which has provided the banking sector in Hong Kong with ample liquidity and drove the interbank interest rates to very low levels. Nonetheless, one would notice that the 1 -month HIBOR had already increased from a low of 0.24% in early September to 0.66% yesterday. If the USD interest rates continue to rise in the future, the interest rate differentials between the USD and the HKD will widen, and at some stage the widened interest rate differentials will lead to selling HKD/buying USD flows and the / 1/2 19/09/22, 13:01 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Statement by Norman T. L. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to th... HKD exchange rate will ease and consequently reach the weak-side Convertibility Undertaking rate of 7.8500. The Monetary Base will shrink gradually as a result, leading to increases in HKD interbank interest rates. However, the rising trend in the HKD interbank interest rates is likely to be gradual, depending on the scale of outflows from HKD, international developments and other related factors. It will be difficult to forecast precisely the pace of increases in HKD interest rates in the wake of considerable uncertainties over the path of US monetary policy normalization. 5.1 would like to remind the pubic to stay vigilant and prepare for the market volatility and risk that may arise from the normalisation of USD and HKD interest rates going forward. Last revision date : 15 December 2016 / 2/2

Title: Welcoming Remarks at the Launching Ceremony of the Fintech Career Accelerator Scheme
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech Dec. 16, 2016 Welcome speech at the launching ceremony of the FinTech Talent Development Program Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority President Shen Zuyao, President Huang Yushan, President Qian Dakang, Mr. Wang Mingxin, Chairman of the Academy of Sciences, and distinguished guests from universities and banks 1. Hello everyone! Today's line-up of guests is very strong: the heads of 11 banks and the presidents or senior representatives of 9 universities attended the ceremony in person, which is a rare event in Hong Kong in recent years, and it proves that everyone here is full of enthusiasm for the cultivation of fintech talents! 2. Following the establishment of the FinTech Promotion Office in March this year, the HKMA has worked to promote a number of fintech efforts, including the launch of the Cybersecurity Fortification Initiative, a cybersecurity initiative to enhance cybersecurity in the banking industry, and a Fintech Innovation Centre to encourage and support research and development. and provide regulatory flexibility in fintech regulatory sandboxes, etc. After just 9 months, the HKMA has worked seamlessly with different partners, including the Hong Kong Institute of Applied Science and Technology (ASTRI), which is present today. Now, Hong Kong's fintech ecosystem has finally made a little progress. 3. For Hong Kong's fintech ecosystem to develop well, it will require government policies, regulators and all stakeholders to work together to promote and cooperate, but in any case, I believe that everyone will agree that talent is the key to developing fintech. As I mentioned at the annual meeting of the Institute of Banking in September this year, the importance of soft power in developing Hong Kong as an international financial centre. Soft power is a core element of whether financial centers can stand out in the fierce competition, and talent is the key to the key. Therefore, without enough expertise to cooperate, the development of fintech will eventually become empty talk. 4. The old saying has clouds: "Ten years of trees, a hundred years of tree people", which means that training talents must be persistent in order to achieve results. Although this sentence is reasonable, in this Internet age, if we act with this "turtle speed", I am afraid that we will not even have the qualifications to look at people's backs! Therefore, we must not be sluggish, and we must change to the mentality of "ten years of tree people" to cultivate talents, in order to maintain Hong Kong's advantages as an international financial center. Of course, speed should also pay attention to quality, and we must not pick seedlings to promote growth. 5. Rome is not built in a day, talent will not emerge overnight, especially financial technology is a new thing, the number of professionals in this area is still limited, the international financial centers around the world are grabbing financial technology talents, I expect that the situation of "robbing talents" will only intensify, in the long run, we must cultivate more local professionals, in order to make the Hong Kong financial technology ecosystem continue to develop. 6. The financial services industry is broad and able to attract talents from different professional fields. As long as we regard the financial industry as the leading industry in Hong Kong and become bigger and stronger, it will drive the development of other industries and make significant contributions to the employment and economic development of the whole society. 7. The Fintech Career Accelerator Scheme (FCAS) offers banking internships for local university students who aspire to pursue careers in the financial technology industry. Different from the short-term internship positions in banks every summer vacation, the internship period of the "FinTech Talent Development Scheme" is 6 months or 12 months, which allows students to participate in specific financial technology project research in the actual working environment, learn practical experience, and be able to apply what they have learned. In addition, the HKMA and ASTRI will also provide courses and lectures to trainees to enhance their understanding of the scope of banking supervision and the latest fintech. 8. I believe that after completing this 6 or 12 months of training in Wooden Man Lane, the interns will inevitably increase their skills, which will be of great benefit to them whether they return to school to continue their studies or devote themselves to social work. For banks, this scheme can not only train young people for the society, but also allow banks to find suitable talents in advance, so as to facilitate future recruitment and recruitment. It's certainly a win-win arrangement. 9. Applications for the FinTech Talent Development Scheme will be available from 11 participating banks offering more than 70 internship positions and applications from 9 universities. The HKMA's FinTech Facilitation Office will also offer 3 internship positions. We will also hold an information day at the HKMA on 21 January next year so that students can directly inquire about the internship position from the bank, and the successful students will start their internship next summer. 10. Distinguished guests, the FinTech Talent Development Scheme is not simply a platform for career matching, but a training programme for Hong Kong's long-term soft power, and whether Hong Kong's financial centre can remain competitive in ten years depends on whether we have the determination and sufficient resources to cultivate relevant professionals today. 11. Finally, I would like to thank the distinguished guests of universities and banks for attending the launching ceremony of today's FinTech Talent Development Programme, which would not have been possible without your participation and support. Of course, I would also like to thank our partners Ying HKUST for providing the administrative and technical support required for the program. Thank you! Last revision date: December 16, 2016

Title: Opening Remarks at Hong Kong ICT Awards 2017: Best Fintech Award Presentation Ceremony
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 27 Mar 2017 Welcome speech at the 2017 Best FinTech Awards Ceremony Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Carrie, Michael, Herman, distinguished guests: Welcome to the HKMA for the Best FinTech Awards Presentation Ceremony 2017. The HKMA has always been committed to promoting the development of fintech in Hong Kong and this time it is the chief supporting organisation of the Best FinTech Award, demonstrating our importance to and support the fintech industry. 2. This year's entries are all 100% original financial technology works from Hong Kong, and the creativity, application, market potential and quality have reached a high level. A number of demonstrations of the award-winning works were arranged, and I am sure that all guests will agree that Hong Kong's fintech development is progressing more and more after enjoying them later. Fintech Talent Development Program 3. In the past year, the HKMA has launched a number of initiatives to foster the development of the fintech industry, including the establishment of the FinTech Facilitation Office (FFO), the launch of the Cyber Defence Scheme for the banking industry, the FinTech Regulatory Sandbox, and the establishment of a FinTech Innovation Centre. In addition, in December last year, we launched the Fintech Talent Development Scheme with 12 banks and 10 institutions of higher learning, which received more than 400 students applying for 100 of the Scheme internship positions, the response was quite enthusiastic. Interviews will be held one after another, and the recruited students will begin their internship for 6 months or 12 months as soon as this summer. In addition to this, I take this opportunity today to announce two new projects launched by FFOs. Fintech Brain Power Programming Accelerator 4. The first is for the HKMA and Cyberport to collaborate to set up the Haccelerator, giving banks a platform to organise the Hackathon and Accelerator ( Accelerator) competition. This platform can encourage more young friends to learn about fintech, and help banks explore innovative solutions, find talents, and even find partners. Fintech friends here should be familiar with these competitions, but I would like to make a brief introduction. First of all, the "Mental Hackathon", in general, is mainly for people who are interested in solving financial technology problems, including college students, or people who are passionate about innovative financial technology. Contestants are required to gather in a specific location within a limited time, usually a weekend, and use their brains to solve a fintech problem or pain point raised by the co-sponsoring bank to provide a solution. In order to buy time to "cross the bridge", the participants will not sleep, and the process of fighting until the last moment is very tense and exciting. 5. As for the "accelerator" race, the format is similar to the "Brain Hackathon", but the participation time is longer, ranging from 2 to 4 months. The participants are mainly start-ups, and the problems to be solved by the participants will be more comprehensive and complex than the mental hackathon. In addition to winning prizes, the winner may have the opportunity to discuss partnerships with co-sponsoring banks to further develop solutions. As for the details of the competition, you can pay attention to our future announcements. Digital Currency Research 6. The second FFO project I would like to announce is for the HKMA, together with three banknote issuing banks, Hong Kong Interbank Clearing Company Limited (HKICL) and the R3 Alliance to conduct research and proof-of-concept work on digital currencies issued by central banks. At present, a number of central banks are actively discussing and studying the digital currency issued by the central bank, a series of related issues arising therefrom, and the matters that policymakers need to pay attention to. Most of these studies have focused on "distributed ledger technology" (Distributed Ledger Technology, DLT). It is applied to the issuance of digital currency and its operating model. The issuance of central bank digital currency involves a series of complex issues, including system and network security, economic benefits, payment efficiency, law and privacy, platform governance, relevant regulatory requirements, and most importantly, the impact on the stability of the currency and financial system. At present, the advantages and disadvantages of the central bank's issuance of digital currency are still not fully established, and the HKMA has no specific plans to launch digital currency, but one of our main functions is to issue currency and maintain monetary stability, so we must take the initiative to understand this issue to decide what to do in the future. 7. We expect to complete the first phase of the central bank's study on the issuance of digital currencies by the end of this year, hoping to provide a preliminary analysis of the feasibility and advantages and disadvantages of using digital currencies for interbank payments and bond settlement in Hong Kong. At that time, we will announce the results of the research to you . 8. Distinguished guests, everyone here today is an important stakeholder in Hong Kong's financial industry, each with different expertise, but we share the same goal of making efforts and contributions to the promotion of financial technology in Hong Kong. 9. Thank you again for your presence and support of today's ceremony. Last revision date: 27 March 2017

Title: Statement by Norman T.L. Chan Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the media
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 10 Apr 2017 The President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Chan Tak-lin, addressed the media on 10 April 2017 Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority First of all, I would like to thank the Financial Secretary and other directors of the mortgage company for their support of the annuity scheme. 2. I would like to start by talking about three important prerequisites and principles for designing this annuity plan: Annuity products should be simple and easy to understand, and must have a certain degree of attractiveness to the insured; ?. Mortgage companies should be able to carefully manage the risks associated with their products, especially the return on investment; ?. The plan needs to be in line with business principles and be financially practical and sustainable. 3. According to the above principles, mortgage securities companies offer fixed monthly annuities of the guaranteed amount for Hong Kong residents aged 65 or above, who can withdraw instantly and can collect a guaranteed amount during their lifetime. This product is basically not available on the market at present. 4. According to the mortgage company's current preliminary estimates, the internal rate of return of a fixed monthly annuity may be in the range of 3% to 4%. It is believed that if the internal return rate is less than 3%, the plan may not be attractive, and the risk of more than 4% is difficult to control. Mortgage securities companies will endeavour to provide the best monthly annuity for policyholders while maintaining the financial viability and continuity of the plan Flat. It is currently estimated that if a man is insured at 65 years old and the internal rate of return is about 4%, the premium forecast for every HK100,000 per month is expected to receive a fixed annuity of about HK5,800 per month, or about HK70,000 per annum (annuity ratio of about 7%) )? 5. To make annuity plans more attractive, mortgage companies offer 105% death protection and early exit mechanisms and protection for policyholders. 6. In terms of risk management, the main risks involved in providing annuity plans are longevity risks and investment return risks, of which controlling investment return risks is of paramount importance. The mortgage securities company is discussing with the HKMA the transfer of premiums collected under annuity schemes to the Exchange Fund for management, with reference to arrangements for the Exchange Fund to manage financial reserves such as the Future Fund. This arrangement is mutually beneficial Pai: This will benefit the programme from the experience and benefits of HKMA's investment team, while supporting the Exchange Fund to play its role in stabilizing the financial market. 7. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee has been informed of the recommendation of mortgage securities companies to introduce a life annuity scheme. The proposal of the mortgage securities company is initially considered feasible and worthy of support. 8. Next, the mortgage securities company will carry out a series of implementation work at full speed, starting with the independent consultant to further verify the annuity level and risk assessment, finalize the details of the plan, and apply to the insurance regulatory authorities for approval, obtain HKMA's support for premium investment management and capital, organize sales networks, prepare education and publicity activities, etc. The scope of these efforts is very broad, and mortgage companies will go all out to launch the plan in the middle of next year Scratch. Chan, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the media on 15 June 2017 Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority The FOMC increased the fed funds target rate by 25 basis points last night, the third time in the past seven months. This suggests that the process of US interest rate normalisation is gathering momentum. The Fed has also announced its plan to reduce its balance sheet this year, including the size and pace of reduction. I believe once the Fed starts to reduce its balance sheet, market liquidity will be tightened gradually. We notice that the HKD exchange rate has recently eased to the level of around 7.80 due to widened interest rate differentials between HKD and USD. If the interest rate differentials widen further, there will be more arbitrage activities involving fund flows from HKD to USD. Interest rate is one of the important factors affecting the property market. The current property market cycle is different from the cycle in 1997. In 1997, the downturn in property market coincided with a downward cycle of interest rates, with mortgage interest rates falling from over 10% to 3-4%. This time round a downward property market cycle may coincide with an upward cycle of mortgage interest rates. I would like to remind everybody that they should remain vigilant and manage risks prudently. Last revision date : 15 June 2017 / 1/1

Title: Opening Remarks at the Briefing-cum-Networking Session on Bank Account Opening and Maintenance for SMEs and Start-up Companies
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 23 June 2017 Welcome speech at the "Opening and Maintaining Bank Accounts for SMEs and Start-ups" Seminar Nguyen Quoc Heng is a Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Dr. Chua, Director Zhen, and distinguished guests, 1. Welcome to today's SME and start-up Bank Account Opening and Maintenance Seminar jointly organised by the Small and Medium-sized Enterprises Committee of the Trade and Industry Department and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. I especially welcome about 100 representatives from local chambers of commerce, professional organisations and the banking industry to participate in today's event to discuss the "difficulty of opening an account" that everyone is concerned about. 2. Over the past few years, the international community's anti-money laundering requirements have become increasingly tight, and the international banking system has accordingly tightened the requirements and standards for customer due diligence. Under this general trend, Hong Kong cannot go against the grain. At the same time, some international banks are also required to comply with the relevant regulations or standards of their headquarters or overseas authorities for various reasons, resulting in risk-averse situations. I believe that everyone understands that today's market situation is more complex than before, and banks and customers need to adapt and cooperate. Of course, it's one thing to understand this, and it's another thing to feel when you're affected. 3. The HKMA is quite concerned about the difficulties encountered by enterprises in opening accounts and has been working with banks, the business community and relevant parties to deal with the situation for some time. Our goal is to maintain a robust anti-money laundering regime in Hong Kong without compromising access to basic banking services for legitimate businesses and the general public. After engaging with the business community and referring to the specific cases collected in question, the HKMA issued guidance to banks in September last year, setting out our consistent requirement that banks should adopt an effective risk-based approach to implement customer due diligence measures, implement controls commensurate with their risk level for individual customers, transactions or services, and maintain good communication with customers in the process, be transparent, Rationality and efficiency enable customers to be treated fairly. We have also clarified to banks some customer due diligence requirements that are often misinterpreted. For example, the HKMA does not require corporate clients to have two or more directors or even all of them present at the same time when opening an account. In addition, it has been pointed out that some banks will require customers to purchase financial or investment products as a prerequisite for opening a bank account, and we have also made it clear to the industry that this is an unacceptable practice. Banking representatives will later provide an update on some of the improvements they have implemented, as well as practical tips on opening and maintaining bank accounts. 4. In order to provide more comprehensive information on bank account opening and account maintenance, and to collect relevant comments and answer questions more proactively, the HKMA launched a special page on its website at the end of March, as well as a dedicated email to facilitate the public and enterprises to reflect their views to the HKMA. The HKMA page covers information including the procedures for opening and maintaining bank accounts, the required documents and information, the bank's contact information, as well as listing some things that banks should not do, and providing some practical tips for customers who are refused to open an account. The webpage also has a "What's New" column, which details the latest initiatives of banks in opening and maintaining accounts. Since the launch of the dedicated email at the end of March, a number of useful comments and enquiries have been received, which have been followed up and replied to by the HKMA's Task Force. Some foreign and local chambers of commerce recently indicated to us that the arrangement of special pages and dedicated emails on the HKMA website provides useful information channels, so they have also provided links in their member newsletters or the Chamber of Commerce webpage to assist in further promoting the HKMA's special pages. I suggest that you may also wish to browse and introduce your members to the HKMA page for useful information. 5. In fact, in response to the HKMA's guidance and the comments of customers, the banking industry has taken some corresponding measures in the past year, and it has been some time since then, and it is time to take a look at the latest developments. I would like to give you a few examples, such as if a bank has set up an account opening hotline, and the relevant trained frontline staff will handle inquiries and make account opening arrangements. In addition, most retail banks in Hong Kong currently have a "pre-review" procedure, which means that the applicant can request the pre-submission of the required account opening information and documents to the bank by email, fax or mail, and the bank will arrange a meeting with the applicant after the preliminary review. This helps to reduce the number of times applicants need to go to the bank in person to submit information and documents. 6. The HKMA is also actively exploring the use of innovative technologies with the banking industry, such as the introduction of the Professional Information Institution platform to enhance the efficiency of bank account opening and maintenance, and other innovative technologies to facilitate remote account opening. You've probably heard of it The term "professional information agency" platform is a third-party platform designed to centrally manage customer data to reduce repeated submission of data by customers and reduce the cost of bank compliance, and to assist banks in managing risks. For example, if a customer applies to several banks to open an account, if they are centrally contacted with the bank through a "professional information agency", the customer does not need to submit the same information or documents to each bank repeatedly. We have had many discussions with major banks and relevant technology providers, and some progress has been made. At the same time, we understand that several banks are considering using innovative technology to open accounts remotely. 7. The comments we have received recently from different sources indicate that bank account opening has improved, and I hope you will feel the same way. While the customer experience is improving, we understand that work is still ongoing. The HKMA will continue to cooperate and communicate with the banking industry and the business community to face this global and very complex issue. If you have any ideas and comments, please feel free to present them at the next seminar, or to speak with the bank representatives present after the meeting, or to provide us with comments using the HKMA's special page and dedicated email. 8. Finally, I hope that this exchange symposium will provide you with useful information on this important topic. Next, we welcome Dr. Tsai Kwan Shen, Chairman of the Small and Medium-sized Enterprises Committee of the Trade and Industry Department, to deliver a speech to us. 9. Thank you. Last revision date: 23 June 2017

Title: Speech at the Launching ceremony for cross-boundary electronic bill presentment and payment between Hong Kong and Guangdong Province
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 27 June 2017 Guangdong-Hong Kong cross-border electronic direct payment business joint press conference speech Lee Tak Chi is Senior Assistant President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. Distinguished Director Gan, Director Fan, President Wang, and distinguished guests. 2. Welcome to the Guangdong-Hong Kong cross-border electronic direct payment business joint conference organized by People's Bank of China Guangzhou Branch and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority . 3. 2017 is a key year for Guangdong and Hong Kong to strengthen financial cooperation and achieve mutual benefit and win-win results. In this year's government work report, Premier Li Keqiang proposed to promote the deepening of cooperation between the mainland and Hong Kong and Macao, study and formulate a development plan for the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, and build a world-class city cluster. Guangdong and Hong Kong have always maintained close ties in economic and trade cooperation and cultural exchanges, and the flow of people, logistics and capital between the two places has become more and more active, which not only combines each other's advantages to play their strengths, but also creates a beautiful atmosphere for the development of the Greater Bay Area. 4. All along, Guangdong and Hong Kong have spared no effort to promote the integration of Guangdong and Hong Kong, which has brought great benefits to the economic development of the two places. As of the end of 2016, Hong Kong's total FDI in Guangdong Province amounted to US255.9 billion, accounting for 63.8% of Guangdong's total, with a total of about 140,000 Hong Kong-funded enterprises approved to operate in Guangdong Province. In 2015, the total import and export trade between Guangdong and Hong Kong was US210 billion. The movement of people between the two places is also very frequent, with an average of more than 600,000 passengers and 43,000 vehicles passing through Guangdong and Hong Kong every day in 2015. The integration of Guangdong and Hong Kong is truly reflected in the daily lives of many residents. 5. This year marks the 20th anniversary of Hong Kong's return to the motherland, and with the close cooperation of the Guangzhou People's Bank and the HKMA, Guangdong and Hong Kong have witnessed vigorous development in the field of financial infrastructure cooperation. In 2004 and 2009 respectively, we launched real-time payment systems for the Hong Kong dollar and US dollars and cross-border RMB trade settlement, which improved the efficiency of cross-border payments by financial institutions and enterprises in the two places. Since 2000, we have also expanded cross-border payment instruments to physical cheques and cross-border direct debit payments in phases, and launched Guangdong-Hong Kong cross-border electronic cheques in 2016 to further facilitate payment for residents of the two places . 6. The Guangdong-Hong Kong cross-border electronic direct payment service is now launched, making it easier for Hong Kong people to pay bills from merchants in Guangdong Province. They can pay water bills and chargeable TV charges directly to merchants in Guangdong Province anytime and anywhere through the online or mobile platforms of Hong Kong banks. They can also check the full payment records through the bank's online or mobile platform without worrying about over-deduction of their accounts. I hope that the banks of the two places will continue their efforts to promote this convenient cross-border bill payment business to customers and merchants, so as to gradually expand the coverage of the service. 7. Finally, I would like to take this opportunity to thank the Guangdong Provincial Government and the Guangzhou People's Bank of China for their policy support, as well as the cooperation of the settlement companies and other units of the two places, which have promoted the smooth launch of the Guangdong-Hong Kong cross-border electronic direct payment business. I hope that Guangdong and Hong Kong will continue to deepen their cooperation and contribute to the improvement of financial infrastructure facilities between the two places and to the promotion of the development of the Greater Bay Area. Thank you! Last revision date: 27 June 2017

Title: Opportunities for Hong Kong Financial Sector Brought by Demand in Infrastructure Financing and RMB Internationalisation under Belt and Road Initiative
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 28 June 2017 The demand for infrastructure investment and financing under the Belt and Road Initiative and the internationalisation of the renminbi have brought opportunities to Hong Kong's financial sector Yuu Wai Man is a Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Theme at the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China - Cross-border Financial Services Forum and Strategic Partner Signing Ceremony: Shuttle Convergence Achievement Opportunities). Chairman Yi Huiman, Deputy Director Qiu Hong (Liaison Office), Deputy Director Leung King Kwok, (Chairman of the Hong Kong Tourism Board) Dr Lam Kin Yuek and Distinguished Guests: Hello everyone. Thank you Chairman Yi for inviting me to attend today's Cross-Border Financial Services Forum hosted by Industrial and Commercial Bank of China. There are still three days to go, and we will usher in the great anniversary of Hong Kong's return to the motherland, and it is of special significance for us to gather here today to discuss the opportunities for cross-border integration between Hong Kong and the mainland . Next, I will focus on three aspects of the development opportunities that the Belt and Road Initiative brings to Hong Kong: First, how can Hong Kong cooperate with the Belt and Road Initiative and give full play to the unique advantages of an international financial centre; The second is the development opportunities brought about by the "Belt and Road" and the internationalization of the renminbi; The third is how Hong Kong's financial industry can seize opportunities and make contributions. How can Hong Kong give full play to its unique advantages as an international financial centre? Promoting infrastructure construction along the Belt and Road is the top priority of the Belt and Road Initiative. According to estimates by the Asian Development Bank, from 2016 to 2030, Asia's infrastructure development will require an annual investment of 1.7 trillion, which is a huge capital need The financial input of the public sector alone is not enough, so it is necessary to broaden the sources of funding and to use and encourage the participation of private institutions. As a leading international financial center in Asia and the world's largest offshore RMB business hub, Hong Kong has always been a window for overseas enterprises to invest in the Mainland and a springboard for Chinese-funded enterprises to go global. With the promotion and implementation of the Belt and Road Initiative, Chinese enterprises' investment in overseas will continue to accelerate, and it is foreseeable that Hong Kong's role as a springboard will become more prominent. Among them, it has unique advantages in promoting infrastructure investment and financing, and can play an active role in fund raising, project matching, risk management, professional support and other aspects. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority set up the Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office (IFFO) last July, marking its first anniversary. IFFO was established to foster infrastructure investment and financing by building a platform that brings together key stakeholders to get to know each other, exchange information and share experiences. We have successfully brought together more than 60 broadly represented partners, including multilateral financial institutions and development banks, public and private institutional investors, large asset management companies, major banks including ICBC, as well as insurance companies, institutions involved in the development and operation of infrastructure projects, accounting and legal professional services firms, and international trade associations. After one year of efforts, IFFO has become a high-level, representative and pragmatic infrastructure financing promotion platform. Over the past year, IFFO has held events on the themes of managing investment risks and connecting project financing. In March this year, we hosted a high-level round table of investors and financiers with total assets of US4 trillion, development and commercial banks, as well as infrastructure project development agencies and operators. Based on the strong interest of institutional investors in infrastructure financing, and taking into account the concerns of these institutional contributions, one of the major outcomes of the roundtable was the development of a "Reference List for Infrastructure Investment", which lists the risks that may be involved in various types of infrastructure investment and the corresponding mitigation measures, so that infrastructure project developers as investors can respond more specifically to the concerns and demands of investors. It also helps to strengthen investor confidence in entering emerging markets. With this list, IFFO will further communicate with the developers of specific infrastructure projects and the relevant authorities of the project location, and deal with the issues of investors' risk appetite and mitigation measures in the investment introduction process. For example, many investors feel hesitant about the political and commercial risks of greenfield projects. To "de-risk" a project, there are ways and strategies to reduce risk, such as "packaged" greenfield projects with other "brownfield projects" that already operate and have cash income. In addition, infrastructure developers and operators in the project location need to improve corporate governance, because most international investors pay great attention to project arrangements such as governance, environmental protection, procurement processes, and anti-corruption measures in addition to focusing on the return on project investment. In addition, investors from different backgrounds can also explore cooperative investment, share or even reduce risks through complementary advantages. IFFO will consider pushing partners to create an Equity Club to build an investment mechanism based on mutual benefit for a number of reputable, long-term and like-minded international institutional investors. Selecting suitable infrastructure projects, sharing information and investment opportunities, and cooperating in investment can play a role model in promoting private capital participation in infrastructure projects. (-) "The development opportunities brought about by the Belt and Road Initiative and the internationalization of the renminbi Next, I would like to talk about the development opportunities brought by the Belt and Road Initiative to the internationalization of the renminbi. In May this year, the Belt and Road Forum for International Cooperation was held in Beijing, proposing to encourage mainland financial institutions to carry out RMB overseas fund business and actively play the role of local currencies, including RMB, in the construction of the Belt and Road Initiative. The advancement of the Belt and Road Initiative will certainly bring huge infrastructure investment and financing activities to the regions along the route, and mainland funds and enterprises, as important participants in the promotion, will have more opportunities to use RMB as a project financing, pricing and transaction currency in the process. The 13th Five-Year Plan supports Hong Kong in strengthening its position as a global offshore RMB business hub. After rapid development in recent years, Hong Kong's RMB business platform has become increasingly mature, providing comprehensive and efficient supporting services for RMB trading in the international market. According to the Society for Global Banking and Financial Telecommunications (SWIFT), about 70% of the world's RMB payment transactions are currently processed through Hong Kong, demonstrating Hong Kong's key role in international RMB transactions. Hong Kong has the world's largest offshore RMB pool, the most active offshore RMB market, and has a rich circus in promoting the interconnection of the Mainland and Hong Kong's capital markets Since the opening of Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect and Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect, the circulation channels and related infrastructure of the two places have been smooth, and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is currently working intensively to closely communicate with relevant mainland institutions and Hong Kong industries to prepare for the launch of Bond Connect, adding an important component to the interconnection of capital markets between the two places. I believe that Hong Kong can continue to leverage its pioneering edge as an offshore RMB centre by providing RMB financing, settlement, asset management and risk management services, providing strong support and impetus for enterprises and investors to widely use RMB along the Belt and Road. How can the financial industry seize opportunities and contribute? Although Hong Kong has advantages in connecting the mainland and the international markets in terms of finance, commerce, and so on, we must keep a sober mind, grasp the changes in the situation, conform to the development of the market, and even more actively grasp the opportunities. The Belt and Road Initiative and the internationalization of the renminbi are all stages on which Hong Kong's financial industry can show its strength. As an international financial center, asset management center and enterprise treasury center, Hong Kong should continuously consolidate and integrate resources on the basis of the original, provide financial intermediary services with higher value and better efficiency, and serve as a safe and efficient fund management and risk management center for funds entering and leaving the mainland. I am confident that with the new wave of global infrastructure investment and financing, Hong Kong's financial industry can seize development opportunities with diversified services and products with international standards, promote the development of financial intermediation and related professional service chains, create more high-value-added positions, and provide a steady stream of impetus for the sustainable development of Hong Kong's economy and society. In conclusion, I wish today's forum every success. Thank you. Last revision date: 28 June 2017
