Title: Challenges in Infrastructure Financing, Belt and Road Opportunities, and The HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office (IFFO)
text: 19/09/22, 13:01 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Challenges in Infrastructure Financing, Belt and Road Opportunities, and The HKMA Infrastru... Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 07 Jul 2017 Challenges in Infrastructure Financing, Belt and Road Opportunities, and The HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office (IFFO) Vincent Lee, Executive Director (External), Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Panel Discussion on Investment Collaboration - Opportunities & Challenges in Asia at the 2017 Colloquium on International Law) 1. Good afternoon Professor Dr Surakiart (Sathirathai), Mr (Gerard) Sanders, Mr (Dieter) Yih, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen. 2. It is indeed a pleasure to be here today to take part in this panel discussion which examines a subject that is crucial to the development of our region. And, I would like to sincerely thank Professor Teresa Cheng for inviting me to the Colloquium. The very title of the panel discussion, "Investment Collaboration - Opportunities and Challenges in Asia", embraces the subject that we have been exploring for a while - the challenges in infrastructure financing, the opportunities in the Belt and Road Initiative, and the recent establishment of the HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office, or IFFO as we like to call it, which helps to facilitate investment collaboration in this region. Challenges in infrastructure financing 3. As you may be aware, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) recently raised the infrastructure funding needs in this region from the previous estimate of US800 billion a year to a new estimate of US1.7 trillion a year from 2016 to 2030. To appreciate how enormous this number is, Hong Kong's entire GDP in 2015 was worth US309 billion, which is less than 2% of the yearly infrastructure funding needs in this region. The power sector alone represents more than half of this infrastructure funding need, followed by the transportation sector. These are basic yet important infrastructures for the development of any economy. 4. Among many sophisticated investors, there is a growing desire to invest their money in infrastructure projects because they have the potential to offer more stable and higher returns over a longer term - think of power plants as just one example. But while there are substantial funding needs for infrastructure projects and a growing interest in the infrastructure asset class, there is a lack of "bankable projects, particularly in emerging markets, including many parts of Asia. 5. This is not hard to understand. At the country level, political, legal and regulatory risks often undermine the feasibility of a project. At the project level, construction risk, cost overrun, demand risk, currency risk, and refinancing risk all add uncertainty to the project's profitability. Funding of cross-border or regional projects becomes even more challenging as these risk factors are magnified. Because of these risk factors, / 1/5 19/09/22, 13:01 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Challenges in Infrastructure Financing, Belt and Road Opportunities, and The HKMA Infrastru... according to the International Finance Corporation, only around 20% of the total annual infrastructure spending in emerging economies is financed by private funding. 6. Indeed, 80% of the infrastructure spending in emerging economies has come from the public sector, such as governments and multilateral development agencies. Historically, these bodies are well equipped to invest in infrastructure projects partly because they can better mobilize long-term funding to invest in these projects. In fact, multilateral development agencies, such as the World Bank, have also acquired the expertise to deal with the country and project risks that I just mentioned. National governments and multilateral development agencies are also seen as having more tools, political or otherwise, at their disposal to deal with situations like non-performing loans. 7. Nevertheless, public sector financing has its limits as well. The balance sheets of the multilateral development agencies alone are simply too small relative to the needs of infrastructure financing. And, many national governments which traditionally sponsor overseas economic developments are now faced with increasing fiscal constraints. The trend that has clearly emerged in recent years is to encourage more private sector involvement in infrastructure financing. However, this is easier said than done. A recent report jointly published by the OECD and the World Bank Group1 notes that the costs and risks faced by private investors in infrastructure remain high. The report suggests that some of the issues facing these investors could be addressed by establishing national infrastructure plans, providing risk mitigation tools, promoting investor education and the pooling of funds. Hence, the key challenge here is how to make these infrastructure projects more "bankable" from the private sector point of view. I will come back to this point later. Belt and Road opportunities 8. China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) probably needs no introduction here. So, I will go straight to three areas where I think the implementation of BRI will provide opportunities for Hong Kong. 9. Firstly, as I am sure you are aware, more and more Chinese corporates are already investing overseas. This process will be given further impetus by the BRI implementation. In 2015, China's overseas direct investment, or ODI, reached US146 billion; with Hong Kong the largest recipient of over 60% of the total. Indeed, Chinese corporates are already using many of Hong Kong's intermediary services, such as legal and banking to support their overseas acquisitions and other investments. Despite some recent concerns about capital outflows, I am confident that this going-out trend by Chinese corporates will resume, and this will bring more business opportunities to Hong Kong. 10. Secondly, BRI is about building connectivity. As China continues to build closer economic ties with Belt and Road countries, the case for transactions in renminbi (RMB) will be even stronger, which will further strengthen internationalization of the currency. In particular, it will boost the RMB as a reserve currency; that is, I expect more Belt and Road countries' central banks will be willing to hold more RMB. And, I also expect the RMB to be used more often as a trade currency and investment currency between China and these Belt and Road countries. As you are no doubt aware, Hong Kong is the largest and most developed offshore RMB business centre. We have the largest pool of RMB deposits anywhere outside Mainland China, and also more than 200 banks in Hong / 2/5 19/09/22, 13:01 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Challenges in Infrastructure Financing, Belt and Road Opportunities, and The HKMA Infrastru... Kong are already capable of conducting RMB business. Therefore, Hong Kong is well- positioned to capture RMB business opportunities arising from the BRI. 11. Thirdly, at the Belt and Road Forum on International Co-operation in May, President Xi Jinping announced that China will provide a total of RMB780 billion to support implementation of the BRI. For example, the Silk Road Fund will be increased by RMB100 billion, and about RMB300 billion has been earmarked to encourage Chinese financial institutions to conduct overseas RMB business. In addition, support will be given to the China Development Bank worth RMB250 billion and to the Export and Import Bank of China worth RMB130 billion to set up special lending schemes to support Belt and Road co-operation, including infrastructure2. So, it goes without saying, the HKMA will be doing all it can to encourage these institutions to make more use of Hong Kong when conducting their Belt and Road businesses. 12. Despite this state support, I believe the Chinese authorities would also like encourage the private sector to play a bigger role in financing the BRI implementation because the state, on its own, cannot address all the financing needs arising from this massive initiative. Indeed, Hong Kong has some of the best privately run companies in the world; and here again opportunities are in abundance for us. IFFO and how it helps to facilitate investment collaboration in Asia 13. IFFO was established in July last year with a mission to expedite infrastructure investments by working with key stakeholders in infrastructure financing. To date, IFFO has built a network of over 60 entities which come from Hong Kong, the Mainland and overseas, covering multilateral financial agencies and development banks, public and private sector investors, asset managers, banks, infrastructure project sponsors, professional service firms, etc. 14. IFFO is uniquely positioned to facilitate investment collaboration in the following ways. Firstly, we have built strong relationships with our Chinese friends like the Silk Road Fund, the China Development Bank and project developers. In talking to some of them, they often mention they'd like to network with their overseas counterparts and share views on the best practices in corporate governance and risk governance when making investments. IFFO is a useful meeting place for our partners from the East and the West. Indeed, since our launch last year, IFFO has organized and participated in more than 10 prominent international and local events on infrastructure financing, including our first executive workshop last October, and the inaugural Debt Financing and Investors' Roundtables in March this year. Looking ahead, IFFO will continue to collaborate with our partners to build capacity and make Hong Kong a more attractive place to conduct infrastructure investment and financing. 15. Secondly, IFFO consists of many private sector representatives and can uniquely offer private sector views on infrastructure financing. The Roundtables held in March gathered together capital owners, including sovereign wealth funds and pension investors from around the world, as well as project developers and operators, to discuss infrastructure investment and financing opportunities in emerging markets; and how infrastructure projects could be made more bankable through different risk mitigation measures. A reference term sheet for infrastructure investment was developed at the Roundtables, which sought to devise a set of common language terms that can be understood and accepted by investors, financiers and sponsors, thereby narrowing the / 3/5 19/09/22, 13:01 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Challenges in Infrastructure Financing, Belt and Road Opportunities, and The HKMA Infrastru... gap in their expectations and bringing them closer to doing deals. The term sheet set out various major factors to be considered for infrastructure investments. For example, as investors tend to be more interested in less-risky brownfield projects, the attractiveness of greenfield projects can be increased by securing land and approval documentation, or by bundling with brownfield projects. Another example is that since institutional investors also attach great importance to governance procedures, infrastructure project operators should put in place such essentials as proper procurement systems and effective anti-corruption policies. Roundtable discussions and the reference term sheet can help make projects more bankable, and strengthen the confidence of investors looking for long term sustainable returns when investing in emerging markets. In fact, these should promote smoother, more effective communication and co-operation between both sides. 16. Last but not least, IFFO will consider forming an Equity Club with our Partners to allow some reputable and like-minded investors who are looking for long term returns, to formulate an investment platform. On a mutually beneficial basis, the investment platform could select projects for experience sharing or even co-investments amongst the investors, that could help generate demonstration effect for the market and to draw in greater private capital participation in infrastructure investments. Conclusion 17. Ladies and gentlemen, I realize I have been on my feet for some little while - some may think for too long! But, I hope you'll indulge me by at least taking away a couple of key points- There is a huge infrastructure gap in Asia that requires not just public but also private sector participation to bridge the gap; and Despite the challenges to "crowding in" private sector capital, IFFO has made a promising start and through its work, we believe the Office will play a key role in facilitating investment collaboration in this region. 18. Title: Keynote Speech at the Opening Ceremony of Asian Financial Cooperation Association in Beijing
text: 19/09/22, 13:01 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Keynote Speech at the Opening Ceremony of Asian Financial Cooperation Association in Beij... Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 24 Jul 2017 Keynote Speech at the Opening Ceremony of Asian Financial Cooperation Association in Beijing on 24 July 2017 Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority The Honourable Vice Chairman Chen Yuan, Chairman Guo Shu-qing, Chairman Tian Guoli, President Jin Liqun, Governor Veerathai, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, It gives me great pleasure to join you today at the grand opening of the Asian Financial Cooperation Association (AFCA), which marks a new chapter of cooperation among financial institutions and industry associations in Asia. I would like to extend my heartfelt congratulations to the founders of AFCA for their foresight and commitment in promoting closer regional financial cooperation. I remember that in late 2015, Chairman Tian Guoli told me about the plan to set up AFCA, I immediately conveyed my full support as I truly believe that this is a meaningful and productive project. Now, I am pleased to note that key industry bodies in Hong Kong, namely the Hong Kong Association of Banks, Hong Kong Institute of Bankers and Treasury Markets Association, have joined as founding members of AFCA. The setting up of AFCA is both timely and necessary. In just 20 years ago, Asia was shaken by a financial crisis that tarnished the once buoyant Asian Tigers and Dragons. Fault lines and cracks in the Asian economies and financial systems were exposed and magnified by the crisis. The resulting pain endured by many Asian economies was hard to describe but we have all learned some useful lessons from our mistakes and have sought to remedy the weak spots after the crisis. Most of us in Asia have strengthened our macroeconomic management and fiscal policies. Our banking and financial sector has been upgraded and our capital markets, which are still not yet very well developed, have been reinforced. All these reform efforts have paid off as can be demonstrated by the fact that most Asian economies came out from the subsequent and bigger Global Financial Crisis relatively unscathed. While the West is still slowly recovering from the trauma caused by the Global Financial Crisis, Asia has resumed its momentum of growth. Asia is the home for about 4.5 billion people or 60% of the worlds population, but it only accounts for 30% of the worlds GDP. Asia, especially China, has become the main driver for global growth, contributing to 46% of the world's growth over the last decade. However, there is an obvious gap in the functioning of Asias financial system. This can be demonstrated by the fact that many Asian economies have huge surplus savings and they are keen to look for productive and profitable investment opportunities but cannot find enough bankable or investible projects in the region. At the same time it is estimated that there is an enormous demand of over US1 trillion a year in infrastructure investments in the region alone. Clearly something is / 1/3 19/09/22, 13:01 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Keynote Speech at the Opening Ceremony of Asian Financial Cooperation Association in Beij... missing that causes this wide gap between savings and investments. This is a structural problem on which all of us in Asia must try hard to overcome if we wish to catch up in promoting the living standards of our people. The task in front of us is how to channel or mobilise the huge amount of savings from the surplus economies to the deficit economies. This clearly involves cross border flows of debt and equity capital as well as technology. The official sector has been doing a lot of work in this regard, notably in the setting up of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the Belt and Road Initiative. However, the official sector cannot do it alone and the private sector must also play its part and collaborate with the official sector. In this regard, I believe that AFCA can play a unique role in furthering regional and international collaboration in financial intermediation in this process. Specifically, there are a few things that AFCA can do well. First, it can articulate more effectively the Asian voice to the policy makers, standard setters and regulators when the international financial reform agenda and new regulatory standards are being debated and formulated. We know that, for example, the Institute of International Finance (IIF) has been very proactive in providing useful industry feedback and views on the international financial reform agenda. There is no reason why AFCA cannot contribute to the process by injecting the relevant Asian views and perspective. Second, AFCA could seek to identify legal or policy barriers to cross border financial flows and propose ideas or solutions to overcome such barriers. Third, AFCA could help promote professionalism, sound risk management practices and good corporate culture, which will help enhance the safety, soundness and ethical standards of the private sector financial firms. On the point of culture, I strongly believe that no matter how hard a regulator tries to impose rules and standards from the outside, there is no substitute for good corporate culture in achieving long term profitability and sustainability of any financial firm. It is a lot easier to preach good culture and ethics if the industry body as a whole share this objective and join the public sector in its promotion amongst its members. Ladies and gentlemen, Asia is very different from what it used to be 20 years ago. In 1997, the combined GDP of emerging Asia including China was merely US3 trillion, but now its GDP is US18 trillion. While Asia has been the growth engine for the world in recent years and will remain so in the years to come, the benefits of growth have not been evenly shared within the region. Some economies have found it tough to catch up because they lack the necessary capital and technology in developing the basic infrastructure that will enable them to move forward. It is now time for Asia to do a lot more to promote infrastructure investments, without which the bottlenecks will impair economic development and trade within the region. This is why once the Belt and Road Initiative was announced, it has been met with overwhelming response from so many key stakeholders. I am sure that AFCA will be able to serve as the catalyst as well as facilitator in helping bring the financial sector in Asia to a higher level. Finally, let me wish AFCA every success in its future work. I can assure AFCA that Hong Kong will offer full support to the Association in its future endeavours. Thank you once again for inviting me to this memorable event! / 2/3 19/09/22, 13:01 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Keynote Speech at the Opening Ceremony of Asian Financial Cooperation Association in Beij... Title: Response on Federal Open Markets Committee Meeting
text: 19/09/22, 13:00 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Response on Federal Open Markets Committee Meeting Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 27 Jul 2017 Response on Federal Open Markets Committee Meeting Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority While the US FOMC, as the market widely expected, kept its monetary policy unchanged at yesterday's meeting, it noted that it expected to begin the reduction of the Fed's balance sheet relatively soon. Although the probability of a FOMC rate hike by year-end as implied by the futures market has declined to around 40%, we have to point out that the pace of US interest rate increase and the starting time of the Fed's balance sheet reduction remain uncertain. Title: Press Statement by Eddie Yue, Acting Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority
text: Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Press Statement by Eddie Yue, Acting Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ... 19/09/22, 13:00 Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 21 Sep 2017 Press Statement by Eddie Yue, Acting Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority on 21 September 2017 Eddie Yue, Acting Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority As widely expected by the market, the US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decided to keep its interest rate target unchanged, but announced the beginning of the reduction of the US Fed's balance sheet in October 2017. The FOMC already announced the detailed arrangements for its balance sheet reduction programme in June, and the announcement simply went a step further to confirm the starting time. It is however worth noting that the terminal size of the Feds balance sheet and also the impact of balance sheet reduction on global capital flows are still very much uncertain. Market liquidity should tighten gradually, and that may affect global capital flows. Asset prices may also become more volatile. Given the abundant liquidity in the Hong Kong dollar system, local interest rates remain low despite the USs four rate hikes since December 2015. We believe that over time the interest rate gaps may lead to the easing of the HKD to 7.85 against the US dollar and trigger the weak-side Convertibility Undertaking. HKD interest rates will then increase as capital flows out of the HKD. These are all part of the design and operating mechanisms of the Linked Exchange Rate System. There is nothing to be concerned about. Apart from the path of US rate hike and impact of balance sheet normalisation, the global financial market is also facing a range of uncertainties, such as the US debt ceiling and geopolitical risks. Their developments may lead to rapid changes in local interest rates or financial conditions. US monetary policy normalisation and other market uncertainties may affect capital flows and increase market volatilities. We would like to remind banks, corporates, and individuals to manage their risks prudently. Last revision date : 21 September 2017 / 1/1

text: 19/09/22, 13:00 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Statement by Norman T.L. Chan Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the ... Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 14 Dec 2017 Statement by Norman T.L. Chan Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to the media on 14 December 2017 Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority As expected by the market, last night the US FOMC made a 25 basis points rate hike. This morning, the HKMA also adjusted our Base Rate for the Discount Window by 25 basis points to 1.75%. The widening of the gap between HKD interest rates and USD interest rates will eventually lead to capital flowing out of the HKD. This will result in the gradual increase in HKD interest rates. However, capital outflow is not the only factor that can push up HKD interest rates. For instance, as seen recently, other market activities (e.g. IPO) can also tighten market liquidity and lead to increase in HKD interbank interest rates. In addition, US tax reform, which will be passed soon, may also affect HKD interest rates. Three areas are worth attention: (i) tax cuts will provide short-term stimulus to the US economy and employment. This may have an impact on US inflation. US companies repatriating their foreign earnings back to the US may tighten global (ii) liquidity, including in the emerging markets. the US federal government might need to issue more debts to finance larger short- fl ii) term budget deficits. This may push up bond yields. In view of the above, we should pay attention to the risk of US inflation and interest rates rising faster than the market is expecting. HKD interest rates are still very low. As US interest rates continue to normalise, HKD interest rates will gradually normalise as well. We hope everyone manage their risks prudently when they enter into financial arrangements. Lastly, there is an incorrect market saying that the HKMA does not want to see the weakening of HKD exchange rate and the triggering of our weak-side convertibility undertaking rate of 7.8500.1 would like to point out that under the design of the Linked Exchange Rate System, the outflow of capital, weakening of the HKD exchange rate, triggering of the weak-side convertibility undertaking, and the reduction in the Monetary Base are part of the necessary process of HKD interest rate normalisation. Title: Welcoming Remarks at the 9th Annual International Conference on the Chinese Economy
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 18 Jan 2018 Opening speech of the 9th International Symposium on China's Economy Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Deputy Director of Long (Guoqiang), Director Xu (Zhong), distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen Good Morning and a very warm welcome to all of you. Thank you for attending the 9th Annual International Conference on the Chinese Economy. Today7 s conference is very special. It is co-organised by Hong Kong Institute for Monetary Research, the Institute of Market Economy of Development Centre of the State Council, and the Financial Research Institute of the People7 s Bank of China. I would also like to express my special gratitude to those who have travelled a long way to Hong Kong. The theme of this conference is truly important, and I will explain why. For governments and regulators, the real estate market is likely to be the most complex, the most difficult to understand, and the most difficult to manage. Why? I have several reasons: (i) Housing is the basic living needs of citizens. In both Eastern and Western societies, helping ordinary people to buy a home is a universal and normal public policy in many countries; (ii) However, the average person needs to borrow money to buy a house. These financings are usually secured from the banking system, characterized by a long term (e.g. mortgage loans in Hong Kong with a term of 20 to 30 years) and very high leverage. Before 2007/08, the United States generally got 90% or 100% of the mortgage loan for buying a house, some even 105%, and the interest on mortgage contributions on the owner's home is tax-deductible. (iii) The dividing line between real residential demand, investment and speculation in the real estate market is very blurry and difficult to distinguish. Sometimes even buyers who have worked so hard to come up with a down payment may not be clear on their own. (iv) The government's policy measures to encourage home ownership, such as tax incentives, looser loan thresholds, etc., coupled with other factors , especially supply imbalances, may lead to significant overheating or bubbles in the real estate market; (v) Past real estate bubbles have been fueled by the loose credit environment of banks or financial systems. Therefore, the explosion of real estate bubbles will inevitably have a major impact on the financial system and the economy as a whole. Hong Kong is a very good example. In the 1990s, Hong Kong formed a very large real estate bubble, which eventually exploded in the 3rd quarter of 1997. Then came a very painful and unforgettable experience for Hong Kong: (i) Residential home prices fell 66 percentage points over the next six years; (ii) The economy contracted by 9 percentage points in one year; (hi) The unemployment rate jumped from 2.2% in 1997 at the peak of 2.2% to 8.5% in 2003, the highest since Hong Kong's unemployment rate was counted; (iv) The Consumer Price Index (CPI) fell by 16 percentage points over five years. The downturn in Hong Kong's housing market ended in the third quarter of 2003 before slowly recovering. In the United States in 2007/08, and later in Spain and Ireland, the real estate market explosions also had devastating consequences. In these examples from Europe and the United States, it is clear that the explosion of the real estate market bubble will have a serious impact on economic and financial stability, and these stem from the close connection between the positive and negative wealth effects of the real estate market, the financial system, and the real estate market cycle. In these examples, it's worth noting that most people don't realize or believe that the real estate market is bubbling up during the upswing or bull run. At the peak of the bubble, people will always find many reasons to prove that "this time is different"! Looking back at history, we now realize how naefve and ridiculous this statement is. Let's look at Chinese mainland again. There are still many people who believe that the real estate market is not seriously overheated or bubbling, despite the growing gap between rising house prices and the purchasing power of citizens. This idea of "house prices only rising and not falling" is actually equivalent to believing that China's real estate market will not have a cycle. Another expression of this optimism is "We are different." But is that really the case? Will China really be different? Or has China not yet experienced a complete real estate market cycle, so misunderstanding that China's real estate market is different from others, there will be no cycle? I hope that this issue will be explored in this meeting, although I am not sure whether there will be a definite conclusion in the end. But in any case, the focus of the meeting was to understand how the mainland real estate market is linked to the financial system and the real economy, and the extent to which they are linked. Once these linkages can be identified, it will be easier to assess the extent to which different stages of the development of the real estate market affect financial and economic stability. Ladies and gentlemen, "The house is for living, not for speculation!" I agree with this view, but how to achieve this goal is a very important topic that deserves to be explored in depth! I am pleased that today's conference has invited many experts from government departments, academia and domestic and overseas markets. I hope that the discussions will be fully exchanged and fruitful in the discussions of the two days and the future . Thank you! Last revision date: 18 January 2018

Title: Welcoming Remarks at the Launching Ceremony of Fintech Career Accelerator Scheme 2.0
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 31 Jan 2018 Welcome speech at the launching ceremony of FinTech Talent Development Program 2.0 Li Shupei is the Assistant President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Financial Infrastructure). Mr. Wang Mingxin, Chairman of ASTRI, Dr. Lam Ka Li, Chairman of Cyberport, Mr. Wong Ke-keung, Chief Executive Officer of Science and Technology Park, and distinguished guests from academia and banking 1. Hello everyone! Thank you for attending the launch of the new Fintech Career Accelerator Scheme (FCAS). 2. Fintech is important for Hong Kong's future development, with the HKMA Chief Executive Mr Chan Tak-lam announcing last September that Hong Kong is about to enter Since the "New Era of Wisdom Banking", the HKMA has spared no effort to implement seven relevant measures, of which the cultivation of fintech people is an important part, and the new FCAS is precisely to match the development of this aspect. 3. The first FCAS was implemented very smoothly and won the reputation of the industry. This year, we continue to work hard to upgrade FCAS to 2.0 - the entire program covers a wider range, from entrepreneurship training during the school period, to summer work practice, to gap year internships, to post-graduation fledgling employment training, providing a four-stage all-round cultivation program. 4. First of all, the first stage of study is the entrepreneurial training during the school period, hoping to cultivate the international vision of Hong Kong young people and learn from overseas experience, in order to achieve the stone of other mountains and can attack jade. This year, FCAS, for the first time, joined the Cyberport University Partnership Programme and will select about 60 Enthusiastic and creative university students who are interested in fintech will receive a two-month training in Hong Kong in groups of 3 to 5 people. After learning the basic "Zama Bu", we will go overseas to participate in a close-paced and rich "Entrepreneurship Camp" training for about 10 days, learn about financial technology and meet with local industry leaders to strengthen financial investment, business governance and leadership. After completing the "Entrepreneurship Camp", students return to Hong Kong to make their own fintech products and compete with other teams on Demo Day. The 10th to 15th teams with the best performance will each receive a HK100,000 seed fund for entrepreneurship to pave the way for future start-ups. 5. In addition to overseas experience, the rapid development of fintech in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area has also brought rare opportunities for university students to work and practice. Therefore, this year, FCAS also offered a summer internship position in Shenzhen for the first time for 6 weeks. I am delighted to have invited many of the region's leading fintech companies to offer about 50 internship positions. This not only gives Hong Kong university students the opportunity to access cutting-edge technologies such as big data and artificial intelligence, but also allows them to experience and hear for the first time during their internship during the summer vacation, which is of great benefit to their future development. 6. Looking back at the inaugural FCAS, we offered fintech internship positions to approximately 70 university students. I am very happy to hear that during the internship, my classmates have participated in different financial technology projects, including blockchain, big data, artificial intelligence, machine learning, social networking, network security, etc. This proves that the banks participating in FCAS attach great importance to the training of their classmates and recognize their abilities. Four students will share their internship experience later. This year, FCAS continued to receive strong support from 10 local universities and universities, while the number of participating banks increased from 12 to 20, providing about 130 internship positions. 7. At the same time, FCAS 2.0 is no longer limited to internship positions, this year's training scope will be extended to recent college graduates, and fintech start-ups in Cyberport and Science Park will provide about 20 full-time job positions, providing more complete and more adequate talent training for the fintech production circle. 8. Dear guests, financial technology is unstoppable, and Hong Kong must move towards a new era of smart banking, not only to go fast, but also to go far, and the task of cultivating financial technology talents is arduous and long. I am delighted to see more and more stakeholders identify with FCAS, support FCAS, and join FCAS. The new FCAS will offer about 260 training opportunities at different stages, and I hope for the next five years FCAS can produce between 500 and 1,000 professionals in Hong Kong. I would like to once again thank the participating institutions, banks, and Cyberport, ASTRI and Science Park, which have been working closely with us. We will continue to work together to contribute to the growth of Hong Kong's fintech talent pool. Thank you! Last revision date: 31 January 2018

Title: CE/MA remarks after FOMC Meeting
text: 19/09/22, 12:58 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - CE/MA remarks after FOMC Meeting Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 22 Mar 2018 CE/MA remarks after FOMC Meeting Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority Last night, the US FOMC made a 25 basis points rate hike. This morning, the HKMA also adjusted our Base Rate for the Discount Window by 25 basis points to 2%. While the US rate hike is expected by the market, it is worth noting that yesterday, the US Fed also lifted their economic forecasts and median projection on US interest rates for 2018 and 2019. In particular, among the 15 FOMC participants, seven of them saw US interest rates rising by at least four times this year, six of them saw by three times, and two of them saw by less than three times. This shows some divergence in terms of interest rate projection within the Fed. I see some uncertainties in the path of US inflation and interest rates. First, although US unemployment rate is currently low (4.1%), an acceleration in economic growth and tightening of labour market may cause wages to rise faster than expected. This will affect US prices and inflation. Secondly, there are growing risks of large scale trade conflicts and disputes. Should this materialise, it will affect the economic and inflation outlook. Arising from last nights interest rate hike, the gap between HKD and USD interest rates widened further. This is expected to create more incentives for carry trades. The HKD exchange rate has weakened recently, and is only some 40 to 50 pips away from the weak- side Convertibility Undertaking rate of 7.85. The rise in US interest rates may lead to the triggering of weak-side Convertibility Undertaking in the short term. If so, the HKMA will buy HKD and sell USD, the Monetary Base will shrink, thereby creating a conducive environment for HKD interest rates to normalise. The HKMA reiterates that we will act to ensure that the HKD exchange rate will not weaken beyond HK7.8500 to one USD. This is part of the design and operations of the Link Exchange Rate System. There is no need to be concerned. Although the HKD interbank, savings, and borrowing interest rates have not risen as much as their USD counterparts, HKD interest rates will eventually normalise. It is not reasonable to expect that HKD interest rates will stay low for prolonged period. When taking out a loan, one should take into account different factors, and manage risks prudently. Title: Speaking Points of Media Standup on outflow from Hong Kong dollar
text: 19/09/22, 12:58 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Speaking Points of Media Standup on outflow from Hong Kong dollar Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 13 Apr 2018 Speaking Points of Media Standup on outflow from Hong Kong dollar Howard Lee, Deputy Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority During yesterday's London and New York trading hours, the HKMA conducted two foreign exchange transactions, buying Hong Kong dollars for US dollars for a total of HK3.26 billion. These forex transactions were made at the weak-side Convertibility Undertaking (CU) rate of HK7.8500 to the US dollar. The two transactions were conducted in accordance with the design of the Linked Exchange Rate System (LERS) and upon banks' request. Under the LERS, the Aggregate Balance of the banking sector will shrink on Monday upon settlement of the forex transactions from the existing HK180 billion to HK176.5 billion. As we have previously explained to the public, the reduction in the Aggregate Balance will create a conducive environment for the gradual normalisation of Hong Kongs monetary conditions. It will also provide the condition for HKD interest rates to move closer to their US counterparts. The Aggregate Balance is currently at a rather high level of HK180 billion. We expect the pace of HKD interest rate normalisation to be gradual, where local interest rates will slowly move closer to their USD counterparts. It is worth noting that even before the triggering of weak-side CU, interbank interest rates have already been rising slowly as US interest rates continued to rise. For example, one- month HIBOR increased from 0.22% around the end of 2015 to 0.80% recently, even briefly touching 1.00% at times. The HKMA has pointed out on many occasions that in view of the rate hikes, borrowers should be mindful of higher interest expenses. They should manage risk prudently to ensure that their interest expenses would be affordable having regard to their income. We would like to emphasise that both our forex operations and the outflow of funds from the Hong Kong dollar system are in line with our expectation and in accordance with the design of the LERS. The HKMA is fully prepared for capital outflows. The US130 billion inflows into the HKD system after the Global Financial Crisis are invested by the Exchange Fund in highly liquid USD assets. These USD assets are readily available for meeting the triggering of weak- side CU by market participants. The level of liquidity in our banking sector is high. In particular, banks in Hong Kong hold HK4 trillion worth of highly liquid assets. They are fully capable of managing capital outflows. We should all note that the current market condition will facilitate a gradual rise in / 1/2 19/09/22, 12:58 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Speaking Points of Media Standup on outflow from Hong Kong dollar the Hong Kong dollar interest rates, and both the HKMA and the banking sector are fully capable of coping with this. Before yesterdays triggering of the weak-side CU, the HKD had briefly touched the 7.8500 level but the HKMA did not act in the market. We should note that many banks and financial institutions trade the HKD among themselves during a day, and some deals may be done at 7.8500 without the need to involve the HKMA. An institution may also have customers' orders to buy HKD so that it does not need to sell HKD to the HKMA at 7.8500. But when a bank contacts us and requests us to do so, the HKMA will buy HKD from it. The HKMA will announce our forex transactions on the "interbank liquidity" page, published via certain financial data platforms and our official website. Interested parties may wish to check those pages to confirm whether the HKMA has conducted forex transactions. Last revision date : 21 May 2018 / 2/2

Title: Speaking Points of Media Standup on outflow from Hong Kong dollar
text: 19/09/22, 12:57 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Speaking Points of Media Standup on outflow from Hong Kong dollar Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 19 Apr 2018 Speaking Points of Media Standup on outflow from Hong Kong dollar Howard Lee, Deputy Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority Since its first triggering last week, the weak-side Convertibility Undertaking (CU) was triggered repeatedly in the past few days. The HKMA bought HK51 billion in 13 transactions in the forex market so far. The Aggregate Balance of the banking system will reduce accordingly as a result of the transactions. The frequency and scale of the forex transactions are broadly in line with our analysis and expectations. When the strong-side or weak-side CU was triggered in the past, these forex transactions usually persisted for some time. Recently, especially over the past week, the HKMA has closely monitored market activities. We found the market operating in a smooth and sound manner. Under the Linked Exchange Rate System (LERS), when the interest rate spreads between HKD and USD reach a certain level, market participants will conduct carry trades through selling of the HKD in either the spot or the forward market. These carry trade activities are well within expectations under the LERS. Based on the HKMA's market surveillance, there are no large-scale short-selling of the HKD or sizeable positions speculating that the HKD will weaken significantly away from the weak- side CU level. Rather, the media and analysts have shown very strong confidence in the HKMA's commitment to maintaining the stability of the HKD and the LERS. The HKMA will stay alerted. We will continue to monitor the market situation closely and duly address abnormal market situations as necessary. Some media recently raised the question as to whether the Aggregate Balance will fall to zero as funds keep flowing out of the HKD. As the Aggregate Balance shrinks, interest rates should gradually go up. With the triggering of the weak-side CU of HK50 billion in the past few days, HIBOR of different tenors have gone up gradually. For instance, the overnight HIBOR rose by 10 basis points from last week while one-month HIBOR rose by 12 basis points. This situation is expected to continue. In addition, as HKD interest rates rise, the scale and incentive for capital flowing out of the HKD would reduce; the HKD would stabilise. There is no need to be concerned about abrupt surges in HKD interest rates as the Aggregate Balance starts to shrink. Relative to the HK150 billion of Aggregate Balance, the current outflow of HK50 billion may look sizeable, but comparing it against the over HK1 trillion inflows into the HKD system in the past few years, the HK50 billion is actually quite small. Besides, banks hold a sizeable amount - about HK1 trillion - of Exchange Fund Bills / 1/2 19/09/22, 12:57 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Speaking Points of Media Standup on outflow from Hong Kong dollar and Notes (EFBNs). When liquidity tightens, banks can use the EFBNs to obtain HKD liquidity via the discount window. The HKMA also has arrangements to adjust the amount of EFBNs and increase the Aggregate Balance so as to release liquidity back to the market should liquidity become so tight that market functioning is impaired. The triggering of the weak-side CU in the past few days has taken place as designed. The market continued to operate smoothly, and market confidence in the HKMA and the LERS remained strong. The current outflow only accounts for a small portion of the HK1 trillion inflows in the past few years. As outflows continue, interest rate will adjust. The public should pay attention to the upward movements of interest rates. The HKMA will continue to monitor the market closely, and ensure the stability of the HKD and the smooth functioning of the market. Last revision date : 21 May 2018 / 2/2

Title: "Integrating into the Greater Bay Area Development by Capitalising on Hong Kong's Advantages"
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 03 May 2018 "Making Good Use of Hong Kong's Strengths to Integrate into the Development of the Bay Area" Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (Speech at the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Summit Forum) President Sun Qilie, Chairman Dai Beibei, Chairman Huang Youjia, and distinguished guests 1. Hello everyone! It is a pleasure to attend today's luncheon to share with you a few of my views on how Hong Kong can make good use of its advantages and integrate into the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. Greater Bay Area: The concept of geographical area has been upgraded to the concept of economic region 2. From a geographical point of view, the Greater Bay Area covers nearly 56,000 square kilometers of the Pearl River Delta, consisting of nine mainland cities and Hong Kong and Macao, with a population of more than 69 million and an economic scale of US1.4 billion, making it the most dynamic and innovative region in China. Compared with the world's large urban agglomerations, such as the New York Bay Area in the United States, the Bay Area of California or the Tokyo Bay Area in Japan, they are not inferior. 3. But one of the great differences between China's Greater Bay Area and the world's large urban agglomerations is that we have two special administrative regions and three customs areas, and all goods and people across the border must be inspected before they can pass. One country, two systems is the best solution to the problems of Hong Kong and Macao left over from history, and it is also the best system for maintaining long-term prosperity and stability after the return of Hong Kong and Macao to the motherland. However, at the same time, one country, two systems has also brought challenges to the integration of economic development between Hong Kong, Macao and the mainland, especially the flow of goods, personnel and capital between the mainland cities in the Greater Bay Area and Hong Kong and Macao, which has brought out problems that other large metropolitan agglomerations in the world do not have. In foreign urban agglomerations, where factors of production flow largely freely and without obstacles, the most common problem is that transportation infrastructure cannot keep up with development, such as traffic jams, reducing the efficiency of people flow and logistics. But in general, the rest of the world's largest metropolitan agglomerations are essentially areas of geographic and economic integration. 4. However, our Greater Bay Area is different, under one country, two systems, the cross-border flow of goods, personnel and funds needs to be cleared. In order to form an economic region with complementary advantages in the Greater Bay Area, the primary task is to work basic transportation and customs clearance port facilities, and to do our best to invest resources. In this regard, a new situation will emerge in the Greater Bay Area, as with the opening of the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge and the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong high-speed rail line this year, as well as the opening of a new port in Liantang at a later date, the infrastructure for the connection between Hong Kong and the Mainland Greater Bay Area metropolitan agglomeration will be greatly enhanced, which will facilitate the cross-border movement of people and goods between the two places. 5. However, I think that it is not enough to increase the transport infrastructure, because the flow of people between the mainland urban agglomerations in the Greater Bay Area and Hong Kong and Macao is amazing, but at the same time it is normal. Last year, Hong Kong's daily sea and land crossings exceeded 680,000, and this will continue to increase with the formation and development of the Greater Bay Area's living and working circles. Therefore, we must have the courage to innovate, dare to think new and make full use of the new bio-certified technology that has made great progress in recent years, especially the facial appearance and vein authentication, to simplify the cross-border movement of residents in the two places, whether it is one place and two inspections, the procedures and time required, as far as possible to promote the efficiency of cross-border movement of personnel in the Greater Bay Area urban agglomeration. Capital flows for residents of the Greater Bay Area 6. The world's developed large urban agglomerations allow the factors of production to flow completely freely within the region, so they can form an economic integration within a region. Our Greater Bay Area is different, but as long as we can achieve the basic and efficient passage and movement of people from both places, then the Greater Bay Area is well positioned to develop into the world's most promising and dynamic super economic bay area composed of large urban agglomerations . 7. "Money goes with people" is a superficial truth. So the first thing to solve is to solve the problem of transportation and customs clearance. After solving these problems, it is still necessary to deal with the cross-border movement of people in Hong Kong and the mainland cities in the Greater Bay Area, whether it is the demand for capital flow and management arising from work, business, leisure, residence, retirement. There are three aspects to this need: The most basic demand for capital flow is payment: In recent years, the mainland's mobile payment system has developed rapidly, and many shopping consumption and personal payments are made through third-party payment platforms such as Alipay or WeChat Pay. Although Hong Kong's e-wallets are also developing rapidly, including those operated by some mainland payment providers in Hong Kong, they have not yet been used across borders in the mainland, making it very inconvenient for Hong Kong residents to spend and pay in the mainland. Therefore, we hope to open and rationalize cross-border payment arrangements for Hong Kong residents when entering the Greater Bay Area as soon as possible. In fact, mainland residents who come to Hong Kong for consumption can already use their wallets and bank cards at many merchants in Hong Kong without hindrance. (2) Basic banking services : The cross-border movement of residents of the two places often requires basic banking services in addition to daily consumption and shopping payments. Hong Kong is an international financial center, banks are open to all non-residents, and it is basically not a problem for mainland residents in the Greater Bay Area to open accounts in Hong Kong. However, Hong Kong residents are subject to some restrictions on opening accounts in the Mainland, and the procedures are more complicated and not easy. To facilitate the effective movement of people in the Greater Bay Area and to facilitate cross-border leisure, work and retirement, it is necessary to step up research and implement a set of simple and feasible new arrangements for Hong Kong residents to open accounts in the mainland. (3) The third aspect is wealth management: as more and more Hong Kong people work, buy property and retire in mainland cities in the Greater Bay Area, in addition to basic banking services, there will also be financial needs. Of course, there is still a management and control of capital account inflows and outflows in the Mainland, but in order to promote the strategic development of the Greater Bay Area, it is necessary to consider introducing a set of first-to-try management methods so that residents of the two places can transfer funds across borders within a specified range or scale for financial purposes. 8. The preparation of the Development Plan for the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area by the National Development and Reform Commission has been basically completed and is expected to be issued in the near future. Under the strategic direction and framework of the Plan, the HKMA and the relevant mainland authorities will expedite the study of appropriate measures to meet the needs of Hong Kong residents in cross-border payments and fund management in the Mainland. How Hong Kong can help mainland enterprises in the Greater Bay Area go global 9. Chinese mainland since 2005, corporate direct investment abroad has grown rapidly, and since 2013, the amount of outbound direct investment has exceeded US100 billion, including, of course, infrastructure investment along the Belt and Road. Hong Kong has always been a springboard and hub for mainland enterprises to go global, accounting for nearly 60 percent of all outbound direct investment in the mainland for a long time. Why has Hong Kong become the preferred springboard for mainland enterprises to go global? Of course, Hong Kong is Asia's premier international business and financial centre, which is why it is important. However, I would like to point out that compared with other international commercial and financial centres, Hong Kong has three unique advantages that cannot be imitated or replaced: (-) Location of Hong Kong: Hong Kong is adjacent to the mainland, and the urban agglomeration of the Greater Bay Area can basically be reached by car or boat within three hours, forming a super-large living and working circle with a population of more than 60 million. This geographical factor makes it easier for mainland enterprises in the Greater Bay Area to use Hong Kong's business and financial platforms to go out and enter the international market. This is also incomparable to any city or financial center at home and abroad. (2) One country, two systems arrangement : As mentioned above, the one country, two systems arrangement has formed a situation in the Greater Bay Area where three customs areas and cross-border flows of personnel need to be cleared. However, one country, two systems also provides very favorable conditions for Hong Kong to play a role as a platform for mainland enterprises to go global, especially to participate in the construction of the Belt and Road Initiative. The central government has always vigorously supported Hong Kong in giving play to its strong position, so that Hong Kong can integrate into the overall development situation of the mainland and Hong Kong can maintain long-term prosperity and stability. With the support of the central government, Hong Kong can certainly help enterprises in the Mainland, especially in the adjacent Greater Bay Area, to go global and accelerate the expansion and implementation of the Belt and Road Initiative. (iii) Hong Kong's truly bilingual common law legal system in both Chinese and English: It is understood that international commercial and financial activities and contracts mainly use common law laws and arbitration systems. Among the common law places in the world, Hong Kong is a truly bilingual Chinese and English judicial region. All of Hong Kong's statutory laws and regulations have the same legal effect in both Chinese and English. Moreover, according to some statistics, more than 80% of solicitors and 60% of barristers in Hong Kong are bilingual. In the judiciary, about 90 per cent of judges are now bilingual. In Hong Kong, with the exception of the Court of Final Appeal, which uses English only, a significant proportion of courts at all levels use Chinese. I believe that Hong Kong's bilingual common law system in both Chinese and English will provide extremely attractive conditions for mainland enterprises to go out to operate international business and investment , which will greatly benefit mainland enterprises to use Hong Kong as a springboard and management center for international business. 10. Finally, I would like to say that the national leaders have repeatedly reiterated that China will adhere to reform and opening up in the future, including promoting the Belt and Road Initiative and the internationalization of the renminbi. Hong Kong has the conditions of time, place, and people, as long as we work hard, make unremitting efforts to improve ourselves, and play a good role With the strategic positioning of "backing the mainland and facing the world" and making good use of its unique advantages, Hong Kong will have endless opportunities and bright futures 11. Thank you all! Last revision date: 12 June 2018

Title: Remarks after FOMC Meeting
text: 19/09/22, 12:56 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Remarks after FOMC Meeting Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 14Jun2018 Remarks after FOMC Meeting Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority Last night, the US FOMC raised its policy rate by 25 basis points. This morning, the HKMA also adjusted our Base Rate for the Discount Window by 25 basis points to 2.25%. The Fed has raised the median projection of interest rate hike to four times in 2018. This is not surprising at all because: (a) US economy continues to have solid growth; (b) US labour market continues to tighten; and (c) Inflation appears to be on a rising trend. Under the Linked Exchange Rate System, HKD interest rates will rise as US monetary policy continues to normalise. The HKMA does not actively manage HKD interest rates. The rise in HKD interest rates will occur through money flowing out of the HKD. With one-month HIBOR now over 1.5%, the trend of a rising HIBOR is clear. I believe it is just a matter of time that banks increase their savings deposit rate and Best Lending Rate. Many people are concerned about the overheating of Hong Kong's property market. HKD interest rate normalisation will be conducive to a more healthy development of the asset markets, including the property market. But some volatility is unavoidable in the process. The HKMA would like to remind the public, once again, to manage their interest rate risks and market risks prudently. Last revision date : 14 June 2018 / 1/1

Title: Keynote speech at the Bond Connect Anniversary Summit
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 03 Jul 2018 Bond Keynote Speech at the Bond Connect Annual Forum Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Vice President Pan Gongsheng, Deputy Director Qiu Hong, Chief Executive Officer of Ashley Alder, President Li Xiaojia, President Zhang Yi, distinguished guests: 1. Hello everyone! It is a great pleasure to join you today in witnessing the first anniversary of Bond Connect. Thanks to the joint efforts of the central and SAR governments, as well as a number of institutions in both places, Bond Connect was successfully launched in July last year and has been working well. 2. Bond Connect is an important initiative to promote the integration of the mainland and international markets. Although some foreign investors had direct access to China's interbank bond market a few years ago, they could only settle and hold mainland bonds through primary custody, which is different from the multi-tier custody method commonly used by international investors and causes some inconveniences. By strengthening the financial infrastructure connection between the two places, Bond Connect has introduced a multi-tier custody model for the mainland bond market to integrate with the international market without weakening the regulatory penetration of bond trading. Regulators, exchanges, clearing houses, etc. in the two places have made great efforts to realize Bond Connect, with the aim of providing more choices and flexibility for foreign investors. 3. Driven by favorable factors such as the further internationalization of the renminbi and the inclusion of renminbi bonds in international indices, I am confident that overseas investors will be more active in participating in Bond Connect. At the same time, we, together with the People's Bank of China and other units, will continue to work hard to optimize the specific arrangements and operations of the Bond Connect. Just now, Vice President Pan Gongsheng has already made an introduction, and I will not repeat it. 4. Ladies and gentlemen, since the opening of Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect in 2014, Hong Kong has built different interconnection bridges between the equities, funds and bond markets and the Mainland, becoming a platform and channel for the Mainland to connect with the world's financial markets. However, if Hong Kong is to do a good job in this financial intermediation role, it must continuously enhance the competitiveness of our market, including optimizing Hong Kong's financial infrastructure. In this regard, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has been promoting Hong Kong's financial infrastructure for many years by adopting the principle of being active and promising, as the HKMA not only has a regulatory role, but also has the task of advocates and promoters. In order to develop financial infrastructure well, it is necessary to have a broad and long-term vision, not to consider short-term benefits, not to take advantage of profits, and to revise policies and regulatory arrangements to match them in many cases. 5. In addition to Bond Connect, we have also launched a number of initiatives, such as our announcement in May of the Bond Funding Pilot Scheme to provide funding to attract more domestic and foreign enterprises to issue bonds in Hong Kong. The HKMA also co-hosted the annual General Assembly and Conference on Green and Social Responsibility Bonds Principles with the International Capital Market Association last month; The next day, a joint symposium was held with the People's Bank of China on green financial opportunities in the Mainland and Hong Kong, with the aim of promoting Hong Kong's development as a platform for green bond issuance. In addition, the HKSAR Government also intends to launch a HK100 billion green bond calculation through the HKMA Scratch. In the coming years, the momentum of Hong Kong's bond market development will be greatly strengthened. 6. In conclusion, I wish today's Bond Connect Anniversary Forum every success. Thank you. Title: Unveiling Ceremony of the New Series Hong Kong Banknotes 2018
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 24 Jul 2018 "2018 Hong Kong New Banknote Series" Launch Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority The Financial Secretary, the Presidents and Representatives of the Three Banknote Issuing Banks, Distinguished Guests, Media Friends: 1. Welcome to the launch ceremony of Hong Kong's 2018 New Banknote Series today. 2. The last time Hong Kong issued a new series of banknotes was the 2010 series, which has been in circulation for seven or eight years. As elsewhere, we design and launch new series of banknotes at regular intervals with the aim of enabling banknotes in circulation to incorporate the latest printing technology and make it difficult for counterfeit syndicates to imitate or replicate them. We must know that in ancient and modern China and abroad, printing counterfeit banknotes has always been the dream goal of outlaws. There are currently 2,660 million Hong Kong dollar banknotes in circulation in Hong Kong, with a face value of HK460 billion. However, the number of counterfeit banknotes seized by the police in recent years is small, with less than 1 in every million banknotes. This proportion of counterfeit banknotes is a very low level in the world. We have such good results, in addition to relying on the efficient detection work of Hong Kong's law enforcement organs and the public's high awareness and vigilance of banknotes, to a large extent, Hong Kong can keep pace with the times, explore and study the latest technology every once in a while, adopt the world's most advanced banknote anti-counterfeiting technology, introduce new ideas, and increase the difficulty of manufacturing counterfeit banknotes To maintain public confidence in the banknotes in circulation of the Hong Kong dollar. 3. When it was realized, the 2010 edition of the series of banknotes was in circulation, and the latest anti-counterfeiting technology of that year had been introduced. So far, the police have seized counterfeit banknotes, and no anti-counterfeiting features have been found to be highly simulated or successfully imitated. But we cannot let our guard down, because I am convinced that counterfeit syndicates will continue to work hard to imitate our banknotes. Just as in 2013, we found a very highly simulated 2003 series of 1,000 yuan counterfeit banknotes, which contained imitation metal wire and fluorescent silver code. The emergence of this batch of counterfeit banknotes has affected the public's confidence in the banknotes in circulation of the Hong Kong dollar and caused inconvenience to merchants. However, fortunately, we had already issued the new series of banknotes in 2010, and the HKMA decided to speed up the recovery of the 2003 series of banknotes, reduce the circulation and greatly reduce the risk of the public accidentally receiving and using counterfeit banknotes. The lesson of this is that we must always be vigilant and not take it lightly. For this reason, the HKMA has been discussing and preparing to launch a new series of banknotes with consultants and experts and three banknote issuing banks as early as three years ago. 4. Due to scientific and technological progress, the most advanced anti-counterfeiting features, in addition to being difficult to imitate or copy, will also facilitate the public to easily identify without the need for special light or machine assistance. This new collection of banknotes in Hong Kong 2018 features cutting-edge technology, including a rolling pattern made with color-changing inks and a more recognizable rolling pattern metal wire. Later, Vice President Li Dazhi will introduce these new anti-counterfeiting technologies and features. 5. The biggest difference between this new banknote series and the 2010 edition is that, in addition to the introduction of the latest anti-counterfeiting technology, it is to unify the design of the back of the banknotes of the three banknotes with five themes that are closely related to Hong Kong and reflect the characteristics of Hong Kong. In other words, new banknotes of the same denomination, three banknote issuing banks will all use the same theme to design and create. Since each of these five themes is special, we and the banknote issuing bank have specially invited relevant experts to provide technical guidance in order to be rigorous. I would like to thank the experts of the Eight Harmony Hall, the West Kowloon Cultural District Authority, the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department and the Academy for Performing Arts for their valuable advice on the design of the banknote. 6. Another feature of the new 2018 series of banknotes is that the back design is vertical rather than the traditional horizontal design. The vertical pattern is a relatively new design, which will not only bring freshness to the public, but also make it easy for the public to identify the old and new series of banknotes. 7. In terms of caring for the visually impaired, we will continue to provide an accessible platform to help visually impaired people identify banknotes. In addition to retaining the 2010 version of the braille silver code in the lower left corner of the banknote and the feel line on both sides of the banknote, we invited the blind tutoring committee to develop a mobile phone application "Reading Money", using the lens of the mobile phone to scan the banknote, you can read the banknote silver code. Nope It should be noted that since the mobile phone lens does not have the function of distinguishing the authenticity of the banknote, the program can only read the silver code of the banknote, but we believe that this application can make it easier for the visually impaired to use the banknote in their daily lives. 8. Following today's new banknote launch ceremony, tomorrow the HKMA will launch a series of promotional activities, including a travelling exhibition and seminar in various districts. The first stop on the tour is the International Finance Center Mall. Our Student Ambassadors will distribute leaflets to merchants in various districts to promote the anti-counterfeiting features and theme design of the new banknote collection to the public. Tomorrow, at the start of the first round of the exhibition, we will launch a mobile app game at the same time, hoping to attract more members of the public to visit the exhibition and learn about new banknotes. I sincerely invite all media friends to attend the opening ceremony of the traveling exhibition at the IFC Mall at 11:15 tomorrow, and try out this new mobile app game after visiting the exhibition. 9. Speaking of which, everyone should be wondering what the five featured themes of the 2018 new banknote collection are. The five themes are the HK1,000 International Financial Centre, the HK500 Hong Kong Geopark, the HK100 Cantonese Opera, the HK50 Hong Kong Butterfly, and the HK20 Hong Kong dollar tea drinking culture. We've also made a short film that introduces each of these five design themes one by one, which will be played later for everyone to enjoy. 10. Thank you! Last revision date: 24 July 2018

Title: Response on triggering of the weak-side CU at 7.85
text: Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Response on triggering of the weak-side CU at 7.85 19/09/22, 12:56 Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 16 Aug 2018 Response on triggering of the weak-side CU at 7.85 Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority The triggering of the weak side Convertibility Undertaking (CU) in the order of HK16.8 billion in the last two days was mainly driven by interest arbitrage trades. This is the reversal of massive inflow into Hong Kong dollar (HKD) of around 1 trillion previously. The outflow of funds from Hong Kong is a normal and inevitable process for HKD interest rate normalisation under the Linked Exchange Rate System. The HKMA will continue to buy HKD at 7.85 when the weak-side CU is triggered to ensure HKD exchange rate stability. I wish to remind the public again to manage the market and interest rate risks prudently. Hong Kong banking system has adequate liquidity to cope with outflow of funds. The HKMA also stands ready to calibrate the issuance of Exchange Fund Bills, which amount to 1 trillion in total, to release liquidity in order to deal with possible sharp outflow from HKD. Last revision date : 16 August 2018 / 1/1

Title: Remarks after FOMC Meeting
text: 19/09/22, 12:56 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Remarks after FOMC Meeting Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 27 Sep 2018 Remarks after FOMC Meeting Norman T.L. Chan, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority Remarks on 27 September 2018 As widely expected, the FOMC raised its policy rate by 25 basis points last night. This morning, the HKMA also adjusted our Base Rate for the Discount Window by 25 basis points to 2.5%. USA I believe that the Fed is highly likely to continue to raise interest rates because: a) in the short run the US economic growth momentum continues to be strong thanks to the front loading of the massive fiscal stimulus; b) labour market conditions are tight, which could lead to higher wage pressure; c) commodity and energy prices have been holding up with oil prices at US80 per barrel; and d) the trade tariffs, if implemented fully, may lead to higher consumer goods prices. All these could lead to rising inflation pressure in the US. The Fed expects one more hike this year and three times in 2019. However, there is the risk that inflation and interest rates in the US may rise at a pace faster than the market has expected. Hong Kong The HKD interest rates have been steadily rising from the low levels in 2017. One-month HIBOR is now at 2.2%, a rise of 1.8% from the low of 0.4% in 2017. Many banks have raised also their term deposit rates in recent months. With the rising HIBOR and term deposit rates in line with the hike in US interest rates, the funding cost of the banking system has increased. Many market participants are now expecting that the prime lending rates and savings deposit rates may soon be raised. If this should happen, it will be the first hike in the last 12 years. Banks have different funding cost structures. It is a commercial decision for them to decide whether, when and by how much they wish to adjust their interest rates. / 1/2 19/09/22, 12:56 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Remarks after FOMC Meeting Conclusion The current global economic conditions and financial environment are full of uncertainties for Hong Kong. It is unclear whether the asset market, especially the property market, would undergo significant adjustments, or whether China/US trade tension would worsen and drag on, or whether the pace of US interest rate normalisation would be quicker than expected. The public is well advised to be on high alert and remain vigilant of these uncertainties and to manage the risks prudently. Last revision date : 27 September 2018 / 2/2

Title: Welcoming Remarks at the FPS Activation Ceremony
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 28 Sep 2018 Welcome speech at the opening ceremony of "FPS" Chan Tak Lin is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority The Financial Secretary, representatives of banks and operators of stored value payment instruments, distinguished guests, friends of the media, 1. Welcome to the opening ceremony of the Express Payment System today. Since we announced the launch of FPS on 17 September and started accepting public registration as payees, more than 450,000 people have registered so far. The day after tomorrow (September 30th), "Rpm Fast" will be fully opened. At that time, Hong Kong will enter a new era of electronic payment, because "FPS" is the world's only micropayment system, and once opened, we can enjoy the year-round, easy to operate, clear and secure, full access, support for Hong Kong dollars and RMB, as well as personal small transfer free of charge instant payment services. 2. In addition to FPS, the HKMA's Common QR Code standard and application tool is also the world's first. Starting from today, merchants no longer need to place a bunch of QR codes for different payment instruments at the cashier, only need a common QR code, they can collect payments for different electronic payment instruments. Hong Kong has entered a new era of payment, not only fast payment, but also simple and fast collection! 3. With the launch of FPS, the retail payment ecosystem in Hong Kong will undergo significant changes. In addition to the competition between banks and stored value payment tool operators between users and merchant groups, the living habits of citizens (including shopping and payment) will gradually change. "Fast Turns" coupled with fintech developments, such as virtual banking, will help Hong Kong's banking sector enter one "A New Age of Wisdom". In this new era, nothing is "static", only "progress" is "eternal". I would like to thank the FPS banks and SVF operators, the Hong Kong Association of Banks and HKIBEX, as well as my colleagues from the HKMA, who have worked together to overcome the difficulties that have enabled us to launch and launch FPS. 4. I estimate that many of your friends have already registered for "FPS", if not, I encourage you to register quickly so that you can feel the new payment experience brought by "FPS" from the day after tomorrow. After today's opening ceremony, guests and media friends are welcome to visit the demonstration booth specially set up by banks and payment instrument operators to take the lead in testing the new user experience after the launch of the FPS system. Thank you! Last revision date: 28 September 2018
