Title: Speech at the Annual Conference of Financial Street Forum 2020: Promoting Higher-level RMB Capital Account Liberalisation
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech Nov. 30, 2020 2020 Financial Street Forum Annual Meeting Speech: Promoting a Higher Level of RMB Capital Account Opening Yu Weiwen, President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Distinguished guests: Hello everyone! It is a great pleasure to attend this year's Financial Street Forum Annual Meeting and discuss the integration and change under the global changes with friends from all over the world through videos . In 2020, the global economy and financial markets experienced unprecedented shocks. In the face of the COVID-19 pandemic, governments everywhere have introduced different fiscal and monetary policies to do their best to support the real economy, preserve employment, and assist enterprises and individuals to cope with difficulties. Except for brief fluctuations, global financial markets have remained largely stable, with both Chinese mainland and Hong Kong's financial markets showing a high degree of earthquake resilience, both financial systems remaining stable, and financing and trading activities proceeding in an orderly manner. More importantly, the mainland's reform and opening up continues to make great strides forward, and in the financial field, the mainland market continues to integrate with the international market. More international financial institutions are able to participate to a greater extent in the activities of the mainland's financial markets, which is a very encouraging development. When it comes to financial cooperation and change, the internationalization of the renminbi is certainly an important component. How to promote a higher level of opening up of capital projects in today's complex environment? In this process, what role can Hong Kong play and what contribution? I would like to share with you some of my observations. Let's first look at the positive role played by Hong Kong in the process of opening up the renminbi capital account in the past. The opening of the renminbi capital account and the internationalization of the renminbi complement each other. In the past ten years of RMB internationalization, Hong Kong has always participated in and matched, playing a pioneering role: in 2004, Hong Kong has launched retail RMB business; In 2007, the first batch of dim sum bonds was issued in Hong Kong; In 2009, in line with the pilot work of RMB settlement business for cross-border trade in the Mainland, Hong Kong's offshore RMB business was expanded from individuals to enterprises. This was followed by a series of major measures to open up the renminbi capital account, with Hong Kong financial institutions piloting RQFII in 2011; The opening of Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect and Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect in 2014 and 2016 respectively, and the launch of Bond Connect in 2017, have made Hong Kong a major springboard for international investors to invest in the mainland equity and bond market. As a pioneer in offshore RMB business, Hong Kong has an important mission, and financial stability is the most basic condition. In the face of the epidemic and the complicated internal and external situation in the past year, Hong Kong's financial system has remained stable: the linked exchange rate system has operated smoothly, the banking system has been stable, and the capital market has operated in an orderly manner. At the same time, the financial linkage between Hong Kong and the mainland has been continuously strengthened: the transaction volume of the interconnection mechanism has steadily increased. In the first 8 months of this year, Bond Connect trading volume increased by 1.4 times compared with the same period last year; Stock Connect North Connect trading volume rose by more than 70% per cent. Hong Kong's stock IPO market is very active, with total IPOs totaling more than US27 billion in the first nine months of this year. 58% more than last year. These indicators reflect the advantages of Hong Kong's international financial services platform and play an important role in opening up the RMB capital account. Looking ahead, the demand for RMB asset allocation by foreign investors will have a long-term upward trend. Affected by the epidemic, the global economy is in a downturn, but China is the first to get out of the epidemic, and it is also a small number of major economies with GDP growth, which is a driving force for the global economy to come out of the trough. On the other hand, the ultra-low interest rate environment in developed countries is expected to last for some time, putting some pressure on the return of assets. Against this backdrop, the rate of return on RMB assets is significantly higher than that of most assets in Europe and the United States, which is quite attractive to foreign investors. More importantly, since the beginning of the internationalization of the renminbi, the mainland has vigorously promoted the market-oriented reform of the exchange rate and interest rate formation mechanism, and the achievements are obvious to all. International investors' confidence in RMB assets and the mainland capital markets is increasing. In the past period of time, under the background of good economic recovery, the effective exchange rate of the renminbi against a basket of currencies has remained stable, creating favorable conditions for the acceleration of the internationalization of the renminbi and the further opening up of the capital account. In the past few years, major international indices have successively incorporated A-shares and RMB bonds, and gradually increased their weight, which reflects the high recognition of RMB assets in the global financial market. The latest example is FTSE Russell's announcement last month that it will include Chinese government bonds in the world government bond index in phases starting next October. Since its inclusion in this index, RMB bonds have been included in the three most important indices in the global bond market, which is also conducive to further enhancing the status of RMB assets as the main international reserve assets. The market estimates that passive funds that track the three major indexes alone will attract hundreds of billions of dollars of money into the mainland bond market. The market effect of RMB bonds in these indices is actually obvious. From the beginning of 2019 to September this year, the holdings of foreign investors in the domestic interbank bond market increased by more than one trillion yuan, an increase of less than 70% by less than 70%. The feast of international capital investing heavily in RMB assets is just a prelude, and the RMB assets held by foreign investors currently account for only a small part of the total amount of the mainland's financial market, and by the middle of this year, foreign investors have only held 3 percent of the bonds in the interbank bond market, and the A holdings have been held The share market share is less than 4%. We have every reason to believe that the future is more worthy of our expectations. In the future, I will focus on how to give full play to Hong Kong's advantages and help deepen the opening up of the RMB capital account. One of the keys to the opening up of the RMB capital account to the next level is whether it can greatly increase the international holdings of RMB assets, and the offshore market can play an important role in this regard through the continuous improvement of its own capabilities and the docking and cooperation with the onshore market. As a major financial centre and offshore RMB hub, Hong Kong has a highly market-oriented and internationally integrated financial market and infrastructure, and is the main gateway for the mainland's capital market to attract international capital. The Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect, Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect and Bond Connect launched in the past few years are to give full play to Hong Kong's characteristics and ensure that the mainland financial market can introduce foreign investors in an orderly manner at the lowest institutional cost under the premise of controllable risks, promote the exchange of RMB capital accounts, and accumulate experience for the further opening up and development of the onshore market. For example, Bond Connect, by strengthening the connection between the financial infrastructure of the two places, has introduced a multi-tier custody model for the mainland bond market without reducing regulatory penetration. Bond Connect has been running smoothly since its launch three years ago, proving that multi-tiered custody is a viable model. This successful institutional arrangement can be replicated into other investment channels, bringing more choices and greater convenience to investors. The connectivity mechanism has yielded fruitful results since its opening. The People's Bank of China, the Monetary Authority and other relevant institutions have also continued to explore innovations, follow the needs of the market, and constantly introduce various optimization measures, such as increasing the trading platform of Bond Connect, improving settlement arrangements, increasing the daily quota of Stock Connect, and so on. These measures have improved operational efficiency, reduced transaction costs and provided investors with more diversified options. Recently, the mainland regulatory authorities have introduced several important measures to open up the bond market to the outside world, including optimizing the foreign exchange arrangements for international investors to participate in the Bond Connect, and Hong Kong will actively cooperate in promoting relevant work to better serve the majority of investors. Both Equity Connect and Bond Connect have achieved very good results over the past few years, and the next step is to expand connectivity to other asset classes. In June this year, the People's Bank of China, together with the HKMA and relevant regulators, announced the launch of a pilot cross-border wealth management business in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. At present, the regulators of the three places are stepping up the formulation of business arrangements, hoping to strive to start the wealth management link as soon as possible. In the past few years, the opening of the capital account has made good progress, but to achieve a higher level of openness, I think one of the important issues is to provide the market with more products and channels for risk management. When the proportion of RMB assets of international investors rises, their need for risk management will certainly increase. If the demand in this regard cannot be met, it will certainly cause resistance for international capital to further increase its holdings of RMB assets. At the same time, in order to introduce various derivative transactions that manage risks, we must also be careful to deal with the associated risks. RMB foreign exchange and interest rate derivatives trading in Hong Kong is relatively mature, and the trading rules and regulatory requirements are in line with international standards. According to triennial statistics from the Bank for International Settlements, Hong Kong maintained its position as the world's most active RMB foreign exchange and derivatives trading center last year, with a daily trading volume of US107.6 billion, up nearly 40% from three years ago. Therefore, Hong Kong has relatively mature conditions to provide better services for international investors investing in RMB assets. In the next step, we will work closely with the Mainland to launch equity and bond-related derivative instruments on the basis of interconnection to meet market demand to the greatest extent possible under the condition of controllable risks. Distinguished guests, the further opening up of the Chinese mainland capital account and the significant increase in RMB asset allocation by international investors are rare opportunities in the future, and there are even comments in the market that this is once in a lifetime. To be prepared for this opportunity, we should make full use of both onshore and offshore market resources. Hong Kong is the link between onshore and offshore markets and the best strategic stronghold for financial institutions and investors to seize this golden opportunity. We look forward to Hong Kong continuing to play a unique role in the process of opening up the RMB capital account. Finally, I hope that this forum will be a complete success. Thank you. Title: Opening Remarks at China Shenzhen Fintech Global Summit 2020
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech December 14, 2020 Opening Speech of China (Shenzhen) Fintech Global Summit 2020 Liu Yingbin is Senior Assistant President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, Hello everyone. It is a great honor to participate in this year's China (Shenzhen) Fintech Global Summit and share the opportunities that Hong Kong can bring to fintech companies in Shenzhen and other regions through video with friends in Shenzhen and around the world. As an important international financial centre in the world, I believe that Hong Kong's financial system can withstand shocks as a prerequisite if Hong Kong is to bring various opportunities to domestic and foreign enterprises and investors. Therefore, I would like to talk to you here about how Hong Kong is facing various challenges. In the past year, the new crown epidemic has seriously hit the global economy and society, geopolitics is impacting the international order established over the years, and various accumulated contradictions have erupted over time. In the face of the epidemic and the complex internal and external situation in Hong Kong, the financial system remains stable, the banking system remains stable, and the total amount of deposits has risen steadily. In terms of the money market, the orderly operation of the linked exchange rate system has firmly stabilized investors' confidence. All kinds of data reflect the confidence of international investors in Hong Kong as an international financial center, and have strongly shattered the rumors and rumors of so-called "capital gouging". In terms of capital markets, global stock markets have become volatile in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, but fundraising activity in Hong Kong remains very active: in the first 10 months of this year, IPO fundraising has exceeded US32 billion, an increase of 66% over the same period last year. At the same time, the financial linkage between Hong Kong and the Mainland has been strengthened, and the trading volume of the interconnection mechanism has increased steadily: the average trading volume of Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect and Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect in the first three quarters of this year reached RMB110 billion, and the Bond Connect reached nearly RMB20 billion, both of which increased year-on-year 115%, which fully reflects Hong Kong's role as a bridge for the introduction of international capital into the mainland market. In the face of various severe challenges, Hong Kong can still move forward steadily and face difficulties, and I believe that there will be a more stable foundation for continued development in the future , and bring greater development opportunities to financial and science and technology innovation enterprises at home and abroad. Let me now talk to you about the three major opportunities that Hong Kong can bring to the financial and technological innovation enterprises in the Greater Bay Area under the new global economic pattern. First of all, Hong Kong is an international banking center, with more than 70% of the world's top 100 banks operating in Hong Kong. Hong Kong is also the top choice for companies to raise funds on the market, with 7 years of IPO fundraising in the past 11 years ranking globally. The mature financial industry has created strong demand for fintech companies and provided financing channels for innovative enterprises that need to raise funds. Recently, many large Chinese-funded enterprises have chosen to list in Hong Kong and have received enthusiastic responses from the market, with Hong Kong's international market advantages, Hong Kong can help financial science and technology enterprises in the Greater Bay Area to go global. Second, after several years of efforts, Hong Kong has established a dynamic platform for financial and technological enterprises at home and abroad, and Hong Kong's efforts in the field of fintech and innovation have been internationally recognized. For example, Hong Kong has a world-class communications and financial infrastructure, of which our Instant Payment and Settlement System (RTGS) is the only payment system in the world that supports four currencies simultaneously (i.e. HKD, USD, EUR and RMB), handling transactions of over HK1 trillion and RMB per day. With these advantages, the HKMA has taken a multi-pronged approach to promote the development of financial technology. In terms of infrastructure, the fast payment system "FPS" launched in 2018 has opened up bank accounts and e-wallets, and has recorded more than 6 million registered accounts, and the cumulative transaction amount has increased to about HK1.8 billion. We are also exploring a new financial infrastructure called Business Data Connect to enable SMEs to use their data to obtain better financial services and to address the long-standing financing difficulties of SMEs. In the banking sector, we have introduced healthy competition to accelerate financial innovation, and last year we licensed eight virtual banks, seven of which have been formally put into service, providing the public with a more diversified and innovative banking service experience and enhancing the competitiveness of Hong Kong's banking industry. In particular, our regulatory sandbox allows banks to develop products flexibly, as well as allowing regulators to assess risks early and provide policy support. With the above new projects and initiatives, we welcome domestic and foreign financial technology companies to participate in the development and jointly develop innovative products to bring innovative experiences to customers. Third, the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area is an important growth engine for the country and a hinterland for financial technology innovation. To develop into a financial technology hub in the region, it is particularly important to promote cross-border cooperation, especially cross-border applications between the Mainland and Hong Kong. Since the HKMA promoted the establishment of the trade finance platform trade linkage in 2018, regulators and operators of the two places have actively built platforms to promote cross-border trade financing. Trade Linkage and People's Bank of China Trade Finance Platform were successfully connected in October this year and trade finance transactions have been completed for seven banks, involving a total trade amount of more than HK26 million. In the future, we expect to also work closely with the Mainland on digital currencies and cross-border payments, so we believe that closer cross-border fintech cooperation will bring greater development opportunities to science and technology enterprises in both places." conclusion Combined with the mainland's leading edge in technology application and Hong Kong's international financial technology advantages, Hong Kong can support mainland financial science and technology enterprises to go global. Looking ahead, I hope that Hong Kong will deepen cooperation with China in the field of financial technology, strengthen financial technology innovation exchanges and interactions, and create new heights for the financial science and technology innovation of the two places. Thank you. Note: The Summit was held on December 13, 2020 Last revision date: December 14, 2020

Title: Keynote Address at ISDA Virtual Conference: Benchmark Strategies Forum Asia Pacific
text: 19/09/22, 12:50 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Keynote Address at ISDA Virtual Conference: Benchmark Strategies Forum Asia Pacific Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 17 Mar 2021 Keynote Address at ISDA Virtual Conference: Benchmark Strategies Forum Asia Pacific Edmond Lau, Senior Executive Director, Hong Kong Monetary Authority Opening 1. Good morning. I'm very glad to join you virtually today at this ISDA conference. First of all, let me take this opportunity to thank ISDA for organising this event and inviting me to speak here. As we moved into 2021 which is a critical year for LIBOR transition, this subject has become one of the most topical talks in the market. I understand that there will be three panels in today's conference, which will further discuss some of the issues and challenges arising from LIBOR transition. With the presence of all the distinguished speakers at this conference, I'm sure that we will all benefit a lot from the conference today and get valuable insights on useful ways and approaches to a smooth LIBOR transition. "3Cs" Toolkit 2.1 think no one would disagree that LIBOR transition is one of the key priorities for the global financial markets this year, with the backdrop that LIBOR has been so deeply ingrained in the market, and widely used across multiple asset classes globally. 3. Hong Kong is the third largest USD trading centre in the world, right after London and New York. Given the large amount of USD transactions in our economy and also our close linkages with other financial markets around the world, it is inevitable that there is a considerable amount of financial activities linked to LIBOR in our financial market. According to the HKMAs latest survey results, there were US615 billion of assets and US180 billion of liabilities in our banking system referencing LIBOR at the end of September 2020, representing about 30% and 10% respectively of the banking system's total assets and total liabilities denominated in foreign currencies. Additionally, there were derivatives contracts with an aggregate amount of US4.1 trillion in notional value referencing LIBOR. The sheer size of these LIBOR-based transactions speak for the importance of ensuring a smooth and orderly LIBOR transition in the banking sector. 4. To facilitate our banking sector in preparing for this transition, the HKMA issued in July 2020 a series of "transition milestones" for banks. The three milestones are: (i) First, we expect banks to be in a position to offer products referencing the alternative reference rates to LIBOR from 1 January 2021; (ii) Second, we require banks to include adequate fall-back provisions in all newly issued LIBOR-linked contracts that will mature after 2021 from 1 January 2021; and / 1/5 19/09/22, 12:50 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Keynote Address at ISDA Virtual Conference: Benchmark Strategies Forum Asia Pacific (iii)Third, banks should cease to issue new LIBOR-linked products that will mature after 2021 by 30 June 2021. 5. While I'm pleased to note the growing awareness of LIBOR transition across the financial markets, the work ahead remains substantial. As we get closer and closer to end-2021, it is important for us to continue our efforts to facilitate transition. In that respect, I would like to highlight three crucial elements that we think are essential to LIBOR transition, and hopefully they could offer some useful guidance to the market as we move along this unprecedented journey. To keep it short and simple, I would summarise these elements by 3Cs, which are Capability, Coordination and Commitment. Capability 6. Let me start with the first "C", which is Capability. We all know LIBOR cessation is going to happen, and all of us want to ensure that the transition will take place as smoothly as possible. A critical element in achieving this goal is to have the right toolkit and necessary capabilities to manage the transition. When I say Capability, I am referring to the operational and system capabilities of a bank that would enable a transition from LIBOR to the alternative reference rates in their day-to-day trading activities and workflows. 7. We appreciate that a lot of work is underway to support this transition, such as IT system set-ups, operational model adjustments, risk management and accounting system upgrades, to name but a few. All these ground work is fundamental to the implementation of the transition, especially with regard to the different characteristics of LIBOR vis-a-vis the alternative reference rates, which would no doubt bring about changes to our market conventions and business practices that have been in place for years. 8. In fact, that is also why we have asked banks, as part of our transition milestones, to get themselves ready, with effect from this year, to offer products referencing the alternative reference rates to LIBOR. Having the necessary operational and system capabilities is a vital building block in supporting any new product offerings. As at today, we are pleased to note that many banks in Hong Kong can offer products referencing the alternative reference rates. 9. At the same time, we understand the importance of promoting market awareness, and encourage all relevant parties, not only banks, but also their corporate clients, to get prepared and build the necessary capabilities in supporting this transition. On this front, the HKMA has been active in working with the industry associations to host various webinars to keep the practitioners up to speed and to facilitate contact among individual institutions to enable timely exchange of views and information, e.g., on the relevant tax and accounting issues. Moreover, the HKMA has worked closely with the Treasury Markets Association (TMA) to develop a short note for corporate treasurers on the benchmark reforms, and encouraged banks to distribute it to their corporate customers to impress upon them the need to make early preparation. Coordination 10. The second "C" is Coordination. In addition to having the right toolkit as I just described, it is equally important to ensure effective coordination to address issues relating to LIBOR transition that are of common interest to the market. / 2/5 19/09/22, 12:50 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Keynote Address at ISDA Virtual Conference: Benchmark Strategies Forum Asia Pacific 11. On this, I would like to applaud the hard work and rigorous efforts of industry organisations like ISDA in bringing together market participants across the globe to discuss and work collectively in developing industry-wide solutions and driving market consensus. Given the evolving and complex nature of this subject, the ongoing dialogue with market participants also brings firms up to speed on the latest developments and enhance their readiness for the transition. 12. One example I would like to share is the IBOR (interbank offered rates) Fallbacks Supplement and Protocol launched by ISDA, which took effect in January. These documents enable market participants to incorporate appropriate fallbacks into their new and legacy derivatives contracts referenced to key IBORs, including LIBOR. This is an especially effective move by ISDA in helping the industry prepare for the cessation of LIBOR. And, thanks to ISDAs efforts in promoting a wider use of these documents, more than 13,000 firms across the globe - from Asia, Europe, the US, to the rest of the world have already adhered to the protocol. Without doubt, the ISDA protocol provides an efficient way for market participants to handle their legacy contracts, and offers a viable back-up for LIBOR cessation. 13. We strongly encourage banks in Hong Kong to adhere to these documents. Having said that, we understand that the documents may not be able to resolve all the issues for the legacy derivative contracts. In particular, some commercial counterparties may prefer tailor-made solutions for their LIBOR-linked contracts. In this respect, we note that ISDA has also published templates to help firms bilaterally agree with their counterparties to include the new fallbacks into their legacy derivatives transactions. This provides market participants with greater flexibility when considering the best way forward for their own cases. 14. But, as you could imagine, bilateral discussion often takes longer time and requires greater efforts. Therefore, we have been encouraging banks to proactively reach out to their clients to discuss transition plans and amend derivative contracts in a timely manner. We are particularly pleased to note that steady progress has been made in this respect. As at end-December 2020, all banks in Hong Kong have already developed a communication plan for re-negotiating existing contracts with their clients, and a majority of them have completed or in the process of remediating relevant contracts. 15. When we talk about coordination, another important pillar is regulatory coordination. Over the past years, there has been strong collaboration among regulators and central banks globally to discuss and address issues on benchmark transition. We at the HKMA are mindful of the importance of ensuring close coordination with our counterparts around the world. 16. At the international level, we have been actively participating in various fora to contribute to the ongoing developments. In the context of the Financial Stability Board (FSB), we are a member of the Official Sector Steering Group which was established under the FSB to coordinate the work on interest rate benchmark reforms globally. We are also leading the work to conduct a follow-up survey to update the jurisdictional LIBOR exposures and understand how different economies are tackling the transition and supervisory challenges under the Standing Committee on Supervisory and Regulatory Cooperation. 17. Closer to home, we are also actively taking part on the coordination work at the regional level. For example, I am currently serving as the chair of the Executives' Meeting of East Asia-Pacific Central Banks (EMEAP) Working Group on Financial Markets (WGFM). / 3/5 19/09/22, 12:50 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Keynote Address at ISDA Virtual Conference: Benchmark Strategies Forum Asia Pacific Leveraging the capabilities and experience of ISDA, and having regard to the need for smooth IBOR transition in the EMEAP economies, it should be of mutual benefit to explore the development of a second ISDA IBOR Fallbacks protocol to cover fallbacks for IBORs that are not currently captured by the protocol launched last year. 18. That should be conducive to facilitating a smooth benchmark transition in the region. The HKMA would be happy to facilitate further exchange of views and information between ISDA and EMEAP WGFM. I believe that this course of action resonates well with ISDA's action plan, as it aligns with ISDAs efforts to incorporate regional voices on an ongoing basis as evidenced by, for example, a panel focusing on "The Regional Approach" in the conference today. Commitment 19. Let me now turn to the last "C": Commitment. We all know there is no one-size-fits-all solution, and it is important for banks to consider their own needs and constraints when they tailor-make respective transition programs that work best for themselves. However, I would say that all these transition programs share one thing in common - that is the full commitment and support from the top management of the bank. These cover important aspects such as resources allocation, action plan formulation, and stakeholders engagement. The stakeholders include your staff internally and your business counterparties externally. You need to make sure that they both fully understand the importance of LIBOR transition and know what needs to be done to ensure the smooth transition. 20. We fully appreciate the dynamic and evolving nature of this subject on LIBOR transition. We know that there are different moving parts, which may impact on your respective action plans along the way. This means that we all need to continue to monitor closely international and market developments. The IBAs extension on the publication of key USD LIBOR settings until end-June 2023 is one such example. The extension would allow time for more legacy USD LIBOR contracts to mature, and give counterparties more time to renegotiate and amend USD LIBOR contracts maturing after end-June 2023. Banks should not relax their efforts in preparing themselves for the cessation of LIBOR. Closing 21. At the beginning of my remarks, I suggested the "3Cs" as a useful tool on what each entity could do individually to attain the important LIBOR transition goal. In closing, if you would allow me to add a final "C", which is "Collective". LIBOR transition is so complicated and involves so many parties in both bilateral and multilateral negotiation so that smooth transition will require collective and timely efforts from all of us to make it happen. With that, I encourage all of you to continue your collaborative efforts to prepare for the transition and make best use of ISDA Fallback Protocol and Supplement in these collaborative efforts. 22.1 hope all of you will have a fruitful and productive discussion today. Thank you. / 19/09/22, 12:50 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Keynote Address at ISDA Virtual Conference: Benchmark Strategies Forum Asia Pacific Last revision date : 17 March 2021 / 5/5

Title: Opening Keynote at Hong Kong Economic Summit 2021
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 23 Mar 2021 Opening Speech at the Hong Kong Economic Summit 2021 Yu Weiwen is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. Hello everyone! It is a pleasure to attend the Hong Kong Economic Summit again. 2. The theme of this year's summit is "Recovery, Reconstruction, Regeneration", which is indeed an appropriate proposition for Hong Kong, which has experienced social events and is looking forward to getting rid of the new crown pneumonia. Today, I would like to borrow these three concepts to talk about some of the current situations and trends in the development of Hong Kong's financial industry. 3. Healing the wounds and treating the sick is basically carried out in accordance with the three stages of rehabilitation, reconstruction and regeneration, but due to the importance of the financial industry to Hong Kong, the work of the HKMA is advancing almost simultaneously in three aspects. Our aim is to preserve our foundations, enhance the competitiveness of the financial industry and create opportunities for long-term development. rehabilitation 4. When it comes to restoration, we must first stabilize our foundations. Under the multiple blows, Hong Kong's economy has been challenged as never before, and small and medium-sized enterprises with fewer resources have borne the brunt of it. SMEs are an important pillar of Hong Kong's economy, accounting for more than 98% of the total number of enterprises and 45% of the private sector. To stabilize the economy, maintain employment, and retain strength for economic recovery, small and medium-sized enterprises are the primary objects of support. 5. In the old concept, banks would generally "rain down", but this time, the Government, the HKMA and the banking industry have worked together to protect SMEs from the wind and rain in the face of adversity. In May last year, with the support of the HKMA, the banking industry launched the "Pre-approval Repayment of Interest and Non-Repayment" scheme to gain breathing space for SMEs. Since its launch, the Scheme, together with other mitigation measures by banks, has supported about 91,000 cases, including corporate and individual customers, involving an amount of approximately HK800 billion. 6. We recently announced that we will extend this scheme for another six months to October this year, and the HKMA's mortgage securities companies have also embarked on an enhancement of the "100% Guaranteed Preferential Lending" measure launched in April last year to benefit more SMEs. 7. At the same time, the Certified Public Trust Company is working with the Government to step up preparations for the 100% Guaranteed Personal Preferential Loan Scheme to provide support to the unemployed. 8. It is key for the banking industry to work with us in an extraordinary time, and it is also a strong backing for Hong Kong's financial and banking system . 9. I would like to summarize it as an excellent ecosystem for Hong Kong's financial industry. In the face of many challenges, the rock-solid linked exchange rate system has once again come into play. The HKD exchange rate has been at a strong level since 2020, with continued inflows of funds, with the HKMA absorbing US50 billion from the market and injecting HK400 billion into the banking system accordingly to ensure that the market is well funded. 10. In fact, the total amount of bank deposits in Hong Kong has increased by 8.4% in the past two years, making the claim of 'capital go' untrue. 11. As the source of the economy, Hong Kong's banking industry has long been better than its international counterparts in terms of capital adequacy ratio, liquidity ratio or bad debt ratio. These figures seem to be the icing on the cake when the economy is booming, and they become powerful tools to send charcoal in the snow when the economy is in a downturn. Over the past two years, the HKMA has enabled the banking sector to free up HK1 trillion in lending space by reducing banks' buffer capital ratios and other measures, with greater capacity to support corporate and individual customers. 12. Another feature of Hong Kong's financial ecosystem is that it is both deep and wide, from commercial banks, investment banks, stocks, bonds, assets and wealth management, to foreign exchange transactions, etc., we are in a leading position in the region in all financial fields, with strong competitiveness, and the financial industry can still maintain its prosperity and support various economic activities in the face of serious economic shocks. 13. The mature financial industry extends to a variety of professional services. Hong Kong's first-class level of legal, accounting, taxation, risk management and compliance, coupled with Hong Kong's reputable rule of law system, independent judiciary, unique bilingual common law, and a financial regulatory system that keeps pace with the times, all work together to form a fair and reliable ecosystem that creates favorable conditions for the sustainable development of the financial industry and provides strong support for economic recovery. reconstruction 14. For nearly two years, our reconstruction efforts have focused on the word faith. Reputation is extremely important for maintaining confidence in the financial markets, and from time to time false rumors about Hong Kong's financial markets have been circulating in the market, which, coupled with widespread circulation on social media, has more or less weakened the confidence of market participants, including international investors, in Hong Kong. 15. Over the past year, the HKMA has been in close communication with stakeholders and organised and participated in more than 60 online networking events to explain the real situation in Hong Kong to more than 15,000 stakeholders in the local and international financial markets on facts and figures and respond to their concerns about Hong Kong. We understand that confidence is the accumulation and operation of a long time, and the HKMA will continue to work hard to do a good job in external communication, and the golden paint signboard of the provincial beautiful international financial center. regeneration 16. We must also prepare for the resurgence of the economy and pave the way for Hong Kong's future financial development. I will summarize the future development trend of the financial industry with three key words: mainland opportunities, green finance, and financial technology. Mainland opportunities 17. Mainland opportunities, more accurately in the sense of Hong Kong's access to the Mainland and international financial markets. For many years, Hong Kong has been the main gateway connecting the two capital markets. We just mentioned that Hong Kong's excellent ecosystem, coupled with "one country, two systems", has created this special status. 18. As part of China, Hong Kong has been a window to support the mainland's economic development for the past four decades. We provide a familiar environment and reliable access to the Mainland market for global investors. In recent years, we have often encountered a question: When the mainland's capital market is fully opened, international capital will bypass Hong Kong and directly enter the mainland, will Hong Kong's value fade? 19. Indeed, the mainland's capital markets have been opening up and progressing, such as relaxing the shareholding restrictions of foreign financial institutions, introducing a series of institutional reforms for qualified foreign institutional investors (QFIIs), and further improving the channels for foreign investors to enter the mainland interbank bond market. 20. We welcome these changes, the mainland's huge economic scale must be supported by financial services that match the level and scale, the mainland's financial industry will certainly grow, and Hong Kong's internationally competitive financial industry will certainly benefit from this demand. 21. Taking Bond Connect as an example, foreign investors can already directly participate in the onshore bond market as early as 2010, while the offshore channel of Bond Connect was only opened in 2017, but it has achieved significant growth in more than three years, and the average daily trading volume has tripled in 2019. Another 82% increase was recorded in 2020, and about half of international investor transactions are now conducted through Hong Kong Bond Connect. This example proves that opening up two channels, onshore and offshore, and allowing international investors to choose according to their needs, is the best path for the opening up of the mainland's financial market. 22. We are in close communication with People's Bank of China and look forward to the early opening of Southbound Bond Connect. At the same time, we will enhance the system and services of the Central Clearing and Settlement System (CMU) for Debt Instruments in Xianggang to take advantage of the opportunities brought about by the development of Bond Connect. 23. Another bright spot for the mainland's opportunities is the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. One of our priorities is to strive to implement the "Wealth Management Connect" as soon as possible. With a population of over 70 million and one of the richest areas in the Mainland, the wealth management needs of residents are in the take-off stage, and Wealth Management Connect will provide convenient channels for cross-border investment for residents of the Greater Bay Area and bring new growth points to Hong Kong's wealth management industry. 24. In February this year, the mainland, Hong Kong and Macao regulatory authorities signed a memorandum of understanding on cooperation to lay the foundation for financial cooperation in supervision, and the three places are stepping up preparations to open this eagerly awaited plan at an early date. 25. We are pleased to note that in the just-adopted 14th Five-Year Plan of the People's Republic of China, Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre, a global offshore RMB business hub, an international asset management centre and a risk management centre has been reconfirmed, and calls for deepening and expanding the connectivity between the Mainland and Hong Kong's financial markets. These positions are conducive to Hong Kong's financial industry continuing to play a unique role in the overall situation of national development and seeking greater opportunities. Green and sustainable finance 26. Everyone, green finance and fintech are the two main driving forces leading the development of the global financial industry in the future, and Hong Kong is also in a leading position in these two aspects. 27. Let's start with green finance. To meet the Paris Agreement's climate change goals, the world needs to be carbon neutral by 2050, with an estimated annual expenditure of 1 trillion to 2 trillion. This seemingly distant goal of 2050 is forcing green finance to accelerate across the board. 28. Hong Kong stands at the forefront of green and sustainable development and is taking action. First, governments are committed to achieving carbon neutrality by 2050, a step forward in the commitment of more advanced economies. The HKMA is working with other financial regulators and government departments to promote green and sustainable development, including banking, capital markets, asset management and other financial sectors, and to coordinate the financial sector's response to climate change risks. 29. In fact, Hong Kong is the first Asian economy to require industries to comply with the G20 Task Force on Climate-related Financial by 2025 or earlier Disclosures) to make disclosures of climate-related information. 30. Hong Kong is also a pioneer in the government's green bond scheme. In February this year, the HKMA assisted the government in issuing US2.5 billion green bonds, which are very popular with investors around the world. In response to strong market demand, the Financial Secretary announced in the Annual Budget that he would double the borrowing ceiling of the Government's Green Bond Scheme to HK200 billion, plan to reissue a total of HK175.5 billion in green bonds in the next five years in accordance with market conditions, and attract investors of all types by increasing the diversity of green bond issuance. For example, we plan to launch retail green bonds so that the public can personally support the green and sustainable development of Hong Kong. 31. In terms of market expansion, the Government will launch the Green and Sustainable Finance Funding Scheme in the middle of this year to encourage more financial institutions, enterprises and green certification bodies to participate in Hong Kong's green and sustainable financial market, and we will also strengthen promotion in the Greater Bay Area to further enrich Hong Kong's green financial ecosystem. 32. As the manager of the Exchange Fund, the HKMA also practices responsible investment and we have incorporated environmental, social and governance factors, the so-called ESG, into our investment considerations. Our principle is that ESG investments are prioritized when they are similar in the long-term returns of other investments. Fintech 33. Fintech is another driving force. In recent years, fintech has developed rapidly in Hong Kong. Since the HKMA launched a number of measures of "Wisdom Banking", it has promoted the digitization of banking services, bringing a more convenient and diversified experience to enterprises and the public. 34. Since the HKMA issued the first batch of virtual banking licences in 2019, all 8 virtual banks have been put into operation, the highest number in Asia. At present, the number of accounts opened has reached 580,000, and the total amount of deposits is nearly 20 billion yuan, which has achieved quite good results in the initial stage and injected new impetus into the retail banking market. 35. Looking ahead, data is the key to fintech better serving the real economy and businesses. We are embarking on a new generation of financial infrastructure and plan to launch the Business Data Connect in 2023 to provide a channel for businesses to share their "digital footprint" with banks as they wish. Through this platform, banks can provide new loan products or processes, making it easier and cheaper for SMEs to obtain bank credit than before. 36. In addition, the application of new technologies can also solve some long-standing pain points, and cross-border remittances are a good example. The HKMA and the Central Bank of Thailand have jointly launched a central bank digital currency (CBDC) project for cross-border payments, and the Bank for International Settlements, the People's Bank of China and the Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates have also joined the research program to explore the use of blockchain technology to facilitate real-time cross-border payments, reduce costs and improve the transparency of payment processes. And put this technology in more application scenarios, including cross-border capital transfer, international trade settlement, capital market transactions, etc. We are looking forward to the project making substantial progress in providing cheaper and faster remittance services for businesses and the public. 37. Another focus of the HKMA's future fintech development is to promote the application of compliance technology (Regtech) by banks. Regtech can help banks reduce risk management costs and improve the efficiency of their compliance efforts. One third of banks are already using compliant technology solutions. 38. To promote the application of compliant technology, the HKMA has formulated a two-year plan to build a thriving ecosystem through large-scale events and competitions, the launch of an adoption index, the issuance of practical guidelines, the construction of an information platform, and the establishment of a skills framework for compliance technology talents . Our vision is to establish Hong Kong as a compliant technology hub within five years. conclusion 39. Folks, this process from restoration to regeneration will not be completed overnight, nor will it be smooth sailing. But I am full of confidence in the future, which comes from our sound and powerful financial system, from Hong Kong's unique advantages as an international financial centre, and from the opportunities we have created for tomorrow through our efforts today. A vibrant financial ecosystem will be the solid foundation and powerful engine needed to maintain Hong Kong's prosperity and stability. 40. Thank you! Last revision date: 23 March 2021

Title: Speech at National Security Education Day 2021
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech 15 Apr 2021 National Security Education Day 2021 Speech Yu Weiwen is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Hello everyone: 1. It is a great pleasure to attend this year's National Security Day to share with you the significance of national security in the financial field, and I will talk about three aspects: First, the relationship between national security and financial security; The second is the importance of ensuring financial security and stability; The third is the relevant work of the HKMA . - The relationship between national security and financial security 2. National security and financial security are interdependent and mutually reinforcing. Finance is the foundation supporting the modern economy and society, and a stable financial system is the prerequisite for the people's peace of mind. In the absence of financial security, there will be shortcomings in national security. On the other hand, only on the basis of national security and social stability can financial security be guaranteed and financial development be sustained. 3. When we talk about financial risk and stability, we generally consider market and business risks. However, in recent years, with the rapid digitization and networking of the financial industry, the hidden dangers of cyber attacks have increased; Attempts to transfer unlawful funds through the financial system; From time to time, social media has malicious dissemination and agitation of statements and actions that are detrimental to financial stability; This, coupled with the possibility of finance becoming a geopolitical tool, among other things, poses significant challenges to financial security. At the same time, the financial industry is characterized by a highly sensitive market, strong contagiousness, fast transmission, great influence, and a very destructive force. Looking back at everything Hong Kong has experienced in the past two years, we must not fail to be vigilant, and our concerns about financial stability and security are by no means catching the wind and catching the shadows. Second, the importance of financial security and stability 4. The importance of financial stability and security to citizens, Hong Kong, the country and even the international community cannot be ignored. Hong Kong is the international financial center, and the financial industry is an important pillar of the economy, accounting for 21% of GDP and 7% of employment, and it is also an industry with a high competitive advantage. The total assets of Hong Kong's banking industry reached HK26 trillion, and the total assets of the asset management industry amounted to HK29 trillion, which is 9.5 times and 10 times of Hong Kong's GDP respectively. A significant portion is the savings and working capital of more than 7 million Hong Kong residents and countless businesses. 5. On the other hand, Hong Kong is a major equity pooling and trading centre, the world's third largest US dollar trading centre and the fourth largest foreign exchange trading centre, the largest offshore RMB hub, bringing together 4,000 multinational corporations and being closely linked to the Mainland's financial markets through various interconnected channels. The accumulation and trading of so many wealth assets in Hong Kong fully reflects the trust of mainland and international investors and enterprises in Hong Kong's financial system. Therefore, it is our mission to ensure Hong Kong's financial security, as well as our responsibility for the country's financial security and even global financial stability. 3. The relevant work of the HKMA 6. In terms of financial security, the work of the HKMA is mainly reflected in ensuring three stability and adhering to four lines of defense. 7. The first priority is monetary stability. Hong Kong is a small, highly open economy and an important international financial center , and a stable and credible monetary system is essential. Hong Kong's remittance system has experienced many financial crises, especially in the past one or two years, Hong Kong's society is unstable, and the international financial market has once fluctuated sharply due to the epidemic The anxiety triggered by the "financial sanctions" and the combination of various factors have created many new challenges. 8. Even at the juncture of market volatility and timidity, the HKMA has firmly grasped the rudder of Lianhui. Over the past year or so, the Hong Kong dollar has been on the strong side, the total amount of money flowing into the Hong Kong dollar has reached the scale of 50 billion, and the payment system continues to operate safely and efficiently. All these reflect the market's vote of confidence in Hong Kong's monetary system and the HKMA's determination and ability to maintain monetary stability, once again proving the strong vitality of the exchange system. 9. The second stability is bank stability. I must express my sincere gratitude to my friends in the banking industry in Hong Kong. The social turmoil in 2019, especially the violent sabotage of banks, caused great disruption to the normal operation of many banks. The ensuing epidemic is another major test, and banks must do a good job in responding to the epidemic, while working with the government and regulatory agencies to conceive and implement measures to support enterprises and citizens to overcome economic difficulties, and to properly deal with various geopolitical risks. Crucially, the banking industry delivered a satisfactory report card in this test. 10. This outcome is no accident, but the result of years of collaboration between the banking industry and the HKMA. Hong Kong's banking system has always been robust, outperforming other financial centres in terms of capital adequacy ratios, liquidity coverage ratios and asset quality. What is more important is to be able to think of danger in times of peace and establish appropriate buffers through various counter-cyclical regulatory measures, so that banks can release and use these buffers when needed, such as during the anti-epidemic period, and continue to provide credit to support the real economy. 11. Thinking of danger in times of peace is also reflected in the fact that the banking industry has formulated contingency plans for various situations that may affect normal operations, and through exercises, reviews and improvement of these contingency plans, it is also reflected in the fact that the banking industry can maintain its service to customers as much as possible in the event of unexpected situations. In terms of system, the HKMA has also formulated liquidity support measures and disposal mechanisms, coupled with a deposit protection system, which is committed to protecting the interests of bank customers and strengthening public confidence in the banking system. 12. The third stability is cross-market stability. The international financial market is highly connected, various spot, futures and derivatives markets are mutually influential, and financial products are constantly innovating, which brings new challenges to the stability and security of the financial system. The HKMA team maintains close communication with other financial regulators, exchanges information, monitors international and local market dynamics, and strives to identify potential risks affecting market stability in a timely manner, sound the siren/follow up in a timely manner, and respond in a timely manner. We are implementing digital projects to better use technology to flexibly, timely and targeted analysis of various financial data and do a good job in market monitoring. 13. Let's talk about four lines of defense, the first of which is cybersecurity. To prevent criminals from invading the network to steal information, sabotage systems and steal property, the HKMA introduced the Cyber Defense Scheme in 2016 to provide a framework for the banking industry to enhance cybersecurity, assist banks in assessing cyber risks, continuously improve professional skills, and promote the sharing of information by financial institutions. 14. The second line of defense is for financial institutions to operate in accordance with the law. It is an international consensus to strengthen the fight against the transfer of illicit funds through the financial system, and Hong Kong's work in this regard has been fully affirmed by international standard-setting organizations. On this basis, we will continue to strictly require financial institutions to operate their business in accordance with the law and compliance, assist law enforcement agencies in cracking down on illegal capital transfers in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, and apply new technologies to enhance the effectiveness of data analysis and risk management measures and maintain the integrity of the financial system and public confidence. 15. The third line of defense is firm faith. We must prevent the spread of false news that undermines financial stability. When Hong Kong was facing serious street violence, rumors spread on social platforms that Hong Kong would implement capital controls, and some people even encouraged the normal operation of the United Exchange and the banks. Although these remarks are untenable, we have not taken them lightly, but have dispelled rumors in a timely manner to stabilize the market and the public's confidence in Hong Kong's financial system. 16. The fourth and most critical is the line of consciousness. In the face of a complex environment, it is necessary to think about the bottom line, carefully assess the various potential risks affecting financial stability and security, and make a comprehensive and detailed response plan. Of course, we hope that these options will be prepared and not used, but it is responsible to be fully prepared and to remain vigilant. 17. Ladies and gentlemen, the challenges that Hong Kong has experienced in recent times have made us realize that the reputation of a safe city built over the years can be ruthlessly destroyed in a short period of time, and therefore needs to be cherished and protected by each and every one of us. In the past year, especially since the implementation of the Hong Kong National Security Law, society has gradually restored tranquility and stability, and the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress recently adopted a decision to improve Hong Kong's election system, so that we have more space, a more stable environment, and a more complete system to think, plan, and implement the way forward for Hong Kong to start again and achieve long-term peace and stability. The HKMA will continue to strive to act as a financial guardian and provide a sound financial environment for Hong Kong's stability and development. 18. Thank you. Last revision date: 15 April 2021

Title: Opening Keynote Speech at Fraud and Financial Crime Asia 2021 Conference
text: 19/09/22, 12:50 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Opening Keynote Speech at Fraud and Financial Crime Asia 2021 Conference Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 21 Jul 2021 Opening Keynote Speech at Fraud and Financial Crime Asia 2021 Conference Carmen Chu, Executive Director (Enforcement and AML), Hong Kong Monetary Authority Anti-Money Laundering and Financial Crime Risk: How effective are we? 1. It is a great pleasure for me to participate in Fraud and Financial Crime Asia 2021 Conference. Among various themes, I will focus my opening remarks on the challenges presented by online fraud and related money laundering and how regulators, working with the industry, are helping to shape an effective response to deter, detect and disrupt new and emerging threats to businesses and individuals. 2.1 will focus on the need to introduce best practices more consistently across the global network so that our respective AML and risk management systems are able to deliver a more effective return on the huge investment at the institutional, sectoral and national levels. The necessary changes include richer data streams like digital footprints to drive the gains from analytics; technology-enabled information sharing partnerships to deliver more responsive and actionable suspicious activity reporting; and, for regulators, data- driven supervision and industry engagement. Epidemic of Online Fraud 3. The last 12 to 18 months have been a landmark for the banking sector in Hong Kong. The successful launch of eight Virtual Banks and collective efforts across the entire banking sector to overcome major challenges arising from the pandemic - banks had to make changes to meet customer demand within a very short time to launch or expand digital and online financial services. While this is in the interests of customers and has brought huge benefits, the global AML community, led by the Financial Action Task Force, saw increased levels of online fraud and cybercrime. 4. The scale at which the online economy was developing has been matched only by the increasingly sophisticated attempts of criminal networks to exploit it. Both the scale and speed with which this has happened are breathtaking; fraudulent websites and spam emails targeting Government-led pandemic relief efforts, for example, often surfaced within hours of the initiatives being launched. 5. Hong Kong has not been immune to this global phenomenon. There were over 15,000 deception cases in 2020, almost doubling from about 8,000 cases in the previous year. A similar increase was noted by the HKMA in bank customer complaints related to fraud and financial crime, which rose by about 120% in the first half of 2021 when compared with the same period a year ago. 6. It's not all bad news, however. When we coordinate effectively, when we formulate and implement strategies for the public and private sectors to work closely together and / 1/4 19/09/22, 12:50 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Opening Keynote Speech at Fraud and Financial Crime Asia 2021 Conference take timely actions, we can make an impact. The Anti-Deception Coordination Centre of the Police, which leads action against fraud, has intercepted HK6.3 billion conned from victims of phone and internet scams in its first three years of operation since 2017. The Centre intercepted a staggering HK3 billion in a single year in 2020, and none of this success would be possible without the close cooperation of banks, 24 hours a day and 7 days a week, in helping disrupt fraud and financial crime and protecting customers from losses. 7. These numbers must be a matter of concern for everyone in the global AML ecosystem and the wider economies. We all need to reflect on how effective we are being, while staying alert to new tricks and doubling our efforts to slow and reverse the tide. This is not to say that we expect to be able to pre-empt all fraud and financial crime, but that when these crimes unfortunately happen, our responses are quick and targeted. Our Approach 8. The HKMA's approach is guided by our continuing commitment to international standards and best practices in how AML and financial crime risk management systems are implemented. Our 'Fintech 2025' strategy also outlines how innovative technologies can help achieve effective outcomes. 9. We have been working to realise our vision, beginning with an AML/CFT RegTech Forum in 2019 to raise industry awareness and explore the role that technology could play in AML work. The HKMA also publishes various papers and reports from time to time to share Regtech use cases including AML, and will be putting all relevant resources in our centralised "Regtech Knowledge Hub". In particular, I would strongly recommend our report titled AML/CFT Regtech: Case studies and Insights of January 2021 as a "must read". The report collates insights from our engagement with around 40 banks at different stages of AML Regtech adoption since our 2019 forum. It highlights the opportunities Regtech offers to transform effectiveness and efficiency, sharing real-life examples and specific technologies and data applications, as well as robotic process automation in handling transaction monitoring alerts. 10. We must also talk about data - quality data - to drive Regtech adoption. Specifically, the availability of richer data streams, such as digital footprint data, with proper integration, can have a significant impact on system effectiveness. Other external data and information are also becoming increasingly important in monitoring customer risk and to this end, we have recently shared key observations and best practices from a thematic review to assist banks in identifying and using these resources. We will also further these pieces of work later in the year when we launch our first interactive lab session featuring machine learning in the area of monitoring. 11. Some of those technologies featured prominently in the successes we have seen in identifying and disrupting mule account networks linked to COVID-19 and investment scams, which have been shared through our public-private information sharing partnership, the Fraud and Money Laundering Intelligence Taskforce - or FMLIT. The FMLIT partnership has seen remarkable growth in the last three years, bringing about clear improvements in our collective abilities to identify and disrupt financial crime. Since its launch in 2017, actions taken by banks through FMLIT have identified over 11,000 bank accounts which were previously unknown to law enforcement agencies, leading to restraint or confiscation of about HK700 million in crime proceeds mainly from investment scams and other frauds involving financial impacts on customers and/or banks themselves. / 2/4 19/09/22, 12:50 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Opening Keynote Speech at Fraud and Financial Crime Asia 2021 Conference 12. In one case, a FMLIT member bank developed the capability to incorporate digital footprint data such as IP addresses into its analysis, and as a result, successfully identified a network of mule accounts linked to a fraud syndicate. This information was subsequently shared resulting in further responsive reporting. In another example, one of our virtual banks successfully used data related to customers' mobile devices to identify a network of mule accounts which led to a number of suspicious transaction reports being filed and dozens of counterparty accounts being closed down. The subsequent police investigation safeguarded more than HK10 million worth of assets. 13. This of course is only half the story. Robust yet customer-friendly front-end controls are also an important part of the response. To address impersonation risk, we have issued guidance on expectations for remote onboarding technology and worked with the industry to better educate bank staff and customers on fraud prevention. The HKMA and the industry associations have also undertaken various initiatives, including sharing sessions and publicity campaigns, to promote awareness of fraud prevention and detection among bank staff, and remind customers to stay alert of phishing instant message and protect their personal information. AML/CFT Supervision in the Age of Digital Innovation 14. Returning to the question I posed: how effective are we in our AML and financial crime work? It is essential for regulators to ask ourselves how AML/CFT supervision needs to change in the age of digital innovation. The HKMA's approach is to build on our strong foundations as a risk-based AML supervisor, while recognising the need to constantly learn and adapt to the digital age. We are implementing a series of changes to better leverage the latest technology in our supervisory work, while building capacity to allow us to adopt new technologies and techniques as they emerge. 15. One key area we are currently focusing on, and which will impact the Hong Kong banking sector, is to significantly upgrade our ability to source, store, process, and more importantly, use data to enhance and support our AML/CFT supervisors, while investing in other talent - data specialists - to help drive this initiative. The improvements we are making in our data, technology and people will be closely aligned to the outcomes we want to achieve in combatting financial crime. Read more about our agenda and priorities in the AML section of the HKMA website. International Cooperation to drive greater global consistency 16. International cooperation with other supervisors and global standard-setting bodies is more vital than ever if we are to fight against cross-border criminal syndicates and illicit fund flows. The FATF has shown considerable leadership both in terms of the response to the pandemic, and the frauds and money laundering it has given rise to, and has recently issued guidance on the opportunities and challenges of new technologies for AML/CFT. I'm sure that the available and emerging technology-based solutions described will be highly relevant to many of you as they are for the HKMA. Building an AML Regime for the Future 17. To round off, we must recognise that the COVID-19 situation has demonstrated how quickly financial services can change when they need to. Today, I have highlighted three aspects which we feel will help shape AML/CFT systems to be effective and fit for the future, particularly in the light of the "fraud pandemic" that we are increasingly facing: / 3/4 19/09/22, 12:50 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Opening Keynote Speech at Fraud and Financial Crime Asia 2021 Conference  First, data  to expand the use of non-traditional and new data streams, including digital footprints, to realise the full potential of analytics capabilities and AML Regtech;  Second, technology  to leverage on information-sharing and network analytics to help curb risk displacement across the system. The objective must be more responsive reporting, earlier and at a scale commensurate with the threat; and  Third, collaboration  transformation is needed for AML regulators as much as for banks, and maximum benefits will be gained through public-private partnership and engagement. Those who are data-driven, technology-led and collaborative will do the best in meeting new challenges. 18.1 understand that a number of these issues will be discussed in the next two days, so I hope I have provided an overview, not only of how we are responding, but also how to assess effectiveness of that response. I believe these will be relevant to your firms and people, so let me end by reiterating the importance of data, technology and collaboration to enhance effectiveness and achieve our common vision for AML and financial crime risk. 19.1 wish the event every success and look forward to fruitful discussion. Thank you. Last revision date : 21 July 2021 / 4/4

Title: Remarks by CE/MA at Media Standup - Southbound Trading under Bond Connect (Abridged version)
text: 19/09/22, 12:50 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Remarks by CE/MA at Media Standup - Southbound Trading under Bond Connect (Abridged ... Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 15 Sep 2021 Remarks by CE/MA at Media Standup - Southbound Trading under Bond Connect (Abridged version) Eddie Yue, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority Earlier today, the People's Bank of China and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority made a joint announcement on Southbound Trading under Bond Connect. It gives me great pleasure to see that the long-awaited Southbound Trading will start trading on 24 September. Southbound Trading marks another important milestone in the two-way opening up of the Mainland financial markets. It will promote the vibrant development of Hong Kong's bond market and further consolidate our status as an international financial centre. Northbound Trading has proved to be a major success. In just four years since its launch in 2017, the scheme has attracted over 2,700 investors worldwide and has facilitated the inclusion of Chinese sovereign bonds in major global bond indices. In August this year, it accounted for 60% of foreign investors total turnover in the China Interbank Bond Market. The success of Northbound Trading has laid a solid foundation for the launch of Southbound Trading. With the large foreign inflows into the Mainland financial markets and the steady accumulation of onshore wealth, Mainland financial institutions' demand for overseas asset allocation has continued to grow. Southbound Trading will enable Mainland financial institutions to increase their allocation to offshore bond assets through Hong Kong in a convenient and secure manner. At the same time, it will provide incentives for international financial institutions to strengthen their presence in Hong Kong to better provide underwriting, trading, custodian and related services to Southbound investors. In the long run, the launch of Southbound Trading will attract more Mainland capital to invest in the Hong Kong bond market and broaden the local fixed income investor base. Issuers will have a greater incentive to issue bonds in Hong Kong, and that will further enrich the product offerings of the Hong Kong bond market. Connect schemes werent built in a day. Similar to the experience of other Connect schemes, we expect to see Southbound Trading develop in a gradual manner with proper risk management. As you may recall, when Northbound Trading was first launched, the scheme recorded an average daily turnover of just RMB 1.5 billion. But in just four years' time, daily turnover has seen a 17-fold increase to RMB 26 billion. This was made possible by the prudent launch and the continuous and incremental enhancements that followed. We will adopt the same prudent and incremental approach in developing Southbound Trading. / 1/2 19/09/22, 12:50 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Remarks by CE/MA at Media Standup - Southbound Trading under Bond Connect (Abridged ...
