Title: Welcoming Remarks at Anti-Money Laundering Webinar 2021
text: 19/09/22, 12:49 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Welcoming Remarks at Anti-Money Laundering Webinar 2021 Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 16 Sep 2021 Welcoming Remarks at Anti-Money Laundering Webinar 2021 Carmen Chu, Executive Director (Enforcement and AML), Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. It is my great pleasure to welcome you all to our AML Seminar, an event we have in the past conducted physically in the Central Library or in the HKMA premises. It is perhaps fitting that we are for the first time delivering the programme in a webinar format because we will focus on: "collaboration", "technology" and "data", three key themes that the HKMA has reinforced in recent years, and which we believe can help shape a more effective response to detect, deter and disrupt new and emerging ML/TF threats collectively. 2. Making reference to accurate, timely and objective information for risk assessment is a prerequisite for an effective risk-based approach. The HKMA has recently updated the sectoral risk assessment in the light of emerging threats, such as online scams and new payment methods, and considered that the risk remains high for the banking sector being abused for financial crime activities. We are currently gathering further inputs and comments from the industry, and when the collective understanding of sectoral risks is clear, institutional ML/TF risk assessments, including customer and product risk assessments, can be updated accordingly by individual firms. An effective RBA helps banks, including virtual banks, to stay resilient and focus resources on control measures commensurate with assessed risks. 3. The concrete steps that banks and SVF licensees have been taking, as key frontline gatekeepers of our financial system, play an important part in how results in the eco- system are achieved. Following the HKMAs guidance, and as part of their risk-based approach, more institutions are now leveraging richer data streams like digital footprint information to drive the gains from analytics and technology-enabled information sharing partnership to deliver more responsive and actionable suspicious activity reporting. 4. Domestic and international financial crime typologies and cases are being shared through the Fraud and Money Laundering Intelligence Taskforce (FMLIT) and the Anti- Deception Coordination Centre (ADCC), as well as reporting suspicion to and feedback from the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit (JFIU). 5. Important though typologies may be, data across the global AML system suggests that the sharing of case specific information through collaborative platforms, that is, an intelligence-led approach, is one of the key differentials to achieving better results. To name a few positive outcomes so far, through FMLIT, banks have identified and reported over 12,000 accounts previously unknown to LEAs; banks' round-the-clock assistance to ADCC which intercepted HK3 billion in 2020; and in line with international experience, significant share (85%) of over 57,000 STRs last year were made by the banking sector to the JFIU for law enforcement action. / 1/2 19/09/22, 12:49 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Welcoming Remarks at Anti-Money Laundering Webinar 2021 6. We also understand the importance of clear communication of our expectations regarding the mandate which Boards and senior management of banks need to provide to their financial crime compliance teams on responsible innovation. In particular, we continue to encourage and facilitate AML and Financial Crime Regtech adoption initiatives that were launched in the AML/CFT Regtech Forum in 2019. 7. We also make sure that actions Xo dismantle perceived or real barriers to innovation form a core part of our risk-based AML supervisory engagement with banks and SVF licensees, and also contribute to the HKMAs Fintech 2025 Strategy. When it comes to technology and innovation, any actions cannot be prescribed; rather, the process should be agile and iterative, with sharing of real-life examples through our publications and circulars, as well as supervisory engagement through Fintech Supervisory Sandbox and Chatroom on use case proposals. And later this year, we will launch the AML and Financial Crime Regtech Labs to facilitate the necessary testing environment for banks before adoption. 8. Today's webinar will be divided into two parts: the first part is presented by public sector authorities in the AML eco-system, in which the HKMA will provide an update of the sectoral risk assessment and feedback from our supervisory work; the newly formed Financial Intelligence and Investigation Bureau will introduce its work priorities including its exciting project on the Financial Data Analytic Platform as well as providing feedback on STRs; and the Commercial Crime Bureau will underscore the importance of the public-private partnership approach through both FMLIT and ADCC platforms to collectively achieve a more effective response to online fraud and mule account networks. May I extend our gratitude to colleagues from the Hong Kong Police Force for joining us today to share their important perspective. 9. We also understand that events like this, where industry practitioners share their experience, is an important way of encouraging learning and collaboration. I would like to particularly thank the subject matter experts from Bank of China (Hong Kong), Citibank (Hong Kong), and one of our virtual banks - Mox for providing rich industry perspectives, in the second half of the webinar. 10. The last point that I would like to make is that if we want these success stories to become the industry norm, we need more input from more banks and closer cooperation in public-private partnership in the AML ecosystem. So, at the risk of repeating myself, please do not hesitate to raise ideas and explore together when you feel any changes might offer genuine benefits. 11.1 hope you will enjoy the programme. Thank you. Last revision date : 16 September 2021 / 2/2

Title: Remarks by CE/MA at the Launch Ceremony of Southbound Trading under Bond Connect
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech September 24, 2021 Speech by the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Bond Connect Southbound Connectivity Opening Ceremony Yu Weiwen is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Honorable Vice President Pan Gongsheng (Vice President People's Bank of China), Deputy Director Deng Zhonghua (Deputy Director of the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the State Council), Secretary Chen Maobo (Financial Secretary), Deputy Director Yin Zonghua (Deputy Director of the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region), distinguished guests, friends, good morning. It is an honor for me to gather with you today to witness Bond Connect take to the next level. On the solid foundation of the Northbound Connect, the Bond Connect to the South was officially launched, realizing the common aspiration of the Bond Connect in both directions. The opening of the "Southbound Connect" has multiple significances. The first is the further improvement of the interconnection mechanism. In the past few years, the demand for RMB assets by international investors has increased, and connectivity has played an active role in promoting the allocation of international capital to financial assets on the mainland. At the same time, the mainland's economy has continued to grow, domestic wealth has been accumulating, and the demand of mainland institutions and individuals for the allocation of overseas assets has been increasing. Two weeks ago, the "Cross-border Wealth Management Connect" for personal financial needs was launched, and today we usher in the "Southbound Connect" of bonds, adding a diversified and convenient channel for mainland financial institutions to invest in overseas bond assets through the Hong Kong market, meet the needs of the mainland market , and promote the development of the Hong Kong bond market. Second, further deepening the interconnection of the bond markets of Hong Kong and the Mainland and strengthening the connection between the market infrastructure of the two places is an important measure for the two-way opening up of the mainland's financial market. Third, The "Southbound Connect" has built a risk-controllable channel to allow the orderly cross-border outflow of funds from within the mainland, once again highlighting that the Hong Kong financial market is a safe and reliable channel and window for the mainland to open up to the outside world. In the future, the HKMA will actively cooperate with the People's Bank of China to do a good job in the implementation of the "Southbound Connect", continuously improve and enhance the coverage and operation mechanism of the "Southbound Connect" in accordance with market development and the needs of investors, and work with the "Northbound Connect" to better serve the majority of investors at home and abroad and promote the healthy development of the financial markets of the two places. Finally, I wish the bond connection a smooth start to the southbound and continue to make new breakthroughs. Thank you. Last revision date: 24 September 2021

Title: Remarks by CE/MA at the Press Conference for the Issuance of Offshore RMB Municipal Bonds in Hong Kong by the Shenzhen Government
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech October 12, 2021 Speech by the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Shenzhen Launches Offshore RMB Local Government Bonds in Hong Kong Yu Weiwen is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Honorable Chief Executive Carrie Lam, Honorable Vice Minister Xu Hongcai (Vice Minister of Finance), Vice President Pan Gongsheng (Vice President of the People's Bank of Chinese), Deputy Director Huang Liuzhuo (Deputy Director of the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the State Council), Secretary Wang Weizhong (Secretary of the Shenzhen Municipal Party Committee), Mayor Qin Weizhong (Mayor of Shenzhen), Director Chen Maobo, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen Hello everyone! It is a great pleasure to witness the historical moment of the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government's issuance of bonds in Hong Kong. This bond issuance has special exemplary significance in many aspects: First of all, on the basis of the successful regular issuance of treasury bonds and central bank bills by the Ministry of Finance and the People's Bank of China in Hong Kong, Shenzhen is the first local government to issue bonds abroad, and the yield curve of new local bonds added in addition to the main bonds is a major breakthrough, once again highlighting Shenzhen's role as a pioneer in reform and opening up. Second, Shenzhen is the first local government to issue RMB bonds overseas, which further enriches the offshore RMB products that foreign investors can allot, which is conducive to prudently promoting the process of RMB internationalization. Third, a considerable part of the bonds issued this time are green bonds, which is the first time that a mainland government agency has issued green bonds abroad, which is of symbolic significance for the development of green finance in the mainland and for the introduction of overseas funds to participate in the realization of China's "3060" double carbon target. Of course, the choice to issue bonds in Hong Kong is also an important symbol of Shenzhen-Hong Kong financial cooperation and the joint construction of a green Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. In the preparation and implementation of this bond issuance, as well as future secondary market activities, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is honored to have the opportunity to actively participate and cooperate in all aspects The first is to introduce the situation and operation of the Hong Kong bond market to the relevant departments of the municipal government in the preparatory stage, and share our experience in assisting the Hong Kong SAR government in issuing green bonds. The second is to update the HKMA's arrangement to provide RMB liquidity to banks, so that bonds issued by the Shenzhen Municipal Government can be used as collateral. The third is that the HKMA's Central Settlement System for Debt Instruments, known as CMU, provides custody services for the bonds. This is the second time that CMU has provided custody services for mainland government debt instruments after the government bonds and central bank bills. We thank the city government for its trust and support to CMU. In fact, CMU, as one of the relevant important financial infrastructures, docks with domestic and foreign investors and provides efficient, safe and convenient settlement, settlement and custody services for bond issuance and trading through years of optimization and improvement. Looking ahead, CMU will actively follow market demand, take advantage of the development opportunities brought by Bond Connect, continuously improve functions, efficiency and services, strengthen promotion work, and strive to become a central securities custodian in Asia and even internationally. Everyone, as an international financial centre, Asia's major bond market and green finance hub, Hong Kong will continue to make unremitting efforts to play the unique role of in-communicado and external links, to better serve international and Mainland bond issuers and investors, and to promote the development of green finance in the region. We also expect that with this successful experience, the financial cooperation between Shenzhen and Hong Kong will continue to deepen in the future, and encourage more mainland issuers to use Hong Kong's bond platform." Finally, once again, congratulations to the Shenzhen Municipal Government on the successful results of this bond issuance! Last revision date: October 12, 2021

Title: Luncheon Keynote Address at 2021 ESG and Green Finance Opportunities Forum
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech October 20, 2021 Lunch-based keynote speech at the 2021 Environmental, Social and Governance and Green Finance Opportunities Forum Yu Weiwen is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Chairman Leung Ka Cheung (Chairman of the Hong Kong Chamber of Listed Companies, Distinguished Guests: 1. Hello everyone! Thank you very much to the Hong Kong Chamber of Listed Companies for the invitation to attend today's forum to share with you the HKMA's work in promoting green finance and addressing climate change in Hong Kong. 2. Hong Kong has just experienced the hottest September on record, and October recorded the highest rainfall in a single day, constantly reminding us that extreme weather is not just the subject of academic research. Two weeks ago, the HKSAR government unveiled a new blueprint for climate action, pledging to achieve carbon neutrality in Hong Kong by 2050 and setting out clear and specific carbon reduction strategies and actions. The Chamber of Commerce is holding this forum today, and the timing is superb! 3. Climate change is one of the main risks affecting the long-term well-being of mankind, and the importance and urgency of addressing climate change has become a global consensus. The Asian region in which we live has a huge population and economic scale, and the damage caused by climate change to the ecological environment will pose a huge threat to the lives and economic development of residents in these countries and regions. 4. Since the Paris Climate Agreement in 2015, countries around the world have continued to strengthen cooperation in reducing carbon emissions and promoting sustainable development, and local governments have continuously introduced new countermeasures and policies, both for the overall economy and for individual industries. Therefore, enterprises must manage the risks of climate change to real assets, the so-called physical risk, but also need to be prepared to cooperate with various emission reduction policies to deal with the transition risks transition risk )? 5. It is worth noting that the global financial industry is also facing the same challenge, and financial institutions will adjust the standards, considerations and conditions for providing financing due to the need to manage climate risks, which may have a direct impact on enterprises. Many of the listed companies represented by the guests are located in Asia and around the world, and I believe that they have a considerable grasp of this trend. 6. There are always two sides to everything, and from another perspective, managing climate risk can translate into creating green financial opportunities. According to market estimates, an estimated 66 trillion in climate investment will be needed in Asia alone over the next three decades to meet the goal of limiting global warming to 1.5b0C 1? It can be expected that in the future, global funds will continue to flow to low-carbon, sustainable and climate-resilient investment programs, products and enterprises. 7. As an international financial center and a green financial hub in Asia, Hong Kong takes the financial industry as the starting point, which on the one hand can maintain Hong Kong's competitiveness and leading position in the international financial industry, and on the other hand, it can promote Hong Kong's transformation into a green economy and a low-carbon economy. The HKMA's work in this area follows three main lines: first, the banking industry controls climate risks, second, creates favorable market support, and third, promotes market awareness and participation. Climate risk management 8. Banking is an important part of Hong Kong's financial system. Good management of climate risks in the banking sector contributes to financial stability and ensures a smooth economy. 9. As a regulator, the HKMA is committed to building the resilience of the banking system to climate risks and enhancing the transparency of climate risk disclosures in the banking industry. We move forward in this area in three phases: 10. In the first phase, the HKMA launched a common framework for assessing banks' "green" benchmarks in May 2020, and the banking sector has completed the first round of self-assessments. 11. In the second phase, we published a white paper in June last year setting out the HKMA's initial concept of setting regulatory expectations, followed by a circular to share with the industry practical approaches to managing climate risks. In July this year, we launched an industry consultation on regulatory requirements with the aim of setting a set of specific targets to enhance the green and sustainable development of Hong Kong's banking sector. 12. The third stage, the implementation, review and assessment of the Bank's progress in this regard, will be a lasting exercise. 13. At the same time, the HKMA launched a pilot scheme for climate risk stress testing earlier this year, the main purpose of which is to (a) assess the ability of the banking industry as a whole to cope with climate risks; (b) Promote banks to establish climate risk management frameworks, take climate risk factors into account in the development of business plans, and develop strategies to reduce climate risks; (c) Promote banks to build capacity to assess climate risks. 14. In addition to internal governance and strategy, external disclosure and sustainability reporting are equally important to help companies better identify, assess and manage climate-related risks and opportunities. On the other hand, risk disclosure can give financial markets more information about how companies and assets will be affected by climate change, help investors more accurately assess the value of companies and projects, identify investment opportunities, and avoid investment risks. Reliable, timely and transparent disclosure is therefore key to assessing and mitigating climate-related risks, contributing to the efficient allocation of capital and promoting market discipline. Information disclosure is an effective tool to prevent the "drifting" of the market and the public. 15. As a result, regulators, including the HKMA, are actively promoting climate-related disclosures. Candidates from listed companies are confident that you are very familiar with HKEX's requirements for the environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting framework for listed companies, including key performance indicators, disclosures on significant climate-related matters, and the timeliness of ESG information release. 16. In this regard, the HKMA and other financial regulators, including the HKEx, are also committed to promoting climate change reporting in various sectors of the financial sector in accordance with the framework of the G20 Working Group on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) by 2025 or earlier. 17. In the banking sector, the HKMA conducted a consultation in July this year, expecting banks to disclose climate-related information in accordance with TCFD recommendations as soon as possible, in mid-2023 Prior to the first disclosure. At the same time, HKEx is preparing a new practical guide to help listed companies prepare disclosures as recommended by the TCFD. 18. In addition, China and the EU are working together to develop a Common Ground Taxonomy to develop a more consistent definition of activities that make a significant contribution to climate change mitigation and adaptation. We look forward to the catalogue being published later this year to largely address the pain points of the current international standards. Hong Kong's financial regulators have made it clear that our goal is to adopt this common green catalogue and to study areas that can be adapted and applied at the local level. 19. We also support the International Sustainability Standards Board of the IFRS Foundation in developing new standards based on the TCFD framework. 20. We believe that through these measures, enterprises can have a clearer, more authoritative and standardized basis for making information disclosure, so as to improve the reliability and timeliness of disclosure information. 21. Enhanced climate-related disclosures are already a global megatrend, and we encourage listed companies and financial institutions to make such disclosures an important element of their business strategies and day-to-day operations, making risk management more comprehensive, more transparent and further consolidating market confidence. Tie fei mane insect unitary self 22. To promote the "greening" of the industry, the initiative of the enterprise itself is important, but it is also necessary to consider providing appropriate incentives and assisting the market to solve some shortcomings. We observe that the main challenges facing the market now include data, limitations in talent skills, and the associated costs of adopting green finance. 23. In terms of talent and data, the Inter-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance, initiated by the HKMA and other regulators and government departments, has recently established the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance, which is responsible for coordinating the training, research and policy formulation work of regulators, relevant government departments, industry stakeholders and academic institutions, as well as establishing a knowledge base to share asset management, data and analytical tools to enhance the transparency of climate-related information. Enhance synergies. 24. In terms of skills training, we have co-sponsored the Green Business Bank Alliance with the International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group. As a founding member of the Alliance Asia and the first Regional Executive Director, the HKMA works with IFC and stakeholders in the Asian region to jointly develop, build and enhance green finance capabilities, promote climate-related investment, and support the development of green finance in the region by organising green finance research, market analysis, professional competence enhancement and training. 25. In terms of reducing costs, the HKMA also assisted the Government in launching the Green and Sustainable Financial Assistance Scheme in May this year to fund the issuance of eligible bond issuers and borrowers and the expenditure of external independent review services. We believe that the Scheme can facilitate green and sustainable bond issuance and lending activities in Hong Kong and attract more brick-and-mortar enterprises and financial institutions to use Hong Kong's green financing platforms and professional services. Strengthen market awareness and participation 26. Finally, I would like to talk about how to strengthen market awareness and participation. The international investment climate has shifted, with investors looking at ESGBs and the need for sustainable investment growing. According to market statistics, global mutual funds and exchange-traded funds invested 360 billion in sustainable assets in 2020, more than double the amount in 201912. 27. As the manager of the Exchange Fund, the HKMA practices responsible investment. We have incorporated ESG into the investment management process of the open market and private markets of the Exchange Fund. Our principle is that ESG investments are prioritized when they have similar long-term returns to other investments. We are also gradually increasing the share of Exchange Fund ESG investments. 28. We are also committed to using government power to develop green financial markets. The HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing the HK200 billion green bond scheme to gradually establish a variety of green bond yield curves to provide a practical benchmark for corporate bond issuance. 29. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing a total of US3.5 billion in green bonds in two phases in 2019 and February this year. We plan to expand the currencies of green bond issuance, the types of projects, the models and channels of issuance, including preparing for the issuance of retail green bonds, further enriching Hong Kong's green and sustainable financial ecology, and showcasing to potential green bond issuers that Hong Kong can provide one-stop services, and promoting Hong Kong as the preferred platform for issuing green products. A recent successful example is the Shenzhen Municipal Government's successful issuance of offshore renminbi green bonds in Hong Kong last week, which has played a great exemplary role in attracting more mainland issuers, especially in the Greater Bay Area, to issue bonds in Hong Kong. conclusion 30. Folks, Hong Kong has a huge capital market and is a major international financial centre, and we are well placed to make a positive contribution to achieving the global goal of net zero emissions. In this process, in addition to the financial industry's own risk management and investment considerations, the greater significance lies in exerting leverage to promote the transformation of enterprises and economies to low-carbon through financing activities. 31. I sincerely hope that the financial industry can work hand in hand with the business community to create a green, healthy and sustainable society for Hong Kong and for our next generation ." 32. Thank you. Title: Keynote Speech at the Annual Conference of Financial Street Forum 2021
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech October 20, 2021 Keynote speech at the 2021 Financial Street Forum Annual Conference Yu Weiwen is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Grasp the "golden key" of financial technology and usher in a new era of financial development Dear leaders, organizers, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, 1. Hello everyone! We are delighted to attend the Financial Street Forum Annual Meeting again, and this year we are once again discussing financial cooperation and future development in the Mainland and Hong Kong with our friends from all over the world by video. 2. Over the past year, the COVID-19 pandemic has brought uncertainty to the economy, but Hong Kong's financial system has remained stable, providing a solid foundation for Hong Kong to continue to leverage its unique strengths as an international financial centre. Financial institutions around the world remain confident in Hong Kong, with more than three-quarters of the world's top 100 banks operating in Hong Kong, and 15 of the 20 largest private equity funds at home and abroad based in Hong Kong, most of which are regional headquarters. Thanks to Hong Kong's robust and mature regulatory system, rigorous systemic risk monitoring system and the Lianbin exchange rate system supported by a huge foreign exchange fund, Hong Kong's financial market has been operating smoothly and even surpassed before. Hong Kong's total bank deposits grew by 5.4% last year, and in the first half of this year, it maintained an upward trend, an increase of 4.6%, and the capital adequacy ratio was 19.8%. The liquidity ratio is 154%, which is much higher than international standards. Last year, IPO raised HK397.5 billion, ranking second in the world. The bond market is also booming, with US196 billion in international bond issuances arranged by Hong Kong last year, the highest in Asia. The 14th Five-Year Plan adopted by the state in March this year It has set a clear policy for the future development direction of Hong Kong and consolidated Hong Kong's competitive advantage. Grasp the key to development: financial technology 3. Making good use of its own advantages, relying on the motherland and facing the international community has been Hong Kong's development policy all along. Hong Kong will certainly seize the opportunity to continue to enhance its position as an international financial, shipping and trade centre with the support of the 14th Five-Year Plan, and to strengthen its functions as an offshore RMB business hub, an international asset management centre and a risk management centre worldwide. To have good development, we must first have a clear direction of development, just as the ship must not be rudderless. To this end, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has three major deployments: the Financial Services Section Technology, green finance, cross-border cooperation. We believe that the use of technology will be the key to success, and financial technology is the golden key to open the door to future development. So, today we will focus on fintech. Development status: At the forefront of the development of financial technology 4. In recent years, Hong Kong's fintech has developed rapidly and has emerged on the world stage. Hong Kong, in partnership with the International Settlement Bank, has launched the world's first innovation hub to foster collaboration between central banks and elevate the application of innovative technologies to the global level. We work with the Bank of Thailand on wholesale central bank digital currencies and have been rated by market research as the most mature project of its kind in the world. Hong Kong's banking industry has also actively used technological innovation to strengthen and accelerate the application of financial technology, coupled with the full investment of eight virtual banks into services, injecting new impetus into the development of the industry. All of the above shows that the current level of development of financial technology in Hong Kong has been greatly improved, compared with a few years ago, it is really not the same, I believe it will be higher in the future. Face the future: set a good strategy and do your best 5. When it comes to the future, Hong Kong must strive for excellence, first set a strategy, and then develop its strengths. Therefore, in June this year, our HKMA formulated the "FinTech 2025" strategic framework to assist the financial industry to fully apply fintech by 2025 to provide reasonable and efficient financial services to benefit the people of Hong Kong and the economy as a whole. With FinTech 2025 as the backbone of our strategy, we will take a multi-pronged approach to promoting the development of FinTech, including comprehensively promoting the digitalization of banks, deepening the central bank's digital currency research, harnessing the potential of data infrastructure, expanding the FinTech talent pool, and making good use of resource policies to support development. 6. With a specific direction, how can Hong Kong show its strengths? First of all, Hong Kong should make good use of its advantages as an international financial center and an international trade center and display its strengths externally and internally. 7. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority actively promotes financial innovation with international financial institutions and other central bank organizations, such as the Hong Kong Center, the innovation hub of the International Settlement Bank, the Digital Currency Research Institute of the People's Bank of China, the Bank of Thailand and the Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates, to develop a variety of central bank digital currency cross-border networks (mBridge) to apply central bank digital currency to cross-border payments. Connecting payment systems around the world makes international fund transfers faster and cheaper. 8. At the same time, we are committed to using technology to promote cross-border trade. Earlier, Hong Kong's trade finance platform Trade Linkage and the People's Bank of China The successful docking of the "trade finance blockchain platform" has laid the foundation for digital cross-border trade financing for many banks in the two places, and in the future, we hope to introduce the research results of the central bank's digital currency project to open up the flow of funds for north-south trade settlement, and truly do a comprehensive information and financial integration of cross-border trade. In addition, in order to facilitate cross-border payment services for residents of the two places, the HKMA has also continued to cooperate with the People's Bank of China to promote the technical testing of the digital renminbi (e-CNY) in Hong Kong. 9. In addition, we can also leverage Hong Kong's mature regulatory experience to invest in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and achieve regulatory innovation. The HKMA has been in discussions with the People's Bank of China to connect the People's Bank of China's "Fintech Innovation Regulatory Tool" with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Fintech Regulatory Sandbox" through the "Internet" approach, and the progress has been very promising. As a result, financial institutions and science and technology companies in the two places can submit test applications for cross-border projects through a "one-stop" platform and receive timely feedback from relevant regulatory authorities. I believe that the networking of fintech innovation regulatory tools between the two places will greatly help promote innovation and development in the region. 10. The above-mentioned trade platforms, digital currency cooperation, and the networking of fintech innovation regulatory tools can fully leverage Hong Kong's advantages and lay an important foundation for cross-border financial development in the future. summary 11. Looking ahead, we will continue to work with the industry to seize opportunities and work closely with the Mainland to leverage Hong Kong's unique role as a bridge and consolidate and enhance Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre. Especially in the aspect of financial technology innovation, Hong Kong's strategy and development direction are clear and clear, and we will certainly make good use of our unique advantages, seize opportunities, focus on promoting the development of financial technology, and strengthen cooperation between the two places. 12. In conclusion, I wish this forum every success. Thank you all! Last revision date: October 20, 2021

Title: Remarks at the Signing Announcement of the Memorandum of Understanding on Fintech Innovation Supervisory Cooperation at the Annual Conference of Financial Street Forum 2021
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech October 21, 2021 2021 Financial Street Forum Annual Meeting Fintech Innovation Regulatory Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding was signed to deliver a speech at the press conference Yu Weiwen is the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Honorable Vice President Fan Yifei (Vice President People's Bank of China), Honorable Vice Mayor Yin Yong (Vice Mayor of Beijing), distinguished guests, friends, hello. Today, I am honored to join you in witnessing the networking of fintech innovation regulatory tools between the two places. People's Bank of China, the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission, the China Securities Regulatory Commission and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange jointly issued the Opinions on Financial Support for the Construction of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area in May 2020 to implement the requirements of the Outline Development Plan for the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, further promote financial opening up and innovation, and deepen financial cooperation between the Mainland and Hong Kong and Macao. The 28th item of the "Opinions" is to promote the improvement of financial regulatory rules in the field of innovation and study the establishment of a regulatory sandbox for cross-border financial innovation. In this regard, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the People's Bank of China have been in close communication and have reached consensus on the cooperation model of fintech innovation supervision between the two places. Through the "networking" method, the People's Bank of China's "Fintech Innovation Regulatory Tool" is connected with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Fintech Regulatory Sandbox", providing a "one-stop" platform that enables cross-border fintech projects to be tested before they are launched on the market, obtain feedback from regulators and user opinions at an early stage, and facilitate appropriate modifications to new technology products, thereby accelerating the launch of fintech products and reducing development costs. In addition to facilitating the launch of cross-border fintech projects, the networking can create synergies in the cooperation between the People's Bank of China and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, encourage the development and innovation of more cross-border fintech projects, and promote the development of fintech in the Greater Bay Area. At the same time, it will strengthen the exchange of financial technology supervision between Guangdong and Hong Kong, and deepen the cooperation between the mainland and Hong Kong in various fields such as finance, science and technology and supervision . In the future, the HKMA will actively cooperate with the People's Bank of China to do a good job in the implementation of regulatory cooperation, continue to deepen Guangdong-Hong Kong financial science and technology innovation exchanges and cooperation, increase financial support for the construction of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, and promote the high-quality financial development of the Mainland and Hong Kong. Finally, I wish this regulatory cooperation to inject more vitality into the development of cross-border fintech in the Greater Bay Area. Thank you. Last revision date: October 21, 2021

Title: Opening remarks at AML Regtech Lab (AMLab)
text: 19/09/22, 12:49 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Opening remarks at AML Regtech Lab (AMLab) Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 05 Nov 2021 Opening remarks at AML Regtech Lab (AMLab) Carmen Chu, Executive Director (Enforcement and AML), Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, 2. It's a great pleasure to welcome you all to the first AML Regtech Lab, or AMLab, which the HKMA is hosting in collaboration with Cyberport and working with InvestHK as part of Hong Kong FinTech Week 2021. 3. Today, the launch of AMLab represents the latest phase of the HKMA's engagement with the banking sector on AML Regtech, supported by our consultant Deloitte. Our industry engagement began with the forum in 2019 to examine opportunities and challenges from the greater use of technology, and followed up with our case study guidance issued this January. 4. The focus of this first AMLab is network analytics, which has great value in identifying hidden connections between accounts, and providing high-quality information for sharing with other stakeholders in the AML ecosystem. We aim to empower a group of banks, which are not using this technology yet - but which we are aware have the vision and data to do so, to work with data experts to experiment, for the first time, using synthetic data to simulate a fraud mule-account network. These experiments will also look at integrating alternative data, beyond the usual customer and transaction information, to help develop the skills and capabilities in network analytics and risk identification. 5. Network analytics is just one example of technology that can help banks to prevent and detect fraud and financial crime more effectively, which is necessary if we are to keep up with the rapid technological advances and potential spillover of risks across the banking sector. These skills and capabilities are especially important with the growing popularity of online shopping and e-banking; there has been a four-fold increase in complaints against banks in relation to scams and frauds over the past two years. Our goal is to enhance banks capabilities to detect bank account networks implicated in suspected fraud syndicates, early and efficiently. 6. The knowledge and experience participants will gain from this event will help banks decisions about the most appropriate Regtech solutions to take their AML work to the next level; improve customer experience by reducing touch points in account opening and maintenance; and reduce risk displacement across the sector by expanding the group of banks deploying this tool. 7. AMLab provides a collaborative platform for banks and fintech community to promote the wider use of data and technology. Future AMLabs will look at other areas where Regtech can support banks' gatekeeper role in the AML ecosystem and help safeguard customer accounts. We will announce further details nearer the time, and meanwhile, I hope you will find this one enjoyable, challenging and productive. / 1/2 19/09/22, 12:49 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Opening remarks at AML Regtech Lab (AMLab) 8. Thank you. Last revision date : 05 November 2021 / 2/2

Title: Regulatory Keynote Address at 1LoD's Virtual Conference "XLoD Global" : Importance of Incentive Systems in Motivating Desirable Behaviour
text: 19/09/22, 12:49 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Regulatory Keynote Address at ILoD's Virtual Conference "XLoD Global": Importance of Inc... Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY if  at hi M 17 Nov 2021 Regulatory Keynote Address at 1 LoD's Virtual Conference "XLoD Global": Importance of Incentive Systems in Motivating Desirable Behaviour Alan Au, Executive Director (Banking Conduct), Hong Kong Monetary Authority Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, 1. Good morning, good afternoon and good evening everyone. I would like to thank 1 LoD for inviting me again to address this year's virtual event "XLoD Global". I'm very glad to join you all virtually at this event. Having said that, I believe that most of us miss a face- to-face dialogue, and this reminds me that Covid is still having a deep impact on many matters, including bank culture. 2. Those of you who attended the "XLoD Global" event last year may recall that I spoke about sound bank culture being more important than ever in times of pandemic. During Covid, we have seen a substantial increase in the popularity of digital banking among customers. As an example, total applications for personal banking credit products via digital channels in Hong Kong surged more than 40% in the second half of 2020 compared to the first half year, with those made via mobile apps contributing to 40% of the total digital applications. The rapid development of digital banking has enabled a much more customer-friendly online journey. However, at the same time, we must not lose sight of the need to ensure adequate customer protection in such new banking era. And this cannot wholly rely on control measures imposed by banks, we also need the strong support of a sound bank culture. 3. We at the HKMA have been very enthusiastic in advocating a sound banking culture since we initiated the bank culture reform back in early 2017. All along, we emphasise that there is no "one-size-fits-all" approach and no single formulation of "sound" culture. Instead, a bank and its staff must internalise sound culture in such a way that the staff behave properly because they think it is the right thing to do so. Overall, we encourage banks to focus on three fundamental elements, which are: (a) A strong "tone from the top" supported by a sound governance framework; (b) An appropriate incentive system that drives desirable behaviour; and (c) An effective feedback mechanism which can "echo from the bottom". / 1/4 19/09/22, 12:49 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Regulatory Keynote Address at ILoD's Virtual Conference "XLoD Global": Importance of Inc... 4. Through the various culture initiatives spearheaded by the HKMA in the past few years, we are glad to see good progress made by the Hong Kong banking industry. This year, we are advancing further to dive deeply into studying the incentive systems of front offices through a focused review among retail banks in Hong Kong. Incentive system is also of fundamental importance to "1 st Line Control" which is one of the foci of the discussion in the XLoD event this week. I am going to talk more about our Focused Review in the next few minutes. What drives behaviour 5. Before I go more deeply into the Focused Review, let us first take a look at what drives behaviour, which constitutes the norm and shapes a bank's culture. In an attempt to answer this question, psychologists point to "motivation". 6. People are motivated, on one hand, by our biological drives, such as hunger and safety. This is what psychologists commonly call the "push" side of motivation. On the other hand, we are also "pulled" to act because we are attracted to particular rewards, or in other words, "incentives". So, it would certainly make sense for banks to dig deeper to find out what motivates their staff so that they would behave in ways that lead to good customer outcomes. An appropriate incentive system is certainly a centre piece of the "pull" factors. Focused Review on incentive systems 7. Based on the insights drawn from a previous self-assessment exercise undertaken by the HKMA which covered 30 banks, including all major retail banks and selected foreign bank branches with substantial operations in Hong Kong, we published a "Report on Review of Self-assessments on Bank Culture" in May 2020 to provide a range of sound culture practices as well as common themes for the industrys reference. In respect of incentive systems, while we are pleased to note from the self-assessment exercise that there is an increasing trend towards a greater use of a balanced scorecard approach and banks now consider both "what" (i.e. financial factors) and "how" (i.e. non-financial factors), banks culture effort in incentive systems is still very much an area of "work-in- progress". Therefore, we commenced a Focused Review on incentive systems of front offices in March this year. 8. With a view to identifying industry-wide practices and an aim for better alignment of incentive systems among banks with the desired culture, the Review studies a number of specific areas, including how the incentive systems of front offices drive behaviour of frontline staff, in particular, their role in achieving better customer outcomes and minimising potential misconduct behaviour and mis-selling practices in the sale and distribution of banking, investment and insurance products. 9. The Focused Review is a large scale industry-wide exercise covering 20 retail banks in Hong Kong. Insights will be drawn from data collected through a range of activities, including an employee survey, focus group discussions, interviews with staff as well as a document review. Up till now, we have already completed the industry-wide employee survey which aims at gauging frontline employees' perception of their banks' incentive / 2/4 19/09/22, 12:49 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Regulatory Keynote Address at ILoD's Virtual Conference "XLoD Global": Importance of Inc... systems and culture. It is encouraging to see that the survey received an impressive response rate, at around 70%, which is much higher when compared to similar exercise undertaken in other places. Interim insights of the Focused Review 10. From the survey response collected, we have identified some preliminary observations which I am pleased to take this opportunity to share with you. 11. As you may expect, according to the survey results, financial incentives such as bonus payments on top of the fixed pay remain to be a heavily weighted motivator for bank staff. In particular, some banks are using tactical incentive programmes to achieve specific targeted outcomes, while some banks are adopting non-linear pay structure with a view to making the impact on pay more significant. That said, it is encouraging to note that other intrinsic motivators (such as upholding the bank's reputation, achieving good customer outcomes and contributing to team objectives) are also considered by the frontline staff as important. In fact, 90% of respondents in the employee survey find it rewarding to achieve good customer outcomes and even more frontline staff regard upholding his or her bank's reputation as their responsibility. This sort of conscientiousness and sense of responsibility is a key driver in guarding against misconduct behavior. 12. Interestingly, the perception of incentive systems generally differs at different staff levels. The survey findings indicate that frontline staff generally feel that performance in terms of meeting business targets is of high priority, whereas their supervisors and senior leaders tend to think that the incentive systems are more balanced. 13. It is also noted that some banks, when compared to others, have more staff responding favourably to survey questions relating to positive customer and conduct outcomes, such as fair treatment of customers and customer satisfaction of products and services. For these banks, their staff tend to see a more balanced focus on the "how- factors" (i.e. the non-financial aspects of the incentive systems) in addition to the "what- factors" (i.e. the financial aspects). Moreover, in these banks, staff are generally provided with greater recognition for behaviour that are conducive to sound culture. 14. So it is quite obvious that an appropriate incentive system does help shape the perception of bank staff and induce the desired behaviour at all levels. But how should banks design their incentive systems to achieve the desired customer outcome? 15. As a start, we note from the Focused Review some interesting incentive practices used by banks for motivating desirable staff behaviour. For example, some banks use non- financial key performance indicators (KPIs) as the "gate opener" for variable remuneration. That is, a bank staff needs to demonstrate satisfactory performance on non-financial KPIs first, in order to be qualified for variable remuneration in the performance assessment. Those who cannot meet the conduct-related non-financial KPIs would not even be eligible for the variable remuneration. Such design may encourage frontline staff to focus more on delivering behaviour that lead to positive customer outcome than purely chasing for variable remuneration. As regards / 3/4 19/09/22, 12:49 Hong Kong Monetary Authority - Regulatory Keynote Address at ILoD's Virtual Conference "XLoD Global": Importance of Inc... disincentives for undesirable behaviour, some banks use non-financial KPIs as "gate- closer", where deductions in remuneration are made in respect of undesirable behaviour. This approach could possibly lead to a consequence that staff may only meet minimum behaviour standard to avoid penalties. Some banks are therefore going beyond the "gate" approach, with satisfactory performance in non-financial KPIs contributing positively to the quantum of variable remuneration alongside the financial KPIs. However, measuring "outperformance" in non-financial KPIs may not be straightforward. All in all, different approaches in using non-financial performance assessment as a mechanism to determine variable remuneration may have different motivational impact on frontline staff. Tuning the formula to achieve the desired outcome could be more an art than science, and we are seeing institutions experimenting and refining their remuneration practices from time to time taking into account actual experiences. Next steps 16. At this stage, the findings that I have just shared with you are still preliminary. We are now advancing to the next phase of the Focused Review to further explore any emerging themes and practices. Upon completion, which is expected to be around early next year, we plan to share further observations and insights as well as effective incentive practices with the banking industry. Closing remarks 17. Ladies and gentlemen, I trust that you would all agree with me the importance of incentive systems in motivating desirable staff behaviour. Through the Focused Review, we aim to find out how incentive systems drive staff behaviour and affect customer outcomes. Our goal is to achieve better alignment of the interests of bank staff and customers whilst preventing potential misconduct behavior, through the design of the incentive systems for bank staff. We trust that the Focused Review would set another important milestone in our journey in promoting sound bank culture. 18.1 would like to thank 1 LoD again for inviting me to share with you our work in promoting bank culture today. I hope that my sharing has "pulled" you to think more deeply on the importance of incentive systems, and I am sure fruitful programme of the XLoD event this year will inspire all of us as we continue our culture journey. 19. Thank you very much. Last revision date : 17 November 2021 / 4/4

Title: Keynote speech at the 4th Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Financial Development Forum
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech December 13, 2021 Keynote speech at the 4th Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Financial Development Forum Liu Yingbin is a Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Finding opportunities in challenges: how Hong Kong's financial sector can support the development of the Greater Bay Area Distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, Hello everyone. I am very pleased to participate in the 4th Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Financial Development Forum and discuss with you how Hong Kong's financial industry can find opportunities from challenges, seek breakthroughs and support the development of the Greater Bay Area under the background of the National 14th Five-Year Plan. This year marks the beginning of the 14th Five-Year Plan. The 14th Five-Year Plan proposes a new development pattern in which "the domestic cycle is the mainstay and the domestic dual cycle promotes each other", and clearly calls for continued coordinated regional development. The Greater Bay Area is the best entry point for Hong Kong to participate in the internal cycle. For many years, Hong Kong has always been the country's international financial center and a reliable overseas financing platform for mainland enterprises, which has played a role as a security barrier to prevent and defuse various risks while assisting the country in promoting the reform and opening up of the capital market . The development of the Greater Bay Area focuses on promoting the freer flow of production factors such as capital, talents and technology. In the past few years, the regulatory departments of the two places have worked together to introduce a number of financial facilitation measures, which have solved the problems of many residents living and working across the border in the Greater Bay Area, as well as enterprises carrying out cross-border business. Let me talk about the challenges faced by these residents and enterprises from several aspects, and also share how Hong Kong, as an international financial center, can find opportunities from these challenges, promote cross-border financial cooperation, and support economic development and social exchanges in the Greater Bay Area. The first challenge comes from the financing needs of enterprises in the Greater Bay Area. The Greater Bay Area is an important engine of economic development in the Mainland, and in the 14th Five-Year Plan, the state promotes high-quality development, and the financing needs of enterprises in the region, especially those related to innovation, technology and green, are more intense. Hong Kong's capital markets are the best way to meet these needs. Hong Kong's equities, bond markets and banking system have always been the preferred offshore financing platform for mainland enterprises. In terms of the stock market, Hong Kong is one of the world's leading IPO fundraising venues. Seven times since 2009, it has topped the annual global IPO fundraising rankings. More than half of the companies currently listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange are mainland companies, accounting for about 80% of the total value of the Hong Kong stock market. Since HKEX implemented the new listing regime in April 2018, Hong Kong has become the preferred listing place for an increasing number of mainland biotech companies and is currently the second largest biotech financing centre in the world. Hong Kong is also Asia's leading bond market and Asia's largest international bond issuance centre, accounting for 34% of Asia's international bond issuance in 2020. The green bond market has also boomed in recent years, with more than US38 billion in green bonds and loans arranged and issued in Hong Kong as of the end of last year. Issuers are mainly mainland institutions and enterprises, accounting for 60% of the total issuance in 2020. Recently, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued 5 billion yuan of offshore RMB bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, of which 3.9 billion yuan were green bonds, which not only enriched the products of Hong Kong's green bond market, but also played a great demonstration role in the issuance of green bonds by mainland issuers in Hong Kong. For a large number of SMEs, Hong Kong's banking sector is also an important source of investment and working capital. As of June this year, loans from Hong Kong's banking system and mainland institutions totaled more than HK4.8 trillion, accounting for 16 percent of total assets, covering a large number of state-owned enterprises, private enterprises, and multinational and Hong Kong enterprises with operations on the mainland. These figures illustrate that Hong Kong is an important financial platform in the development of the Greater Bay Area. We will continue to enhance the competitiveness of the capital market, play a good role as a bridge connecting the Mainland and the world, and support the real economic activities of the Greater Bay Area. In terms of green finance, our mature financial system and professional service platform can help the Greater Bay Area play an important role in the country's green finance development and contribute to the country's achievement of the 30/60 double carbon target. The second challenge is related to the transfer of cross-border funds by enterprises in the Greater Bay Area. The Greater Bay Area is an important window for opening up to the outside world. Many enterprises in the zone have frequent cross-border business transactions, and there is a higher demand for the efficiency of cross-border capital management. Hong Kong's financial system is well-equipped with a wide range of products and services offered by financial institutions, making it an ideal location for enterprises to establish treasury centres. The Hong Kong government introduced tax incentives in 2016 to attract more multinational enterprises to carry out treasury activities in Hong Kong. After several years of promotion, a number of mainland enterprises have set up treasury centres in Hong Kong, many of which are headquartered in the Greater Bay Area. We have also noted that in recent years, the Mainland has introduced different versions of cross-border pooling arrangements. This year, Shenzhen became one of the first to carry out the pilot project of integrating local and foreign currency capital pools of multinational companies to further facilitate the cross-border use of funds by qualified enterprises. We welcome more Greater Bay Area enterprises to Hong Kong for treasury management and hope that the cross-border capital pool arrangement can be extended to more Greater Bay Area enterprises so that they can manage cross-border funds more efficiently. In addition, some markets and public opinions reflect that there is still a lot of room for improvement in the use of cross-border financial services by individuals. One of them is cross-border payment services, a few years ago, Hong Kong residents to the mainland to live, work and travel to the mainland can not avoid exchanging a certain amount of RMB cash in advance in Hong Kong. With the joint support of the regulatory authorities of the two places, various financial institutions have seized the opportunity to launch various innovations in cross-border retail payments. For example, some Hong Kong-issued e-wallet users can now make electronic payments in the mainland, including the Greater Bay Area, covering merchants, shops, restaurants and even some public transportation in major cities in the Greater Bay Area, bringing convenience to Hong Kong residents to live and work in the Greater Bay Area. We are currently looking at more convenience measures, one of which is the digital yuan. The HKMA is cooperating with the People's Bank of China to conduct a technical test of the use of the digital yuan in Hong Kong, hoping to provide residents of the two places with one more cross-border payment method option in the future. In terms of personal cross-border financial services , it is necessary to mention the demand for cross-border financial services. The mainland's economic growth has led to the accumulation of people's wealth, and mainland investors have greater demand for diversification and increase overseas asset allocation. On the other hand, for Hong Kong individual investors, factors such as higher returns to RMB assets and seeking risk diversification have also contributed to their increased demand for asset allocation on the mainland. The recently launched Cross-Border Wealth Management Connect is a major breakthrough. This arrangement not only brings more investment options to individual investors in the Greater Bay Area, but also creates new opportunities for the banking and wealth management industry. As of 26 November, 19 Hong Kong banks and their Mainland partner banks have launched Cross-Border Wealth Management Connect, with more than 14,500 individual investors participating. The total amount of cross-border remittances amounted to RMB300 million. At present, Cross-Border Wealth Management Connect is only in its infancy, and the open investment products are relatively stable, and there are some restrictions on sales arrangements. We will keep an eye on the operation of Cross-Border Wealth Management Connect and discuss with the relevant departments of the industry and the relevant Mainland authorities in a timely manner the flexibility of expansion plans and enhanced arrangements . Fintech is a major trend in the development of the global financial industry. Combining the dual advantages of technological innovation in the mainland cities of the Greater Bay Area and Hong Kong's position as an international financial center, the Greater Bay Area has unique development conditions to promote the development of financial technology. However, the fintech market has lacked a channel of connectivity. To promote the development of fintech in the Greater Bay Area, the HKMA and the People's Bank of China signed a memorandum of understanding in October agreeing to connect regulatory tools between the two places through the "Internet". This arrangement allows financial institutions and technology companies in the Greater Bay Area to pass A "one-stop" platform to simultaneously test their cross-border fintech projects in both places, so that new products can be marketed early in terms of regulatory feedback and user feedback. Since the announcement of the arrangement, more than 10 Hong Kong banks/fintech companies have been in operation or have expressed interest in testing their cross-border fintech projects through networking in Hong Kong and mainland Greater Bay Area cities. Many of these projects are related to cross-border wealth management and may be applied to cross-border wealth management links. conclusion Dear friends, in the past few years, in the process of deepening the economic integration of the Greater Bay Area, new progress has been made in the field of cross-border financial cooperation. This year is also a bumper harvest year, and the cross-border wealth management link will push the financial cooperation in the Greater Bay Area and the interconnection of the financial markets of the two places to a new level; The networking of fintech regulation also marks the further deepening of financial cooperation between the two places. In addition, the state announced in September the "Plan for Comprehensively Deepening the Reform and Opening Up of the Qianhai Shenzhen-Hong Kong Modern Service Industry Cooperation Zone", allowing Shenzhen and Hong Kong to explore new space for development to promote financial cooperation and help the construction of the Greater Bay Area. As an international financial centre, Hong Kong will continue to seize the opportunities of the Greater Bay Area, explore more diversified and convenient financial innovations, support the real economic development of the Greater Bay Area, play a unique role in the national 14th Five-Year Plan, promote the economic integration of the Greater Bay Area, and create new impetus for Hong Kong's economic development. Thank you. Note: The forum was held on December 12, 2021 Last revision date: December 13, 2021

Title: Keynote Speech at the 12th Caixin Summit (Greater Bay Area Session)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY Hong Kong Monetary Authority Speech December 15, 2021 Keynote speech at the 12th Caixin Summit (Greater Bay Area). Liu Yingbin, Vice President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Dear President Hu Shuli, leaders and distinguished guests: 1. Hello everyone! I am very pleased to have the opportunity to participate in the Greater Bay Area Session of this year's Caixin Summit. 2. Soon, we will bid farewell to 2021. Taking stock of the opening year of the 14th Five-Year Plan, it can be said that it is a bumper harvest year, not only ushering in a new breakthrough in the interconnection mechanism between the mainland and Hong Kong, but also making significant progress in cooperation between the two places in the fields of green finance and financial technology. 3. Today, I would like to take the opportunity of the summit to talk about how Hong Kong can play its role as an international financial center, as a "participant" in the internal cycle and a " facilitator" of the external cycle, integrate into the new pattern of China's economic "double circulation", and help deepen reform and opening up. 4. Review the course of reform and opening up - from the initial promotion of trade exchanges, to the introduction of foreign investment, to assist mainland enterprises to get out To deepen the two-way connection of financial markets, along the way, Hong Kong has always been an important window and bridge for the mainland to connect with the world. At present, two-thirds of the direct investment in and out of the mainland is through Hong Kong, while more than half of the foreign investment in mainland stocks and bonds is made through Hong Kong. The mainland's market opening and financial integration have created unprecedented development opportunities for Hong Kong and created Hong Kong's special status as an international financial center. 5. The 14th Five-Year Plan puts forward higher requirements for Hong Kong's role in the economic development of the mainland. On the one hand, Hong Kong needs to continue to play its strengths in the "external circulation", make good use of its role as a bridge to help introduce international capital, and support the orderly development of mainland funds to the world; On the other hand, in the context of the mainland's high-quality development driving demand and optimizing the "internal circulation", Hong Kong should also seize the opportunity to make more pioneering progress in some new areas such as green finance and financial technology, actively participate in and cooperate with the mainland's innovation, high-quality development and increase domestic demand, so as to provide impetus for Hong Kong's economic transformation. 6. I would like to talk about how Hong Kong can give full play to its traditional advantages and promote the efficient connection between the mainland and international capital markets. Hong Kong has a highly marketable capital market and financial infrastructure in line with international standards, as well as perfect supporting services and a mature financial ecosystem, which not only provides efficient channels for the two-way opening of the mainland financial market, but also undertakes the function of a firewall to effectively manage potential risks. The Shanghai-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect and the Northbound Bond Stock Connect, launched in the past few years, have given full play to Hong Kong's characteristics and ensured that the mainland's stock and bond markets can exchange lower institutional costs for greater results in opening up under the premise of controllable risks, and at the same time accumulate experience for opening up in other fields. 7. As proposed in the 14th Five-Year Plan, Hong Kong will further expand its connectivity with the Mainland's financial markets and strengthen its functions as a global offshore RMB business hub, an international asset management centre and a risk management centre. In the past year, we have made many new breakthroughs. The Bond Connect was successfully launched in September this year, realizing the two-way connection between the Mainland and Hong Kong bond markets. The launch of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Cross-border Wealth Management Connect marks the expansion of connectivity from institutional investors to personal wealth management, which not only brings more diversified wealth allocation options for individual investors in the Greater Bay Area, but also creates new development opportunities for the banking and wealth management industry, which is a major policy breakthrough. As of the end of November, 19 Hong Kong banks and their Mainland partner banks have been engaged in business, attracting more than 14,000 individual investors1 to participate in cross-border remittances 2 more than 300 million yuan. 8. Start steadily, and naturally go far. In the next step, we will continue to improve and enhance various interconnection mechanisms, especially to provide more risk management products and channels for the market. As international investors continue to increase their holdings of RMB assets, so will their demand for related risk management tools. Hong Kong's foreign exchange and interest rate derivatives markets are relatively mature, trading rules and regulatory requirements are in line with international standards, and it has good conditions as a risk management center to provide better supporting risk management services for financial institutions investing in RMB assets. This will help strengthen the investment and value storage functions of the renminbi, which in turn will further expand the wider use of the renminbi in terms of payment and settlement. In addition, we will take a "multi-pronged approach" to expand market liquidity, enrich market products and enhance infrastructure to enhance the competitiveness of Hong Kong's offshore RMB business hub. 9. In addition to giving full play to its traditional advantages, Hong Kong's financial industry needs to make continuous innovations so that the Hong Kong market can better serve the transformation and upgrading of the mainland's real economy and move towards high-quality development. In my opinion, in the two fields of green finance and financial technology, Hong Kong has a lot of room for development. 10. The state proposes to gradually and orderly realize the transformation of China's economy to green and low-carbon under the framework of 30/60 carbon peak and carbon neutrality. In order to achieve this goal, a large amount of money needs to be invested. Hong Kong's financing platform can guide international funds to accelerate investment in the mainland's green assets and support the mainland's economic transformation. In recent years, Hong Kong has made significant progress in the development of green finance. In 2020, a total of US12 billion in green bonds and loans were arranged and issued in Hong Kong, three times as much as in 2017 Above. In October this year, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government successfully issued RMB green bonds in Hong Kong, which is the first time that a mainland government agency has issued green bonds abroad, and it is also an important symbol of Shenzhen-Hong Kong financial cooperation and the joint construction of a green Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. We hope that this issuance can play an exemplary role, open up a new overseas financing channel, and drive more mainland issuers to use Hong Kong's green bond platform to introduce overseas funds to participate in the realization of the national double carbon target. 11. To promote high-quality development, scientific and technological innovation is the key. In this area, Hong Kong will actively promote the research and application of local fintech to strengthen its competitiveness and strengthen its ties with the Mainland. In June, the HKMA formulated a FinTech 2025 Strategic Framework to help Hong Kong's financial sector fully adopt FinTech by 2025. In addition to laying a good foundation for Hong Kong's own fintech, we will also actively build a fintech network with the mainland. The HKMA and the People's Bank of China have recently implemented the docking of the network of financial technology innovation regulatory tools between the two places, which is to facilitate the testing of cross-border projects by financial institutions and technology companies in the two places. At the same time, we will continue to cooperate with the People's Bank of China to cooperate with the technical testing of the digital yuan (e-CNY) in Hong Kong, and develop a variety of central bank digital currency cross-border payment networks (mBridge) with multiple central bank institutions . 12. Folks, as the theme of this summit says, China's reform and opening up is in progress. In this ongoing process, we will give full play to Hong Kong's strengths and serve the needs of the country. As long as Hong Kong's sound and excellent financial infrastructure and the characteristics of orderly and free entry and exit of funds are made good use, and through pioneering and innovating in green finance, financial technology and other fields, we will certainly be able to further enhance the competitiveness of the financial platform, which will not only provide assistance for the high-quality development of the mainland economy, but also promote better connectivity between domestic and international capital markets. We believe that in the new pattern of mutual promotion and synergy between internal and external circulation, Hong Kong's status as an international financial center will also be further enhanced 13. Thank you! 1Including Hong Kong and Macau 2Including Hong Kong and Macau Last revision date: December 15, 2021

Title: Keynote Address at Association of Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialists (ACAMS) 13th Annual AML & Anti-Financial Crime Conference - APAC
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY # Si W 3 M Speeches 25 Apr 2022 Keynote Address at Association of Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialists (ACAMS) 13th Annual AML & Anti-Financial Crime Conference - APAC Carmen Chu, Executive Director (Enforcement and AML), Hong Kong Monetary Authority Next-Generation Anti-Money Laundering (AML) 1. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. 2. It is my great pleasure to speak at todays conference. Thanks to ACAMS for the invitation to participate in this important dialogue with public and private AML practitioners from across the region. 3. This is a challenging time. Against the background of Covid and technological development, there is increasing evidence that our global response to money laundering and terrorist financing (ML/TF) is under challenge. Growing popularity of online activities during the pandemic, coupled with speedy, remote bank account opening and operation powered by Fintech, while bringing great benefits and convenience, is also fuelling a surge in fraud and money mules. It requires speedy detection and disruption to address the emerging threats, and protect banks as well as their customers from resultant financial losses. 4. New technologies are also driving changes in international standards; virtual assets are now subject to the same AML regulation as traditional financial assets, with cybersecurity risk and investor protection also under close check globally and in a holistic manner. At the same time, the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) has been promoting the use of Regtech, which is sharpening our anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorist (AML/CFT) efforts and better protecting our economies across the APAC region. 5. International standards remain our anchor in responding to threats, and cascading through these standards is the assessment of emerging risks. In Hong Kong, we are currently updating the ML/TF risk assessment for our ecosystem. The banking sector, which the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) supervises, remains at high risk of being exploited for illicit fund flows. This is no surprise given Hong Kongs role as an international financial centre and global development in technological innovation in recent years. Our risk assessment builds on detailed information on typologies and trends, which is shared day-to-day through public-private partnerships among banks, law enforcement agencies and the HKMA. This forms the baseline for our risk-based approach to AML. 6. Let me turn to the actions necessary to address these identified risks. Innovation in our response will not only make compliance more effective, but also achieve better outcomes, sustainable over the longer term.
