I will highlight three areas of our work 11 AKAI wnere innovation is reaiiy accelerating tne move to next-generation approacnes to aivil, or what I also call AML - Analytics, Monitoring and Link-up. 7. The value of Analytics has already been demonstrated through more banks being able to examine bigger volumes of data and as a result, speedily identify connections between accounts which would not otherwise be seen. And it is important to share success stories, that is one of the reasons why we are all here. Leveraging more advanced technology and capabilities, Analytics provides high-quality and actionable information to support other stakeholders in the AML ecosystem to disrupt fraud and financial crime. Compliance effectiveness is improved under the overarching objective of protecting the integrity and safety of our system. 8. Network analytics was selected as the theme of our first AML Regtech Lab (AMLab), which was launched last November under the HKMAs Fintech 2025 Strategy, to provide a collaborative platform for banks and the Fintech community to explore the wider use of data and technology. AMLab is part of a broader strategy to support AML Regtech adoption and empowers banks that are less familiar with these tools to develop skills and capabilities in network analytics, and to integrate alternative data sources to strengthen entity resolution. 9. And it is the job of regulators such as the HKMA to ensure that such capabilities are deployed consistently across the banking sector, a mission to which we are whole- heartedly committed to help address the four-fold increase in complaints against banks in relation to online scams and fraud over the last two years, alongside the growing popularity of online banking and commerce. The positive response to the first AMLab has set our future direction for Regtech engagement and we will arrange further AMLabs on more themes, such as lower-technology solutions that are more accessible to smaller banks to widen the impact of this initiative. 10. As for the HKMA itself, we are also transforming our approach to the collection, storage and analysis of data, in support of more data-driven supervision and targeted interventions. I am referring here to our AML surveillance enhancement programme, a long-term commitment and investment in data, technology as well as supporting capabilities and culture. The objective is to better understand and target higher risks in banks we supervise - such as fraud and global money laundering networks that may prejudice customers interests and threaten banking stability. 11. The second theme is Monitoring. A common pain point is how to get the best from rules- based monitoring systems and address inefficiencies arising from large volumes of sometimes unproductive alerts. Ill be brief here noting one of todays sessions is dedicated to this topic. My view is that transaction monitoring systems will remain an important part of AML efforts, reflected by the fact that technology firms are offering innovative ideas and add-on enhancements that promise to make such systems more effective and efficient. 12. While customer on-boarding remains the first line of defence, and whether this is done remotely or in-person, or whether and what technology solutions are employed, the same standards apply. Realistically, on-boarding process is not a zero failure concept; it is impossible to stop all criminals from entering the financial system solely by the on- boarding process. Therefore, ongoing transaction monitoring by financial institutions is extremely important for detecting and reporting suspicious transactions early, and assisting investigations by law enforcement agencies to disrupt bad acts. 13. Next-generation transaction monitoring is an area we have been looking at since the first AMI /OFT RantAch Forum in 2019 Mark At fAAdhack suonasts that a flaxihla approach will deliver the best results, integrating subject matter expertise with an approach that is customised to each bank. With this in mind, the HKMA is currently undertaking thematic work, supported by a leading Regtech provider, to review performance of a number of banks transaction monitoring systems. 14. In addition, we are updating our guidance on name screening, transaction monitoring and suspicious transaction reporting, incorporating sound practices as well as insights from engagement with other stakeholders. We will continue to maintain close contact with the industry to assist banks in their important gatekeeper role in the AML ecosystem. 15. This brings me to the third theme, which is Link-up. Our efforts to apply analytics, improve monitoring, and use the power of the cloud to interrogate increased data sources will be for nothing if there is no link-up across the ecosystem. In Hong Kong, banks and law enforcement agencies as well as the HKMA are linked up through public- private partnerships, notably the Fraud and Money Laundering Intelligence Taskforce (FMLIT)1 which has been scaled up since its inception in 2017 and now includes all 8 virtual banks and 15 major retail banks. A total of 25 alerts were issued to share modus operandi information and good practices across the wider industry. Close collaboration in FMLIT has helped improve our ecosystem response to fraud and financial crime, with around HK820 million in crime proceeds restrained or confiscated up to March 2022. 16. In addition, the HKMA has been closely working with the Anti-Deception Coordination Centre (ADCC)2 to strengthen the banking industrys capability to intercept fraudulent payments. With the rise in online fraud and mule account networks globally, it is important for banks to be agile and responsive as threats arise. Under the 24/7 stop payment mechanisms, the banking industry helped intercept over HK2.2 billion in suspected fraudulent payments in 2021. 17. The local banking industry, similar to that in other international financial centres, contributed over 80% of suspicious transaction reports filed to the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit (JFIU), providing timely and actionable intelligence leading to criminal investigations. We also support more collaboration at the regional and international levels, for examples through ACAMS events such as this one, and the HKMAs active participation in FATF discussion including its co-chairmanship of the FATF Evaluations and Compliance Working Group. Closing 18. The pandemic, advances in technology and the move to a digital economy are all transforming the landscape to which AML work responds. It is now very clear that innovative tools - adoption of Analytics and technology to supplement and enhance Monitoring systems, with Link-up of public-private as well as regional and international efforts - will allow AML work to focus on keeping up with current and emerging risks. To reap these benefits, financial institutions must continue to innovate and adapt their approaches to Analytics, Monitoring and Link-up for AML. 19. Ladies and gentlemen, an open, timely dialogue like this one will help us navigate and accelerate the AML journey in a prudent and agile manner. We must collectively ensure that the APAC region leads the way on innovation in AML/CFT work, delivering higher levels of effectiveness and better outcomes to safeguard our financial systems from being abused for illicit fund flows and to protect consumers from financial losses. I look forward to further insights and fruitful discussions in the remaining part of the programme. 20. Thank you. 1 Established in May 2017, the FMLIT is a public-private partnership for information sharing among the Hong Kong Police Force, the HKMA and 23 banks. 2 The Anti-Deception Coordination Centre was established in July 2017 by Hong Kong Police Force to combat against deception and enhance public awareness of various kinds of scams. Remark: The conference was held on April 23 - 24, 2022. Last revision date : 25 April 2022

Title: Keynote Speech at TVB Financial Forum - Environmental, Social, Governance (Chinese version)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  Speeches 09.06.2022 Keynote speech on "TVB Finance Forum - Environmental, Social and Governance". Eddie Yue, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Dear guests and friends, Hello everyone! It is my great pleasure to attend the "Finance Forum 2022J" organised by TVB to share with you the latest developments and future opportunities in green finance in Hong Kong.  In recent years, the problem of extreme weather has become increasingly serious, and the international community has generally realized that it is urgent to address climate change. In 2020 and 2021 respectively, the HKSAR Government announced that Hong Kong would strive to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050 and halve its carbon emissions by 2035 from 2005 levels. To this end, the Government has set up an inter-departmental Steering Committee on Climate Change and Carbon Neutrality to formulate an overall strategy and oversee the synergy of various initiatives.  To achieve the dual carbon goals, the mainland needs to invest in the amount of RMB 100 billion. Hong Kong has also invested considerably in this area, with the HKSAR Government allocating over HK47 billion over the past decade or so to implement various decarbonisation measures. In the next 15 to 20 years, the Government will invest about HK240 billion to implement various climate change mitigation and adaptation measures, including renewable energy, energy conservation and green buildings, green transport and waste management. It is believed that the private sector will also invest heavily in carbon reduction. The huge financing needs of both places will directly accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong.  The Central Government has been very supportive of Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance development, enacted in 2019 and 2020 respectively The "Outline Development Plan for the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area" and the "Opinions on Financial Support for the Development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area" put forward support for Hong Kong's development into a green finance centre in the Greater Bay Area. As an international financial centre and a hub connecting China and the rest of the world, Hong Kong can give full play to its advantages in connecting the effective supply and demand of green and sustainable finance at home and abroad, thereby promoting green and low-carbon development at the national and local levels.  In fact, Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance market is becoming more and more vibrant. Last year, the amount of green and sustainable debt financing arranged and issued in Hong Kong reached a new high of US57 billion, a four-fold year-on-year increase. Among them, international bonds totalled US31.3 billion, accounting for one-third of the Asian market, and ranked first in terms of arrangement.  The HKSAR Government works with financial regulators and the industry to adopt a multi-pronged strategy to promote green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. To date, the Government has successfully issued institutional and retail green bonds with a total value of nearly US10 billion equivalent, which have been well received by international and local investors and provide an important new benchmark for potential issuers in Hong Kong and the region to enrich green and sustainable finance production  These issuances have led to a number of breakthroughs. For example, the US2.5 billion government green bond issued in February last year was the world's largest government dollar green bond at the time, and the 30-year bond was the longest government dollar green bond in Asia. In November 2021, we issued approximately US4 billion equivalent of government green bonds, including Eurobonds and RMB bonds for the first time, with the 20-year Eurobond being the longest maturity of the government euro green bond in Asia at the time.  We just issued our first batch of HK20 billion retail green bonds in May, the largest issuance in the world to date. The launch of the Government's retail green bonds not only provides a channel for the public to participate in green and sustainable finance, but also expands the range of green and sustainable products, further promoting the local retail bond market, and is another important milestone in the development of Hong Kong's bond market and green and sustainable finance market. This initiative will also allow citizens to share the fruits of the green economy and achieve financial inclusion.  In addition to the green bonds issued by the HKSAR Government, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government also issued a total of 5 billion offshore bonds in Hong Kong in October last year Local government bonds, of which 3.9 billion are green bonds. This is the first time that a local government in the Mainland has issued bonds overseas, which is of great significance as it will enhance Hong Kong's status as a green finance centre in the Greater Bay Area, play a strategic role as a gateway to the Mainland, connect the flow of green funds from the Mainland and abroad, and become the preferred platform for the issuance of green products.  In addition to issuing government bonds, we also hope to attract corporates from around the world to use Hong Kong's green financing platform, and encourage more financial and professional service providers and external assessors to establish a foothold in Hong Kong, a hub in the region. To this end, the HKSAR Government launched a three-year Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme in May 2021 to subsidise eligible bond issuers and borrowers for bond issuance and external review services.  Since its launch, nearly 100 applications have been approved for the issuance of US30 billion worth of green and sustainable bonds and loans, many of which are to fund external review costs related to green and sustainable loans. In order to facilitate green financing for smaller enterprises, we lowered the minimum loan amount threshold for applying for external review fee funding from 200 million to 100 million in March this year.  In 2020, the relevant policy bureaux and financial regulators of the HKSAR Government formed a Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to co-ordinate the financial sector's measures to address climate and environmental risks. In December of the same year, the Steering Group published a strategic plan to strengthen Hong Kong's financial ecosystem on various fronts and implement a short-term action plan to build a greener and more sustainable future in the long run.  In particular, in order to address the pain point of the lack of uniform standards in the financial industry, the Steering Group continues to monitor the progress of the work of the international sustainable finance platform. In November last year, the International Sustainable Finance Platform (IFF) published a report on the Common Green Taxonomy, which compares the taxonomies of countries and the EU in detail and identifies the commonalities between the two, which can help define activities that make a significant contribution to mitigating climate change and reduce the risk of greenwashing. In this regard, the Steering Group is exploring the establishment of a green taxonomy framework for adoption in the Hong Kong market based on the Common Green Taxonomy (CRC), with a view to facilitating the interface between the above-mentioned Common Green Taxonomy and the Mainland and EU Green Taxonomies.  Talent and data are important elements in the development of green finance and the management of climate risks. As such, the Steering Group has established a cross-sector Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance to co-ordinate the work of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders and academic institutions in areas such as training and data collection and analysis. In the near future, the Centre will launch a resource repository to facilitate easier access to data, training and practice resources for industry and academia to support climate risk management and other green and sustainable finance-related analysis and research. We are also preparing to launch the "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" announced earlier in the Budget to provide funding support for people from the financial and related sectors to participate in training and obtain professional qualifications.  The carbon market also plays an important role in the low-carbon transition of the global economy. At the end of March this year, the Steering Group published a preliminary feasibility assessment of the opportunities in Hong Kong's carbon market. Based on the preliminary assessment, Hong Kong could draw on the work and financial expertise of the relevant international voluntary carbon market organisations to develop a central voluntary carbon market on the exchange floor to provide an additional and transparent purchasing channel for buyers of voluntary emission reductions in Hong Kong, the Mainland and overseas. At the same time, it can deepen regional and international ties, and seek new opportunities for the construction of a unified carbon market in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, connecting international investors with the mainland carbon market. The Steering Group will study the most appropriate market and regulatory model and will work out further details in consultation with market experts and relevant authorities.  Looking ahead, we will continue to work hard and work with the financial sector and relevant stakeholders to develop and promote Hong Kong as a green and sustainable finance hub in the region, seize the huge green finance opportunities brought about by the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and the Belt and Road Initiative, and become the preferred investment and financing platform for overseas and Mainland green enterprises/projects, and raise funds through multiple channels such as bond issuance, funds and initial public offerings.  In closing, I wish today's forum a complete success, as well as a greater social consensus for the sustainable development of green finance in Hong Kong and more opportunities for Hong Kong's financial centre. Thank you. Last revision date: 09 June 2022

Title: Remarks after the US Fed FOMC Meeting
text: IIONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY # Mi W 3 M Speeches 16 Jun 2022 Remarks after the US Fed FOMC Meeting Eddie Yue, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. The Federal Open Market Committee of the Federal Reserve (the Fed) announced a rate hike of 75 basis points at the early hours today (Hong Kong time) after its two-day meeting, raising the target range for the federal funds rate to 1.5%-1.75%. The HKMA has adjusted the Base Rate upward by 75 basis points to 2% according to the established mechanism with immediate effect. 2. The Feds 75-basis-point rate hike is higher than the expected level conveyed by the Fed after its last meeting, mainly due to the latest US inflation data hitting another 40- year high, but is still consistent with recent market expectation. 3. Hong Kongs monetary and financial markets continue to remain stable despite the USs multiple rate hikes, with the foreign exchange market operating in an orderly manner and market liquidity being ample. As the US raised interest rates again, there will be incentives for market participants to conduct carry trades when the Hong Kong dollar and US dollar interest rate differentials are sufficiently wide, driving funds to gradually flow from the Hong Kong dollar to the US dollar. Therefore it is normal for the Hong Kong dollar to remain weak. 4. According to the design of the LERS, when the weak-side Convertibility Undertaking at 7.85 is triggered, the HKMA will buy Hong Kong dollars and sell US dollars. This was exactly what happened in May and this week. All these are normal operations in accordance with the design of the LERS. 5. Under the LERS, the Hong Kong dollar interbank rates will gradually track the US dollar interbank rates. However, the speed and magnitude of the Hong Kong dollar interbank rates catching up with their US dollar counterparts will still be subject to the supply and demand of the Hong Kong dollar funding in the local market. As for the commercial interest rates of banks, they will decide on the timing and magnitude of adjusting their saving and lending interest rates having regard to their own funding cost structures and other relevant considerations. The public should carefully assess and manage the relevant risks when making property purchase, mortgage or relevant decisions. 6. The HKMA will continue to closely monitor market situations with a view to maintaining monetary and financial stability. Last revision date : 16 June 2022

Title: Opening remarks at The 4th Master Insight Finance Summit cum ESG Award Ceremony (Chinese version)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  Speeches 2022-06-17 Opening speech at the 4th Financial Summit & ESG Awards Ceremony David Chan, Executive Director (External), Hong Kong Monetary Authority Dear guests and friends, morning everyone! We would like to thank our insightful experts for their invitation to attend the 4th Finance Summit & ESG Awards Ceremony. I would like to take this opportunity to share with you the new opportunities of green finance in Hong Kong. When we talk about green finance, the focus is often on financial instruments, but tools are only means, and more importantly, the adoption and application of green finance in the real economy, and the investment of funds in specific projects and daily operations, this is the purpose of green finance. Therefore, the selection and awarding of ESG awards by Insight Masters reflects the true meaning of green finance. I would like to extend my heartfelt congratulations to the many companies that have received the ESG Leadership Award and the ESG Business Model Award today. I noticed that many of the award-winning companies are pioneers in Hong Kong's green finance, who have created one successful green finance case after another based on their own characteristics and combined with the green services and products provided by Hong Kong's financial industry, which have contributed to the fight against climate change and created value for their corporate brands, and have also played a good role model for more enterprises to pay attention to and accept green finance. Hong Kong is uniquely positioned to play a role in green finance. Asia accounted for 52% of global CO2 emissions in 2020. To meet the requirements of the Paris Agreement, Asia is expected to need US66 trillion in climate investment over the next 30 years. On the mainland, the central government has set the 3060 dual carbon target, which conservatively estimates that more than 100 trillion yuan of green investment will be needed in the next 30 years to achieve carbon neutrality. Hong Kong is a major international financial centre in Asia and has always been a hub for financial integration in the region. The huge demand for climate finance in Asia is undoubtedly a unique opportunity for Hong Kong's financial sector, especially the bond market and banking sector. In fact, Hong Kong has made many breakthroughs in green finance in recent years. In recent years, the HKMA has partnered with international independent institutions to systematically collect and analyse the development of Hong Kong's green finance market. I will try to make a brief introduction from four aspects: the issuance volume, the ratio of bonds to loans, the issuer of bonds, and the types of products. The first is circulation. The latest data shows that Hong Kong's green and sustainable debt instruments, including bonds and bank loans, reached US57 billion in 2021, a fourfold increase from 2020. Among them, green bonds accounted for 15% of the overall bond issuance, compared with 4% in 2020, an increase is very considerable, which shows that green bonds have become a new force in the bond market Or The second is the classification of green debt instruments, which has also seen significant changes. In 2020, the ratio of green bonds to bank green loans was nine to one, and in 2021, green loans have caught up, and the same ratio has become 55% to 45%, and green loans account for almost half of the country. The third is the change in the issuer of bonds. In 2021, financial institutions accounted for 35%, real estate companies accounted for 37%, other types of enterprises accounted for 18%, and governments and multilateral development banks accounted for 10%. It is worth noting that the proportion of financial institutions increased by 16 percentage points in 2020 from only 19% in 2020, reflecting the increasing intermediary role of financial institutions in raising green funds through the market and then providing them to specific green projects and enterprises. Fourth, green financial products are becoming more and more abundant. In addition to the most common green, sustainable and transitional bonds and loans, financial institutions continue to launch innovative green products, including socially responsible bonds, interest rate swaps linked to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, blue bonds, epidemic prevention and control bonds, related green derivatives and so on. In addition, at the retail level, banks have also launched products such as green deposits and green mortgages. The rapid development of green finance in Hong Kong, market demand and mature financial system are of course the main factors, and the vigorous promotion of the government and regulators has also played a certain role. Let me give you a few examples. The first is the government's green bond program. In 2019, the HKSAR Government set up the Government Green Bond Scheme, which is implemented by the HKMA. The programme, which is capped at HK200 billion, has so far successfully issued green bonds with a total value of nearly US10 billion equivalent, and has recorded a number of records, including the world's largest issuance of US dollar green bonds, Asia's longest maturity government green bonds, Asia's longest maturity government euro green bonds, the first renminbi bond issued by the Hong Kong government, and the world's largest retail green bond. The government's issuance of green bonds has multiple significances: First, it provides funds for the government's green engineering projects. The second is to gradually establish a multi-currency, multi-year bond yield curve to provide a reference benchmark for issuers in Hong Kong and Asia. Third, through the Green Bond Programme, the Hong Kong Government's determination and ability to implement the carbon neutrality goal will be promoted to international investors. In fact, the Hong Kong government's green bond programme has built up a pretty good reputation among institutional investors, and our green bond framework is highly recognized. Fourthly, through the successful experience of government green bonds, we can promote the Hong Kong green bond platform to potential issuers in our first role, so as to attract more institutions to conduct green financing in Hong Kong. One example is the successful issuance of 5 billion of offshore RMB bonds in Hong Kong by the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government in October last year, of which 3.9 billion is green bonds. During the bond issuance process, the HKMA team shared our experience and provided assistance to the best of our ability. In the future, we will continue to strengthen our promotion work in this area. The effect will be more obvious if there is substantial funding to cooperate with publicity and promotion. The issuance of green bonds involves various issuance costs, and green financing, whether it is a bond or a loan, requires an external independent review agency to evaluate the project. In order to attract more issuers to engage in green financing in Hong Kong, the HKSAR Government launched a three-year Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme in May last year to subsidise bond issuers and borrowers to spend on bond issuance and external review services. The HKMA is responsible for the vetting and approval process. The programme has been so well received that nearly 100 applications have been approved in less than a year, involving green and sustainable bonds and loans totalling US30 billion. In order to encourage smaller enterprises to engage in green financing, the Financial Secretary announced in this year's Budget that the minimum loan amount threshold for external review fee funding will be lowered from 200 million to 100 million. Recently, we have started to receive applications from companies benefiting from the new policy. Another objective of the Scheme is to attract more financial institutions and external assessors to set up in Hong Kong to provide professional green financing services through an accreditation arrangement. At present, most of the major external review agencies in the world have set up bases or expanded their business in Hong Kong, and the business model of focusing on sales and services in the past has gradually increased the technical content of professional review. This will be of great benefit to enhancing the depth of knowledge on green finance in Hong Kong. In addition to promoting market development, the HKMA has also promoted the development of a green and sustainable banking industry through our regulatory work, requiring banks to properly address climate risks and introduce the concept of green finance in the four aspects of strategy, governance, risk management and disclosure of banks, so that banks can pay more attention to addressing climate risks in their business and operating models, and introduce more green finance elements in their businesses and products. I just focused on the opportunities, but there are also some challenges to promoting green finance, which I summarized as standards, data, and talent. These challenges cannot be tackled by financial institutions alone, but need to be addressed by a concerted effort by stakeholders from all walks of life. Therefore, the HKMA and the SFC took the lead, together with the relevant policy bureaux of the HKSAR Government and other financial regulators, to form a _LL in 2020 to form a team of experts on the three challenges that have just been mentioned. In response to the lack of a unified green standard, the Sub-committee agreed to adopt the Common Ground Taxonomy, which integrates Chinese and EU standards, to study the establishment of a green taxonomy framework that can be adopted by the Hong Kong market, so as to provide a set of green benchmarks for the Hong Kong financial industry. The Group has also set up a cross-sector Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance, bringing together regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders and academic institutions to explore and implement practical solutions with a focus on green talent pools and data collection and analysis. With the strong support of various departments of the HKSAR Government, the Centre will soon launch a resource information database to help the financial industry and academia find climate-related data more conveniently, and provide one-stop training and internship information to support analysis and research related to climate risk management and green finance. At the same time, the Sub-committee is preparing to launch the "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" announced in this year's Budget to provide assets to support green finance practitioners and university students to participate in training and obtain professional qualifications. We expect to launch the programme within this year. Ladies and gentlemen, green finance is in its infancy, Hong Kong has strong foundations, unique advantages, and more importantly, we have the common confidence to leverage green finance to further diversify Hong Kong as an international financial centre and make finance an important driving force for Hong Kong to achieve its carbon neutrality goals. Finally, I wish the summit a smooth success, and take advantage of the theme of the summit to wish you wisdom and wealth! Thanks a lot. Revised: 17/06/2022

Title: Keynote Speech at the Bond Connect Anniversary Summit 2022 (Chinese version)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  Speeches 04.07.2022 Keynote speech at the Bond Connect Annual Forum 2022 Eddie Yue, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Honorable Chief Executive John Lee (Chief Executive of the Hong Kong S.A.R.), Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po (Financial Secretary), Honorable Vice Governor Pan Kung Shing (Deputy Governor of the People's Bank of China), Deputy Director Wang Linggui (Deputy Director of the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the State Council), Deputy Director Yin Zonghua (Deputy Director of the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the Hong Kong S.A.R.), Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Five years ago, on the first trading day after the 20th anniversary of Hong Kong's return to the motherland, we rang the gong of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in this lobby to officially launch the Northbound Bond Trading. Five years later, on the same day, as we celebrate the 25th anniversary of the reunification, it is of special significance to look back on the achievements of Bond Connect over the past five years and look forward to the future development blueprint. Looking back over the past five years, Bond Connect has become a major channel for international investors to allocate Mainland bonds. In May this year, the total turnover of the Northbound Scheme was about RMB675 billion, accounting for more than 60% of the turnover of international investors in the mainland's interbank bond market. Building on the solid foundation of the Northbound Scheme, the Southbound Scheme was officially launched last year to achieve two-way connectivity between the bond markets of the Mainland and Hong Kong. The success of the Northbound Scheme did not happen overnight. In the first month of opening, the trading volume was only 31 billion yuan. To achieve today's results, we have experienced the process of gradual development and continuous improvement; Based on the market, the two places have continuously optimised various supporting links such as trading, settlement and fund exchange, so as to enhance the operational efficiency and reduce transaction costs of the Northbound Scheme. Today's achievements would not have been possible without the joint efforts of market participants, infrastructure institutions and regulators in both places, and I would like to take this opportunity to express my heartfelt thanks to all of you. The success of the Northbound Scheme also proves that Hong Kong as an international financial centre can play a unique role as a bridge for the opening up of the Mainland's financial market. Under the Northbound Scheme, international investors can easily invest in the Mainland bond market through long-term financial intermediaries in accordance with familiar market practices. On the other hand, the Northbound Trading also assists the Mainland market to attract international investors in an orderly manner while maintaining the existing system and controllable risks, and also provides opportunities for the Mainland market to explore institutional innovations such as multi-level custody. Looking ahead, there is still a lot of room for development under the Northbound Scheme. At present, international investors account for only 2.7% of the mainland bond market. Mainland bonds have been included in major global indices, and the proportion of RMB in the IMF's Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) has increased, and the internationalization of RMB has developed steadily in recent years. Against this backdrop, there is plenty of room for international investors to increase their allocation to mainland bonds. A week ago, the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), together with the People's Bank of China, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and four other central banks, established a RMB liquidity arrangement, is a case in point. As an important supporting package, the demand for relevant risk management tools from international investors will also gradually increase. In the next phase, we will focus on providing diversified risk management tools to investors under the Northbound Scheme and enhancing the function of Hong Kong's risk management centre. The launch of Swap Connect is a timely and important step in deepening financial co-operation between the two places, enabling international investors to manage the interest rate risk associated with bond investment more conveniently, and further enhancing their participation in the Mainland bond market. In terms of deepening the integration of financial infrastructure, the two places will also continue to enhance the transaction settlement arrangements, for example, the CMU (Hong Kong's debt facility settlement system) will be automatically connected with the Mainland's central securities depositories to enhance the settlement efficiency of Bond Connect. At the same time, the HKMA will seize the opportunities arising from the Southbound Scheme to enhance the depth and breadth of Hong Kong's bond market, especially the dim sum bond market. On the one hand, it will meet the needs of mainland investors for diversified allocation of overseas bonds, and on the other hand, it will attract more domestic and foreign institutions to issue bonds in Hong Kong, and develop CMU into a major international central securities depository platform in Asia. This morning, the People's Bank of China (PBoC) and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced that the existing currency swap agreement will be renewed on a regular basis and expanded from RMB500 billion to RMB800 billion. I would like to thank the People's Bank of China (PBoC) for its support of Hong Kong's offshore RMB liquidity, and I believe that this standing currency swap agreement will lay a very solid foundation for the further development of Hong Kong's RMB products and strengthen Hong Kong's position as a global offshore RMB business hub. I believe that with our joint efforts, the next five years of Bond Connect will be even more exciting, and the mutual access between the financial markets of the Mainland and Hong Kong will continue to make new breakthroughs. Thank you! Revised: 04.07.2022

Title: Opening Keynote Speech at Fraud and Financial Crime Asia 2022 Conference
text: @IIONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  & Si a M Speeches 13 Jul 2022 Opening Keynote Speech at Fraud and Financial Crime Asia 2022 Conference Carmen Chu, Executive Director (Enforcement and AML), Hong Kong Monetary Authority Innovative ways of working in AML/CFT: Collaboration powered by data, technology and analytics 1. Good morning everyone. I want to start by thanking Regulation Asia for inviting me to this event again to further our discussions on combatting fraud and financial crime more effectively and efficiently. 2. Im going to address two points I made a year ago, and in doing so share my reflections on how we have been doing - our score card if you like. Firstly, I spoke about the need for us to question how effective we really were in tackling fraud, cyber-crime and money laundering; and secondly, the roles of data, technology and collaboration in protecting the integrity of our financial system amid the fast- changing and more complex global landscape. 3. Over the past 12 months, financial crime, especially fraud and cyber-crime, have continued to proliferate. The global economy has faced, and continues to face, unprecedented challenges brought about by the pandemic and developments in geopolitics. These challenges include rises in the cost of living, climate change, and disrupted global supply chains to name just a few. For the first time in many years, we are seeing significant inflation in many parts of the world, and at levels not seen for a generation. 4. In times of economic uncertainty, incentives and opportunities to commit financial crime increase. Normal patterns of business are disrupted, people may be tempted to take more risks in how they handle and invest their money. Government subsidies and loan guarantees to alleviate economic pain in hard-hit sectors also become targets for the unscrupulous. 5. Globally, fraud is still far too common, especially online fraud, which together with cybercrime, has increased sharply during the pandemic, as companies and individuals have moved more of their activities online. And much of this crime affects individuals and small businesses, who are less able to protect themselves. Often, the victims are among the most vulnerable in society, with the elderly and unemployed often targeted by fraud and money laundering syndicates. 6. At times like this, it is all the more important that the financial sector plays its gatekeeper role in the Anti-Money Laundering (AML) ecosystem in helping to identify and stop fraudsters and cyber criminals who prey on the vulnerable. 7. Its more than a question of compliance: tackling fraud and cybercrime and the money flows that result from them is a stability issue. Apart from the direct costs to people and businesses that tall victim to tnese crimes, it we don't get a nandie on this, there is a real risk that confidence in our financial and payment systems may be undermined, with potentially serious consequences for stability. Confidence and stability are inextricably linked. It must be a priority to show that financial institutions with which the public entrust their savings, and the regulators who supervise them, do care about these threats and, more importantly, are addressing them proactively to reduce and prevent serious harm. 8. In Hong Kong, our second Money-laundering and Terrorist-financing (ML/TF) risk assessment reflects that almost 20,000 deception cases were reported last year, up 24% from over a year ago. About 60% of fraud cases originated outside Hong Kong, mainly online fraud and accounting for a much larger share of proceeds than domestic cases. 9. This trend is global; according to a paper discussed at the recent Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Plenary meeting, one estimate indicates that unauthorised credit card transactions, identity theft and cyber fraud are the most prevalent crime in the UK, costing up to GBP190 billion a year; in the US, US6.1 billion was reported in losses related to internet crime last year; and in Singapore, cyber-enabled fraud cases increased to about 52% of all reported crime last year from 42% the year before. We have similar observations: credit card fraud, phishing instant messages and investment scams involving remittance have topped the list of fraud-related complaints against banks handled by the HKMA. 10. These shared experiences show that cyber-enabled crime is complex and the proceeds often move across borders. We therefore welcome the announcement by the incoming President that the FATF would build on current work on digital transformation to further explore contemporary money-laundering and terrorist- financing risks associated with cross-border, cyber-enabled crimes, including those concerning virtual assets. 11. We at the HKMA, in collaboration with our partners both domestically and overseas, are committed to doing our part. 12. The thrust behind the FATF proposals is that tackling economic crime is a shared mission, beyond the capacity of individual agencies or jurisdictions. Only by enabling stakeholders to work collaboratively across the entire AML eco-system, powered by data and technology, can we deliver improved outcomes. 13. One area that we are particularly keen to explore further is how the policy and regulatory framework can enable capacity in the system to be released from low- value activities, and refocussed where it can have the greatest impact against priority threats. 14. Information and intelligence sharing partnerships are hugely important in this context, and in the last five years or so, have made great progress across the Asian region. Take for example the Fraud and Money Laundering Intelligence Taskforce, or FMLIT, in Hong Kong. Since its establishment in 2017, the HKMA has been an active participant collaborating with a number of major retail banks, to share information and intelligence on fraud and other financial crime. This forum has been extremely effective in delivering the right data that presents better opportunities for banks to stop the harm of financial crime faster. 15. Title: Remarks after the US Fed FOMC Meeting
text: IIONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY f o  w x Speeches 22 Sep 2022 Remarks after the US Fed FOMC Meeting Eddie Yue, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) of the Federal Reserve (the Fed) announced a rate hike of 75 basis points at the early hours today (Hong Kong time) after its two-day meeting, raising the target range for the federal funds rate to 3-3.25%. The HKMA has adjusted the Base Rate upward by 75 basis points to 3.5% according to the established mechanism with immediate effect. 2. Since March, the Fed has raised the federal funds target range five times by a total of 300 basis points. It announced a 75-basis-point hike this time, which is generally in line with market expectation. According to the latest dot plot, the Fed will continue to hike rate to bring down the high inflation in the US. The pace of its future rate hikes would be dependent on the economic outlook and data. 3. In fact, apart from the Fed, various major central banks around the world are also tightening their monetary policies. Coupled with factors such as geopolitical risks, CO VID development, high inflation and slowing economic growth, the global macro environment is becoming increasingly complex, and risks to the global financial markets are growing. 4. Notwithstanding the highly volatile external environment, Hong Kongs monetary and financial markets continue to remain stable. The foreign exchange market has been operating in a smooth and orderly manner. The Linked Exchange Rate System (LERS) has also continued to work well. The weak-side Convertibility Undertaking (CU) has been triggered multiple times between May and early August. Under the LERS, the HKMA bought Hong Kong dollars and sold US dollars according to the mechanism. The Aggregate Balance shrank as a result, giving the Hong Kong dollar interbank rates more momentum to rise, thus offsetting the incentives for carry trades, and this would stabilise the Hong Kong dollar within the 7.75-7.85 range. As I explained before on various occasions, this adjustment process is entirely within the design and expectations of the LERS. 5. As the Fed continues to tighten its monetary policy, the Hong Kong dollar and US dollar interest rate differentials, particularly the short-term rates, might widen again. This would incentivise market participants to conduct carry trades, which will result in the triggering of the weak-side CU again. The speed and magnitude for the Hong Kong dollar interbank rates to catch up with their US dollar counterparts will ultimately be subject to the supply and demand of the Hong Kong dollar funding in the local market. Having said that, the public should be prepared for the Hong Kong dollar interbank rates to rise further. The Hong Kong dollar interbank rates have been rising gradually since early this year. With the continued rate hikes by the Fed, this trend is expected to continue. 6. On the commercial interest rates of banks, banks will decide on the timing and magnitude of adjusting them having regard to banks own funding cost structures and other relevant considerations. As the Hong Kong dollar interbank rates gradually track the US dollar interbank rates, we notice that some banks have already raised the interest rate cap of newly approved mortgage loans. The Fed has already raised interest rates multiple times, and the market expects it to continue to do so in the remaining FOMC meetings this year. Against this backdrop, banks in Hong Kong will very likely raise the deposit and lending interest rates, including the best lending rates. The public should be prepared for banks to increase the commercial interest rates, and carefully assess and manage the relevant risks when making property purchase, mortgage or other borrowing decisions. 7. The HKMA will continue to closely monitor market situations with a view to maintaining monetary and financial stability. Last revision date : 22 September 2022

Title: Regulatory Keynote Address at "XLoD Global 2022" : Sound bank culture:  The fundamental key to managing conduct risk
text: Speeches HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY # Si W 3 M 16 Nov 2022 Regulatory Keynote Address at "XLoD Global 2022": Sound bank culture: The fundamental key to managing conduct risk Alan Au, Executive Director (Banking Conduct), Hong Kong Monetary Authority Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, 1. First of all, I would like to thank 1 LoD for inviting me again to address this year's "XLoD Global". I am very delighted to share with you all our thoughts and actions on managing conduct risks, which have always been deep in our mind. Managing Conduct Risks 2. Since the Global Financial Crisis in 2008, managing conduct risk has become more important than ever for both supervisors and banks. It is rather clear to everyone that hard rules and codified requirements can only serve as the bottom line when we talk about bank culture and behavior of financial practitioners. Then what are the real drivers behind? And what are the root causes of poor conduct? 3. In the promotion of sound risk culture in the banking industry, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) emphasises that there is no single "sound" culture that is applicable to all banks. And we encourage banks to foster a sound culture through focusing on three pillars: strong governance; appropriate incentive systems and effective assessment and feedback mechanism. Today, I would like to focus on two important pieces in play in shaping the culture of a financial institution - the incentive system and consequence mechanisms of frontline staff. Focused Review on Incentive Systems 4. Incentive systems have to be fit for purpose. Given the sensitive and proprietary nature of incentive systems, banks generally are unable to share and compare their incentive practices, needless to say how to assess what incentive practices are more effective in driving desired staff behaviour. With these in mind, the HKMA conducted a Focused Review to deep dive into the incentive systems of front offices in 20 retail banks in Hong Kong, in order to provide some useful benchmarking reference to the industry. 5. As you can imagine, this was a very large scale industry-wide culture exercise ever conducted in the Hong Kong banking industry, which comprised our first ever industry- wide employee survey, as well as a range of other activities including focus group discussions and individual interviews. The review aims to gauge the inner true voice of the frontline staff who interact with bank customers on a daily basis, and to identify observations common in the industry, plus useful incentive design principles and practices. 6. Let me share with you some very interesting observations. One of which is that good tt _ . _ w j. _ rr ........................................................................... cusiomer outcomes are onen interpreiea Dy Tronmne stan as cusiomer sansiacuon . When speaking of "customer outcome", one may immediately think about how satisfied a customer would feel right after the selling process, for example, whether a customer walked away with a smiley face and thumbs up. But if you think deeper: this "happiness" should not be conveniently taken as good customer outcome. In fact, good customer outcome should focus on, among others, whether customers are provided with accurate and sufficient information, and whether the products or services provided to the customers indeed suit their needs. Imagine, if a frontline staff wants to keep a customer happy by skipping all the due diligence procedures, so as to complete a transaction very quickly to save the customer's time, it calls into the question whether the products or services would really suit the customer's need. And consequences would come later when the market conditions turn sour. 7. Another interesting observation is about perception of importance of business achievement. An area that banks have been putting a great deal of effort in the past few years is reducing the weight of financial performance in incentive systems. It was found in the Review that banks' leaders generally consider that the incentive systems are now quite balanced between financial and non-financial factors. Yet the Review noted that frontline staff still think that financial achievement is of utmost priority in their performance assessment. This reflects that some other forces may be at work. For example, many bank staff may feel excessive pressure to meet business targets through social recognition of business achievements, and at the same time they may not feel that they are receiving recognition or reward for non-financial performance (such as compliance and customer outcomes). It comes rather clear that financial institutions should be mindful of such perception gap and the need for reality check. 8. The HKMA has published the report of this Review in May this year, and the report is definitely worth a read if you wish to find out more. In addition to industry-wide observations and other interesting insights, we have also devised six useful incentive system design principles and 17 sound incentive practices to reinforce good customer and conduct outcomes. We trust that this industry-wide exercise has provided meaningful and valuable inputs to our banks, as well as other financial institutions. Mandatory Reference Checking Scheme 9. Let me now turn to Mandatory Reference Checking Scheme, another important piece of our bank culture efforts. We realise that regardless of how hard one tries to drive desirable staff behaviour through an appropriate incentive system, we cannot naively assume that staff will always behave with integrity. The phrase "rolling bad apples" literally means that individuals, who have committed misconduct behaviour in one institution, are able to obtain subsequent employment elsewhere without disclosing their earlier misconduct to the new employers. In this manner, misconduct risk is transmitted within the system. Indeed, our peers in a number of jurisdictions have the same aspiration in addressing this phenomenon. But when "bad apples" try to "roll" from one institution to another, this cannot be easily dealt with by individual banks alone. It is important for the banking community to work together to collectively tackle the issue and limit the harm inflicted by the "bad apples" on the system. 10. To this end, I am happy to see that the Hong Kong banking industry has been working closely with the HKMA over the past two years, and finalised the Mandatory Reference Checking Scheme in May 2022. 11. Under the Scheme, all banks will share and obtain conduct-specific reference information ahout nroRnaotivA amnlovaaR ii.Rinn a common nrotoool tn Riinnnrt informed employment decisions. The protocol will cover seven years of misconduct behaviours, including breaches of legal and regulatory requirements; incidents which cast serious doubt on honesty and integrity; internal or external disciplinary actions as well as ongoing internal investigations relating to misconduct matters. 12. We understand that some banks may have concerns about reporting ongoing investigations, for fear of litigation risks. But we don't want to create a potential loophole such that "bad apples" could just get around the Scheme by leaving one bank to join another once an investigation commences. To strike a balance, the industry guidelines set out factors that banks should take into account when exercising judgement on whether or not to share information about ongoing internal investigations. To ensure transparent and fair treatment to the job applicants, they will be provided with an opportunity to be heard in case of any negative information. 13. Phase 1 of the Scheme covering senior positions will formally start in May 2023 after one year of preparatory work. We look forward to collaborating with the banking industry to ensure smooth implementation of the Scheme. Closing remarks 14. Ladies and gentlemen, bank culture plays a pivotal role in driving staff behavior, and thus fostering a sound culture is the fundamental key to addressing conduct risk. We have invested a lot over the past few years to promote sound bank culture. We trust that our culture efforts including the Focused Review and the Mandatory Reference Checking Scheme would set an important milestone in the bank culture development in Hong Kong. 15. I would like to thank 1 LoD again for inviting me to talk about our perspective on bank culture today. And I hope very much my remarks will inspire you all to continue your investments in culture of your institutions. 16. Thank you very much. Last revision date : 16 November 2022

Title: Keynote Speech at the Annual Conference of Financial Street Forum 2022 (Chinese version)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  Speeches November 22, 2022 Keynote speech at the 2022 Financial Street Forum Annual Conference David Lee is the Deputy Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Start the development engine of financial technology and embark on a journey of financial service innovation Distinguished leaders, organizers, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen,  Hello everyone! Thank you very much for the invitation, and I am very pleased to be able to participate in this annual meeting of the Financial Street Forum, and meet with all friends through video to discuss the development of financial technology and financial service innovation.  The National 14th Five-Year Plan positions Hong Kong as the country's international financial centre and supports Hong Kong's development into an international innovation and technology centre. At the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China last month, President Xi Jinping also made it clear that he would support Hong Kong's economic development, promote Hong Kong's long-term prosperity and stability, and better integrate into the overall development of the country.  All of the above have set clear development goals for Hong Kong. In the future, we will pursue development in three major directions: 1. consolidate Hong Kong's inherent advantages; 2. Promote the next generation of infrastructure and services at full speed; 3. Actively explore the development of digital finance. In the future, I&T will be an important engine of economic development. We will vigorously promote the development of fintech and promote innovation in financial services, while increasing productivity and taking economic development to the next level. - Consolidate Hong Kong's inherent advantages  As the international financial centre of the motherland, Hong Kong has always given full play to its unique advantages and served as a springboard for the motherland to connect with the rest of the world. In terms of inward and outward direct investment in the motherland, two-thirds of it is made through Hong Kong. Under the Stock Connect, the stock and bond markets are very active and trading is booming, and international investors currently hold A-shares More than 70% of them are invested through Stock Connect. As a gateway between the Motherland and the rest of the world, Hong Kong will continue to invest in new efforts to deepen the mutual access mechanism, including the upcoming launch of Swap Connect to help international investors holding Mainland bonds manage interest rate risk.  Hong Kong is also Asia's leading bond hub, accounting for one-third of the region's issuance in arranging international and Mainland offshore bond issuances. In terms of green bonds, Hong Kong's market is booming, with more than US34 billion of offshore green and sustainable bonds issued by mainland enterprises last year, of which about US25 billion was arranged in Hong Kong. Hong Kong will seize the opportunity We will make every effort to meet the green bond issuance needs of Hong Kong and mainland enterprises and contribute to the country's green transformation.  Three weeks ago, the International Financial Leaders' Investment Summit was successfully held in Hong Kong, and about 120 leaders of international financial institutions came to Hong Kong from all over the world to get first-hand information on the global financial market. We will consolidate our advantages, make use of them, and seek greater development. 2. Promote the next generation of infrastructure and services at full speed  Innovation in financial services requires the support of a new generation of infrastructure. Looking forward to the future, we must not hesitate to make every effort to promote the new generation of financial infrastructure projects, effectively alleviate the pain points faced by the market, realize capital and information integration, and contribute to the development of the real economy.  One of the key points is to enhance the functionality of Faster Payment System (FPS). This fast payment system was launched in 2018 and currently It remains the world's only dual-currency, real-time transfer system that connects all bank and e-wallet accounts. In the future, FPS will actively explore new territories and explore the possibility of cross-border retail payment, bringing more convenience to users and supporting the vigorous development of economic activities.  In addition to enhancing the payment system, we are also working to build a new data infrastructure, called Commercial Data Interchange (CDI), to make commercial data sharing faster and more secure, and unleash the potential of data. With the launch of the CDI last month, the number of participating banks has increased significantly from eight in the pilot phase to 23, and the number of participating data providers has reached 10, promoting multilateral data sharing and financial innovation. In the next step, we will continue to investigate how to expand the scope of CDI data and actively develop new use cases.  At the same time, we are working hard to marketise and enhance our custodian system, the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU). As the financial markets of Hong Kong and the Mainland enter the new era of "Stock Connect 2.0", the smooth implementation of arrangements such as the Southbound Trading of Bond Connect and Cross-boundary Finance Connect, and the optimisation of CMU infrastructure, we can further meet the investment and financing needs of both domestic and foreign countries On the one hand, it will bring investors to the mainland market, and at the same time, it will also help mainland investors go global, strengthen market ties between the mainland and the mainland, and maintain the competitiveness of Hong Kong's financial industry. 3. Actively explore the development of digital finance  As the country's international financial centre, Hong Kong must be at the forefront of the development of digital finance, keep abreast of the latest situation, and at the same time manage risks well, so as to help the real economy under the premise of ensuring financial security.  In terms of digital currency, the mBridge project has entered the trial stage from the experiment, and is currently the world's largest cross-border central bank digital currency (CBDC) trial, and it is one of the first projects to use a variety of CBDCs to conduct real settlement for cross-border transactions of enterprises, which can be said to be the leading project in the world.  In addition to working closely with the People's Bank of China (PBoC) on the mBridge project, Hong Kong is the first cross-border pilot outside the Mainland for the development of the e-CNY. At present, the relevant technical tests have entered the second stage, and the scope and scale of the tests are vast, and the participating banks have also changed from one to four. Hong Kong will continue to support the development of e-CN in Yanan, promote the interconnection of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, and speed up and improve the efficiency of cross-border payment services.  Through the investment in different projects, we deeply understand that digital finance is indispensable for future development. Therefore, Hong Kong's research work will continue to actively explore digital finance and find the most appropriate development path to ensure that digital finance can fully support the development of the digital economy. epilogue  The potential for technological development is limitless, and I am sure you will agree. As President Xi Jinping has emphasized, we must adhere to the principle that "science and technology are the primary productive forces, talent is the primary resource, and innovation is the primary driving force", seize the opportunity to develop science and technology, drive innovation, attract talents, and create a good cycle in which the three drive each other. Hong Kong will continue to make good use of the support of the motherland, give full play to its own advantages, and lead the full speed of financial technology and overall economic development.  Thank you! Note: The Forum was held on 21 and 23 November 2022 Last revision date: 22 November 2022
