Title: Speech at the Annual Conference of Financial Street Forum 2022 (Chinese version)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  Speeches November 23, 2022 Speech at the 2022 Financial Street Forum Annual Conference Chan Wai-man is the Deputy Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Plenary Session - Cross-border Capital Flows and New Trends in Cross-border Investment Distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, and hello everyone! Thank you for the invitation to participate in the 2022 Financial Street Forum Annual Conference. I would like to take this opportunity to share some of our observations on cross-border capital flows and some development trends from the perspective of Hong Kong as an international financial center, as well as some of Hong Kong's priorities in promoting the orderly flow of capital across borders under the new situation. Changing financial conditions  First, let's talk about the big picture. The global investment environment has changed dramatically in recent times. In just over two years, financial markets have rapidly reversed from an extremely loose monetary policy environment to a recently tightened monetary policy. At the same time, geopolitical and regional conflicts have made the international situation more complex and volatile, and the new crown epidemic is still affecting economic and social development to varying degrees, and many major economies are facing a pattern of high inflation and low growth. The combination of all these factors exacerbates the volatility of financial markets and affects the flow of cross-border capital.  We have our sights set on the Asia-Pacific region. Asia has benefited from a global low-interest rate environment for quite some time, but the situation has reversed since last year. Inflationary pressures in the region's economies have risen as global commodity prices have risen sharply and supply bottlenecks persisted. Many central banks in the region need to tighten monetary policy to deal with inflationary pressures, but the path of monetary policy normalization is relatively modest, with interest rate differentials driving outflows from the region's bond markets and varying degrees of currency depreciation. The mainland's economic tone is sound, and there is room for monetary and fiscal policies to support economic stability and growth, but there will still be some uncertainty about short-term cross-border capital flows amid widening interest rate differentials between China and the United States and the economy still facing some challenges. Cross-border capital flows from a Hong Kong perspective  Hong Kong's real economy and financial market are highly open to the outside world, and it is also a gateway between the mainland and the world, and the financial platform brings together market participants from all over the world, including the mainland. Because of these characteristics, our market is relatively sensitive to global political and economic changes and cross-border capital flows. In the face of a complex and volatile situation, it is all the more important to maintain the stability of Hong Kong's financial system and enhance the resilience of the market. Over the past few years, Hong Kong's financial system has remained stable and sustained despite drastic changes in external markets and volatile capital flows. In general, we have the following observations: First, cross-border capital flows fluctuate and the exchange rate system operates in an orderly manner: similar to the trend of capital flows in the region, Hong Kong's stock market has fallen since the United States entered the interest rate hike cycle. At the same time, driven by interest rate differentials, funds flowed out of the Hong Kong dollar system. The Hong Kong dollar has been on the weak side against the US dollar since May this year. Of course, this phenomenon is in line with the design and expectation of the linked exchange rate system. Therefore, despite the outflow of funds out of the Hong Kong dollar, the market maintains a high level of confidence in the Linked Exchange Rate System, which plays an important role in maintaining Hong Kong's financial stability. Second, financing activities have shown a cyclical decline, but there are still new bright spots in the market: rising US dollar interest rates and volatile market conditions have affected financing and trading activities in Hong Kong's stock and bond markets to a certain extent. The overall lending activity of banks in Hong Kong has been basically flat since the beginning of this year, and the banking system is sound, with various indicators such as liquidity, capital adequacy ratio and asset quality remaining at a healthy level. At the same time, the rising cost of US dollar financing has provided an incentive for institutions and enterprises in the region to switch from US dollars to local currencies for financing. In Hong Kong, offshore renminbi financing activities have steadily increased over the past year or so. A notable example is that dim sum bond issuance reached RMB110 billion in 2021, an increase of 87% over 2020. On this basis, the issuance volume in the first 10 months of this year has exceeded RMB100 billion, the highest since 2014. Hong Kong continued to play an important role in facilitating cross-border capital flows between the two countries: Northbound trading under Stock Connect recorded overall net inflows in the first three quarters of this year, with average daily trading remaining at a relatively high level of over RMB100 billion. At present, more than 70% of the A-shares held by international investors are invested through the Northbound Scheme. At the same time, the average daily trading volume of Southbound Stock Connect remained at RMB24 billion. On Bond Connect, the average daily trading volume of Northbound Trading has reached a record high since its launch so far this year, with more than half of international investors' onshore bond trading through Northbound Trading. Southbound trading has also been running smoothly since its launch in September last year, and the market has responded positively. From financial stability to financial development  These figures reflect the soundness and resilience of Hong Kong's financial markets. Even in the face of changes in the global political and economic situation and turbulent financial markets, Hong Kong still provides a reliable and efficient financial platform for market participants. However, how to control market fluctuations and find new opportunities from them is a test for investors, financial institutions, enterprises, and other market players. Similarly, it is also a challenging task for policymakers to ensure financial security and stability in the face of the current market environment, while at the same time creating a favorable market environment and formulating policies that meet the needs of the market to promote development.  Over the years, Hong Kong has experienced ups and downs in economic cycles, short-term market fluctuations, various financial crises and various socio-economic challenges, but under the protection of "one country, two systems", with the strong support of the Mainland, and combined with its own advantages, Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre has been continuously consolidated and enhanced. On this solid foundation, we must also be soberly aware of the need to continuously enhance the competitiveness of financial centers. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has taken proactive measures to adapt to market development trends and needs, continuously optimize the market environment and policy support, create more development opportunities for domestic and foreign market participants, and provide better conditions for promoting cross-border investment in an orderly manner. I would like to focus on three aspects of work. The first is to vigorously promote the development of offshore RMB business in Hong Kong, so that market players can use RMB for financial transactions more smoothly, and also give them more diversified options for RMB financial investment and risk management. We are optimising the development of Hong Kong's offshore renminbi market in three aspects. The first is to improve offshore RMB liquidity: The People's Bank of China (PBoC) and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) established a standing currency swap arrangement in July this year and significantly increased the swap quota to RMB800 billion, which will help provide more stable liquidity support for the Hong Kong market. The HKMA has also enhanced the RMB liquidity facility provided to banks to provide liquidity protection to increase various offshore RMB activities and develop more RMB products. Another point is to promote the diversification of RMB products: the deepening of the Stock Connect mechanism provides foreign investors with a diversified choice of RMB assets. To meet the needs of international investors to manage their risk, we aim to launch Swap Connect in the near future to assist international investors in managing the interest rate risk of investing in onshore renminbi bonds. At the same time, we are also stepping up preparations for the use of renminbi in Hong Kong stock trading, and strive for more onshore and foreign institutions to issue renminbi bonds in Hong Kong. The recent successful issuance of offshore renminbi bonds by the Hainan and Shenzhen municipal governments in Hong Kong is a good example. In addition, upgrading the financial market infrastructure is also one of the key points to consolidate Hong Kong's offshore RMB business hub, and one of the most important tasks is to upgrade the CMU Central Moneymarkets System (CMU) and develop it into a major central securities depository platform in Asia to better support cross-border clearing, transaction settlement and custody of RMB. The second aspect is to follow the trend of green finance and fintech, and strive to promote Hong Kong's financial ecosystem to be at the forefront and promote the vigorous development of financial innovation. In terms of green finance development, Hong Kong's traditional advantage as a bridge can attract international capital to participate in the process of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality in the Mainland, and contribute to the country's green transformation. In recent years, Hong Kong has made breakthroughs in green and sustainable finance, becoming the preferred destination for green financing in Asia. In 2021, for example, a record US57 billion was allocated to international green bond issuance and bank green loans in Hong Kong, with 80% of the green bonds issued by mainland institutions, mainly to finance green projects on the mainland. On the Fintech front, the HKMA's Fintech 2025 Strategy, announced last year, has seen fruition so far. For example, the cross-border central bank digital currency (CBDC) recently entered a pilot phase, with a number of banks from the Mainland, Hong Kong, Thailand and the U.A.E. participating and successfully conducting cross-border real settlements. At the same time, we are also conducting technical tests in Hong Kong for cross-border use of e-CNY and preparing to connect retail payment systems in Hong Kong with Thailand. Through these different projects, we are actively exploring the use of technology to open up more efficient, lower-cost, safer and more reliable cross-border payment channels for enterprises and individuals in the field of payment. The third aspect is to strengthen market ties and promotion. The role of the financial center is to serve the market. In recent years, Hong Kong has experienced multiple trials and challenges, which has made us realize the importance of maintaining market confidence. Therefore, we have strengthened our work of market liaison and contacted market participants and heads of financial institutions at home and abroad in different forms, so that they can have a more comprehensive and accurate understanding of the situation in Hong Kong, a deeper grasp of the development opportunities that Hong Kong and the mainland can provide, and an understanding of the challenges and pain points they may encounter in their development in Hong Kong, and do our best to reflect, respond to and solve them. At the same time, we are also in close communication with the relevant regulatory authorities in the Mainland to create more policy space for connecting the flow of capital between the Mainland and the world in an orderly and steady manner, and implement good policies. epilogue  Ladies and gentlemen, financial stability and financial development are inseparable from the two keywords of financial stability and financial development to provide a stable environment for the market to adapt to changes in cross-border capital flows and for them to find new opportunities in the new trend of cross-border investment. The stability of Hong Kong's financial market is not only the foundation for Hong Kong's continuous development as an international financial centre, but also the key to Hong Kong's continued role as a "firewall" in the Mainland's financial opening-up. In the current market environment where risks and opportunities coexist, Hong Kong will continue to strengthen its role as an international financial centre connecting the Mainland and the rest of the world in the spirit of putting stability first and seeking progress while maintaining stability.  Finally, I wish this forum a success. Thank you! Note: The Forum was held on 21 and 23 November 2022 Last revision date: 23 November 2022

Title: Speech at the Bund Summit 2022 (Chinese version)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  Speeches December 09, 2022 Speech at the 4th Bund Finance Summit David Lee is the Deputy Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority The Bund Roundtable: Financial Market Interconnection and Two-way Opening Dear guests, ladies and gentlemen, hello everyone!  Thank you for the invitation and it is my pleasure to participate in the 4th Bund Finance Summit and share with you the unique role of Hong Kong as an international financial centre in the opening up of the Mainland's financial market, as well as some of the key points of future work in promoting cross-border capital flows and the development of the offshore RMB market.  With the rapid growth of China's economy, the opening up of the mainland's financial market has also been continuously improved. The inclusion of renminbi assets in major global indices and the increase in the weight of renminbi in the Special Drawing Rights basket by the International Monetary Fund fully reflect the confidence of international investors in China's long-term economic growth. However, compared with China's economic strength, there is still a lot of room for development in the degree of participation of international investors in the mainland financial market and the internationalization of the renminbi. In order to maintain the smooth two-way flow of cross-border capital and promote the internationalization of the RMB in an orderly manner, China needs to continue to expand the opening up of the financial market. Hong Kong's role in the opening up of China's financial markets  China's 14th Five-Year Plan clearly defines Hong Kong as an international financial centre and a global offshore RMB business hub. In his report to the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, President Xi Jinping also stressed the support for Hong Kong to continue to leverage its advantages and characteristics, consolidate and enhance its position in international finance and other fields, and better integrate into the overall development of the country. In fact, Hong Kong has been a reliable "testing ground" for the Mainland's financial opening-up for many years  In the following, I will share how Hong Kong has contributed to the liberalisation of China's financial market and the internationalisation of the renminbi from four aspects: (1) current account facilitation, (8) capital account liberalisation, (iii) financial infrastructure development, and (iv) convergence of market mechanism arrangements with international practices.  In the early days of RMB internationalisation, all RMB settlement services were piloted in Hong Kong. The launch of the cross-border RMB trade settlement pilot in Hong Kong in 2009 was a major breakthrough in the use of RMB overseas. In 2021, the amount of RMB trade settlements processed by Hong Kong banks exceeded RMB7 trillion, a record high.  With the orderly liberalization of the capital account in the Mainland, Hong Kong's key role in the two-way flow of capital has been further strengthened. As one of the first batch of QFII and RQFI investors, Hong Kong institutions have taken the lead in bringing more overseas long-term funds to the Mainland financial market. The mutual access mechanism between the two financial markets has also facilitated the inclusion of Mainland stocks and bonds in major international indices. At the same time, Hong Kong institutions assist high-quality bond issuers such as provincial and municipal governments in the Mainland to raise funds in the offshore market, promote the development of the country's real economy, and enrich offshore RMB bond products.  Hong Kong also plays a key role in improving the offshore RMB financial infrastructure to enhance the efficiency and security of cross-border RMB business. At present, about 70% of global RMB cross-border payments are processed through the Hong Kong Renminbi Real Time Gross Settlement System (RTGS). In addition, about 80% of the transactions processed through Hong Kong's renminbi RTGS system are between offshore markets.  Thanks to Bond Connect, Hong Kong's Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) has successfully leveraged its unique advantages in connecting the Mainland and the rest of the world to expand its business scale and influence. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has launched a three-year plan to comprehensively upgrade CMU's system services This will better support the connectivity between the Mainland and the international financial markets.  Being familiar with the Mainland and connecting with the rest of the world is Hong Kong's unique advantage. In China, we refer to the experience of the international market and deepen the process of financial reform Hong Kong has always played the role of a "firewall". For example, by strengthening the connection between the financial infrastructure of the two places, Bond Connect has introduced a multi-level custody model for the mainland bond market while maintaining regulatory penetration, which has greatly increased the willingness of international investors to participate. Further deepen the opening up of the financial market  Nevertheless, there is still room for improvement in the openness of the Mainland's financial markets and the facilitation of business operations. Hong Kong will continue to leverage its advantages to further deepen the mutual access between the financial markets of the Mainland and Hong Kong. Here are our priorities for the future.  On current account facilitation, under the new format of the Mainland's foreign trade, we will maintain communication with the industry to understand the needs of banking and corporate customers, so as to ensure the sustainable development of the relevant business in the ever-changing market, and further promote the use of RMB in cross-border real economic activities.  For capital account opening, we will continue to enhance the Stock Connect mechanism, such as adding renminbi stock trading counters to the Southbound Stock Connect, expanding the scope of eligible products under the Cross-boundary Wealth Management Connect, and taking forward the development of the Insurance Connect. We will continue to explore the provision of more offshore risk management tools for overseas investors and promote the further opening up of the onshore derivatives market, so as to enhance the confidence of international investors in holding RMB assets for a long time.  We will continue to enhance our financial infrastructure and facilitate Bond Connect access to the Mainland exchange's bond market. Establish cross-border connectivity with securities custody platforms in more regions to strengthen the connection between the Mainland and the international market; Make good use of the standing currency swap agreement between the HKMA and the People's Bank of China (PBoC) to enhance the offshore RMB liquidity facility and enhance the operational efficiency of the RMB RTGS system.  In addition, the HKMA will continue to take forward the Multilateral Central Bank Digital Currency Bridge (i.e. mBridge) project to promote the cross-border application of e-RMB. mBridge is the largest cross-border CBDC pilot to date, and is expected to provide a low-cost and fast payment method for international trade settlement. In the long run, it will help deepen the two-way cross-border flow of capital and facilitate the internationalization of the RMB.  Finally, in terms of promoting the integration of the Mainland's market mechanism arrangements with international standards, the implementation of Swap Connect will help further promote the application of the ISDA Master Agreement in the Mainland and promote the enhancement of the Mainland's derivatives delivery and clearing mechanism. In addition, foreign investors' acceptance of Mainland credit bonds needs to be improved. Hong Kong can actively promote the integration of the Mainland's credit bond and related derivatives markets with international standards. For example, Hong Kong's regulatory mechanism for rating agencies is relatively well-established, and the credit event handling system is relatively mature, which can provide a reference for the construction of relevant standards in the Mainland and enhance the international recognition of the Mainland market. summary  In the face of complex internal and external situations, Hong Kong's financial system has remained stable and its linkage with the mainland has been strengthened. This fully reflects the vitality of Hong Kong. As an international financial centre and offshore renminbi centre, Hong Kong will continue to promote the coordinated development of the capital markets of the two places, deepen the mutual access between the domestic and overseas markets, and strengthen its role as a "testing ground" and "firewall".  Thank you! Last revision date: 09 December 2022

Title: Opening Remarks at Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Seminar 2022
text: @IIONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  & Si a M Speeches 15 Dec 2022 Opening Remarks at Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Seminar 2022 Carmen Chu, Executive Director (Enforcement and AML), Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. 2. It is my great pleasure to welcome you all to our AML seminar. This is an important part of our engagement with subject matter experts at banks, sharing our in-year review and 2023 outlook. 3. We continue to face a very challenging environment: a downturn in the global economy, rising fraud and financial crime, complex geopolitical developments, to name a few. These bring into sharp focus the need for banks to be agile, effective and risk- based in their essential role as gatekeepers of the AML ecosystem, helping safeguard the stability and integrity of the financial system. 4. During the year, there have been a number of developments to empower banks to drive more effective AML outcomes. Let me highlight three key aspects. 5. First, legislation and regulation. Changes have just been made to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance to align with the latest international standards and practices, including a new licensing regime for Virtual Asset Service Providers. On a related note, the HKMA adopts a risk-based approach to supervising banks interface with VA activities, based on the principle of same risk, same regulation. 6. The technical definition of Politically Exposed Persons has also been amended in line with the international standard, while a new concept of former PEP has also been adopted to allow a risk-based approach when determining the extent of customer due diligence based on identified risk in individual circumstances. We are now in the process of engaging consultancy services to assist with a review of international best practices to inform a risk-based, and practical guidance for banks to meet their ODD obligations in relation to PEPs. Also, the HKMA will soon consult the banking sector on changes to the AML/CFT Guideline in preparation for the legislative amendment to take effect next June. 7. The second focus concerns AML Suptech and Regtech. The latest legislative update clarifies that a recognised digital identification system such as iAM Smart can satisfy additional requirements where a customer is not physically present. This is important, as more than 90% of retail banks in Hong Kong have launched remote customer onboarding services, or are actively planning to do so. 8. And over the past year, three AMLab sessions have been held, bringing together banks, technology firms and data experts to experiment with network analytics capabilities and enabling technologies. With the wider adoption of AML Regtech, banks have significantly increased the identification and reporting of suspicious accounts and networks, leading to more timely restraint of criminal proceeds by law enforcement agencies. 9. The HKMA has also recently started its own pilot on the application of data analytics using granular financial crime data across multiple banks for the first time. The objective is to make our AML supervisory work more data-driven, and thus more timely in identifying risk displacement, and preventing serious harm from mule account networks used for fraud and financial crime. 10. Thirdly, the importance of an ecosystem response is increasingly recognised globally. In Hong Kong, financial institutions, government bureaux, regulators and law enforcement agencies are all collaborating closely through public-private partnership for information sharing, as well as engagement sessions like this one. It is a joint effort by all stakeholders of the AML ecosystem to prevent, detect and disrupt the abuse of the financial system for illicit fund flows. At the same time, we will keep demonstrating the value of AML work in protecting members of the public and reducing losses from fraud and financial crime. 11. We are very pleased that the Commerce and Economic Development Bureau will join todays programme to share the latest guidance on proliferation financing risk assessment and mitigation, drawing reference to the international standards. The HKMA will elaborate the risk-based approach to source of wealth requirements, based on observations noted through its supervision and various engagement sessions with private banks. It is also our honour to have the Financial Intelligence and Investigation Bureau providing feedback on Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR). This is very relevant topic for banks which contributed over 80% of STRs in Hong Kong, similar to banks in other international financial centres. 12. Last but not least, I would like to thank our speakers again for being so generous in sharing their expert views. The presentation materials will also be uploaded to our training platform to reach out to the widest audience in banks. I hope you will find todays seminar interesting, informative and insightful. Thank you. Last revision date : 15 December 2022

Title: Remarks after the US Fed FOMC Meeting
text: IIONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY # Mi W 3 M Speeches 02 Feb 2023 Remarks after the US Fed FOMC Meeting Eddie Yue, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) of the Federal Reserve (the Fed) announced a rate hike of 25 basis points at the early hours today (Hong Kong time) after its two-day meeting, raising the target range for the federal funds rate to 4.5- 4.75%. The HKMA has adjusted the Base Rate upward to 5% according to the established mechanism with immediate effect. 2. Since March last year, the Fed has raised interest rates consecutively by a total of 450 basis points. The pace of rate hike has further moderated since the last rate decision. This reflects the need for the Fed to more carefully assess the US economic and inflationary trends, as well as the effect of previous rate hikes, in determining the magnitude and pacing of future hikes. 3. Rate hikes in the US will not affect the financial and monetary stability of Hong Kong. Our monetary and financial markets continue to operate in a smooth and orderly manner. The Linked Exchange Rate System (LERS) and the automatic interest rate adjustment mechanism under the LERS also continue to work well. The mechanism is well understood by the market, which continues to have strong confidence in the LERS. 4. The rate hike cycle in the US has not yet been completed. The Hong Kong dollar interbank rates might remain at elevated levels for some time. Therefore, the public should be prepared for the likelihood that banks lending rates may go further higher, and should carefully assess and manage the relevant risks when making property purchase, taking out mortgage or making other borrowing decisions. 5. The HKMA will continue to closely monitor market situation and maintain monetary and financial stability in Hong Kong. Last revision date : 02 February 2023

Title: Keynote speech at the ICMA The Asian International Bond Markets: Development and Trends Report Launch Event
text: @IIONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  & Si a M Speeches 30 Mar 2023 Keynote speech at the ICMA The Asian International Bond Markets: Development and Trends Report Launch Event Darryl Chan, Deputy Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority Bryan, Mushtaq, Andy, Distinguished panellists, Ladies and gentlemen: 1. Good afternoon. 2. It is a great pleasure to join you today for presentation of the latest ICMA report on Asias international bond markets. 3. On behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, let me first congratulate ICMA on another year of success in publishing this report. I would also like to thank their dedicated efforts in keeping us abreast of the important trends and developments in the regional bond market. 4. This is the third year that ICMA publishes this report. After two years of virtual presentations, I am very excited to see this event taking place physically for the first time. 5. The year 2022 was a difficult year for the global bond market. Market sentiment was affected by rising inflation and interest rates, uncertain macro-economic outlook, and heightened geopolitical tensions. The Asia market was no exception. In line with the global trend, the annual issuance volume of international bonds in the region declined by more than 40% in 2022, back to the 2015 level. 6. Despite all these challenges, there have been a number of bright spots as highlighted in the report. 7. First is the continued growth in green and sustainable finance in Asia, and the resilience of the green segment relative to the broader market slow down last year. 8. More specifically, as a proportion of overall issuances, green and sustainable issuances notably increased to 23%, from 16% in the previous year. Geographically, the uptake was broad-based. An increased proportion of green issuances was observed in Mainland China, South Korea, India, Malaysia as well as Hong Kong. 9. Second is the continued impetus to the regional market from Chinese offshore issuances. Notwithstanding the challenges to the Chinese real estate sector in the past two years, China remained the largest source of international issuance in Asia. 10. As the ICMA report has suggested, a number of factors have contributed to the significant growth in international issuance by Chinese issuers over the years, namely, to cater for overseas operational and financing needs, to diversify fundraising channels, and to broaden the investor reach. 11. More recently we start to see the footprint of local government issuers. The governments of the Shenzhen municipality and Hainan province debuted their offshore bond issuances during 2021 and 2022 respectively. 12. The investor base is also growing. With Bond Connect extending from Northbound to Southbound, the offshore market is opened up as an alternative channel to reach onshore investors. 13. Hong Kong has a natural edge in arranging these Chinese issuances. This put us at the top spot, for 7 consecutive years including 2022, in terms of arranging Asias international issuances. We arranged one-third of the regions overall issuances, as well as green issuances. 14. The regional bond market has started the year of 2023 with much improved sentiment. Here in Hong Kong, the Government came to market in the very first week of January with the largest ESG bond issuance in Asia. The bonds were well received by global investors. 15. We are mindful that the market will continue to face uncertainties. Just in recent weeks, events in the banking sector sent shock waves across the global capital markets. And market participants need to stay vigilant. 16. At the same time, it is equally important that we position ourselves well for opportunities that may arise. 17. One key development is digitalisation. The ICMA report highlights the accelerating and mainstreaming of technology adoption in Asias bond markets. Indeed, in recent years both the public and private sectors have done digital bond projects of varying scale to explore how distributed ledger technology (or DLT) may enhance market efficiencies. 18. In Hong Kong, we also did our first tokenized government green bond issuance last month, which was also the first of its kind globally. It proves our capacity in providing a flexible and favourable legal and regulatory environment for innovative forms of bond issuance. Reflecting on the experience gained through this issuance, we are engaging with market participants to map out the next steps of the project. 19. With that, we look forward to hearing ICMAs key findings and the panelists' insightful sharing. 20. Thank you ICMA, and once again congratulations on the launch of the report. I wish you all a fruitful event ahead. Last revision date : 30 March 2023

Title: Keynote Speech at 2023 Annual Conference of China Society for Finance & Banking / China Monetary & Financial Forum (Chinese version)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  Speeches 04.04.2023 Keynote speech at the 2023 Annual Conference of the China Society for Finance and Banking and the Annual Conference of the China Finance Forum Eddie Yue, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Make good use of Hong Kong's advantages as a financial centre to support the Mainland's financial reform and opening up Dear President Yi Jiao, distinguished guests, hello everyone!  Thank you for the invitation of the Institute of Financial Research of the People's Bank of China, and it is a great pleasure to gather with all new and old friends in Beijing. I have also benefited a lot from your speeches. I would like to take this opportunity today to talk about how Hong Kong can make good use of its unique advantages as an international financial centre to help the development of the Mainland's financial market, open up to the outside world at a high level, and serve the high-quality development of China's real economy. Historical review  In the historical process of the mainland's financial reform and opening up, Hong Kong has made important contributions. As a bridge between the mainland and the world, we make full use of the international capital market, financial infrastructure and institutional rules to serve as a liaison between mainland enterprises and the international market in the traditional economic and trade fields, and also provide a convenient and efficient overseas fundraising platform for mainland enterprises to promote the rapid development of China's economy.  Hong Kong is the window for attracting investment from the Mainland, with more than 60% of foreign direct investment (FDI) in the Mainland going through Hong Kong. Hong Kong is also a hub and springboard for mainland enterprises to go global, and 60% of the mainland's outward direct investment (ODI) is invested in Hong Kong, or through Hong Kong to other regions.  Relying on Hong Kong's high-quality banking services and mature stock and bond markets, Hong Kong has always been the preferred overseas fundraising platform for mainland enterprises. First of all, Hong Kong's banking sector provides financial support for mainland enterprises' onshore and offshore businesses, and mainland-related loans account for about 40% of Hong Kong's total bank loans. With the development of the mainland's financial industry, Hong Kong has also become a window for Chinese financial institutions to go out and participate in the international market, among which Chinese banks have developed rapidly in Hong Kong in recent years, and the proportion of assets in Hong Kong's banking system has continued to rise.  On the other hand, foreign and Hong Kong banks are also increasing their manpower and resources, using Hong Kong as a base to vigorously expand their business with the Mainland. Taking the stock market as an example, more than half of the companies listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange are mainland enterprises, accounting for about 80% of the total value of the Hong Kong stock market. In recent years, Hong Kong has also been actively enhancing its listing regime to facilitate high-quality technology and technology enterprises to raise funds in Hong Kong, allowing pre-revenue biotech companies to list in Hong Kong, and at the end of last month, a new listing regime for specialist technology companies was introduced. These enhancement measures have opened up overseas financing channels for new science and technology enterprises in the mainland. In addition, Hong Kong is Asia's largest international bond issuance centre, accounting for one-third of the region's bond issuance, with more than 80% of the issuers being Mainland institutions and enterprises  It is worth mentioning that Hong Kong also plays an important role in the orderly liberalization of the Mainland's capital account. Looking back at the introduction of international institutional investors to the Mainland financial market, for example, when launching QFIIs and RQFIIs, Hong Kong institutions were among the first to enter the market, taking the lead in introducing long-term overseas funds to the Mainland financial market. Key work for the future  China's development now stands at a higher historical starting point, and the financial industry will also undertake a new historical mission in the course of modernization. Hong Kong will continue to leverage its advantages as an international financial centre to help the Mainland's financial market better serve the high-quality development of the real economy. Next, I would like to focus on the key work of Hong Kong's future development as an international financial centre, including the financial markets of the two places There are four areas: market connectivity, RMB internationalization, green financing and the development of the Greater Bay Area. Connectivity  The first is to deepen the mutual access mechanism between the financial markets of the two places. With the support and impetus of the central government, especially the relevant regulatory authorities in the Mainland, new breakthroughs have been made in the mutual access between the financial markets of the Mainland and Hong Kong. The launch of Stock Connect in 2014 and Bond Connect in 2017 are both forward-looking and significant initiatives, which are not only the driving force behind the development of Hong Kong's financial market in recent years, but also provide more convenience for international investors to allocate their Mainland stock and bond assets by following international market practices and familiar overseas intermediaries. At present, nearly 70% of the A-share assets of international investors are held through stock connectivity Yes, 60% of transactions in the interbank bond market are conducted through Bond Connect. It can be said that the Stock Connect has greatly enhanced the recognition and participation of international investors in the Mainland financial market, enhanced the international influence of RMB assets, and facilitated the inclusion of Mainland stocks and bonds in major indices in the international market.  Looking ahead, there is still huge room for the Mainland's financial opening-up. At present, foreign holdings account for only 4% of the mainland stock market and less than 3% of the bond market. Further enhancement and expansion of the Stock Connect mechanism, such as providing more risk management tools, will help enhance the depth and breadth of international investors' participation in the Mainland's financial market, thereby enhancing the vitality and international competitiveness of the Mainland's financial market. The two places can focus on the following aspects.  First, the financial regulators of the two places will work closely together to launch Swap Connect Northbound trading as soon as possible. At present, Bond Connect investors still lack effective interest rate risk management tools and can only use offshore RMB swap products for hedging. Investors generally want to enter the onshore interest rate swap market, reduce transaction costs, and also improve their hedging efficiency. If they can enter a more liquid interest rate swap market, they can avoid selling cash bonds when the market is volatile, reduce market volatility, and also contribute to financial stability. The Northbound Trading of the Swap Connect provides them with a safe and convenient channel to enter the market. In the next step, we will also work with mainland regulators to launch offshore treasury bond futures in Hong Kong. And I think we also need to look at how to provide diversified liquidity risk management tools for international investors.  We also hope to expand the investment objective of the Bond Northbound Trading to provide international investors with more comprehensive asset allocation options. At present, international investors mainly allocate interest rate bonds, and nearly two-thirds of foreign fixed income assets in China are concentrated in treasury bonds, and there is great room for improvement in the allocation of credit bonds. After the announcement of the Interbank and Exchange Bond Market Connect Arrangement (i.e. the Stock Connect), foreign investors are paying close attention to the progress. The Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) of the HKMA will actively cooperate with the relevant Mainland authorities to make technical preparations to facilitate foreign investors to gain access to the Mainland's interbank and exchange bond markets through Hong Kong, increase their holdings of credit bonds, and further enhance the level of opening up of the Mainland's bond market.  Of course, we will not ignore the optimization of the existing interconnection mechanism at the technical and operational levels. For example, the CMU will actively implement the two-way automated docking with the Shanghai Clearing House, and will continue to explore with government bond companies to introduce similar enhancement measures to further enhance the settlement efficiency of Bond Connect and facilitate international investors to increase their holdings of Mainland bonds. Internationalization of the renminbi  Another focus of our work is the internationalization of the renminbi. Ladies and gentlemen, Hong Kong's role as an offshore renminbi hub can help the renminbi to be used more broadly internationally. Since the launch of personal RMB banking in 2004 and the completion of the first RMB cross-border trade settlement in 2009, Hong Kong's offshore RMB business has grown steadily over the past 20 years. Hong Kong has the largest offshore RMB liquidity pool, world-leading RMB settlement capabilities, and a mature offshore RMB ecosystem. In 2022, the amount of RMB trade settlement processed by Hong Kong banks has reached RMB9.3 trillion. It can be said that Hong Kong is in a unique position to cooperate with the country to promote the application of RMB in cross-border trade settlement and other real economic activities, and to promote the internationalization of RMB in an orderly manner. The implementation of RCEP and the deepening of cooperation between China and countries in the Gulf region will further enhance the demand for RMB from domestic and foreign enterprises in regional economic activities, and bring new momentum to the internationalization of RMB. Hong Kong will create more favourable conditions for domestic and foreign entities to hold and use RMB in terms of liquidity, products and financial market infrastructure, in particular, to facilitate domestic enterprises to use more local currencies in cross-border transactions and reduce the risk of currency mismatch.  On the liquidity front, the People's Bank of China (PBoC) and the HKMA established a standing currency swap arrangement last year and significantly increased the swap quota to RMB800 billion, further enhancing the stability of RMB liquidity supply in Hong Kong's offshore market.  We are also committed to developing a diversified portfolio of offshore RMB assets so that RMB holders have more investment options Promote the mother 7 Bu Zheng mercury Shi J loss page  1 Shi ffi Ren Shi Fu Zhi Si Yuan Silent Prayer Han Bai Ding 51 Ba Ni 1 Ni Fu - Ren Shi Fu Zhi Counter Market Making Mechanism", at present, a number of major listed companies have expressed their intention to add RMB counters. In addition, Hong Kong has a mature RMB foreign exchange and OTC derivatives trading market, which ranks first in the offshore market in the world in terms of trading volume, and can provide supporting risk management services for institutions investing in and holding RMB assets. We are working with the relevant regulatory authorities in the Mainland to explore the possibility of providing more diversified offshore RMB risk management products, such as the launch of offshore treasury bond futures in Hong Kong, as mentioned earlier, to facilitate investors to effectively hedge the interest rate risk of medium- and long-term bonds.  In terms of financial infrastructure, we are continuously enhancing Hong Kong's offshore RMB payment and clearing capabilities. First of all, we will upgrade the functions of the CMU, do a good job of market connection and promotion, and develop it into an international central securities depository (ICSD). We will also actively promote the research and application of cross-border payment of e-RMB. Strengthen collaboration with the People's Bank of China (PBoC) to test e-RMB cross-border payment tools in Hong Kong to enhance cross-border service efficiency and user experience; In cooperation with the Bank for International Settlements, we actively promote mBridge, a cross-border central bank digital currency (CBDC) work project involving a number of central banks, including the People's Bank of China, to optimize the process of cross-border payments, improve the efficiency of cross-border transactions, and reduce costs. Green financing  Next, I would like to talk about green financing. China's economy has gradually moved away from its dependence on resource-intensive industries and transformed into a low-carbon economy driven by scientific and technological innovation. Financial support is also needed to achieve the goals of carbon peak and carbon neutrality, and to realize the modernization of harmonious coexistence between man and nature. As a green finance hub in the region, Hong Kong has a lot to offer in terms of fundraising.  In recent years, Hong Kong has been committed to promoting the development of green and sustainable finance, adopting internationally recognised regulatory rules and standards. Hong Kong's green bond market is not only one of the largest in Asia, but also has an international investor base. In 2022, the issuance of green and sustainable bonds arranged in Hong Kong and internationally oriented, as well as green and sustainable loans from banks, reached a record US81 billion, up more than 40% from US57 billion in 2021 and more than five-fold from US12 billion in 2020 More than 80% of the green and sustainable bonds were issued by mainland institutions, providing sufficient financial support for green projects in the mainland. We will continue to actively promote the Hong Kong Green Bond Platform to potential issuers, promote the research and practice of tokenized issuance, and attract more international funds to participate in the low-carbon transformation of China's economy. Development of the Greater Bay Area  Finally, the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area can play a leading and exemplary role in the high-level opening of the country's financial market and financial support for the real economy. The Greater Bay Area (GBA) has strong economic strength and institutional advantages under the "One Country, Two Systems" principle, and is uniquely positioned to explore financial innovation. Our primary task is to facilitate the cross-border flow of people, goods, capital and information, and to truly integrate economic, trade and investment activities and economic development in the region. In this process, we should make the best use of the existing policy space, find the greatest common ground among the existing systems of the three places under the framework of "one country, two systems", and take the lead in pilot policy innovation in the Greater Bay Area, such as exploring cross-border credit investigation cooperation between Shenzhen and Hong Kong, so as to facilitate the development of cross-border corporate lending business. In addition to serving enterprises, it is also necessary to improve personal cross-border financial business, especially wealth management business, by optimizing the cross-border flow of employees and information, so as to better serve the residents of the Bay Area, so that the citizens can share the dividends of the economic and financial development of the Bay Area, and provide demonstration and experience for other regions. summary 0.Ladies and gentlemen, Hong Kong's financial market has also burst into new vitality as the world returns to normalcy after the pandemic. Hong Kong will continue to leverage its advantages of being backed by the motherland and connected to the world, strengthen exchanges and cooperation with the Mainland's financial regulators and industries, deepen the Mainland's financial reform and opening up, and promote the financial industry to play a better role in real economic activities. With the realization of China's Chinese-style modernization and further enhancement of its comprehensive national strength and international influence, I believe that Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre and offshore renminbi centre will also be consolidated. 21. In closing, I wish this meeting a complete success! Thank you. Revised: 04/04/2023

Title: Keynote speech at the 5th Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Financial Development Forum (Chinese version)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  Speeches 2023-04-24 Keynote speech at the 5th Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Financial Development Forum Chan Wai-man is the Deputy Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority The main forum of "Comprehensive Financial Cooperation and Development in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area". Distinguished leaders and guests, ladies and gentlemen, Hello everyone! I am very pleased to have the opportunity to participate in the 5th Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Financial Development Forum and discuss with you the development trend and future opportunities of financial cooperation in the Greater Bay Area. The 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China held in October last year and the two sessions this year pointed out the way forward for the country's future economic and financial work, and made arrangements for the country to promote and achieve high-quality financial development. Two of the clear requirements are high-level opening-up and financial support for the real economy, which will bring inspiration for financial cooperation in the Greater Bay Area and the future development of Hong Kong as an international financial centre. In the following, I will focus on these two key points, and how Hong Kong can rely on the Greater Bay Area to promote the development of Hong Kong as an international financial center on the one hand, and at the same time contribute to the realization of the country's opening up and the development of the real economy. The first is a high level of opening up to the outside world. Hong Kong's competitive advantage has always been that it is backed by the motherland and connected to the world. This uniqueness enables Hong Kong to play an important role as a bridge in the fields of cross-border trade, direct investment and financial investment. In terms of economy and trade, Guangdong Province, including the mainland cities of the Greater Bay Area, has always had extensive and deep exchanges with Hong Kong. In 2021, nearly 80% of FDI into Guangdong came from Hong Kong. As the largest province in the Mainland's external trade, Hong Kong accounted for more than RMB1 trillion of Guangdong's total import and export trade of RMB8.3 trillion in 2022, making it Guangdong's largest trading partner. With the country's continuous opening up of the financial market in recent years, Hong Kong's role as a bridge has been broadened from the economic and trade dimension to the financial market and continues to deepen, highlighting Hong Kong's role in supporting cross-border financial investment. The Stock Connect and Bond Connect arrangements continue to be expanded and optimized, with the average daily trading volume of the Northbound Connect, which reached RMB100 billion and RMB32 billion respectively in 2022, making it an important channel for foreign investors to participate in the Mainland's financial market. The launch of the Cross-boundary Wealth Management Connect in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area in 2021 is another major institutional breakthrough for the connectivity between the two places, bringing more opportunities to financial institutions in the two places and opening up new channels to facilitate cross-border investment and wealth management for residents of the two places. Achieving a high level of opening-up and promoting the internationalization of the RMB in an orderly manner are important components. In this regard, Hong Kong's sizable offshore RMB liquidity pool, well-established market infrastructure and competitive investment and financing platform play a key role in supporting a wide range of cross-border and offshore RMB business and financial activities. Over the past few years, Hong Kong's offshore RMB business has seen strong growth, with considerable growth in activities such as RMB deposits, payments, financing, foreign exchange transactions and cross-border trade settlement. At present, the transaction volume of Hong Kong's renminbi payment system is close to 1.7 trillion yuan per day, an increase of about 40% from three years ago. Hong Kong's total renminbi deposits remained at around RMB1 trillion, increasing by more than 50% in three years. The growth rate of cross-border trade settlement is even more obvious, with an increase of more than 70% in three years, and the total settlement in 2022 will reach 9.3 trillion yuan. Looking to the future, the combination of deepening financial cooperation in the Greater Bay Area and the country's high-level opening-up can yield tremendous benefits. We can step up our efforts in two areas: RMB internationalization and institutional innovation: The first is to further promote the application of RMB in cross-border economic, trade and investment activities in the Greater Bay Area, and help the country promote the internationalization of RMB in an orderly manner. The frequent economic and trade exchanges between Guangdong and Hong Kong, and the high degree of openness of the cities in the Greater Bay Area, are just right for enterprises and banks to use the people Currency for trade settlement, cross-border capital pooling, and cross-border financing provide ideal application scenarios. We note that in recent years, the Mainland has introduced a number of facilitation measures in these areas, and Guangdong Province has taken the lead in implementing these measures in the country, including speeding up and improving the efficiency of cross-border RMB trade settlement for market players, such as the many e-commerce enterprises in the Greater Bay Area, and supporting the development of new forms of foreign trade. At the same time, the pilot project of integrating local and foreign currency capital pools for multinational companies has been expanded from Shenzhen to the whole of Guangdong Province since July last year, benefiting more multinational companies and enhancing their flexibility and efficiency in the use of cross-border funds. In Hong Kong, in recent years, we have also strengthened communication with the industry on relevant issues to understand the challenges and difficulties they face in conducting business, collect their views and follow up appropriately, so as to facilitate them to make good use of RMB for cross-border transaction settlement. The second is to strengthen financial connectivity and innovation in the Greater Bay Area, and provide an exemplary role for the high-level opening up of the country's financial market. The issuance of offshore local government bonds by the Shenzhen Municipal Government in Hong Kong in the past two years is a good example, which not only reflects the cross-border cooperation between the governments and market institutions of the two places, but also provides a good case for mainland bond issuers to issue offshore bonds in Hong Kong. In addition, the Cross-boundary Wealth Management Connect has grown steadily since its implementation for more than a year, and there is still plenty of room for expansion in the future, a unique connectivity mechanism in the Greater Bay Area. The regulators of the two places will, according to market needs, further enhance the institutional arrangements in different directions, such as product scope, sales arrangements and participating institutions, and work with the industry to strengthen investor education to further unleash the huge potential of the Cross-boundary Wealth Management Connect. At the same time, the expansion of the Qianhai Shenzhen-Hong Kong Modern Service Industry Cooperation Zone in terms of geography and policy since September 2021 has brought new opportunities to the market. In February this year, 30 financial measures were launched to support Qianhai's deepening reform and opening up, covering financial innovation in the field of serving people's livelihood, financial market connectivity, expanding the opening up of the financial industry, promoting cross-border trade, and facilitating investment and financing. We look forward to more cross-border financial innovations in the region to provide lessons for a wider range of financial opening-up. Ladies and gentlemen, financial support for the real economy shows the inseparable relationship between finance and economic development, and also emphasizes that the development of the financial industry should adhere to economic construction-oriented. At the perspective of financial development in the Greater Bay Area, we should consider how the financial industry can facilitate the cross-border flow of "people", "logistics", "capital flow" and "information flow" in the region, so as to better support real economic activities. In recent years, the financial authorities in the Greater Bay Area have made unremitting efforts to implement various financial measures to support economic development in line with the principle of benefiting the people and facilitating business. The financial sector has also seized the opportunity to launch a wide range of products and services in areas such as cross-border mobile payment, cross-border personal finance, corporate banking services, and financial technology innovation, so as to effectively facilitate the cross-border flow of resources and elements in the Greater Bay Area and support the economic development of the region. In the next step, Hong Kong can leverage its strengths in several areas. The first is to support the low-carbon transformation of the mainland economy: the country's efforts to promote "3060" carbon peak and carbon neutrality require a large amount of green financing, and Hong Kong is also making every effort to develop a green finance market, which can guide international capital to invest in high-quality green projects in the mainland and help the low-carbon transformation of the mainland economy. In recent years, many mainland enterprises have issued green bonds in Hong Kong, many of which are from the Greater Bay Area, demonstrating the positive role that Hong Kong's green finance market can play in participating in the low-carbon transition of the mainland. Last year, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), together with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, the Guangzhou Branch of the People's Bank of China, the Guangdong Society for Finance and Banking, and other entities jointly released the "Reference on the Process of Mainland Non-financial Enterprises Issuing Green Bonds in the Hong Kong Market", so that more mainland institutions, including bond issuers in the Greater Bay Area, can understand and master the operational points and business processes of issuing green bonds in Hong Kong. We look forward to and welcoming more enterprises and institutions in the Greater Bay Area to make good use of Hong Kong's green finance platform to conduct green financing in Hong Kong, and jointly promote financial support for the low-carbon transformation of society, economy and industries in the Greater Bay Area. Another aspect is to accelerate the development of financial technology and support the construction of a digital economy: the digital transformation of the national economy needs corresponding financial assistance. Promoting digital financial innovation and increasing payment speed and efficiency through scientific and technological means is conducive to supporting the cross-border flow of resource elements. For example, the HKMA is working with the People's Bank of China (PBoC) to conduct a trial in Hong Kong on the use of e-RMB as a cross-border payment tool to enhance the efficiency and user experience of cross-border payment services. Another example is the HKMA, the people The number of subpages of the number of Fu Yan corpse IT and no 7 Bu Gangfeng; Female 7 Bu Dog Ling 6 IRJ  and Loss of Dog Ling number subpage Fu kUt) UUJ  1 Bian  shellfish. It is hoped that the application of CBDC in the future can smooth the process of cross-border payment, improve the efficiency of cross-border transactions, and reduce transaction costs. The Greater Bay Area (GBA) is a gathering place for fintech companies and talents, and Hong Kong will continue to improve the fintech market environment to support the vigorous development of the industry. The third is to facilitate the smooth flow of capital and information and enhance the financial system's ability to serve the real economy: the HKMA launched the Commercial Data Interchange (CDI) in October last year to facilitate authorised access to business data by financial institutions through the establishment of a secure and innovative data infrastructure, with a view to greater digitalisation and streamlining of the know-your-customer, credit assessment, loan approval and risk management processes. To grasp the opportunities in the Greater Bay Area, the market generally believes that as the two places move towards a higher level of financial connectivity and deeper docking, further opening up the cross-border information flow will help improve efficiency and speed up the process of cross-border financing. In this regard, we are working with the financial sector to explore ways to better facilitate cross-border lending and financing activities by facilitating cross-border information flows. Ladies and gentlemen, with the joint efforts of all parties in the financial development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, cities in the region have continuously written a new chapter in the financial cooperation in the Greater Bay Area, and have also made important contributions to the country's high-level opening-up and the development of the real economy in the Greater Bay Area. This year's forum brought together leaders and representatives from government agencies, financial authorities, financial institutions and enterprises to brainstorm and offer suggestions and suggestions, which will play a positive role in promoting future financial cooperation in the Greater Bay Area and better serve enterprises and residents in the region. In conclusion, I wish the Forum every success. Thank you. Note: The Forum will be held on 22 April 2023 Revised: 24/04/2023
