Title: Remarks after the US Fed FOMC Meeting
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY f o  w M Speeches 04 May 2023 Remarks after the US Fed FOMC Meeting Eddie Yue, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. The Federal Open Market Committee of the Federal Reserve (the Fed) announced a rate hike of 25 basis points at the early hours today (Hong Kong time) after its two-day meeting, raising the target range for the federal funds rate to 5-5.25%. The HKMA has adjusted the Base Rate upward to 5.5% according to the established mechanism with immediate effect. 2. The Feds rate-hike decision is consistent with market expectation. More time is needed to assess the impact of continual rate hikes in the past year on the US economy and inflation. The future interest rate path in the US will remain uncertain and will depend on incoming economic data and development. Also, the recent financial distress of individual US regional banks has caused credit tightening, and the impact on economic activities and monetary policy remains to be seen. 3. Rate hikes in the US will not affect the financial and monetary stability of Hong Kong. The wider interest rate differentials between Hong Kong dollar and US dollar provide incentives for carry trades to sell Hong Kong dollar. Coupled with subdued local demand for Hong Kong dollar in recent months, the Hong Kong dollar exchange rate remained soft and the weak-side Convertibility Undertaking has been triggered multiple times this year. With funds flowing out from the Hong Kong dollar system, the interest rate automatic adjustment mechanism will kick in, thereby driving the Hong Kong dollar interbank rates to gradually rise and track the US dollar interbank rates. This will help offset the incentives for carry trades and stabilise the Hong Kong dollar within the 7.75- 7.85 range. 4. The adjustment process is completely within the design and expectations of the LERS. Similar adjustment occurred during the last US rate-hike cycle in 2015 to 2018. Most importantly, the market has sufficient understanding and operational experience of the LERS and continues to have strong confidence in the system. The market has continued to operate in a smooth and orderly manner, and the total deposits in the banking system in Hong Kong have also remained stable. 5. On interest rates, we noticed that over the past few months, interbank rates have been rising gradually. As the US raised interest rates again, this trend is expected to continue. It is worth noting that the speed and magnitude for the Hong Kong dollar interbank rates to catch up with their US dollar counterparts will be subject to the supply and demand of Hong Kong dollar in the local funding market. 6. On the commercial interest rates of banks, banks will decide on the timing and magnitude of adjusting them having regard to the structure of their own funding cost and other relevant considerations. The public should be prepared for the movements of banks lending rates, and should carefully assess and manage the relevant risks when making property purchase, taking out mortgages or making other borrowing decisions. 7. The HKMA will continue to closely monitor market developments and maintain monetary and financial stability. Last revision date : 04 May 2023

Title: Keynote speech at the Tsinghua PBCSF Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (Shenzhen) Finance Forum (Chinese version)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  Speeches 2023-05-11 Keynote speech at Tsinghua PBC Greater Bay Area (Shenzhen) Financial Forum Chan Wai-man is the Deputy Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Distinguished leaders and guests, good morning! It is my great pleasure to represent the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) in the Tsinghua PBC Greater Bay Area (Shenzhen) Financial Forum. The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) is a strong, vibrant and potential region, which ranks among the top in the world in terms of economic scale, infrastructure, scientific research level, innovation capacity, financial strength and high-end talents. More importantly, there is still a huge potential for us to explore and play in the future. The forum discussed how finance can contribute to the high-quality economic development of the Greater Bay Area, and I believe that the key words are hidden in the theme of the forum: innovation, openness and cooperation. Today's Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area is a witness and participant in the reform and opening up for more than 40 years. In its proximity to Hong Kong and Macao, Guangdong has always been a leader and pioneer in opening up to the outside world. Among the major measures taken by China's financial sector to open up to the outside world, Guangdong's presence can be seen in the introduction and going out of banking, securities and insurance, from the Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect to the cross-border wealth management connect (wealth management connect), from the overseas fund-raising of enterprises to the issuance of offshore RMB bonds by the first local government. Summing up practical experience and gradually opening up the financial sector in an orderly and steady manner is conducive to the introduction of foreign capital and experience, and the effective allocation of production resources through finance, thereby enhancing the efficiency and competitiveness of enterprises and strengthening their market-oriented and international operation capabilities. Today, when we talk about high-quality economic development, we need to adhere to the high-level opening up of the financial industry and reflect financial support for the real economy. Looking back at the development in recent years, the opening up of the Mainland's financial industry to the outside world has been moving towards a high level, as evidenced by the mutual access with Hong Kong's financial market. From the initial listing of mainland enterprises in Hong Kong, to the gradual opening of QFII and QDII, to Stock Connect, Bond Connect, Wealth Management Connect, ETF Connect, and the opening of the swap link for risk management products next week, the channels are becoming more and more extensive, and the various investment channels are constantly improving and upgrading after the opening. The gradual opening up of the capital market has opened up new sources of funds in addition to trade and direct investment, and at the same time, it has also enabled foreign investors to share the dividends of China's rapid economic development. On the other hand, Hong Kong has been playing an active role in this process, not only as a key link between China and the rest of the world, but also as a continuous reinforcement and enhancement of its status as an international financial centre. Today, more than half of foreign investors' A-share holdings and onshore bond trading are conducted through Stock Connect and Bond Connect. As these connectivity channels involve RMB, they provide a strong boost to the orderly internationalisation of RMB, and also make Hong Kong's role as an offshore RMB business hub more prominent. It can be said that this is a successful example of promoting win-win cooperation through openness. Expanding the circle of friends through cooperation and seeking common interests through cooperation is of special significance in today's complex and changeable situation. In the future, financial cooperation in the Greater Bay Area should be aimed at supporting high-quality economic development and using innovation as a means. To support the economy, it is necessary to consider and match the actual needs of Taiwan's enterprises for operation and development, and better meet the people's demand for high-quality financial services. Relying on innovation requires us to conform to the progress of the times, actively explore and use new scientific and technological means, dare to seek moderate innovation and breakthroughs in the system, and let finance become a help rather than a hindrance. Both the government, enterprises and the people, both within and outside the region, have high hopes and expectations for the future of the Greater Bay Area. The common vision allows us to have more room for imagination. We must quicken the pace of cooperation when conditions are ripe, intensify our efforts, and go all out to carry out them. For matters that require further study, it is advisable to adopt the form of pilot projects, take the lead in experimenting, and create conditions. Next, I would like to give you a few examples of how we can do a good job in financial cooperation in the Greater Bay Area. The first is to help enterprises in the GBA better manage cross-border capital flows and obtain financing more easily. Enterprises in the Bay Area have strong international competitiveness and are important participants in external circulation, with great demand for trade settlement, cross-border capital pooling and cross-border financing, and provide ideal application scenarios for RMB internationalization. In recent years, the mainland has introduced a number of facilitation measures in these areas, and Guangdong Province is at the forefront of the country, speeding up and improving the efficiency of cross-border RMB trade settlement for mainland market entities, including many e-commerce enterprises, and supporting the development of new forms of foreign trade. On the other hand, the pilot project of integrated domestic and foreign currency capital pooling for multinational companies has been expanded from Shenzhen to the whole of Guangdong Province since July last year, so that more multinational companies can improve the flexibility and efficiency of cross-border capital dispatch. We note that the Mainland regulators have recently proposed that the next step will be to study the introduction of a pilot policy for the "lower version" of capital pools for multinational companies, and to study the upgrading of the "high version" of the pilot policy for the pooling of funds to facilitate the co-ordination of cross-border funds by enterprise groups of different sizes. In rolling out these enhancement measures, consideration could be given to using the Greater Bay Area as a pilot and combining it with Hong Kong's preferential policies to promote corporate treasury centres to serve the needs of enterprises in effectively managing cross-border funds in a more comprehensive manner. In addition to policy support, we can also promote digital financial innovation and improve payment efficiency through technological means. In this regard, the HKMA is working with the People's Bank of China (PBoC) to test the e-CNY as a cross-border payment tool in Hong Kong, with a view to enhancing service efficiency and user experience, and providing an additional secure, convenient and innovative option for cross-border payments in the future. Another major initiative in this regard is the cross-border CBDC project in which the HKMA, the People's Bank of China's Digital Currency Research Institute, the Bank for International Settlements and two other overseas central banks are involved. The project is progressing well and has already proven its feasibility and practicality through real transactions. With the continuous deepening and implementation of the project, the wide application in the future can fundamentally solve the long-standing pain points of cross-border payment, such as many intermediate links, high cost and slow speed, and greatly improve the efficiency of cross-border capital flow of enterprises in the Greater Bay Area In addition to enterprises, financial co-operation in the Greater Bay Area also needs to serve the needs of the people in the region, and the Cross-boundary Wealth Management Connect is a landmark project that provides more investment options for residents of Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao, while at the same time opening up new development space for financial institutions in the three places. Since the implementation of the WMC for more than a year, it has been operating smoothly, especially after the resumption of full border clearance between the Mainland and Hong Kong, and the account opening and capital investment are growing steadily. This unique connectivity mechanism in the Greater Bay Area has tremendous development prospects. Based on the experience gained since the launch of the two places, and based on the feedback from participating institutions and residents, the regulators of the two places are seeking to further optimize the institutional arrangements in terms of product scope, sales arrangements and sales channels, and work with the industry to strengthen investor publicity and education efforts to further unleash the potential of cross-border financial connect. High-quality economic development and low-carbon transformation are one of the key points. The country's commitment to carbon peak and carbon neutrality requires a large amount of green financing. Hong Kong is making every effort to develop a green finance market, and is a leading player in the Asia-Pacific region, with a market environment that has a good reputation in the field of international green financing, and is well positioned to guide international capital to invest in high-quality green projects in the Mainland, so as to facilitate the low-carbon transformation of the Mainland economy. In recent years, many mainland enterprises have issued green bonds in Hong Kong, many of which are from the Greater Bay Area. In particular, the Shenzhen Municipal Government has twice issued offshore RMB green bonds in Hong Kong, which have been well received by the market and have played a successful demonstration role, demonstrating the role of Hong Kong's green finance market in participating in the low-carbon transformation of the Mainland. In the future, we will continue to promote Hong Kong's green finance platform to enterprises and institutions in the Greater Bay Area, and encourage green financing in Hong Kong. We should also actively explore ways to make full use of the region's carbon emission trading resources, and jointly promote financial support for the low-carbon transformation of the society, economy and industry in the Greater Bay Area. He W.: From the spirit of work promotion to the promotion of high-quality economic development as an indicator to measure the role of finance, it will surely make important contributions to the country's promotion of high-level opening up to the outside world and the economic, social and people's livelihood development of the Greater Bay Area. Finally, I wish the Forum every success and offer suggestions for deepening financial cooperation in the Greater Bay Area. Thank you. Revised: 11 May 2023

Title: Keynote Address at the Swap Connect Launch Ceremony (Chinese version)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  Speeches 2023-05-15 Keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the Swap Connect Eddie Yue, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Honorable Chief Executive John Lee, Secretary General Chen Maobo, Honorable Vice President Pan Gongsheng, Deputy Director Wang Linggui, Deputy Director Yin Zonghua Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. It is a great pleasure to witness with you today that the mutual financial markets of the Mainland and Hong Kong have welcomed a new member  Swap Connect. Stock Connect and Bond Connect have achieved two-way connectivity between the capital markets of the two places, and have become a popular investment channel, which has played a very positive role in expanding the scale of the capital markets in the Mainland and Hong Kong, as well as in expanding the diversification of investors. The Northbound Swap Connect further extends mutual access to the derivatives market, which is another milestone in the financial co-operation between the two places, and also reflects Hong Kong's uniqueness as a window for the Mainland to deepen the opening up of the financial market. For bond investors, effective management of interest rate risk is an important consideration. In recent years, international investors' interest in Chinese bond assets has increased, so their demand for related risk management tools has become more prominent. In the past, Bond Connect investors mainly used offshore RMB swap products to hedge interest rate risk, and Northbound Swap Connect provides a convenient channel for Hong Kong's financial infrastructure and intermediaries to access the more liquid onshore interest rate swap market, which can more effectively control interest rate risk. The launch of the Northbound Swap Connect will provide favourable conditions for international investors to further participate in the onshore bond market, and will also facilitate the use of risk management to maintain market stability. It is of particular significance to enhance the recognition and confidence of RMB bonds in the international market. At the same time, the Northbound Swap Connect will further enhance the liquidity and depth of the onshore derivatives market by diversifying the trading entities of onshore RMB swaps. The HKMA will closely monitor the implementation of the Northbound Swap Connect with the regulators of both places, and communicate with market participants in a timely manner to ensure the smooth operation of this new initiative and its intended effect. Looking ahead, we will continue to explore ways to provide international investors with more diversified risk management tools to promote the healthy and sustainable development of the financial markets in both places. With the deepening of the interconnection between the financial markets of the Mainland and Hong Kong, Hong Kong's financial institutions will usher in more opportunities, and Hong Kong's status as a risk management centre and offshore RMB hub will be further strengthened. Finally, I wish the Northbound Swap Connect every success and the continuous breakthrough of connectivity between the two places. Thank you! Revised: 15/05/2023

Title: Keynote speech at the Bank of China: The Belt and Road Initiative and RMB Internationalization Forum
text: IIONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY # Mi W 3 M Speeches 06 Jun 2023 Keynote speech at the Bank of China: The Belt and Road Initiative and RMB Internationalization Forum Darryl Chan, Deputy Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority Good morning. It gives me great pleasure to join you today at the Belt and Road Initiative and RMB Internationalization Forum. Thank you Mr Sun and Bank of China (BoC) colleagues for organising this special event. I also look forward to the release of your annual White Paper on Renminbi (RMB) Internationalisation. Being the first RMB clearing bank with substantial expertise and stake in this subject, BoC(HK), I am sure, has lots of insights to share with us. Today I would like to talk about the opportunities for Hong Kong as RMB gains wider global acceptance, in particular in the Belt & Road context, and how Hong Kong in return can contribute to this process. RMB internationalisation has made great strides in the past decade or so. Since the launch of the cross-border RMB trade settlement arrangement in 2009, the channels of cross- border usage have kept expanding  from trade settlement to direct investment, to portfolio investment. Conduits that connect onshore and offshore markets have continuously become wider and deeper. By now, a well-developed two-way RMB circulation system is in place, enabling corporates and financial institutions to conduct different types of cross-border RMB transactions based on their needs. Such circulation system is getting more frictionless and mature over time, leading to increasing acceptance and use of RMB globally. For example, last year the International Monetary Fund raised the weight of the RMB in the Special Drawing Rights; percentage of RMB in foreign exchange market transactions has been picking up; and lately the share of Mainland's external trade settled in RMB has seen renewed momentum. The growth momentum is supported by, and in turn promotes, Hong Kongs development as the leading offshore RMB business hub. Let me share a few data points. Today, with total deposit close to RMB 1 trillion, Hong Kong is home to the largest offshore RMB liquidity pool. This accounts for about 60% of global aggregate and supports the liquidity needs of other offshore RMB centres. The size of RMB payments routed through Hong Kongs RMB RTGS system has made quantum leaps, with a remarkable daily turnover of RMB1.6 trillion, surpassing that of Hong Kong dollar. Hong Kong also handles over 70% of global RMB payments and ranks number one globally in RMB foreign exchange transaction volume. Another bright spot is capital market activities involving RMB. Each day Northbound and Southbound Stock Connect records close to RMB 140 billion worth of transactions, and Northbound Bond Connect records RMB 40 billion. Southbound Bond Connect has also added impetus to dim sum bond issuance and trading in Hong Kong. Last year the issuance of dim sum bonds totalled RMB 330 billion, hitting an eight-year high. We are excited to see continued breakthroughs and expansion of product offerings denominated in RMB. A few weeks ago Swap Connect was launched, opening up a new avenue for investors to manage interest rate risks associated with their RMB bond holdings. Just last week, the Government Green Bond Programme successfully issued a record RMB15 billion of green bonds and extended the tenor from previous five years to ten years. In two weeks time, Hong Kong dollar and RMB dual-counter trading of selected Hong Kong-listed stocks will commence. All these positive developments have contributed to the increasing onshore-offshore circulation of RMB and more offshore-to-offshore activities. Looking ahead, Chinas continued economic growth, its strength in external trade activities and its expanding financial markets lay solid foundation for RMB to further increase its international footprint. RMBs usage in cross-border trade settlement, global foreign exchange transactions, international payments, and official reserves has ample potential to further increase. The future path will be guided by two themes. First is to promote RMB internationalisation in an orderly manner. Second is that financial development should serve the real sector in high-quality economic development. Against this backdrop, there are two issues to be addressed: how can RMB internationalisation benefit market entities and real sector activities, capturing the opportunities offered by the Belt and Road Initiative; how should Hong Kong leverage its competitive edge to support the process? The merchandise trade volume between the Mainland and some 150 countries along the Belt and Road reached RMB14 trillion last year, while the scale of two-way investment has also been expanding steadily. This provides fertile ground for the growth of RMB usage in trade and investment activities. For Mainland corporates, using local currency in external transactions helps reduce currency mismatch and lower exchange costs. For overseas entities, especially for those with close business ties with China, settlement and investment using RMB directly would help diversify currency exposure and reduce transaction costs. Another relevant consideration is that the performance of RMB assets has displayed low correlation with their global and developed market peers, providing a good tool for investment diversification. In short, the use of RMB in cross-border trade settlement, investment, and treasury management can achieve a win-win outcome for both Mainland and overseas corporates. Hong Kong plays a unique role in supporting China's capital account opening and the Belt and Road Initiative. As an international financial centre and offshore RMB hub, Hong Kong banks have built strong capability and extensive network, both locally and globally, in support of a wide range of RMB transactions that covers trade settlement and payments, corporate investment, fund raising and treasury management. To maintain Hong Kong's lead, we need to continue to work hard on three fronts: liquidity, products, and infrastructure. On liquidity, the much enhanced Currency Swap Agreement between the People's Bank of China and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority last year has enabled us to provide the necessary liquidity support to the offshore market through the RMB liquidity facilities set up by the HKMA. This provides a favourable environment for financial institutions to expand their RMB-related activities and services. The Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) under the aegis of the HKMA is undergoing a major overhaul to upgrade its operational capacity and product offerings, with the aim to better support the growth of RMB bond issuances and associated custodian services. To increase the cross-border payment efficiency of RMB, we are supporting the pilot testing of eCNY under various cross-border payment scenarios. We are also pressing ahead with the mBridge project that promotes cross-border wholesale payments using central bank digital currencies including RMB. Ladies and gentlemen, we have made good progress on RMB internationalisation. The future trajectory depends on the joint effort of policy makers and, more importantly, market participants including both the real sector and the financial sector. Title: Keynote Speech at the Caixin Summer Summit 2023 (Hong Kong Session) (Chinese version)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  Speeches 09.06.2023 Keynote speech at the 2023 Caixin Summer Summit in Hong Kong Eddie Yue, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen! First of all, I would like to thank Caixin very much for inviting me to participate in this year's Summer Summit.  The theme of today's summit is Creating a New Paradigm of Opening-up, and it covers a wide range of topics, including a panel discussion on the internationalisation of the renminbi, and I would like to share our thoughts on the HKMA and our work in this area in recent years.  The internationalization of the renminbi has been developing in an orderly manner over the past decade. With the gradual opening up of the Mainland's financial market, the gradual flow of overseas capital into the Mainland's RMB market has become a long-term trend. The proportion of the renminbi in global foreign exchange reserves and foreign exchange market transactions has also increased steadily. Plus the International Monetary Fund (IMF) last year put the renminbi in the Special Drawing Right (SDR), these developments are a testament to the gradual increase in the recognition of the renminbi in the international market and the acceptance of cross-border use. At the policy level, the country's policy direction for promoting the internationalization of the renminbi is clear and clear, and the opening up of the mainland market continues unabated, which provides better conditions for the application and circulation of the renminbi in the international market.  With the mainland's capital account not yet fully liberalized, the offshore renminbi market has a unique role to play in the process of renminbi internationalization. For market participants, they can trade RMB in the offshore market with reference to their usual market practices; For the mainland authorities, the offshore market acts as a firewall to prevent fluctuations and risks from spreading to the mainland. Therefore, the development of offshore RMB in Hong Kong and the internationalization of RMB go hand in hand. In this process of development, it can be roughly divided into two major directions: the real economy and the capital market.  In terms of the real economy, Hong Kong launched the personal renminbi business as early as 2004 to facilitate people-to-people exchanges between the Mainland and Hong Kong in the process of economic and trade integration between the two places. More importantly, in 2009, when the country implemented cross-border RMB settlement, Hong Kong became one of the first batch of overseas pilot areas, and Hong Kong's RMB business has since embarked on a new level, expanding from individual business to enterprises and institutions. Since then, the cross-border use of RMB has been continuously improved, and the mainland's foreign trade settled in RMB ratio to j column has risen from 2010)2% to 20% at present, and there is still great potential for further growth in the future. The renminbi trade settlement volume handled by the Bank of Hong Kong has also risen from less than RMB400 billion in 2010 to more than RMB9 trillion in 2022, laying a solid foundation for the renminbi's status on the international stage.  Since 2010, the state has allowed some foreign institutions to invest in the interbank bond market, launched the RMB Qualified Foreign Institutional Investor Programme in 2011, and launched various mutual access schemes in Hong Kong since 2014. It is precisely because Hong Kong is an international financial centre that international investors are more familiar with Hong Kong's market environment that the Stock Connect Scheme has become a major channel for international investors to invest in the Mainland, with about two-thirds of international investors investing in Mainland stocks through Stock Connect, and about 60 per cent of those who trade Mainland onshore bonds through Bond Connect. Hong Kong's unique mutual access arrangement has also contributed to the inclusion of mainland stocks and renminbi bonds in the world's major stock and bond indices since 2018, allowing renminbi-denominated products to go global.  In developing Hong Kong's offshore RMB business, we hope to achieve the effect of RMB in the real economy and financial investment in promoting each other, and to form an effective circulation of cross-border RMB in different fields. For example, overseas enterprises can use RMB to settle trade through the Hong Kong market, and after mainland enterprises get the RMB funds, they can also use Hong Kong's banks and Hong Kong's market at the same time to invest in mainland financial assets or simply invest in Hong Kong's offshore products through mutual access. In this transaction chain, it not only derives the needs of RMB payment and settlement, investment and financing, and risk management, but more importantly, drives the use of RMB in global cross-border commerce and financial investment. Therefore, the internationalisation of RMB and Hong Kong's offshore RMB market are closely linked and mutually reinforcing. After nearly 20 years of development, Hong Kong has continued to consolidate its role as a global offshore RMB business hub. At present, almost 70 percent of the world's renminbi payments are processed through Hong Kong, and the average daily turnover of renminbi foreign exchange transactions in Hong Kong is nearly US200 billion, and our banking system also has 1 trillion yuan in deposits.  So how can we further develop Hong Kong's function as an offshore renminbi centre? We will step up our work in three areas: (1) increasing RMB liquidity, (2) promoting RMB products, and (3) enhancing RMB financial infrastructure.  On the liquidity front, the HKMA expanded its currency swap arrangement with the People's Bank of China (PBoC) to RMB800 billion last year and enhanced it to a standing agreement to enhance market confidence. On this basis, we have enhanced our RMB liquidity facilities for banks in Hong Kong, including expanding the funding quota, extending operating hours and reducing repo rates, to support the continued development of Hong Kong's offshore RMB market and to enable banks in Hong Kong to serve customers in different time zones and other offshore centres.  Second, we need to promote the development of renminbi products so that enterprises holding renminbi can have more ways to invest in renminbi, so as to increase their willingness to hold renminbi. In terms of the equity market, I am pleased that RMB stocks can be traded in just over a week, allowing issuers and investors to trade in RMB. In terms of the bond market, we are seeking and encouraging more financial institutions and enterprises to raise RMB and issue dim sum bonds in Hong Kong. The total amount of offshore renminbi bonds issued in Hong Kong last year reached RMB330 billion, more than double that of 2021, and the issuance of offshore renminbi local government bonds in Hong Kong by the Hainan Provincial People's Government and the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government, including green bonds and blue bonds related to marine conservation, also helped to further enrich the renminbi financial products in the Hong Kong market. In terms of risk management products, the Northbound Swap Connect was successfully launched in May this year, allowing international investors to participate in the Mainland's interest rate swap market, enhancing hedging efficiency and reducing transaction costs. In the next step, the HKMA will continue to work with the Mainland regulators to explore issues such as the launch of offshore treasury bond futures in Hong Kong to provide investors with more diversified risk management tools and make the offshore RMB capital market more mature. 4. The third part of the work is to enhance the financial infrastructure of Hong Kong's renminbi. The first is to enhance the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) of the HKMA, which we hope will develop into a major international central securities depository (ICSD) platform in Asia to better support cross-border clearing, trade settlement and custody services in RMB. In addition, the HKMA has actively assisted in advancing the research and application of e-CNY cross-border payments, including working with the People's Bank of China (PBoC) to test the cross-border use of e-CNY in Hong Kong. In terms of international cooperation, the HKMA is working with the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) to actively promote mBridge, a cross-border central bank digital currency (CBDC) work project involving a number of central banks, including the People's Bank of China. The goal is to use CBDC to make cross-border payments, including RMB, faster and cheaper.  In the coming days, the international status of the renminbi will continue to improve, and with the Belt and Road Initiative and the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), we will see more overseas enterprises and financial institutions using the renminbi for capital transactions Because RMB is accumulating in various places, it is a natural phenomenon that more offshore RMB business centers may be born overseas. With the support of the National 14th Five-Year Plan, Hong Kong will continue to strengthen its role as a global offshore RMB business hub and leverage its nearly 20 years of experience and resources as a pioneer to provide further support for the development of offshore RMB business overseas Promote and catalyze the development of RMB business of overseas enterprises and banks with the support of Hong Kong's payment, foreign exchange and liquidity, and grasp the current opportunities of RMB business development together. The involvement of the financial community is very important in this process. We look forward to working together to make good use of Hong Kong's market foundation, promote more innovation in cross-border and offshore business, support the effective circulation of RMB funds in the onshore and overseas markets, build a more complete RMB ecosystem, and further promote the internationalization of RMB."  In conclusion, I wish today's summit every success. Thank you. Revised: 09 June 2023

Title: Remarks after the US Fed FOMC Meeting
text: IIONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY # Mi W 3 M Speeches 15 Jun 2023 Remarks after the US Fed FOMC Meeting Eddie Yue, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. The Federal Open Market Committee of the Federal Reserve (the Fed) announced early today (Hong Kong time) that it has decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate unchanged at 5-5.25%. 2. The Feds policy decision is generally in line with market expectations. However, the high interest rate environment in the US may last for some time, and the Fed may hike rates again. The Fed will continue to take into account inflation and employment data, as well as the impact of earlier rate hikes on the economy, in making future interest rate decisions. The interest rate path in the US will remain uncertain. 3. Since the US began raising rates in March last year, the widening interest-rate differential between the Hong Kong dollar and the US dollar has incentivized carry trades. This led to selling of Hong Kong dollars with the weak-side Convertibility Undertaking being triggered repeatedly and a corresponding decline in the Aggregate Balance, which has gradually driven up Hong Kong dollar interest rates. This process is in line with the design and expected functioning of the LERS. The market has continued to operate in a smooth and orderly manner. The Hong Kong dollar exchange rate has strengthened since early May, mainly driven by dividend payment-related demand from listed companies and seasonal factors, such as half-year-end funding needs by corporates. With the half-year-end approaching, coupled with the need to pay dividends, the possibility that Hong Kong dollar interbank rates will catch up with, or even overshoot, their US dollar counterparts on certain days cannot be ruled out. The public should be mindful of the Hong Kong dollar interbank rate movements. 4. When determining commercial interest rates, banks will consider the structure of their own funding cost and other relevant factors. As the high interest rate environment may last for some time, the public should be mindful of interest rate movements and relevant risks when purchasing property, taking out mortgages or making other borrowing decisions. 5. The HKMA will continue to closely monitor market developments and maintain monetary and financial stability. Last revision date : 15 June 2023

Title: Opening Remarks at the Anti-Scam Consumer Protection Charter (Chinese version)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  Speeches 2023-06-29 Opening remarks of the Charter on Consumer Fraud Prevention Eddie Yue, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Hello everyone! Welcome to today's Consumer Deception Protection Charter event. With the development of technology and changes in consumer behaviour, online consumption has become an important part of Hong Kong people's daily lives. It can be done with a single click, and I am sure that all of you have used online platforms or mobile phones to shop, pay bills, enjoy food delivery services, or use online banking services or transfer money to friends. On the other hand, fraudsters are also "keeping up with the times", using a variety of tricks and technology to carry out fraudulent activities, and sending phishing messages is a common example. Phishing messages are often falsely claimed to be sent by credible institutions, banks or merchants, etc., and are often accompanied by hyperlinks to fraudulent web pages in an attempt to deceive victims into providing personal or credit card information. If the public is not careful, they may fall into the trap of deception at any time. In view of this, the HKMA and the banking sector have been stepping up efforts to enhance the security measures and consumer education of banking services to enhance consumer protection. Today, we have taken a step forward by joining hands with other stakeholders from different sectors to help the public guard against credit card fraud through a multi-pronged approach. Consumer Deception Protection Charter  Four Principles Led by the HKMA and the Hong Kong Association of Banks, with the full support of the Hong Kong Police Force and the Consumer Council, the event was joined by 23 local card-issuing banks and 15 major merchants from different industries, including retail, telecommunications, catering, transportation and logistics, to conceive the Consumer Deception Protection Charter (the Charter). It is hoped that through the four principles of the Charter, the public will be vigilant against phishing and fraudulent messages sent by banks and merchants The four principles of the Covenant include: First, the Participating Organisations will not send hyperlinks to customers through any instant electronic messaging (e.g. SMS, WhatsApp, WeChat, etc.) asking them to provide their personal and credit card information online; Second, the Participating Organisations will disseminate to the public through their official websites, mobile applications, and other publicity and promotion channels to beware of suspicious messages that may be from banks or merchants, and remind the public not to click on hyperlinks in messages or provide personal and credit card information through hyperlinks; Third, the Participating Organisations will provide contact information on their official websites, mobile applications and other appropriate channels to allow customers to check and verify the identity of the sender of the information or the authenticity of the information;  Fourth, the Participating Organisations will provide appropriate training on the Charter to frontline staff to effectively handle enquiries from customers suspected of being defrauded. In conclusion, all card-issuing banks and participating merchants in Hong Kong do not ask customers for personal and credit card information through hyperlinks in real-time electronic messages, so members of the public should always be vigilant if they receive such information and do not click on the hyperlinks attached to suspicious messages to provide personal and credit card information. Latest Measures to Enhance Credit Card Customer Protection In addition to the multi-stakeholder collaboration, the HKMA also launched last Tuesday a total of 33 measures to enhance consumer protection for credit cards in four areas in four areas, in consultation with the banking industry. The bank is actively implementing the relevant work and expects to implement it in phases within the year Conclusion Public education is an important part of consumer protection. We will continue to work with stakeholders from different sectors to launch more publicity and education to keep the public abreast of the latest fraud modus operandi of credit cards and bogus electronic messages, with a view to taking a multi-pronged approach to reduce the chances of deception among the public. Last but not least, I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to the Hong Kong Association of Banks, all card-issuing banks in Hong Kong, various merchants and supporting organisations (including the Hong Kong Police Force and the Consumer Council) for their positive response and support over the past two months in making the Charter a smooth launch. Thank you very much. Revised: 29/06/2023

Title: Keynote Speech at the Bond Connect Anniversary Summit 2023 (Chinese version)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  Speeches 07/04/2023 Keynote speech at the Bond Connect Annual Forum 2023 Eddie Yue, Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. It is a great pleasure to celebrate the 6th anniversary of Bond Connect. Since its launch, Bond Connect has achieved very good results and has become a major channel for Chinese and foreign investors to allocate bond assets across borders, greatly enhancing the status of RMB assets in the global market and strongly promoting the high-level two-way opening up of the mainland bond market. Despite the recent volatility in the global market, trading under Bond Connect has remained buoyant. In May this year, for example, the trading volume of the Northbound Trading exceeded RMB970 billion, a record high, accounting for 70% of the total turnover of international investors in the Mainland's interbank bond market. One of the keys to the success of Bond Connect is that the regulatory authorities and financial infrastructure of the two places have been market-oriented and have continuously improved all aspects of trading and settlement. Just like the newly launched basket trading function under the Northbound Scheme, and the one-stop online reporting service for failed trade settlements, it may seem like some technical enhancement measures, but it is very important to improve the trading efficiency and operational convenience of Bond Connect, and more importantly, it reflects the continuous pursuit of breakthroughs and progress on the Bond Connect platform. The Southbound Scheme has started steadily and developed steadily, bringing development opportunities to Hong Kong's bond market. In recent years, Hong Kong has introduced various incentives and tax policies to strengthen Hong Kong's position as a bond issuance hub in Asia, especially to promote the faster development of the green bond and dim sum bond markets. Through the joint efforts of the industry, Hong Kong has become a leading green finance centre in Asia, arranging for the issuance of green and sustainable bonds for the mainland last year, as well as green and sustainable loans from banks, reaching a record US80.5 billion, an increase of more than 40% over 2021, of which more than 80% of the green and sustainable bonds were issued by mainland institutions, bringing in international funds for the low-carbon transformation of the Chinese economy. The dim sum bond market is also booming, with issuance exceeding RMB330 billion in 2022, more than double that of 2021. The Southbound Scheme has played a positive role. There is still a lot of room for further improvement in Bond Connect, and I would like to briefly outline the HKMA's priorities for the next phase. The first is to enrich the risk management toolbox of Northbound investors. In the past year, due to the inversion of interest rates between China and the United States, the epidemic and other factors, the market has experienced certain fluctuations, and investors' demand for risk management tools has become more prominent. The Northbound Swap Connect was successfully launched in May this year to facilitate foreign investors to access the more liquid onshore interest rate swap market and manage short-term bond interest rate risk more effectively. We also note that at present, about 40% of the Northbound Scheme investments are concentrated in bonds with maturities of five years or above, and there is a lack of effective ways to hedge the relevant interest rate risks, resulting in a great demand for treasury bond futures. We will work with the regulatory authorities of the two places to explore the launch of offshore treasury bond futures, which will provide an important supporting package for the Northbound Scheme, attract more medium- to long-term institutional investors to participate in the Mainland bond market, and promote the development of Hong Kong as an international risk management centre. The next step is to study and introduce more arrangements that are common in the bond market to revitalize stocks and provide liquidity, such as repurchases, so that investors can use their bond holdings more effectively for liquidity management and promote market vitality and healthy development. In addition, we will enhance the operational arrangements of the Southbound Scheme. The market is generally optimistic about the future development potential of the Southbound Scheme and has a strong interest in participating in the market-making business of the Southbound Scheme. The HKMA will expand the scope of market makers to further enhance liquidity in the secondary market, provide investors with more diversified choices and increase the attractiveness of Hong Kong's bond market. Finally, we will continue to comprehensively upgrade and expand Hong Kong's debt instruments clearing system, CMU, and promote its development into a major international central securities depository (ICSD) platform in Asia. Major improvements include continuing to strengthen cooperation with the Mainland's financial infrastructure, and CMU will implement two-way automated docking with the Shanghai Clearing House within the year to further enhance the efficiency of cross-border settlement. At the same time, the CMU will also introduce more market-oriented measures and arrangements to enhance service levels, enhance competitiveness, and better facilitate issuers and investors to participate in the Hong Kong bond market in terms of settlement, custody and liquidity management, so as to better cooperate with the two-way opening up of the mainland bond market and the process of RMB internationalization. Finally, I wish the Bond Connect Annual Forum a complete success and continue to seek breakthroughs on the existing basis. Thank you! Revised: 04 July 2023

Title: Remarks by CE/MA at Media Standup
text: @IIONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  & Si a M Speeches 07 Jul 2023 Remarks by CE/MA at Media Standup Eddie Yue, Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority Today I would like to announce that, after careful consideration, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has decided to adjust the countercyclical macroprudential measures for property mortgage loans. 2. Since the measures were implemented in 2009, the HKMA has been closely monitoring market conditions, including property prices and transaction volumes, and the local and external economic environment, with the aim of evaluating the need for appropriate adjustments to the measures to ensure that banks manage the risks over their property mortgage lending business effectively, and have sufficient capacity to cope with challenges from a sharp correction in property prices. 3. Following the COVID-19 pandemic and with interest rates rising, there has been a correction in housing prices in Hong Kong since 2022. Despite a rebound early this year, market data showed that at the end of June housing prices were down 13% from their peak in 2021. The situation in the non-residential property market was similar. The prices of offices, flatted factories and retail premises fell by 20%, 8% and 17% respectively from their peaks in 2018-2019. 4. Externally, as major economies continue to face high inflationary pressures, interest rates may remain elevated for some time. Any slow-down in the global economy due to high interest rates would inevitably affect the local economy. Taking all relevant factors into account, the HKMA has decided to make several adjustments to the countercyclical macroprudential measures for property mortgage loans, while continuing to maintain banking stability and ensuring the proper risk management of property mortgage loans. These adjustments include:  Adjusting the maximum loan-to-value (LTV) ratio for self-occupied residential properties. The maximum LTV ratio for residential properties with a value of HK15 million or below will be increased to 70%. For properties valued at more than HK15 million and up to HK30 million, the maximum LTV ratio will be increased to 60%. For residential properties with a value above HK30 million, the maximum LTV ratio will remain unchanged at 50%. To avoid a sudden drop in applicable LTV ratios, ratios for properties in certain value ranges will change gradually. The maximum LTV ratio for non-self-use residential properties will remain unchanged at 50%.  Increasing the maximum LTV ratio for non-residential properties from 50% to 60%.  Increasing the maximum LTV ratio for property mortgage loans assessed based on the net worth of borrowers from 40% to 50%. This adjustment is applicable to both residential and non-residential properties. 5. Since these adjustments are a relaxation of the countercyclical macroprudential measures, they can take ettect trom today and will apply to property transactions with provisional sale and purchase agreements signed today or subsequently. 6. This is the first time the HKMA has relaxed the countercyclical macroprudential measures for residential properties since they were introduced in 2009. We would like to emphasise that, even with these adjustments, the Hong Kong banking sector has ample buffers to cope with any challenges from a sharp correction in property prices. Therefore we consider that there is room to relax these measures. 7. Following these adjustments, property buyers will be able to take out mortgage loans at higher LTV ratios. But I would like to take this opportunity to remind everyone that buying a property is an important life decision. Prospective buyers should carefully assess their ability to afford to purchase a property and the financial risks involved. 8. Later today HKMC Insurance Limited will announce amendments to the Mortgage Insurance Programme aimed at better helping homebuyers to address their housing needs. Last revision date : 07 July 2023

Title: Opening Keynote Speech at Fraud and Financial Crime Asia Summit 2023
text: IIONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY # Mi W 3 M Speeches 13 Jul 2023 Opening Keynote Speech at Fraud and Financial Crime Asia Summit 2023 Carmen Chu, Executive Director (Enforcement and AML), Hong Kong Monetary Authority Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. It is my great pleasure to address the Fraud and Financial Crime Summit again this year. Let me start by thanking Regulation Asia - there really is no substitute for face-to-face events to share knowledge and experience in our objective of combating fraud and financial crime. And I dont need to highlight here that our common task has got harder. In the last few years, financial crime, especially digital fraud, has become a more serious concern. A number of reasons account for this. The pandemic which pushed more of our financial business online was a contributing factor, as were the rapid advances in financial technology that make things so convenient for us, in particular the rise in online-only services and real-time payments, which have also proved very attractive to criminals. The speed of some of the changes has been unprecedented. The situation is worrying: in Hong Kong, a city with a population of 7.5 million, deception cases reported to the Police have more than tripled in recent years with similar increases in financial losses to victims, local and overseas. And there are no signs of this slowing down yet: the HKMA received 637 fraud-related banking complaints in the first six months, already exceeding the total of 555 cases for the whole of last year. Im sure you can all quote similar figures from your own jurisdictions. This leads me to the theme of this forum: How do financial institutions, regulators and law enforcement agencies innovate their response to fraud? How will financial crime systems evolve in the coming years, and what does a more strategic, proactive response look like? We have all heard much about data-driven and technology-aided response to tackle increasing financial crime, and today I want to place these terms in the wider context of a whole-system strategy, and discuss the role of the public sector, in particular regulators, in driving this agenda. The banking sector not only acts as gatekeeper but also provides the majority of data and intelligence on which the success of our mission depends. As the banking regulator, we have been challenging ourselves: how can we be more dynamic and creative, and how should we adapt our own supervision to encourage and enable banks in adapting their front-line controls in a way that collectively improves outcomes for our anti-money laundering regime? How can regulators and financial institutions work together to make sure that the public has strong confidence to conduct business online with financial institutions (FIs), and has faith that effective financial systems could help protect customers against the harm, and the sometimes lite-changing losses, trom traud and tinancial crime? Let me start with the role of data, or evidence, and what we have been doing under our data-driven supervision initiative. By using more complete, accurate, and timely data, both supervisor and banks can analyse threats and track the results more effectively - or put another way, we can better measure and judge the success of our efforts to mitigate identified threats. Based on that understanding, the HKMA has transformed its supervisory approach to the collection, storage and analysis of data, in support of more data-driven supervision, which in turn drives more targeted interventions. We call this our Anti-Money Laundering (AML) surveillance enhancement programme, a long-term commitment to and investment in data and technology, as well as supporting capabilities and culture. The objectives are to better understand and target higher risks in banks, and to create such supervisory and data and analytics environment that supports larger data sets and uses technologies to perform enhanced risk profiling. The implication is an uplift in how we engage with banks on AML data - we will shortly move to an automated common submission portal for data - through which each bank is able to demonstrate effectiveness based on its risks and corresponding Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) programme. Another important part of our roadmap towards a more effective response is the role of technology in aggregating and analysing the huge volume of data that financial crime models generate. Starting in 2019, we engaged banks to understand where they were on their Regtech adoption journeys and then tailored tools and approaches to suit different levels of maturity and use cases, where we and banks see value. Since then we have published a number of guidance documents providing insights and case studies, while in parallel organising AML Regtech Labs - or AMLabs - which allow small groups of banks to target common pain points, identify relevant technology solutions, and gain hands-on experience working alongside technology and data experts. As a result, about 60% of our retail banks are now deploying network analytics, more than twice as many as three years ago, a capability which has already resulted in banks increasing the number of intelligence-led suspicious transaction reports by about 320% in 2022 over a year ago, leading to an increase of over 110% in criminal proceeds restrained or confiscated. The important point to take away is that this roadmap supports a stronger collective response which can tackle changes in threats based on stronger risk understanding and evidence base, and this is where the leadership from the public sector is so important, driving all stakeholders to work more closely together, sharing more data, more information and more know-how. You may have heard this referred to as a whole-system response to financial crime. Public- private partnership amongst the regulator, law enforcement agencies and banks, like the Fraud and Money Laundering Intelligence Taskforce (FMLIT) in Hong Kong is a very good example of this in action, as is the innovative approach to anti-fraud coordination demonstrated by the Anti-Deception Coordination Centre with banks strong support, amidst many similar arrangements including for example Anti-Scam Centre here in O i z-m z-s on lycipui t:. But the roadmap does not end at public-private information sharing channels, successful though they are. The next stage of our roadmap is private-to-private partnership, and when combined with the other elements we have already put in place, such as data analytics capabilities, we start to see the potential which bank-to-bank information sharing represents. The HKMA has collaborated with the industry and Police to recently launch the Financial Intelligence Evaluation Sharing Tool (FINEST), a bank-to-bank information sharing platform which helps increase banks ability to share information for detecting and disrupting fraud and mule account networks more effectively. And we actively participate in international discussions to exchange experiences and adopt consistent approaches in the fight against fraud and financial crime, which poses growing threat to the integrity and stability of global financial systems in the digital era. In parallel to these developments, the HKMA is also running a pilot - Macro Analytics - which for the first time applies analytics to granular financial crime data across multiple banks, including eight retail and virtual banks, to generate new supervisory insights that we hope will help us target and tackle vulnerabilities and threats - such as mule account networks - and therefore help safeguard the integrity and stability of the banking sector. These collaborative approaches are perfect examples of what I spoke of - to be dynamic and creative in how we upscale our results and demonstrate the value we have all invested in the whole-system approach', banks, regulators and law enforcement sharing a common purpose to turn the tables on fraud and financial crime, to reduce harm and losses to members of the public. The public sector stands ready to provide the leadership to embrace new opportunities as part the commitment we have all made as members of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and the Asia Pacific Group on Money Laundering. The private sector is equally important in that commitment and needs to be both dynamic and creative if we are to fully leverage these new opportunities, and make the best possible use of data and technology to empower our new ways of working and innovate our response to the increasing threat which fraud and financial crime present to our societies. I very much hope that I have been able to offer some food for thoughts in the very active debate around effectiveness in anti-financial crime work. I look forward to seeing that debate extended in the panel discussions today and wish you all a truly dynamic and creative day. Thank you. Last revision date : 13 July 2023

Title: Remarks after the US Fed FOMC Meeting
text: IIONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY # Mi W 3 M Speeches 27 Jul 2023 Remarks after the US Fed FOMC Meeting Arthur Yuen, Acting Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1. The Federal Open Market Committee of the Federal Reserve (the Fed) announced a rate hike of 25 basis points early today (Hong Kong time), raising the target range for the federal funds rate to 5.25-5.5%. The HKMA has adjusted the Base Rate upward to 5.75% according to the established mechanism with immediate effect. 2. The 25-basis-point rate hike is in line with market expectations. The Fed has raised the federal funds target range by a total of 525 basis points since March last year. However, inflation in the US remains high, and the high interest rate environment may last for some time. The future interest rate path will be contingent on incoming inflation and employment data, as well as the impact of earlier rate hikes on the economy. 3. Under the Linked Exchange Rate System (LERS), Hong Kong dollar interbank rates generally track their US dollar counterparts. As the US continued to raise interest rates, Hong Kong dollar interbank rates have gradually risen in recent months. The public should be mindful of interest-rate movements and relevant risks when purchasing property, taking out mortgages or making other borrowing decisions. 4. The Hong Kong dollar exchange rate has strengthened in recent months, not only driven by dividend payment-related demand from listed corporations, but also reflecting the effective operation of the automatic interest rate adjustment mechanism under the LERS. 5. The HKMA will continue to closely monitor market developments and maintain monetary and financial stability. Last revision date : 27 July 2023

Title: Welcome remarks at FPS x SME Seminar (Chinese version)
text: HONG KONG MONETARY AUTHORITY  Speeches 2023-09-26 Welcome speech at the "FPS X SMEs" Seminar David Lee is the Deputy Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Hello to SMEs, banks, SVF operators, distinguished guests and media friends!  Thank you for joining the "FPS X SMEs" seminar today, and it is my pleasure to discuss with you the importance and development opportunities of FPS in the SME payment sector.  This September marks the fifth anniversary of the launch of the FPS, and we have witnessed the rapid development of FPS in person-to-person payments, which has been well received by the public. We expect the FPS adoption to reach another milestone and become more widely used at the enterprise level.  Why are SMEs our special focus? This is because SMEs are an important part of Hong Kong's economy. Just like the theme design of the screen wall at this seminar, each square represents a different SME, which plays an important role in building Hong Kong into an international financial centre. We hope to enhance the competitiveness of SMEs by promoting their adoption of FPS and help them integrate into the era of electronic payments, which is one of the objectives of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to promote financial inclusion.  We are organising this seminar to make SMEs more aware of FPS. FPS not only brings business benefits to businesses, but also makes our lives more convenient. In the past, most TCM clinics only accepted cash, but now some TCM clinics accept FPS payment for medical consultations, such as learning to drive, buy cookies, and recharge games, and scan the QR code of the FPS. As you may refer to this SME Testimonial, it can be seen that regardless of size, traditional or emerging industries, as well as start-ups, FPS can improve their operational efficiency, reduce administrative work and increase their cash flow. Later, we have invited two SMEs to share their views on the application and benefits of FPS.  We have been working hard to encourage banks and SVF operators to offer more affordable FPS solutions that meet the needs of SMEs. We would like to thank the industry for their support, in addition to launching different offers for corporate and individual customers in celebration of the 5th anniversary of the FPS, a number of banks and SVF operators have also set up exhibitions at the site today to introduce FPS solutions and offer discounts to SMEs with their products and services. To support this, Hong Kong Interbank Clearing Limited, which operates the FPS, will also waive the settlement fees of banks and SVF operators in processing real-time payments made by enterprises and merchants via FPS in October this year, with a view to encouraging them to give back to SMEs and merchants, attracting more enterprises to adopt FPS and achieve the goals of innovation, efficiency enhancement and business opportunities.  Over the past five years, we have been working with the industry to enhance FPS capabilities and expand application scenarios. We are delighted that FPS has been very well received since its launch. Nearly 13 million registrations have been registered, an average annual growth of 36 per cent.  FPS usage has also continued to grow steadily, with daily HKD real-time trading volume and turnover increasing by an average of 71% and 41% annually over the past five years. In August this year alone, an average of 1.25 million real-time Hong Kong dollar transactions were processed per day.  The application scope of FPS has gradually expanded from person-to-person payments to bill payments, account top-ups, and payments to retail merchants and corporations for collection and payment. In addition, more than 90% of government departments offer FPS as a payment option, providing more convenient and efficient payment options for the public. The data we have been collecting shows that the use of FPS is increasing in different scenarios, and even compared with other payment instruments, the market share has also increased, providing merchants with an additional option to collect payments.  In the future, we will continue to expand our use cases, one of which is to use FPS for cross-border payments. I am pleased that the collaboration between the HKMA and the Central Bank of Thailand has come to fruition, and the scheme for the FPS and Thailand PromptPay interconnection is expected to be launched by the end of this year, when Hong Kong residents can use FPS to make retail payments in Thailand, and Thailand visitors can use rpromptPayj, a local faster payment system, to pay to Hong Kong merchants in Hong Kong, providing a safe, convenient and brand-new payment experience for travellers from both places. This cooperation also lays a good foundation for us to further expand our cross-border payment services in the future.  Last but not least, I would like to thank all SME representatives for their participation, as well as the support of chambers of commerce, banks, SVF operators and Hong Kong Interbank Clearing Limited. The symposium is a unique opportunity to further facilitate exchanges, share experiences and forge closer partnerships between the industry and SMEs. Thank you! Revised: 26/09/2023
